## DL-228 — The reference channel server gains a LOCAL-EXEC `clear_context` MCP tool, gated ORTHOGONALLY to the board tools and never proxied to the bridge

**Date:** 2026-07-24
**Context:** The channel server (`examples/channel-servers/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs`) advertises two board tools (`board_my_cards`/`board_create_card`, DL-217) that it PROXIES to the bridge over HTTP/SSH. A separate need: let an agent clear its own Claude context to save tokens as the deliberate final act of a turn, by spawning the local `clear-agent.sh` helper. That is a self-management action with nothing to do with the board and no bridge round-trip — routing it through the proxy would be wrong (it has no `{tool,args}` bridge contract, and the clear terminates the very session that would await a response). Card 5089.
**Decision — a third MCP tool, `clear_context`, on an independent gate and a LOCAL-EXEC dispatch path that branches BEFORE the proxy.**
- **Advertise gate (`shouldAdvertiseClearContext()`), orthogonal to `shouldAdvertiseTools()`:** listed iff `process.env.STY` is set (the session runs inside GNU `screen`) AND `clear-agent.sh` resolves on `PATH` (idiomatic left-to-right `$PATH` search for an `X_OK` file; no hardcoded path). It shares NONE of the board-tools terms — a bare-channel seat with board tools off can still arm `clear_context`, and a fully board-tools-wired seat with no `$STY`/helper does not. The `tools` MCP capability + the `tools/list`/`tools/call` handlers now register when EITHER family is advertised (`ADVERTISE_ANY_TOOL`).
- **Dispatch:** `tools/call` branches `name === 'clear_context'` FIRST — before the ssh/http proxy — so it never leaves the host even when board tools are on. It spawns `clear-agent.sh` DETACHED (`spawn(helper, [], {detached:true, stdio:'ignore'})` + `unref()`) and returns a normal MCP result immediately without awaiting the child (the clear terminates this session). Called-but-not-armed (`$STY` unset or helper absent) returns a STRUCTURED MCP error, never a silent no-op. The tool's `description` carries the operational guardrails (final-action-of-turn, after committing work + posting handoff, never mid-task) as model-facing usage guidance.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) fold it into the board-tools proxy path — rejected: it is not a board tool, has no bridge contract, and must not depend on `TOOLS_ENABLED`. (b) put the predicate/helpers in `channel-lib.mjs` for unit-testability — rejected: that module is documented as strictly side-effect-free (no env reads, no I/O); `shouldAdvertiseClearContext()` reads `$STY` and does `fs.access`, so it stays in the main file mirroring `shouldAdvertiseTools()`, and the tests drive the REAL server over stdio instead. (c) advertise unconditionally and error only on call — rejected: an unusable tool should not appear in `tools/list`.
**Tests (`tests/clear-context.test.mjs`, 5 cases, real server over the MCP SDK stdio client):** advertised when armed (with the empty inputSchema asserted); ABSENT when `$STY` unset while board tools stay on (orthogonality); advertised with board tools off (orthogonality the other way); a `tools/call` spawns the detached helper (proven by a fake `clear-agent.sh` writing its pid/pgid — a detached child is a session leader so `pgid==pid`) and does NOT hit a live recording bridge endpoint (zero hits); a not-armed call returns a structured error. PROVE-IT-CAN-FAIL: reverting the advertise gate (listing `CLEAR_CONTEXT_TOOL` unconditionally) makes the "absent when `$STY` unset" test go RED — verified. Channel-server `package.json` version bumped 0.7.3 → 0.8.0 (the supply-chain workflow's downstream-drift guard, DL-038). Card 5089.

## DL-229 — `bridge:check` certifies the DEPLOYED channel-server SNAPSHOT (new optional `channel.server_path`), branching existence-before-classification, with a per-language comparator lockstep against the python provisioner

**Date:** 2026-07-24
**Context:** `bridge:check` certified the channel **socket** — the RUNNING process — and never the deployed channel-server **files** the next session respawns from. A stale or unlaunchable `examples/channel-servers` copy therefore reported `channel socket live` and exited **0**; the failure only materialized at the next session start, as live-wake silently never coming back (the worst shape: a green check, then a dark seat). Two real deployment topologies produce it — a **copied** snapshot that drifts behind the checkout, and a **symlinked** one that goes dangling when the checkout moves (`examples/channel-servers/README.md` asserted a symlink "needs no check", which is false: it *trades* drift risk for dangling risk, it does not remove a failure mode). Card 5108.
**Decision — an optional, operator-DECLARED path plus a three-branch check, both fail-loud and both no-ops when undeclared.**
- **(a) New optional `channel.server_path`** (`ChannelConfig::$serverPath`): an absolute path to the deployed channel-server DIRECTORY or its entry `.mjs` (normalized to the directory at load, no stat). Format-validated exactly like `channel.socket` via `SocketPath::isValid` (absolute, no `..`, no null byte ⇒ throws at load); **no `${…}` expansion** (a plain absolute path is sufficient, and reusing the socket's runtime-token helper would import a socket-worded error contract into a directory field). **Absent ⇒ the snapshot legs SKIP with a NOTICE**, never silently and never a FAIL — every existing install keeps its exit code. **[DL-236 renames that NOTICE without changing it: the finding now carries severity `unvalidated`, never `ok`, and renders PLAIN rather than green. The behavior this bullet describes is intact — the legs still skip, the exit code is still untouched, and that promise is now asserted as a property (`emitFinding` returns false IFF `fail`) rather than observed. But "notice" is the name DL-236 alternative (c) explicitly REJECTS: it names a decision about the check, while the operator's question is about the measurement. Read "NOTICE" here as `unvalidated`.]**
- **(b) NEVER INFERRED.** Reading the agent's `.mcp.json` to derive the path was rejected outright: the bridge may run as a **different OS user** and cannot read it, so inference produces a *confident wrong answer* — the worst failure for a diagnostic. The precedent is `board_tools.ssh_account` (DL-224), an optional key added for exactly this reason: `bridge:check` must be **told** an agent-side fact it cannot infer.
- **(c) EXISTENCE BEFORE CLASSIFICATION — the branch order is load-bearing.** The path is resolved **non-strictly** (a strict resolve errors instead of returning a verdict on exactly the seat that most needs one), then: **(1)** the resolved path does not exist ⇒ **FAIL** (*dangling symlink or removed directory; the link target moved, repoint the symlink*), or, when it exists but is **not a directory**, a separate FAIL (*`server_path` names a file, not the channel-server directory*) — `AgentConfig` normalizes only the `.mjs` entry suffix, so an operator pointing at `server.js` / a wrapper resolves fine and must not be sent after a symlink that isn't there — **and neither fatal is asserted unless we can SEE the path** (below); **(2)** `realpath(resolved) === realpath(base_path('examples/channel-servers'))` ⇒ repo-direct-equivalent: the snapshot IS the checkout, so the version compare is a meaningless self-compare and is skipped; **(3)** differs ⇒ a genuine snapshot: run the version leg too. Testing existence FIRST is not cosmetic: a dangling symlink resolves non-strictly to a **stale** path that differs from the checkout, so classifying first would drop it into branch 3 and version-compare against a directory that is not there — **misreporting a fatal condition as a drift question**.
- **(d) Classify on the RESOLVED REALPATH, never a string/prefix test on the configured path.** The common symlink topology (`~/agent-webhook-bridge-channel → <checkout>/examples/channel-servers`) LOOKS external but resolves internal; a prefix test would misclassify it and emit the spurious self-compare this card exists to prevent. Realpath equally handles a link into a **different** bridge checkout (resolves outside ⇒ genuinely a snapshot ⇒ the compare is meaningful).
- **(c′) VISIBILITY IS A PRECONDITION OF EVERY STAT, not a branch — the guard is ONE primitive.** `is_dir()`/`is_file()` return false for EACCES exactly as for ENOENT, so *no* stat-derived verdict is one we are entitled to draw unless this process can traverse to the path. `ChannelSnapshotProbe::visibleOrUnverified()` is that single guard, returning the same **WARN** (*not visible to this user; snapshot could NOT be validated*) in place of a fatal. It is called **once per population whose traversability is an independent question** — TWO sites: the branch-(1) existence test (naming the configured→resolved path), and the **deployed directory, gated once before either leg** (naming the DIRECTORY). Two is the complete set because **every** stat the legs make is a DIRECT CHILD of the deployed directory (`package.json`, the entry file, `node_modules`), so all of them turn on that one `+x` and none needs its own guard. **[DL-230 adds a THIRD site for a third such population — the deployed SUBDIRECTORIES its completeness walk descends into, which the hoisted gate says nothing about, so read "two is the complete set" as the state DL-229 shipped. The rule itself is unchanged; the *count* is what moved.]** Guarding per-*stat* instead was the first shape and it was worse on two counts: they all fired together — emitting the identical WARN **twice** — and each named a **file** (`…/package.json`, then `…/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs`) as the "channel server path", sending the operator to `chmod +x` a file when the directory is what needs it. One deliberate asymmetry: the **bundled** (this checkout's) `package.json` is *not* guarded — an unreadable one already lands on an accurate no-remediation WARN, whereas the guard's message would talk about the agent's deployed directory while naming a checkout file. Putting the guard only on branch (1) was **not sufficient and shipped broken in review**: `ancestorIsTraversable()` starts at `dirname()`, so it fires only when an **ancestor** denies traversal, while the topology DL-227 is actually built around is the **deployment directory itself** being `0700`/`0000` to the bridge's user — statting a directory needs `+x` on its *parent*, not on itself, so `is_dir($resolved)` returns **true**, branch (1) is skipped entirely, and a healthy, current deployment was reported *"entry does not exist — server_path does not point at a channel-server deployment"* with `cp -R` remediation **that would overwrite it**. The converse is unavoidable and accepted: under an untraversable directory a genuinely dangling path also reports unverified rather than fatal — the process cannot distinguish them and no heuristic can, so the snapshot legs are **conclusive only when the bridge can traverse to the deployed directory**, said plainly in `docs/config-schema.md`. **[And DL-237 puts the count BACK: the completeness walk that added the third site is retired, so "two is the complete set" is the current state again — the configured path and the deployed directory. The rule was never what moved; only the count was, twice.]** **[card#6025:** there is no `ChannelSnapshotProbe::visibleOrUnverified()` in the tree today — the entry records the code as it stood; DL-254 hoisted the guard to `PathVisibility::unverifiedUnlessVisible()`.**]**
- **(e) Two legs — plus the branch-(1) fatals in (c), four distinct FAILs in all, each naming one distinct operator action.** **[DL-230 makes it THREE legs and FIVE FAILs — its version-gated completeness leg is the third leg and the fifth FAIL (*claims version X … but is MISSING N of the M files a whole-directory copy delivers*), and it lives INSIDE the version leg because the gate is the two `package.json` versions that leg already read. Read the counts here as the state DL-229 shipped; the "one distinct operator action per FAIL" rule is unchanged and the new FAIL's action is the whole-directory re-copy. This paragraph is otherwise still the complete emission list for the DL-229 legs.]** **Version leg (WARN):** deployed `package.json` `version` vs the checkout's; deployed lower ⇒ warn naming both versions, the one-time re-sync command, **and the permanent cure** — a *symlinked* deployment resolves into the checkout, so the compare becomes a self-compare (branch 2) and the staleness class cannot recur. The symlink is offered, not prescribed: cross-host and separate-OS-user topologies genuinely need a copy, and `docs/multi-host.md` says to leave `server_path` unset there. Never a fail — a stale copy still launches, it just lacks newer fixes. **Presence leg (FAIL ×2):** the **entry file** must exist (absent ⇒ *`server_path` does not point at a channel-server deployment; the MCP server will not launch at next session start* — without this single existence test a `server_path` naming an EMPTY directory certifies clean), and the deployed directory must have a **`node_modules`** (absent ⇒ *dependencies are not installed; run `npm ci` in it*). Bare specifiers *resolving* is npm's business; the directory being absent is not: a `cp -R`'d snapshot whose operator stopped before `npm ci` dies on `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk'` at the next session start — the most common real instance of "green check, then a dark seat", and it is produced by half-completing *this probe's own* re-sync advice. Both apply to the repo-direct branch too: an agent launching straight out of the checkout needs an entry file and `node_modules` exactly as much. **The ok-message claims only what was STAT'ed** — "has its entry file and node_modules — a presence check, not a load test" — never that the entry *loads*: nothing here executes node, so a load claim is one this probe cannot make. **[DL-237 returns the counts to what this paragraph states: the completeness leg and its FAIL are retired, so it is TWO legs and FOUR FAILs again. The version leg gained NOTHING: the `unvalidated` launch disclosure DL-237 adds is appended in `probe()`, once per run that reached the legs and on every branch that did **[DL-251: once per AGENT, not once per run — `ChannelSnapshotCheck` is a `PerAgentCheck`]** — not on the version-EQUAL branch, and not emitted by the version leg at all. (An earlier revision of this amendment said otherwise; it described the narrow first shape, which was rejected in review before it shipped.) It is not a FAIL and never touches the exit code.]**
- **(f) THERE IS NO COMPLETENESS-VS-REFERENCE LEG, and its absence is deliberate.** Two mechanisms for one were built and both were cut: a **text scan** of the deployed entry for relative import specifiers, which failed three consecutive review rounds in the same direction — each round it matched a specifier the source did not really import (comments, string literals, a regex literal leaving an unpaired backtick, a PCRE JIT-stack failure whose `?? $source` fallback handed the unstripped source to the scanner), turning a healthy, `node --check`-valid, operator-**customized** entry into a FAIL whose remediation (`cp -R` over it) destroys the customization; and then a **file-set comparison** against this checkout's `examples/channel-servers`, which removed that surface but reddened the opposite population — a snapshot taken at an older tag is legitimately missing files the checkout has since added (of the 10 files the reference set holds today, `channel-lib.mjs` + `tests/channel-lib.test.mjs` first shipped in v0.69.1, `tests/marker-refusal.test.mjs` in v0.69.0 and `tests/clear-context.test.mjs` in v0.70.0 — verified with `git log --diff-filter=A`), so a **stale-but-complete** whole-directory copy taken before v0.69.0 read as 4 of 10 files missing and FAILed with *"it did not come from a whole-directory copy"*, false about what the operator actually did, on a population `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` records as an observed fleet fact. **It was cut rather than tuned a third time because for a stale install the completeness verdict is not actionable:** the STALE warn already carries the entire remediation (re-copy the whole directory + `npm ci`), which fixes incompleteness too, so the verdict changes nothing the operator does. What survives is the **entry-file presence** test in (e) — one existence check with no false-positive surface, answering "is there anything here to launch?" rather than "does this match the reference?"; the deployed directory is never enumerated and no file's CONTENT is ever read. **[DL-230 reopens the file-set form ONLY, and only version-GATED; the enumeration claim in this sentence describes the state DL-229 shipped. The text scan stays rejected — permanently.]** **[TRUE AGAIN as of DL-237, and for a stronger reason than this paragraph had. DL-230 reopened the file-set form version-gated; it is retired once more, this time because a LAUNCH was measured to be more precise than the enumeration in BOTH directions — the pruned population this paragraph could only hypothesize was observed. The deployed directory is never enumerated and no file's CONTENT is ever read: current state. The text scan stays rejected, permanently, on the original grounds.]**
- **(g) `package.json` unreadability is FOUR causes, not one, and only one of them wants the destructive advice.** The version leg emitted a single *"package.json is missing or unreadable … re-copy the directory (`cp -R …`)"* for all of: absent, present-but-unreadable (`0000`, ordinary under DL-227's cross-user topology and *proven reachable* here — the hoisted `+x` gate passes, so this is a per-FILE read failure, not an invisible path), and malformed/non-object JSON. For three of the four the message was **false** ("missing" when the file is right there) and for two the advice was **wrong**: `cp -R` does not fix a permission denial (the copy lands with the same ownership problem) and does not need to replace a whole directory to repair one corrupt manifest — while it *does* overwrite the entry file and every other local edit on its way past. `readManifest()` returns a `{status, version}` discriminated result and each cause gets its own reason phrase + its own advice (absent ⇒ the re-sync; unreadable ⇒ re-run as the agent's user / grant read; malformed ⇒ repair the manifest). The same split applies to the BUNDLED manifest's message, which carried the identical false "missing or unreadable" disjunction — one copy of a defect fixed and one left is two defects (canon #7). An absent deployed `package.json` is a WARN and not a FAIL: the entry file and `node_modules` are what a launch needs, and both may be present.
**Per-language lockstep with the python provisioner (the subtle part).** The DECLARED AUTHORITY for snapshot comparison semantics is `_version_tuple`/`_package_version` in **`bin/provision-board-tools.py`** — it ships, it is proven, and it is what actually decides whether a deployed snapshot gets replaced. The python is **unmodified**; the PHP conforms to it **for ASCII-digit versions whose chunks fit PHP's integer range** (`ChannelSnapshotProbe::compareVersions`: split on `.`, leading digits per chunk (0 if none), element-wise integer compare, shorter tuple sorts lower). Divergence outside that bound falls in exactly two classes, both **unreachable through an npm `version` field**, and each pinned by an assertion rather than asserted from recall: (1) **non-ASCII digits** — python's `\d` is Unicode-aware, PHP's `[0-9]` is not, so `٣٢` reads as `32` there and `0` here. `/u` does **not** close it: `[0-9]` is an ASCII class with or without the modifier (`preg_match('/^[0-9]+/u', '٣٢')` matches **nothing**, exactly as unmodified — the match-then-cast-to-`0` behavior belongs to `\d` + `/u`, which still does not produce python's `32`), while `/u` alone newly returns `false` on invalid UTF-8, collapsing a chunk that reads fine today (`2\xff` ⇒ `2`). The pattern is spelled `[0-9]` to state the ASCII scope outright, and the four `preg_match` facts above are asserted in `ChannelSnapshotProbeTest::test_version_tuple_is_ascii_digit_scoped` so the refusal to add `/u` rests on executed behavior, not on a remembered mechanism. (2) **integers above `PHP_INT_MAX`**, where PHP saturates and python is arbitrary-precision. Documented bound, pinned by a test, not chased. **PHP's `version_compare()` is forbidden here** and the code carries a comment saying so: it honors the pre-release/build tags the authority deliberately drops, and diverges on **3 of 7** measured vectors (`0.8.0-rc1` vs `0.8.0`, `0.8.0` vs `0.8.0+build5`, `1.0.0-alpha` vs `1.0.0`) — `bridge:check` would say "stale" while the provisioner says "up to date", and re-syncing would never clear the warning. The 7 pairs are a **shared test-vector table asserted in BOTH suites** (`tests/Unit/Support/ChannelSnapshotProbeTest::versionVectors` and `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py` class `VersionComparatorLockstep`), each site naming the other by path so the pair is discoverable, plus a guard that `_deploy_snapshot` still *decides* on `_version_tuple` (a rewrite to a string/float compare would silently unbind the two while every vector still passed). This follows the fleet's write-contract per-language guard rule: a shared contract implemented in N languages carries its own guard in each. **This comparator is the ONLY cross-language contract the probe mirrors** — the deleted file-set leg had a second one (`SnapshotFileSetLockstep`, pinning `copytree`'s `ignore_patterns`), and it went with the leg rather than being left as a guard over a contract nothing reads. **[No longer true as of DL-230: the file-set leg is back (version-gated) and `SnapshotFileSetLockstep` came back with it — it is live at `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py`, paired with the PHP side in `tests/Unit/Support/ChannelSnapshotProbeTest`. There are now TWO cross-language contracts the probe mirrors, this comparator and the enumeration; see DL-230 (d), which is authoritative for the second. Both follow the same fleet write-contract per-language guard rule stated above.]** **[DL-237 restores this paragraph's original claim: `SnapshotFileSetLockstep` is removed a second time, with the leg, exactly as reasoned here — a guard over a conformance no code reads pins nothing. The comparator is once again the ONLY cross-language contract the probe mirrors.]**
**Alternatives considered:** (a) infer `server_path` from the agent's `.mcp.json` — rejected, see (b): unreadable across OS users, and a confident wrong answer is worse than an honest "not validated". (b) Make the whole leg a WARN so `bridge:check` never fails on it — rejected: a dangling path, a `server_path` pointing at nothing launchable, or a dependency-less deployment means the MCP server **will not launch**; that is exactly the silent-at-next-session failure the card exists to make loud, and a warn on a green exit is what we already had. (c) Shell out to `node --check` to establish loadability — rejected: it parses without resolving imports (blind to the actual failure) and adds a Node runtime dependency to `bridge:check`. (d) Shell out to the python provisioner for the version compare (one implementation, no lockstep) — rejected: `bridge:check` would gain a python + script-path dependency for a 12-line pure function; the lockstep vector table is the cheaper, more discoverable guard. (e) Put the check inline in `CheckCommand` — rejected: the comparator is pure and deserves direct unit coverage, so it lives in `App\Bridge\Support\ChannelSnapshotProbe` emitting the same `{severity, message}` findings shape `SshTransportProbe` already established (canon #5). (f) Patch the import text scan a fourth time — rejected, see (f). (g) Keep the file-set comparison and narrow it (only `.mjs` files; only a hand-picked "load-bearing" subset; version-aware — skip files added after the deployed version) — rejected: the first two re-introduce a judgment heuristic with no authority behind it, the third needs a per-file "added in version X" ledger the repo does not have, and none of them changes what a stale operator does (see (f)). **[AMENDED by DL-230 — do not read (g) as rejecting what later shipped. A version-gated file-set comparison IS now in `bridge:check`, and the objection above does not reach it. What (g) weighed was narrowing the COMPARISON so it could still be run against a stale snapshot — "skip files added after the deployed version" is a per-file question and does need the ledger. DL-230 narrows the POPULATION instead: the full, unnarrowed comparison runs only when the deployed and bundled versions are EQUAL, and the leg is skipped entirely otherwise. That needs nothing beyond the two `package.json` versions the version leg already reads — no ledger, no per-file metadata — and (g)'s other objection ("changes nothing a stale operator does") is left intact rather than argued with, because under the gate the stale operator is never asked the question. The "hand-picked load-bearing subset" and ".mjs only" variants stay rejected on the original grounds.]** (h) Downgrade the file-set FAIL to a WARN instead of cutting it — rejected: it would fire on the same stale-but-complete population, adding a second warning line beside the STALE warn that points at the same single action. **[DL-237 note on (g): the version-gated comparison DL-230 shipped is now retired, so (g)'s conclusion — no file-set comparison in `bridge:check` — holds again. Neither (g)'s original objections nor DL-230's answer to them is what decided it: the deciding evidence is that launching the entry answers the question the comparison was approximating, more precisely, in both directions.]**
**Also corrects DL-038** (which stays frozen): its README note "compare your copy's version against canonical; **a symlink never drifts**" was read as *a symlink needs no check* — true about drift, wrong about the failure mode it trades into (silent dangling). Its rejected alternative (c), "a `bridge:check` sub-check comparing a deployed channel server against the reference — the bridge doesn't know where downstream copies live", is what this DL adopts in the narrow form above: `channel.server_path` is precisely the operator **telling** it where. The `README.md` sentence is rewritten and the released `docs/CHANGELOG.md` v0.30.0 parenthetical carries a bracketed correction pointing here.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `tests/Feature/Console/BridgeCommandsTest` — the undeclared-path notice (exit 0) **[DL-236: that test additionally asserts the severity is exactly `unvalidated` and explicitly NOT `ok`, and that the run prints the closing tally; the exit-0 assertion is unchanged]**; the dangling FAIL (exit 1, *repoint the symlink*, and NOT the other FAIL texts); the not-a-deployment FAIL (an empty directory ⇒ exit 1, *does not point at a channel-server deployment*, and NOT the ok text — the assertion that keeps an empty `server_path` from certifying clean); the names-a-file FAIL; the no-`node_modules` FAIL (exit 1, *run npm ci in …*, and NOT the other FAIL texts, and NOT the ok text); the **"never says loads"** assertion on a healthy snapshot; the stale-version WARN (exit 0, naming both versions, `npm ci`, **and the symlink permanent cure**); a current snapshot via the entry-`.mjs` form; the **three split `package.json` causes** — absent (*is not present*, keeps `cp -R`, exit 0), unreadable-`0000` (*exists but is not readable by this user*, exit 0, **no `cp -R`**), malformed (*does not parse as a JSON object*, *repair the manifest*, no `cp -R`) — all three red under a collapse back to the single "missing or unreadable" message; the repo-direct branch (version leg skipped, presence leg still run and asserted rather than special-cased, `node_modules` pinned rather than inherited from the ambient checkout); and the **two visibility siblings** — `chmod 0000` on an ANCESTOR, and on the **deployed directory itself** (the branch-1-only guard's blind spot; also asserting **exactly one** WARN naming the **directory**, not a file). `tests/Feature/Config/AgentConfigTest` — default null, directory kept, entry-`.mjs` normalized, relative / `..` / null-byte throws. `tests/Unit/Support/ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` — the 7 shared vectors (both directions); the `version_compare` divergence pinned to exactly the 3 expected rows **and asserted against the SUT in the same loop**; the ASCII-digit/int-range conformance bound. `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py` — the same 7 vectors against the python authority, plus the guard that `_deploy_snapshot` still DECIDES on `_version_tuple`.
