## DL-230 — The snapshot COMPLETENESS leg returns, gated on VERSION EQUALITY: a deployment claiming to be current may not lack a file the current reference ships (DL-229 (g)'s third option, reopened in the one form that has no false-red population) **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237 — the completeness leg is RETIRED. Measurement, not argument: a pruned-but-working deployment missing 6 of the 10 reference files FAILs this leg while `node` binds and exits 0, and the DL-230 incident itself is caught by a LAUNCH. The launch belongs to the SEAT, not to `bridge:check` — the bridge runs as a different OS user, so launching from there proves the entry loads for the wrong user. Read this entry as the state v0.71.0 shipped; the paragraphs the measurement falsified carry their own notes below.]**

**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Context — DL-229 passes GREEN on the incident that motivated the entire feature.** Reproduced against the shipped check: a deployment whose entry `.mjs` **and** `package.json` were copied from the CURRENT reference, with a `node_modules` left over from a prior install, and `channel-lib.mjs` — the sibling module the entry imports, shipped since v0.69.1 — NOT copied, reports `[ok] snapshot is current (deployed 0.8.1 >= bundled 0.8.1)` + `[ok] deployment has its entry file and node_modules`, **exit 0**, while `node` on that same directory gives `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The cherry-pick carried the **version stamp with it**, so the version leg reads current; the entry and `node_modules` are exactly the two things the presence leg tests, so it is satisfied by construction. Every DL-229 leg is individually right and the SET of them has a hole precisely where the motivating failure lives — a green check, then a dark seat, which is the failure shape card 5108 existed to end. Card 5142.
**Decision — reinstate the file-set comparison DL-229 (f) cut, and gate it on version EQUALITY.** The gate is the whole design; the comparison itself is the same one that was built and cut. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237: the comparison is gone again. The GATE was sound and is not what failed — what failed is the premise underneath BOTH the gated and ungated forms, that a file-set compare is a usable stand-in for "will this launch". It is not, in either direction.]**

| deployed vs checkout | completeness |
| --- | --- |
| `<` (stale) | **SKIPPED entirely** — the STALE warn stands alone |
| `==` | **RUN** — any missing reference file ⇒ **FAIL** |
| `>` (newer) | **SKIPPED**, and said in a message of its own |

- **(a) Why the gate dissolves the objection that cut it.** The leg was cut because *ungated* it reddened the one population that legitimately lacks reference files: a whole-directory copy taken at an older tag is missing everything the checkout has added since (a pre-v0.69.0 copy reads 4 of 10 missing), and for that population the verdict is **not actionable** — the STALE warn already carries the identical remediation (re-copy the whole directory + `npm ci`), so the extra FAIL changes nothing the operator does. Both of those are properties of the STALE population *only*. Gate on equality and that population is never asked the question. What remains is a population with no benign explanation: **any** change to **any** file under `examples/channel-servers/` requires a `package.json` version bump, enforced on every PR by the DL-038 `version-bump-guard` job in `.github/workflows/channel-server-supply-chain.yml` (it diffs `base...HEAD` over the whole directory minus `node_modules` and hard-fails an unbumped `version`). Equal versions therefore mean the same **tracked** file set **by repo-enforced invariant**, not by assumption — which is what makes the incident visible: the cherry-pick carries a current version stamp and reads healthy on every other leg, while lacking a file the reference ships. **The invariant reaches TRACKED content only, and the reference set this leg builds is the WORKING TREE, so it does not warrant a claim about how the deployment was ASSEMBLED — an untracked stray in the checkout puts a faithful whole-directory copy in the same FAIL population (see (f)). The FAIL therefore states the measurement (the two counts, the missing paths, the `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` consequence, the re-copy) and no cause.** The verdict is actionable either way: the remediation is the same whole-directory re-copy. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237 — this bullet is still accurate about the STALE population and about what version equality buys; what it does not survive is "what remains is a population with no benign explanation". A deliberately PRUNED deployment is version-equal, benign, working, and FAILed. It was hypothesized in (f) and has since been OBSERVED.]**
- **(b) `deployed > checkout` SKIPS, and the message says so — a ruling, not a fall-out of `>=`.** The checkout is not authoritative for a deployment newer than itself: a file this reference does not ship may simply not exist here yet, so "missing" would be a claim about the checkout, not about the deployment. Left to the existing `>=` comparison this would have silently become "run it", which is the shape of defect this DL exists to fix — so it is a distinct branch with a distinct `ok` finding naming both versions (*is NEWER than this checkout … completeness … SKIPPED: an older reference cannot say what a newer snapshot should contain*). The `<` branch gets NO such line, deliberately: DL-229 (h) rejected a second line beside the STALE warn pointing at the same single action, and that objection is still right. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237: with no completeness leg there is nothing left to announce a skip OF, so that second `ok` line — whose entire content was "completeness against X SKIPPED" — is REMOVED rather than rewritten. Leaving it would have named machinery that no longer exists, in operator-facing output. The `<` branch still gets no line, on this bullet's own unchanged DL-229 (h) grounds.]**
- **(c) The text scan is NOT reopened and never will be.** DL-229 (f) records three consecutive adversarial rounds in the same direction — every round it matched a specifier the source did not really import, turning a healthy, `node --check`-valid, operator-CUSTOMIZED entry into a FAIL whose remediation destroys the customization. This DL reopens the **file-set** form only. It reads no file's CONTENT, and it compares in ONE direction: **extra** files in the deployment (local modules, scratch files, an operator's own additions) are not a defect and are never looked at.
- **(d) The enumeration conforms to `_deploy_snapshot`, and the conformance is pinned in BOTH languages.** The reference set is not a rule of our choosing: it is whatever `shutil.copytree(source, deploy_dir, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("node_modules"), dirs_exist_ok=True)` in `bin/provision-board-tools.py` actually delivers — **recursive, dotfiles included, anything named `node_modules` excluded at ANY depth** (`.gitignore` and `.mcp.json.example` are two of the ten files today, so "dotfiles included" is load-bearing, not hypothetical). `ChannelSnapshotProbe::referenceFileSet()` mirrors it and is public for the same reason `versionTuple` is: a **shared synthetic tree + expected set** is run through the real `copytree` in `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py` (class `SnapshotFileSetLockstep`) and through the PHP enumerator in `tests/Unit/Support/ChannelSnapshotProbeTest`, each naming the other, plus a source-text pin that `_deploy_snapshot` still copies that way (a switch to a hand-picked file list would otherwise unbind the two while every vector still passed). This is the second cross-language contract the probe mirrors — the comparator (DL-229) is the first — and it follows the same fleet write-contract per-language guard rule. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237: `referenceFileSet()` is deleted and `SnapshotFileSetLockstep` went with it — the same disposition DL-229 gave it the first time, since a guard over a conformance no code depends on pins nothing. `VersionComparatorLockstep` is unaffected; the probe mirrors ONE cross-language contract again.]** *[Additive annotation, 2026-08-21 (card#7127): the SUPERSEDED note above names the deleted member bare, and the doc-sync gate now reads its removed-marker at SENTENCE scope, so it discharges only the citations it repeats. Repeating it here rather than editing either sentence: `ChannelSnapshotProbe::referenceFileSet()` was removed by DL-237 and is declared nowhere in this tree. Both original sentences stand as written, per this log's frozen-original convention (DL-277).]*
- **(e) A THIRD visibility site, and it is load-bearing.** DL-229 (c′) hoisted ONE traversability gate in front of both legs, correct *because* every stat they make is a DIRECT CHILD of the deployed directory. The completeness walk breaks that premise: a reference file under `tests/` is stat'ed through a subdirectory whose own traversability is an independent question, and a `0700` `tests/` in the deployment would otherwise read as "all of its files are missing" and hand out `cp -R` over a healthy deployment — the DL-229 round-1 blocker exactly, one level down. `deployedState()` therefore walks the relative path segment by segment, proving `+x` on each directory *before* statting inside it, and returns the same single "not visible to this user" WARN naming the subdirectory that denies traversal (the message hoisted into `unverifiedWarn()`, still spelled once). `PATH_ABSENT` is conclusive only because the segment above it was proven traversable first. **A blocked path leaves the ACCOUNTING, never the WALK.** The rule is *absence is not conclusive where we could not see*, **not** *one unseeable path voids every seen one* — and the first shape got that wrong: it `return`ed the visibility WARN on the first `PATH_BLOCKED`, discarding every file already proven absent through a traversable parent, so a version-matched deployment genuinely missing `channel-lib.mjs` beside a `0700` `tests/` emitted one WARN and exited **0**. That is this DL's own defect class (green check, dark seat) in a narrow sub-population. The walk therefore continues past a block, still FAILs on anything conclusively missing, and emits the visibility WARN **alongside** the FAIL (deduped to one per distinct denying DIRECTORY — that is what an operator chmods, and each finding still names one distinct action: re-copy vs. grant traversal); the FAIL carries the blocked COUNT (*a further N reference path(s) could not be checked at all*) so its list is never read as a complete accounting. The WARN keeps its single spelled-once wording (*…the snapshot could NOT be validated*) even beside a FAIL, where strictly only the blocked paths went unvalidated: forking a second wording for this one site would re-split the message DL-229 (c′) deliberately hoisted, the overstatement is in the cautious direction, and the FAIL beside it is the actionable line and already names the count. With nothing conclusively missing, blocked paths still suppress the ok verdict — *holds every file* would be a claim about files this process never stat'ed. The **reference** side gets the DL-229 asymmetry: it is this checkout's own directory, so an unreadable one lands on its own accurate, non-destructive WARN rather than the deployment's visibility message — and, critically, an enumeration that fails is NEVER allowed to collapse to an empty set, which would certify "nothing is missing" (a false GREEN, this DL's own defect class). **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237: the per-subdirectory walk (`deployedState()`) is deleted with the leg, so the third visibility site is gone and DL-229 (c′)'s "two is the complete set" is true again. The RULE this bullet establishes — absence is not conclusive where we could not see, and one unseeable path does not void every seen one — is unchanged and still governs `visibleOrUnverified()`.]**
- **(f) The residual FAIL populations, stated rather than discovered later — and why the message claims NO CAUSE.** Under the gate, a FAIL still reaches two operators who did nothing wrong. **(1) A deliberately PRUNED deployment:** an otherwise-current copy with `tests/` or `README.md` dropped to save space, or one deployed by some means other than a whole-directory copy. **(2) A FAITHFUL whole-directory copy that predates an UNTRACKED stray in this checkout.** The DL-038 bump guard is a `git diff --name-only base...HEAD -- examples/channel-servers/`, so it governs the **tracked** set; the reference set this leg builds is the **working tree**, whose only exclusion is the literal name `node_modules`. A `README.md.orig` / `.rej` / editor backup therefore joins the reference set with no version bump behind it (verified: `git check-ignore examples/channel-servers/README.md.orig` reports it NOT ignored — the directory's `.gitignore` covers `node_modules/` only, and the root has no `*.orig`/`*.rej` rule), and a copy taken before it landed reads as MISSING it. `git apply --3way` mints exactly those files on a conflicted port. Near-nil on a clean tag checkout; real on a dev checkout, which is what a bridge **dev** install runs from. **This is what the FAIL may NOT say.** Naming a cause — *"a version-matched snapshot cannot legitimately lack one … so this deployment was assembled file-by-file rather than copied whole"* — is FALSE for (2), which makes it the **DL-229 (f) shape exactly**: a FAIL confidently wrong about what its operator did. So the message claims only what was `stat`'ed, on the same discipline `presenceLeg`'s ok-message follows (*a presence check, not a load test*): the two counts, the missing paths, the `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` consequence, the whole-directory re-copy. **The verdict itself stands for both populations** — it is true as measured (their deployment is not what a whole-directory copy of this reference delivers), the remediation genuinely restores it, both are contrary to what every doc instructs ("copy or symlink the WHOLE directory"), and the escape is one line of YAML: unset `channel.server_path`. Accepted with eyes open rather than softened to a WARN, because a WARN exits 0 and the motivating incident stays green — the entire point of the card. **The trade, weighable rather than asserted:** what DL-229 cut this leg over was an **OBSERVED** population — stale out-of-repo copies, which `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` records as a fleet fact — while both residual populations above are **HYPOTHESIZED, not observed**: neither is recorded anywhere in this repo's docs or decision log as having happened, and (2) was produced deliberately in review (`echo x > <bundled>/README.md.orig` then `bridge:check` ⇒ *MISSING 1 of the 11 files … delivers: README.md.orig*, exit 1) rather than encountered. Trading an observed false-GREEN for an unobserved unearned-RED is the right direction, and it is recorded here as an asymmetry a future reader can re-weigh if either population ever does show up. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-237, and this is the paragraph that superseded itself. Its closing sentence recorded the trade as an asymmetry "a future reader can re-weigh if either population ever does show up" — and population (1), the deliberately PRUNED deployment, showed up: measured on a real artifact by a peer operator, missing 6 of the 10 reference files (`.gitignore`, `.mcp.json.example`, `README.md`, three `tests/*.mjs` — exactly the enumerated-but-not-load-bearing set), FAILing completeness while `node` binds and exits 0. The re-weigh came out the other way: the unearned RED is real, and the check that has neither failure mode is a LAUNCH. Population (2) (the untracked-stray copy) is unaffected in principle and moot in practice, since nothing enumerates the reference any more.]**
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Leave DL-229 as shipped and treat the cherry-pick as operator error — rejected: it is the *observed* incident, it is invisible to every other leg, and "green check, then a dark seat" is the exact failure `bridge:check` exists to make loud. (b) Compare file sets **ungated** — rejected, that is what DL-229 (f) cut, on a population that is still there. (c) Narrow the comparison (only `.mjs`, only a "load-bearing" subset) — still rejected on DL-229 (g)'s original ground: a judgment heuristic with no authority behind it, where `copytree` is an authority we already have. (d) WARN instead of FAIL — rejected, see (f): a warning exits 0 and leaves the incident green. (e) Report a wholly-absent reference subdirectory as one item instead of listing its files — rejected as machinery for a message that is already capped; the per-file list is what an operator diffs against. (f) Compare against `git ls-files` rather than the working tree — rejected as a **code** decision, and it is worth being exact about what it would and would not have answered. It does **not** answer the (f) objection above: that objection is about the *message* invoking a tracked-set invariant the leg never measured, and the fix for that is to stop asserting a cause — not to change what is enumerated. On its own merits: a deployment is produced by `copytree` of the **working tree** (`_deploy_snapshot`), so the working tree is the set the verdict is about, and `git ls-files` would measure a set no deployment is ever made from; and it would put a **git binary + a git repository** dependency inside `bridge:check`, which runs on installs that are legitimately neither (a released tarball, a copied deployment) and often as an OS user that does not own the repo. That is a hard dependency bought for a set difference that is empty in a clean checkout (verified) and that, where it is non-empty, is exactly the untracked strays (f) now names outright instead of hiding. (g) Filter known VCS-stray patterns (`*.orig`, `*.rej`, `*~`) out of the reference enumeration to shrink (f)'s population (2) — rejected on DL-229 (g)'s standing ground: it is a judgment heuristic with no authority behind it, where `copytree` is an authority we already have, and it would unbind the (d) lockstep (the provisioner copies those files, so the two enumerations would no longer describe the same deployment) to soften an **unobserved** population that already has a true verdict, an accurate message, and a working remediation. Revisit only if that population is ever actually observed — and then in the provisioner first, so both sides move together.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, each verified by revert-and-restore):** `tests/Unit/Support/ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` — the shared enumeration lockstep vector (recursive / dotfiles / `node_modules` at any depth); an unreadable reference does NOT enumerate as empty; **version-equal + a missing sibling module ⇒ FAIL** (the motivating incident's exact shape: entry + `package.json` + `node_modules` present) while the version and presence legs still report ok; **version-stale + missing files ⇒ STALE warn and NOTHING else** (no FAIL, no second "skipped" line — the population that got the leg cut); version-newer ⇒ the skip finding, no FAIL; complete ⇒ ok (the positive control that makes the FAIL attributable to the omission); extra files ⇒ ok; repo-direct self-compare ⇒ no completeness leg at all; an untraversable deployed SUBDIRECTORY (nothing else missing) ⇒ one WARN naming that subdirectory, never a FAIL; **a blocked subdirectory BESIDE a conclusively-missing file ⇒ the FAIL survives, carries the blocked count, and the WARN is emitted alongside it** ((e)); **a faithful whole-directory copy plus an untracked `README.md.orig` in the reference ⇒ the FAIL names the measurement and NOT "assembled file-by-file"** ((f)); the missing-list cap. `tests/Feature/Console/BridgeCommandsTest` — the same incident through the REAL `bridge:check` against the REAL checkout reference (exit **1**, naming `channel-lib.mjs`, and asserting the message does not claim file-by-file assembly), its positive control (a whole-directory copy plus an extra local module ⇒ exit **0**), and **the blocked-subdirectory-beside-a-missing-file case asserting exit 1, not 0**; the deployed version is read from the checkout so the fixture stays version-equal across every channel-server bump. `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py` — the shared tree through the real `copytree`, plus the source-text pin on `_deploy_snapshot`. Reverting the equality gate reds the stale case; reverting the `>` branch reds the newer case; reverting the per-subdirectory guard reds the untraversable-subdirectory case; reverting the null-enumeration guard reds the unreadable-reference case; restoring the early `return` on the first blocked path reds the blocked-beside-missing unit case AND drops the feature case's exit back to **0**; restoring the causal sentence reds both file-by-file assertions; reverting the leg reds seven. Card 5142.

## DL-231 — The DL-201 card-token grammar is ASCII-only: the digit class is `[0-9]` in every engine, and the PHP side is pinned against the one-character `/u` edit that would widen it

**Date:** 2026-07-25
**Context — the same ratified token, three engines, and one of them answers differently.** sola-pm reported (roundtable #161 item 4) that the DL-201 card token is implemented in at least three regex engines across the fleet — this repo's `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` / `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN`, the toolkit's bash movers, and the framework's python `kanban-prs-sync.py` — and that python's `\d` matches **Unicode decimal digits** while `int()` accepts them. So `card#٣` (U+0663 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE) correlates to card **3** through the python path and is **invisible** to a bash `[0-9]` path. One token, two engines, two answers, with no error on either side. They did **not** narrow their copy — narrowing a ratified cross-repo grammar unilaterally is the divergence ratification exists to prevent — and asked for a direction so the three engines converge deliberately rather than by whoever edits last. Card 5147.
**Decision — the digit class in the DL-201 grammar is ASCII `[0-9]`, in every engine, and this repo's two token constants are guarded against widening.**
- **(a) Verified state before deciding — both of this fleet's engines already conform, so the divergence is one-sided.** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` (`/\bcard[-#](\d+)/i`) and `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` (`/\bDL-(\d+)/i`) carry `/i` and **no `/u`** — and PCRE `\d` is ASCII-only without that modifier (no pattern constant anywhere in `app/` carries `/u`; grepped). The toolkit's `board-card-start` matchers use `grep -oiE …[0-9]{2,}`, a POSIX range; no `\d` appears in any toolkit python. The kanban repo has no card-token engine at all. Nothing in this fleet had to change — this DL exists so the framework side can narrow **as adoption of a ratified decision** rather than as a unilateral divergence. **[card#6025:** there is no `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` or `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` in the tree today — both grammars moved to `CardTokenGrammar` / `DlTokenGrammar`; the entry records the code as it stood.**]**
- **(b) Why ASCII rather than widening the others.** A card id is a numeric primary key and the token's whole job is to name exactly one card unambiguously. An engine-dependent answer is a **correlation-integrity** defect, not a cosmetic one: the same PR title moves a card through one consumer and silently no-ops through another, which is the DL-201/#5137 failure shape (a token one side accepts and the other rejects) with the additional hazard that here it correlates to a card *the author never named in ASCII*. Widening instead of narrowing would also require every engine to agree on the numeric **conversion**, not just the match — python's `int()` folds Unicode digits, bash has no equivalent without new machinery — so "widen everywhere" is materially more work in exchange for a capability nobody has asked for. Narrowing costs one character class in one python constant.
- **(c) The guard is the point, and it is one character wide.** A ratified grammar with no executable guard is one edit from silent re-divergence, and here the edit is adding `/u` to a pattern constant — plausible as a well-meant "handle unicode input" change. `test_card_and_dl_tokens_accept_ascii_digits_only` asserts `card#٣`, `card-٣`, and `DL-٣` all correlate to **nothing**, with an ASCII positive control (`card#3` → card 3) so the negative assertions are attributable to the digit class rather than the fixture. **Verified by revert-and-restore:** adding `/u` to both constants makes `card#٣` correlate to card 3 and reds the test — i.e. the widening this DL forbids is empirically reachable in *this* engine, not merely a python quirk.
- **(d) Scope — this rules on the digit class only.** The separator question (`card-` vs `card#` vs the glued `card4524` the toolkit accepts and this classifier rejects) is a **different** divergence in the same grammar, tracked as card 5137 / roundtable #159, and is deliberately untouched here: it is a permissive-direction change and needs its own gate.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Answer on the thread without a DL — rejected: sola-pm adopts against a citable decision, and an answer in a comment is one context reset from being unfindable (the same reason a finding gets a tracker, not a comment). (b) Widen the bash + PHP engines to Unicode digits — rejected, see (b): it buys a capability nobody requested and requires cross-engine agreement on numeric conversion that bash cannot supply. (c) Ratify ASCII but ship no test — rejected, see (c): the widening edit is one character and would pass every existing test. (d) Also settle the separator divergence here so the grammar converges in one decision — rejected: it is a permissive change requiring its own approval, and bundling it would let a gated decision ride in on an ungated one.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, verified by revert-and-restore):** `tests/Feature/Classifiers/GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest::test_card_and_dl_tokens_accept_ascii_digits_only` — three Unicode-digit token shapes correlate to nothing; ASCII positive control correlates to card 3. Adding `/u` to `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` and `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` reds it (confirmed: `'card#٣' must not correlate to card 3 — actual size 1 matches expected size 0`). **No production code changed** — both constants already conformed; the test is what makes the conformance non-accidental. Card 5147.

## DL-232 — `impl_wake_deny_actors`: an actor deny-list on the `impl-ci-wake` family, keyed on WHO (never the conclusion), producing a NON-WAKE that flows through `impl_non_wake_disposition` rather than a pre-gate drop

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Context — a standing per-install cost for zero signal, with nothing to configure around it.** sola-pm (roundtable #163) measured one impl seat against one weekly Dependabot batch: 6 PRs × 4 workflows = **24 `workflow_run` wakes** plus 6 `dependabot/*` push events, 23 success + 1 cancelled, every one resolving to "no action" — impl seats don't act on bot PRs, the PM batch-merges them at a release rollup. ×3 impl seats × weekly, per install. Verified independently here that the family's complete config-driven knob set (`benign_conclusions`, `ci_failure_workflow_patterns`, `coord_non_addressed_disposition`, `impl_non_wake_disposition`, `impl_repos`, `provenance_patterns`, `release_branch`, `wake_membership`) contains **nothing keyed on actor or head branch**, so the report's "there is nothing to configure around it" is accurate: `event_filter` is subscription-level and type-keyed (dropping `workflow_run` would kill the legitimate own-branch CI wake), `drop_title_all_of` is `coord-message`-only, and `ci_failure_workflow_patterns` — the closest precedent in *shape* — keys on workflow **name**, which cannot express this because bot CI runs the *same* workflows as human PRs. Also verified that `$ctx->actor` is **already plumbed** into the classifier (used for re-attribution and display), so this is a missing **predicate**, not missing actor-awareness. Card 5156.
**Decision — a config-driven actor deny-list, `impl_wake_deny_actors`, empty/absent ⇒ byte-identical.**
- **(a) Keyed on the ACTOR, not the head branch.** The original proposal was `actor == dependabot[bot]` **OR** `branch matches dependabot/*`. The OR over-reaches: an impl agent pushing a fixup commit onto a bot branch — a real pattern when a bump needs a code change — would have its **own** CI silently suppressed, which is precisely the failure the keep-scope exists to prevent. Actor-keying gets it right by construction: the bot's pushes are the bot's, a human's are not.
- **(b) Keyed on WHO, never on the conclusion.** An automation account's run is non-actionable for an impl seat whether **green or red**, because the PM owns those PRs including the failing ones. A conclusion-keyed filter would suppress exactly the wrong half. The knob therefore silences a *failing* bot run, and the test that proves it is the mirror of the existing `test_workflow_run_failure_wakes` on the same payload and config.
- **(c) A NON-WAKE, not a pre-gate drop — the load-bearing shape, and its LIMIT.** A denied event skips only the wake-signal computation and **falls through to `impl_non_wake_disposition`**, so an `inbox_stage` install still records it (**digest, not drop**) and only an install on the default `drop` loses it. **⚠ CORRECTION (see (h)): that "digest" holds only on a `route_intents:false` channel.** Returning early would make the knob **lossy by default and un-opt-out-able**; an install that genuinely wants them gone already has `drop`. This is the same digest-not-drop position argued on roundtable #160 — a recipient/wake gate used as a volume control destroys information, because "should this reach me eventually" and "should this interrupt me now" are different questions.
- **(d) WHICH actor field, stated in the schema rather than left to whichever the test payload carried.** A `workflow_run` keys on **`triggering_actor`** (who caused *this* run), falling back to `actor` then `sender`; a `push` keys on `sender`. The two `workflow_run` fields diverge only on a **re-run**, and that divergence is the point: a human re-running a bot's workflow is a human asking for that result and must still wake — keying on `actor` (who triggered the *original* run) would wrongly suppress it. **The premise is GitHub's documented semantics and is NOT verified against a real divergent payload:** 200 recent `workflow_run` payloads on this install carried **0** `actor` !== `triggering_actor` and only **2** re-runs, both re-run by the same account. That is a sample that never contained the condition — **not** evidence the fields agree — so the behavior is pinned by SYNTHETIC payloads where the two deliberately differ, and re-reading `actor` first reds exactly one test.
- **(e) A general deny-list, not a Dependabot special case.** Fleet-wide, other installs run renovate, mergify, or their own automation; a list of logins/ids costs the same to implement and needs no second FR when the next bot arrives. Each entry matches **either** the `login` (case-insensitive) **or** the numeric account `id` (exact) — ids are immutable where logins rename, so an operator can pin the durable form, while logins are what they actually know.
- **(f) Not suppressed, deliberately:** `coord_comment` (PM→seat, actionable — a different family entirely); `push`/`workflow_run` on a seat's own feature branches by a non-bot author; PM-seat events generally, since a PM may want dependency merge-awareness where an impl seat does not — which per-agent config gives for free, this knob living alongside the others.
- **(g) This install is not the one paying the cost.** 0 bot-authored `workflow_run` events in the same 200-payload sample, so the 24+6 figure is **not** re-derivable here and is recorded as sola's impl agent's measurement, not ours. That asymmetry is itself the argument for fixing it in the shipped classifier: the seat that feels the cost and the seat that owns the code are different seats, which is exactly when a local workaround is the wrong layer.
- **(h) CORRECTION, same day, before any consumer adopted it — the suppression does NOT hold on a `route_intents:true` channel.** sola-pm reported the general interaction from a live deployment (roundtable #160); verified here at source: `DispatchService.php:233-243` appends a `channel_push` target for **every** staged intent when `channel.route_intents` is true, unconditionally, with no re-check of whether the classifier intended a wake. So the knob's actual reach is:

| install shape | effect of `impl_wake_deny_actors` |
| --- | --- |
| `impl_non_wake_disposition: drop` (the DEFAULT) | denied ⇒ no intent staged ⇒ **fully suppressed**, on any channel |
| `inbox_stage` + `route_intents: false` | staged, no wake ⇒ **suppressed** |
| `inbox_stage` + `route_intents: true` | staged ⇒ **routed ⇒ STILL WAKES — no suppression at all** |

  The knob is not defective and the runtime is unchanged: an operator setting `route_intents:true` has said "push me every staged intent", and the classifier docblock already recorded that shape as *"a broad-wake install"*. What was wrong was **this DL's own wording**, which read as an unconditional quiet digest. The third row is the requester's exact configuration — all three of sola's impl seats run `route_intents:true` with `impl_non_wake_disposition: inbox_stage` — so adopting the knob as written would have delivered **zero** wake reduction on the very install that asked for it. **Such installs must use `impl_non_wake_disposition: drop` to get the benefit.** Pinned by `DispatchServiceTest::test_deny_listed_actor_still_wakes_under_inbox_stage_on_a_route_intents_channel`, a deliberate counter-example so the universal reading cannot be re-derived. The same interaction is the reason sola reverted a `coord_non_addressed_disposition: inbox_stage` change on those seats: on a routing channel that setting is not a quiet digest either, it is a live wake on **all** unaddressed coordination traffic.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) branch-pattern keying — rejected, see (a): it suppresses a human's own CI on a bot branch. (b) Extending `ci_failure_workflow_patterns` — structurally impossible: bot CI runs the same workflow names as human PRs, so any pattern that caught it would suppress legitimate CI. (c) Subscription-level `event_filter` — type-keyed, so it would also kill the legitimate own-branch CI wake. (d) A hard drop before the gate — rejected per (c): lossy by default, and it would silently override an install's explicit `inbox_stage`. (e) Suppressing only *successful* bot runs — rejected per (b): the PM owns the red ones too, so a red bot run is equally non-actionable for the seat.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, both controls verified by revert-and-restore):** `tests/Unit/Classifiers/CoordinationClassifierTest` — a denied actor does not wake **even on a failing run**; matching by numeric id; a **human re-run** of a denied actor's workflow **still wakes** (the synthetic divergent payload); denied ⇒ non-wake that still stages under `inbox_stage` (intent present, targets empty); a `push` keying on `sender`; a non-denied actor unaffected by a populated list (the negative control that makes the suppressions attributable to the LIST, not to the gate existing); an absent list byte-identical. Removing the deny gate reds 4; inverting the field order to read `actor` first reds exactly 1 — the re-run test, confirming it is the assertion that pins the field choice. 1394/1394 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. **No migration, no new `.env`, no change to what the receiver accepts/rejects; default byte-identical.** Card 5156.

## DL-233 — The card token's separator becomes OPTIONAL: the glued `card<id>` spelling correlates, with the toolkit's ≥2-digit floor adopted verbatim on the glued arm

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Context — one grammar, two engines, 14 of 80 PRs silently no-op'd.** sola-pm (roundtable #159) measured it: the toolkit's `board-card-start` has accepted the glued `card4524` branch spelling since **v0.17.0** — deliberately, as *"the natural, most-typed glued spelling"* — while this classifier's `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` required a separator and rejected it. The failure mode is the worst available: the card **moves locally** (the toolkit hook fires on checkout) and then the PR writeback **never correlates**, so the board looks right until the merge that should have advanced it does nothing. The bridge's FR-7 near-miss probe does warn on the shape, but into the bridge log — a surface the PR author never reads. Card 5137.
**Decision — make the separator optional, and take the toolkit's digit floor with it.**

```
/\bcard(?|[-#](\d+)|(\d{2,}))/i
```

- **(a) The asymmetry is deliberate and adopted, not invented.** The GLUED arm requires **≥2 digits**; a SEPARATED token still accepts one. That is exactly `board-card-start`'s `0*[0-9]{2,}`, and the floor is what makes an optional separator safe: without it `\bcard\d+` correlates `card2go` to card **2**, because DL-201 deliberately has **no trailing `\b`** (so a token may be followed by anything). With it, `card2go` and `card4` match nothing while `card-3` still correlates. Widening the separator without the floor would have imported a false-correlation class that the tool being converged toward had already solved.
- **(b) Branch-reset `(?|…)`, so callers are untouched.** Both alternatives share capture group 1, so every `$m[1]` read at the three resolution sites is unchanged. The alternative — two groups and a `$m[1] ?: $m[2]` at each site — would have put the same conditional in three places for no gain.
- **(c) The ratified DL-231 digit class is NOT touched.** This widens the SEPARATOR only; the pattern still carries no `/u`, so the ASCII-only ratification and its guard stand exactly as landed.
- **(d) The lint had to widen in the same change, or it reds what the classifier accepts.** `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` asserted `card[-#]${card_id}`; a title carrying the now-correlating glued token would have failed the check that exists to protect correlation. It now accepts `card[-#]?${card_id}` — the standing rule that **a title the lint passes must correlate** implies its converse here.
- **(e) An existing near-miss assertion changed meaning, and was updated rather than deleted.** `test_near_miss_card_token_in_branch_warns_and_noops` pinned `feat/card3054` as a warn-and-no-op. That is precisely the behavior this DL reverses, so `card3054` LEFT that list (it is now asserted as correlating in `test_glued_card_token_correlates`) and `card.3054` took its place — the residual near-miss population is the separators still not accepted, and it is still asserted non-empty. The test was not weakened to go green; its subject moved.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Narrow the TOOLKIT to require a separator instead — rejected: glued is the spelling operators actually type, the toolkit shipped it deliberately, and narrowing would convert 14 working local moves into 14 loud failures to fix nothing. (b) Keep both grammars and make the PR-title lint reject glued pre-merge — rejected on the merits though it is non-permissive: it kills the silence but forbids a spelling the sibling tool accepts, so the two tools still disagree and the operator is the one who absorbs it. (c) Widen with `[-#]?(\d+)` and no digit floor — rejected per (a): it correlates `card2go`. (d) Add a trailing `\b` to make the floor unnecessary — rejected: that is exactly the DL-201 defect (`card#3054_fix` becomes a silent no-op), and trading a silent no-op for a false correlation is the wrong direction twice over.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted):** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` — glued correlates in both title and head-branch position (`card4524`, `fix/CARD4524-slug`); the glued arm requires 2 digits (`card4`, `card2go` correlate to nothing) with a separated single digit (`card-3`) as the control that makes the floor attributable; `discard4524`/`wildcard-2`/`discard-1` still never correlate (the `\b` boundary is the thing most at risk from an optional separator); the near-miss list keeps warning on the separators still rejected. Restoring `card[-#](\d+)` reds the glued cases. 71/71 on the suite, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. **No migration, no new `.env`.** ⚠ This is a **permissive** change to what the classifier accepts — operator-approved before implementation. Card 5137.

## DL-234 — An UNCONDITIONAL near-miss WARNING on the PR-title lint: a card-ish token that matches no accepted spelling is told to the author pre-merge, keyed on "the grammar did not match" rather than on a list of bad shapes

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Context — DL-231 closed a wrong correlation and opened a silent one.** Narrowing the digit class to ASCII means `card#٣` now correlates to **nothing** — correct, and completely silent. sola-pm relayed the residue from their adoption (roundtable #161); verified here, and the cause is deeper than reported: the FR-7 near-miss probe carries its **own ASCII `\d`**, so it is blind to the same inputs. `card_٣` proves it — `_` **is** in that probe's separator set and `card_3` warns, yet `card_٣` does not. Every Unicode-digit token is invisible to the correlation path *and* the warning path, on every separator. And the one pre-merge gate that could have told the author is **branch-gated**: `pr-title-lint.yml` skips unless the head branch matches `^[a-z-]+/[0-9]+-`, so it exits early on `card-<id>-…` (this repo's own convention), on `fix/…`, and on everything else. Card 5150.

*[Annotation, 2026-08-18 (card#6822, DL-289) — ADDITIVE.] The residue this entry exists to cover is NARROWER since DL-289: the branch gate no longer skips `card-<id>-…` or `fix/card<id>-…`, so those shapes now reach the require step. The residue is not empty — a branch the predicate can read no card id out of still reaches only this unconditional warning — so this entry's reasoning stands on a smaller set.*
**Decision — a second, UNCONDITIONAL step on the same workflow, emitting `::warning::`.**
- **(a) Assert that the ACCEPTED GRAMMAR DID NOT MATCH; never enumerate bad shapes.** The predicate is *looks-like-a-card-token* **AND NOT** *matches the ratified grammar*. That inversion is why it needs **no Unicode awareness at all** — the alternative, a Unicode-aware `grep`, is precisely the machinery DL-231 declined, and it would put engine-dependence back on the warning path immediately after removing it from the correlation path. It also stays correct as the grammar moves: it re-derives "bad" from "not good" instead of hard-coding a list someone must remember to extend. **DL-233 proved that within the same session** — making the separator optional created a brand-new near-miss (single-digit glued `card4`), and the predicate caught it with no edit.
- **(b) Unconditional is the whole point.** The branch gate is *why* the residue exists; reusing it would have re-inherited the blind spot. Its own most-skipped shape is this repo's `card-<id>-slug` convention.
- **(c) WARNING, not error — and the reason is a population, not timidity.** Beyond the genuinely-silent Unicode case, the predicate also catches `card_3` / `card.3` / `card #82`, which are **legal-but-lossy today**: they merge now and fail to correlate now. Turning them into a merge block is a separate decision from closing the silent case, and one with a different blast radius. Warning first; escalate only on evidence.
- **(d) A bare space stays NOT a separator.** DL-201 ruled prose (`supports card 2`) must stay silent and that ruling holds — `card #82` warns via the explicit space-then-hash arm, `card 2` does not. This is the case a naive predicate gets wrong, and sola-pm's mirror lint had exactly that defect in the opposite direction (it *blocked* prose).
- **(e) THE LIMIT, asserted rather than discovered later — the predicate is whole-subject, not per-token.** If ANY accepted token is present across title+branch, nothing warns, even beside a malformed one. Deliberate for a warning leg: a correlating token means the card *does* move, so the PR is not in the silent-failure class this exists to catch. The bounded cost: `card-5150` in the branch plus `card_3054` in the title yields no nudge, and card 3054 stays put. Per-token analysis is a bigger change than a warning justifies, and the co-present-token case that moves the *wrong* card is DL-218's conflict path, not this one. **[Superseded as a step-level claim by card#5961 — suppression is per-stem since the DL arm: an accepted card token no longer quiets a DL near-miss (asserted cross-stem in `PrTitleLintTest`); the card arm's own whole-subject limit is unchanged.]**
- **(f) The lint's bash is now EXECUTED by a test, which it never was.** The grammar has been edited three times (DL-201, DL-233, this) and each round's matrix was driven ad-hoc in review and thrown away, so every later edit re-derived correctness by reading. `PrTitleLintTest` extracts the step's `run:` block from the YAML and drives it under real `bash`, so it cannot drift from what CI runs. This matters most for (a): "the accepted grammar did not match" is only correct while it stays in **lockstep with `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN`**, and nothing but a test can hold that.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Widen the near-miss probe to be Unicode-aware — rejected per (a): it is the declined machinery, and it re-engine-dependences the warning path. (b) Reuse the existing branch gate — rejected per (b): that gate is the defect. (c) Make it an error — rejected per (c) for now, revisitable. (d) Fix it classifier-side instead — the probe already warns, but into the **bridge log, post-merge**, on a surface the PR author never reads; the author-facing gate is the PR check. (e) Per-token analysis — rejected per (e) as disproportionate to a warning leg.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, both controls verified by revert-and-restore):** `tests/Feature/Workflows/PrTitleLintTest` — Unicode-digit tokens warn in all three separator spellings; ASCII near-misses (`card_3054`, `card.3054`, `card:3054`, `card #5082`) warn; single-digit glued `card4` warns (the shape DL-233 created); **no** accepted spelling warns (`card#3`, `card-3`, `card4524`, `CARD4524`); prose and `discard4524`/`wildcard-2` never warn; the head **branch** is examined, not only the title; the leg exits **0** always (if it ever exits non-zero it has silently become a merge gate); it fires on branches the gated step skips; and the whole-subject limit from (e). Silencing the `echo` reds 5; dropping the grammar guard so it warns on everything card-ish reds 3 — the harness observes both directions. **No runtime code touched.** Card 5150.

## DL-235 — `bare_reply_to_own_thread`: a NARROW, echo-guarded default-ON grant so a bare reply to a thread you opened wakes you — `reply-dir B` and nothing wider

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Context — a shipped default that six-plus seats across three independently-configured installs landed on wrong.** A **bare** reply (a comment with no `TO:` line) must fall back to thread membership to decide who wakes; the framework pins this as universal conformance row `reply-dir B`. Under the shipped default `[to_me, to_all, comment_to]` it does not: a thread labelled `from:<me>, to:<other>` plus a bare reply resolves `to:<me>` absent, `to:all` absent, `from_me` not in the default, and `comment_to` finds no `TO:` line to key on — **not for me → dropped**. Measured, independently, by three operators who never compared configs: sola 3 of 4 seats non-conformant, aimla 3 impl seats + 5 auxiliary, this seat conformant **only** because `kanban-solo.yml` sets `from_me` explicitly. `coord_non_addressed_disposition` was **unset on every seat of both other installs**, so the drops were silent rather than deferred; aimla attests **112** dropped coordination comment events per impl agent. Card 5153.
**Decision — add a fourth `wake_membership` member, default-ON, granting ONLY the conformance target.**

```
grant iff  labels contain from:{me}
      AND  RecipientAddressing::addresses(body, me) === null   (BARE — no TO: line)
      AND  RecipientAddressing::author(body) !== me            (echo guard)
```

- **(a) Why NOT `from_me`, the wide knob that already existed — the option I proposed and was refuted on.** It grants on **ALL** activity on an authored thread, which is strictly wider than `reply-dir B` needs, so operators face "violate the conformance row" or "accept wake-on-everything" — and six-plus seats chose the former. Nobody chose the bug; they declined the volume. Flipping it into the default would also **revert DL-190**, a deliberate 3-way-agreed wide→narrow flip *this agent signed off on*, reintroducing the exact over-wake it cured.
- **(b) The echo guard is what makes an authorship-keyed grant safe at all, and DL-213 is why.** That DL rejected `from_me` for the default on a **mechanism**, not a precedent: `comment_to` is *"echo-safe by construction — keys on the comment's directed `TO:` line, **not authorship**, so under the shared account … a comment the agent itself authored does not wake it."* A narrow bare-reply grant still keys on **thread authorship**, so it inherits that hazard in miniature — author a thread, post a bare follow-up on it yourself, wake on your own comment. The third clause keys on the body's `FROM:` line, **the same discriminator shared-account attribution already relies on everywhere else**, using the shipped `RecipientAddressing::author()`. No new machinery. Without it, this would be the cure carrying the disease.
- **(c) It is genuinely narrow, and each conjunct is load-bearing.** BARE only (`=== null`, never `false` — an explicit `TO: someone-else` still denies, the unconditional narrow outranks the grant); OWN-thread only (a bare reply on a thread you neither opened nor were labelled on remains none of your business); NOT-self only. Drop any one and it becomes a knob the fleet already rejected.
- **(d) Default-ON, not opt-in — the evidence is the argument.** `comment_to` (DL-213) made the same call for the same reason: the flow is dark out of the box, and an opt-in doesn't get taken. Here that is not a prediction but a **measurement** — the exposed population is precisely the seats nobody tuned, on three installs, and every PM seat that *was* tuned carries the wider `from_me` already. A default six-plus seats land on wrong is the default choosing for them.
- **(e) An unattributable author (no `FROM:` line) still grants** — `null !== $me`. Deliberate: the narrow has already denied anything addressed elsewhere, a bare unattributed reply on a thread you opened is still a reply to you, and the failure this DL closes is a **missed** wake, so fail-open is the safe direction here.
- **(f) Bounded blast radius, worth stating so nobody over-scopes it.** `comment_to` is already default-ON and covers every **directed** reply. The exposed surface is **only** bare replies — *"the recipient gate is broken"* would overstate a real bug.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Flip `from_me` into the default — **proposed by this agent and refuted**; see (a)/(b). (b) Ship the narrow grant opt-in — rejected per (d): conformance is then still not reached out of the box, on measured evidence that opt-ins are not taken. (c) Decline `reply-dir B` — rejected: a reply to a thread you opened is addressed to you by construction, and dropping it is a silent miss. (d) Key the grant on actor id instead of the body `FROM:` line — rejected per (b): actor id is one shared account fleet-wide, so it cannot discriminate at all. (e) Narrow it further to "bare AND the thread has no other recipient" — rejected as machinery for a case the `to:`/`comment_to` members already cover.
**Tests (RED-when-reverted, both controls verified by revert-and-restore):** `CoordinationClassifierTest` — a bare reply on an own thread wakes by default; **the agent's own bare follow-up does NOT** (the echo guard); a bare reply on someone else's thread still doesn't; an explicit `TO: someone-else` on an own thread still narrows to no-wake; an explicit `wake_membership` list without the member restores pre-DL-235 behavior (the default only reaches installs with no explicit key); a bare reply with no `FROM:` line still grants. Removing the member from the default reds **2**; dropping the echo-guard clause reds **exactly 1** — the self-wake test, confirming that clause is what holds it. 1407/1407 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean. **No migration, no new `.env`.** ⚠ **Permissive** change (more wakes) — operator-approved before implementation. Converged 3/3 on roundtable #160. Card 5153.

## DL-236 — A fourth `bridge:check` severity, `unvalidated`: a check that did NOT run is reported as not-run, never as `ok`, and disclosed in a closing tally that never touches the exit code

**Date:** 2026-07-26
**Context — "green because checked" and "green because nobody looked" were the same output.** `ChannelSnapshotProbe::probe()` returns `self::ok('channel.server_path not declared — snapshot not validated')` for an undeclared `channel.server_path`: the message says *not validated* while carrying `ok`, the severity that means measured-and-clean. `bridge:check` renders it green through `emitFinding()` and exits 0, so an operator reading a clean run has no way to tell a snapshot that was certified from one nobody looked at. The undeclared population is not marginal: **0 of 9** per-agent configs on this seat declare the key, and 0 of 9 on a second, independently-configured install. Card 5170.
**Decision — name what was MEASURED.** A fourth severity `unvalidated`, peer to `ok`/`warn`/`fail`, emitted by the `$serverPath === null` branch (message text unchanged), rendered PLAIN by `emitFinding()`, counted at that same chokepoint, and disclosed once per run as *N severity-reporting check(s) reported `unvalidated` — not a failure, and not a pass either … This is a floor, not an inventory …*, printed only when N > 0. **[The quoted tally text has been narrowed twice since: by DL-248 (stage 8) and again by DL-251 (stage 10), which swept the 21 could-not-measure sites that made "floor" the honest word. It now counts `finding(s)`, not `check(s)`, and discloses the *reported* population rather than a floor. Read the quote as the wording DL-236 shipped; `CheckCommand`'s tally comment owns the current one.]** The DL-196 event-follows-consumer advisory's fail-soft catch — which rendered a skipped run GREEN via `info()` and appeared in no tally — is routed through the same vocabulary.

- **(a) Why not a `warn` — the option this rejects.** A warn is a call to action, and `docs/multi-host.md` **instructs** operators to leave `channel.server_path` unset in the cross-host topology (the bridge on host A cannot `stat` a host-B deployment; declaring it there converts a healthy install into a confident dangling FAIL). So the undeclared population **contains a documented-correct configuration** — that is the deciding evidence. A warn would nag it on every run forever with no action available to silence it, which is how operators learn to skip the warn block, taking the actionable warns down with it. Plain output is the honest "nobody looked" signal: visible, not accusatory. **[DL-237 adds a SECOND permanent population to this severity, and it is worth reading against this bullet's own argument: every declared, healthy, co-located deployment now carries a launch-not-measured line with no action available *inside `bridge:check`* to silence it. That is close to the habituation cost (a) refuses a `warn` over. It is accepted on the difference (a) actually turns on — a warn is a call to action with none available, while that line is a disclosure of a measurement this command structurally cannot make (wrong OS user), whose action is real, named, and on the SEAT. No suppression knob was added: a flag to hide it would let an operator convert a true statement into silence, which is this DL's defect with an opt-in. See DL-237 (c).]**
- **(b) Why not leave it `ok` and fix the wording.** The wording was already honest — the message literally says *not validated*. The defect is that the **severity** contradicts it, and severity is what the rendering, the tally, and every future consumer key on. A vocabulary that has no way to say "not measured" forces every not-measured result into a bucket that means something else.
- **(c) The exit contract is preserved BY CONSTRUCTION, not by observation.** `emitFinding()` returns false only on `'fail'`; every other arm returns true. That is asserted as a property over the whole vocabulary **plus a severity that does not exist yet** (`false` IFF `fail`), so adding a fifth value cannot silently change what `bridge:check` exits. Nothing about what the command accepts or rejects changes.
- **(d) Counted at the chokepoint, reset per run.** The increment lives in `emitFinding()` — the single point every probe finding flows through — so a future probe emitting the severity is tallied with no call-site edit. The counter is reset at the top of `handle()`: console commands are resolved from the container, so a second `Artisan::call('bridge:check')` in one process can reuse the instance and a leaked count would over-report (pinned by a double-invocation test).
- **(e) Silent at zero.** No "0 unvalidated" line. The tally is a disclosure about checks that did not run; an install with none has nothing to disclose, and a permanent zero line is exactly the noise that trains an operator to skip the last line of the output.
- **(f) The widening broke a negative membership proxy, and that is fixed in the same change.** `checkSshTransport()` marked an agent's ssh setup incomplete on `$finding['severity'] !== 'ok'` — a proxy for "warn or fail" that holds only while the vocabulary is exactly `{ok, warn, fail}`. A fourth value silently widens it to sweep `unvalidated`, flagging an agent's setup incomplete on the strength of a check nobody ran. Replaced with the positive predicate `severityMeansSetupIncomplete()` (`in_array($severity, ['warn','fail'], true)`). **Latent, not live** — `SshTransportProbe` emits only ok/warn/fail — so today's behavior is unchanged; the DL-225 advisory is otherwise untouched. **Honest bound on the coverage:** the extracted helper is asserted directly, but NOTHING pins that `checkSshTransport()` still CALLS it — reverting the call site to `!== 'ok'` while leaving the helper in place keeps the whole suite green, because every existing call-site test exercises only `warn`, where the two predicates agree. Accepted rather than fixed: the machinery to pin it (a fake probe emitting a severity the real one cannot produce) would test the fake. So the helper is unguarded against orphaning, and this bullet says so instead of letting the reflection test read as coverage of the call site.

- **(g) The same defect shape lived a second time in this command, and the tally's own claim had to be bounded.** `checkEventFollowsConsumer()`'s fail-soft catch reported a skipped advisory with `info()` — GREEN, exit 0, invisible to the counter: "green because nobody looked", unchanged, thirty lines from the fix. It now emits through `emitFinding()` with severity `unvalidated`, so it renders plain and is counted; the discarded return is safe by construction (only `fail` returns false), so fail-soft is preserved. Finding it also falsified the reach of the summary's original wording: `emitFinding()` is the chokepoint for **findings that carry a severity** and has exactly THREE call sites (the snapshot-probe loop, the ssh-probe wrapper, and now this catch — counted at source), while the command makes **26** other direct `$this->info()` calls that never touch the counter — and, the substance of it, **~75** other `warn()` and **27** other `error()` calls besides (all counted at source, excluding the one of each inside `emitFinding` itself). *"those legs did not run, so a green run does not mean they were validated"* invited reading the ABSENCE of a tally as "every leg ran" — a false assurance one level up from the one being closed. The line now names the operative bound — **only checks reporting `unvalidated` are counted, and a check that could not run usually reports `warn` instead** — and states outright that it is **a floor, not an inventory**. "Counts every check that reports a severity" was the first correction and it was ALSO wrong: true as a necessary condition, but its converse reads as a guarantee the counter cannot give, and it is false by roughly a dozen — the couldn't-probe sites above, plus `ChannelSnapshotProbe`'s four could-not-measure findings, which DO flow through `emitFinding` and are still not tallied because they carry `warn`. The tally is a lower bound on what went unvalidated, permanently.
- **(h) The boundary against the four SIBLING warns, argued rather than left accidental — and the four do NOT all rest on the same discriminator.** `ChannelSnapshotProbe` has four other findings that also report a measurement that did not happen and keep `warn`: `unverifiedWarn()` (*not visible to this user … could NOT be validated*), the deployed-manifest absent/unreadable/malformed warn (*cannot tell whether the deployed copy is stale*), the bundled-manifest warn (*cannot be version-compared*), and the unenumerable-reference warn (*could NOT be checked for completeness*). They split two-and-two:
  - **The DEPLOYED pair (`unverifiedWarn`, deployed-manifest) — the operator ASKED for this measurement.** `server_path` is declared, so something is obstructing a validation they opted into, and a warn is the report that what they asked for could not be delivered. Nobody asked in the undeclared case.
  - **The CHECKOUT pair (bundled-manifest, unenumerable-reference) — a different discriminator, and the first one does NOT stretch to cover them.** Both obstructions are on `$bundledDir`, **this repo's own files**, not the operator's deployment: they asked about their snapshot and what failed to read was OURS. What carries these is that a checkout which cannot read its own tracked `examples/channel-servers` is a REAL, LOCAL DEFECT with a fix in the operator's hands — not an absence of information, but a broken installation reporting itself. `warn` is right for that on its own merits, and saying so is the difference between an argued boundary and one that happens to hold.
  - **What both pairs share, and the undeclared case lacks: an available action** (grant traversal / re-run as the agent's user / re-copy / repair or restore the file), so the warn can be silenced by acting. Leaving `server_path` unset is documented-correct in the cross-host topology and has no action at all — which is why a warn there would nag forever and this one does not.
  - **One divergence found while arguing this, and FIXED rather than filed:** the two CHECKOUT-pair warns are the same shape (*this checkout's X could not be read*) and only the reference one spelled its remedy; the bundled-manifest one stopped at *cannot be version-compared*. That is a mismatched pair, not one message lacking polish — an operator reads the silent half as unactionable when the fix is the same class of thing. The bundled-manifest warn now names it (*that file is tracked in this checkout, so restore or repair it, and check that this process can read it*), and the branch — which had **no test coverage at all**, which is how it drifted — is now pinned by one (red without the clause). Nothing was re-severitied.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Make the undeclared finding a `warn` — rejected per (a): it would nag a documented-correct population forever with no way to silence it, and habituation there costs the actionable warns. (b) Keep `ok` and rely on the message text — rejected per (b): the severity is the machine-readable half and it says the opposite of the message. (c) Name it `skipped` or `notice` — rejected: both name a DECISION about the check ("we chose not to run it" / "here is a note"), while the operator's question is about the MEASUREMENT — what is known about this snapshot, and the answer is nothing. (d) Suppress the line entirely when undeclared — rejected: that is the original defect with the last trace removed. (e) Flip the exit code when anything is unvalidated — rejected: it would fail every multi-host install for following its own runbook, and the exit contract is a hard compatibility surface. (f) Consolidate the severity vocabulary now shared by `ChannelSnapshotProbe` and `SshTransportProbe` (two private copies of ok/warn/fail) — deliberately OUT of scope here and filed as **card#5178**; this change touches neither of `SshTransportProbe`'s ctors, and its `Severity ∈ {ok, warn, fail}` docblock is correct FOR THAT CLASS and deliberately NOT widened. **The producer inventory is THREE sites, not two, and 5178 was filed before the third existed** — so read the card's "both probes" as incomplete: `ChannelSnapshotProbe`'s four private ctors, `SshTransportProbe`'s three, and a **raw array literal behind no ctor at all** in the CONSUMER, `CheckCommand::checkEventFollowsConsumer()`'s fail-soft catch. A migration that converts "both probes" to an enum and stops there leaves that literal as a bare string the type system does not reach — which is precisely how a vocabulary drifts back apart.
**Tests — split by HOW each was proven failable, because the two are not the same evidence.**

*Genuinely RED-when-reverted* (each proven by reverting the production change, re-running, and restoring): `ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` — the undeclared case is exactly `unvalidated` and explicitly NOT `ok`, message substrings unchanged (reds on `unvalidated()`→`ok()`); and the bundled-manifest warn names its remedy, per (h) (reds on removing the clause — first coverage this branch has ever had). `CheckCommandSeverityContractTest` — an `unvalidated` finding renders with NO styling while an `ok` does (reds on removing the arm: the output came back ANSI-green; the `ok` leg is the positive control that the assertion measures the arm and not an unstyled output object); only `unvalidated` increments the tally (reds 0-vs-2 on the same revert); the positive incomplete-setup predicate from (f) (reds on restoring the `!== 'ok'` BODY). `BridgeCommandsTest` — the undeclared run still exits 0 with both message substrings AND now prints the tally (reds on three separate reverts); two `Artisan::call`s in one process report 1, not 2 (reds UNIQUELY on removing the `handle()` reset, which printed `2 …` — the container really does hand back the instance, so the reset is load-bearing rather than defensive); the event-consumer fail-soft catch renders plain and is counted (reds against the pre-fix tree, where it came back ANSI-green and uncounted).

*Failable only by MUTATION, and labelled as such rather than banked as revert coverage:* `test_emit_finding_returns_false_if_and_only_if_the_severity_is_fail` is GREEN against pre-change production code — the old `emitFinding` mapped ok/warn/unvalidated/future→true and fail→false, matching every row — so reverting proves nothing about it. It is a CHARACTERIZATION of the exit contract, kept because that contract is the compatibility promise and nothing else states it; proven failable by mutating `warn` to also return false (reds on the `warn` row only). Likewise `test_check_prints_no_unvalidated_tally_when_every_leg_ran` asserts an ABSENCE and survives every revert; proven failable by mutating the tally guard `> 0` → `>= 0` (a `0 check(s) …` line appeared). **[DL-237 renames it `test_check_prints_no_unvalidated_tally_when_nothing_reported_unvalidated` and changes its fixture. The property is unchanged — silent at zero, failable only by mutating that same guard — but the OLD fixture (a healthy declared `server_path`) can no longer reach zero: every run that reaches the snapshot legs now emits a launch-not-measured `unvalidated`. The new fixture is an agent with no `channel:` block, which never enters the probe. The old NAME was also about to become false: no leg anywhere measures the launch.]**

**No migration, no new `.env`, no exit-code change, no change to what `bridge:check` accepts or rejects.** Gates: 1426/1426 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs.php` clean. Card 5170; the severity-vocabulary consolidation is card#5178.
