## DL-237 — The snapshot COMPLETENESS leg is retired for a SEAT-SIDE LAUNCH-ASSERT (`bin/check-channel-snapshot.py`): assert the thing, not a proxy — and the seat's OS user is the only one whose launch answers the question

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Context — DL-230 (f)'s own re-weigh trigger fired.** That paragraph shipped the version-gated completeness leg while recording, in as many words, that the population it would unfairly redden — a deliberately PRUNED deployment — was **HYPOTHESIZED, not observed**, and that trading an observed false-GREEN for an unobserved unearned-RED "is recorded here as an asymmetry a future reader can re-weigh **if either population ever does show up**". It showed up. **PEER-MEASURED, THEN INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED — two attributions that corroborate rather than compete, and both belong in the record.** aimla-pm measured it on their own box (roundtable #154, Round 10; quoted verbatim in card#5143's description): a retired COPY snapshot missing **6 of the 10** files the reference set holds — `.gitignore`, `.mcp.json.example`, `README.md`, and all three `tests/*.mjs` — **FAILs completeness** while `node` on that same directory **binds and exits 0**. Those six are exactly the enumerated-but-NOT-load-bearing set. It was then reproduced here against this checkout's real `examples/channel-servers` before anything was changed (node v20.20.2; see (a) for the three exit codes). Neither reading rests on the other: an operator-reported measurement and a local reproduction of it are the two halves of canon #2's evidence bar, not a contradiction. Card 5143, roundtable #154 rounds 8–10 plus a verification pass.
**Decision — replace the enumeration with a LAUNCH, and put the launch on the SEAT.** Two independent rulings; the second is the load-bearing one.

- **(a) The launch is strictly more precise than the file-set compare, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — and this is now a measurement, not a reading of the import graph.** Reproduced on this box against the shipped reference (node v20.20.2), stdin closed, exit code read: a whole-directory copy ⇒ **exit 0**; the same copy with the six non-load-bearing files removed ⇒ **exit 0** (completeness FAILs it — the unearned RED); the same copy with `channel-lib.mjs` removed ⇒ **exit 1**, `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '…/channel-lib.mjs' imported from '…/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs'`. The third row is the DL-230 motivating incident, caught. It is caught because the entry really does `import { deriveMeta, relayBridgeResponse } from './channel-lib.mjs'` — read at source (line 47) rather than recalled, and pinned by a test that reds if the shipped entry ever stops importing it, since the whole synthetic regression case stands on that premise. The compare answered "does this directory look like the reference?"; the launch answers the question an operator actually has, which is "will this come up at the next session start?".
- **(b) WHY `bridge:check` MUST NOT RUN THE LAUNCH — the part a future reader will otherwise re-litigate.** The obvious next step is to shell out to `node` from the version-equal branch. It is wrong, and for the same reason the leg it would replace was wrong. **The bridge routinely runs as a DIFFERENT OS user than the agent** — DL-227's same-box topology, with `/home/<agent>` at `drwxr-x---` per seat and the bridge under its own account. A launch from that process proves the entry loads **for the bridge's user**: its `PATH`, its `node` (possibly a different major version, possibly none), its read access to the deployment. That is a **proxy for the question again** — and "assert the thing, not a proxy" is the entire argument for launching instead of enumerating. Swapping one proxy for a slightly better one would have been the third iteration of the same mistake (the import text-scan, then the file-set compare). DL-229 (c) rejected `node --check` on different grounds (it parses without resolving imports, and it puts a Node dependency inside `bridge:check`); the second of those objections stands here too, and this one is stronger: **it would be a confident answer about the wrong user.** So `bridge:check` keeps its stat-only discipline permanently, and the launch is a program the operator runs **on the seat, as the seat's own OS user**. A tool that must be run by a different principal than the one running `bridge:check` cannot be a leg of `bridge:check`; recognizing that is the decision.
- **(c) What `bridge:check` reports instead: the DISCLOSURE, at the severity that means "not measured" — emitted ONCE PER RUN, on EVERY branch that reached the legs.** `probe()` appends one **`unvalidated`** finding after the version and presence legs: *was NOT launch-tested — `bridge:check` never executes node, so a green run here is not evidence the entry will LOAD at the next session start … Run `bin/check-channel-snapshot.py <dir>` ON THAT SEAT, as the OS user whose session launches the channel server*. `unvalidated` is DL-236's severity for exactly this and the fit is not incidental: DL-236 (b) argued that a vocabulary with no way to say "not measured" forces every not-measured result into a bucket that means something else, and an unqualified `is current` on a deployment nobody launched is that bucket. **The exit contract is preserved by construction** — `emitFinding()` returns false only for `'fail'` (DL-236 (c)) — so this never flips an exit code; it renders plain and feeds the existing tally, which is correct and wanted. Asserted end to end (a version-matched deployment missing `channel-lib.mjs` ⇒ exit **0**, the disclosure printed, `1 check(s) reported unvalidated`), not inferred from the return type. **The ergonomics are weighed, not waved past:** every declared, healthy, co-located deployment now carries a PERMANENT `unvalidated` line with no action available *inside `bridge:check`* to silence it — which is close to the habituation argument DL-236 (a) used to REFUSE a `warn` for the undeclared case. It is accepted here on the difference that argument turns on: a warn is a call to action with none available, whereas this is a disclosure of a measurement that genuinely never happens in this command and structurally cannot (the OS user is wrong), and the action for it is real, named, and on the SEAT. Permanence is therefore correct rather than merely tolerable — the day it disappears is the day `bridge:check` starts claiming something it did not measure. **No suppression knob is added**, deliberately: a flag to hide it would let an operator convert a true statement into silence, which is the DL-236 defect with an opt-in. **It is emitted UNCONDITIONALLY of what the legs found**, including beside a presence FAIL: suppressing it there would make it depend on another leg's severity, so a later change to that leg would silently change whether it appears — and the sentence stays true either way (the legs ran; the launch did not). **The four EARLY returns never reach it** — an undeclared `server_path`, the dangling and names-a-file fatals, and the not-visible-to-this-user WARN. Each already states that the legs did not run and each already names its one action, so a second not-measured line beside them is the DL-229 (h) shape for real: two findings, one remediation. Asserted per path (`assertCount(1, …)`), not left to fall out. **[DL-251 (2026-07-31) corrects two labels in this bullet; its reasoning is unchanged. (i) The disclosure is emitted once per AGENT, not once per run — `ChannelSnapshotCheck` is a `PerAgentCheck`, so a two-agent install with no `channel.server_path` declared yields two findings from one check id. (ii) The not-visible-to-this-user path reports `unvalidated`, not a WARN: it was swept with the other 20 sites, because a permission denial means the leg never answered its question.]**
- **(d) THE TOOL: `bin/check-channel-snapshot.py`, stdlib-only and REFERENCE-FREE.** It spawns `node <deployed>/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs` with **stdin closed** and reads the **exit code**. It reads no version, no file list, no bridge config and no bridge checkout — one self-contained file, copyable to a seat that has none of those, which is what makes it the only thing that can certify anything in the cross-host topology where host A cannot `stat` the host-B deployment at all. Its conventions follow `bin/provision-board-tools.py` (argparse, pure testable helpers, a `main(argv=None)` seam). **Exit contract, in `--help` and the module docstring:** **0** launch OK · **1** launch FAILED, conclusive, with the child's own stderr printed (that stderr IS the diagnosis) · **2** COULD NOT CHECK — *not a verdict in either direction* — covering no `node` on PATH at all (an environment fact, not a snapshot fact: reporting it as a failure sends an operator to re-copy a healthy deployment), **`node` found but NOT EXECUTABLE** (an ENOEXEC shim, a `noexec` mount, or a fork refused under `RLIMIT_NPROC`/ENOMEM — see the round-4 finding below), a path that is missing or untraversable **by this user**, a socket-guard refusal, a backstop timeout, **an exit-0 child that never reported a bind** (see (f)), and **a child KILLED BY A SIGNAL**. That last is the same class as "no `node` on PATH" and routed the same way for the same reason: an OOM-kill or a cgroup/container reap yields `returncode == -9` and NO stderr at all, so reporting it as LAUNCH FAILED — *conclusive*, *will not come up* — sends an operator to re-copy a deployment that was never given the chance to start. It is a fact about the machine, not the snapshot. The signal is named readably (`SIGKILL (9)`), never `-9`: a POSIX wait-status encoding is not something an operator should have to decode. **The exit-1 wording carries its bound:** it is conclusive *for the environment this ran in*. A startup refusal driven by an env var this tool does NOT override still fires (today: `BRIDGE_TOOLS_SSH_TARGET` and `BRIDGE_TOOLS_ENDPOINT` both set ⇒ `refuseDeaf`) — a real config defect worth surfacing, but one belonging to the invoking environment — and conversely a refusal configured only in `.mcp.json`'s `env` block is invisible here and can fire at session start without firing now. **⚠ AND PINNING THE TRANSPORT MOVED A REFUSAL *INTO* THAT CLASS RATHER THAN OUT OF IT — an earlier revision of this bullet said the opposite, and the correction matters more than the wording.** An invalid `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT` used to reach the child and refuse loudly; it now cannot reach the child at all, so it is invisible here and still fires at session start. **The population is concrete and it is ours: every deployment.** `examples/channel-servers/.mcp.json.example` ships `"BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT"` in its `env` block and `bin/provision-board-tools.py` writes it there too — so *the transport the session will actually use is the one value this assert now guarantees not to exercise*. Verified: with `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT=bogus` in the parent environment the tool reports LAUNCH OK, and a test asserts exactly that. **Accepted, on the balance in (e):** a false LAUNCH FAILED on every Windows seat is the worse failure, and the module graph — what this tool exists to check — resolves identically under either transport. **Closed operator-side rather than left in the log:** the pass message now discloses that the bind proven is *neither your configured endpoint NOR your configured transport*. One asymmetry worth stating: an entry file **absent while the directory IS traversable** is a conclusive **1** (the absence is real and there is nothing to launch), while an untraversable directory is **2** — `os.path.isfile()` is false for EACCES exactly as for ENOENT, the same rule `visibleOrUnverified()` enforces on the PHP side.
- **(e) BUILD REQUIREMENT 1 — the socket is a THROWAWAY, set EXPLICITLY, and a path this run did not create is never unlinked.** In the entry, `SOCKET_PATH = process.env.BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET || defaultSocketPath()`, and `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_NAME` / `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` feed **only** `defaultSocketPath()`. Every seat exports `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET` into its own environment, so it **wins**: a peer set a throwaway NAME plus a throwaway `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and the server still reached for the **LIVE** socket, declining to bind only because the live socket file happened to exist. Run this assert **before** a session starts — exactly when an operator asks "will it launch?" — and nothing holds that path, so a naive assert **binds the live socket and `unlinkSync`s it on exit**: a diagnostic that breaks live-wake. Reproduced here rather than reasoned about — dropping the explicit override from `child_env()` and re-running the suite made the child reach for this seat's real `/run/user/<uid>/agent-webhook-bridge-channel-<name>.sock` and die on `EADDRINUSE` (it survived only because a live session held it). So: the path is **assigned** (never `setdefault`) inside a private `tempfile.mkdtemp()` this run creates, so it **cannot collide with any configured socket by construction**; the run **REFUSES** rather than launching if that path already exists, and a refusal removes **nothing at all** (not the socket, not the temp dir — if the construction broke, this run does not know what it is looking at); an optional `--live-socket` lets an operator who knows their configured `channel.socket` declare it, and the run refuses if the throwaway path resolves to it. **THE REQUIREMENT IN ITS GENERAL FORM, because the specific one was under-specified TWICE and a future transport would quietly reopen it: the assert must neutralise EVERY channel-addressing input the entry reads — not the socket.** The card's build requirement was written from the unix incident and named only `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET`; that protects only unix seats. **`BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT` was the one still missing, and it was the worst of the four to miss — caught in adversarial review.** The entry defaults it to `unix` when unset (`agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs:50`), and on a Windows seat the real value is exported by the LAUNCHER's process (`examples/start-claude.ps1:129`) and/or by `.mcp.json`'s `env` block — **neither of which a freshly-opened PowerShell inherits.** An unpinned child there therefore sees it unset, defaults to `unix`, binds a filesystem socket, and Node on Win32 rejects that with EACCES: the tool prints **LAUNCH FAILED — *conclusive*, *will not come up*** — about a perfectly healthy deployment, on exactly the seat population this card exists to serve. A confidently-wrong verdict is the worst output a diagnostic can produce, and the earlier text of this bullet reasoned about that population while assuming the var reached the child. **Pinning it to `http` is a better fix than any guard, and that is the general lesson: an ephemeral loopback bind ELIMINATES the live-unix-socket hazard class outright rather than defending against it.** Under `http` the entry never reads the socket path at all, so it can never bind — and therefore never `unlinkSync` — a socket the seat is using; the socket override and both refusals below become belt-and-braces behind it (KEPT, as the layer that still holds if the pin is ever changed). One upstream fix in place of N downstream guards (canon #2/#5), and it is the shape this should have reached for first. **The trade, stated not buried:** the assert then proves an ephemeral LOOPBACK bind, not that the seat's own configured endpoint is bindable — module-graph resolution, which is what the DL-230 incident breaks and why this tool exists, happens before either transport branch and is identical under both. **Standing rule for the next transport:** enumerate the entry's addressing inputs AT SOURCE and assign a throwaway for each before shipping it. Today that is four, all in `child_env()`, all assignments rather than `setdefault`, each asserted individually. **`BRIDGE_CHANNEL_PORT=0` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` are overridden in the same breath, and that is not gold-plating:** under `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT=http` — the default on a fresh Windows seat since v0.69.0 — `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET` is not read at all and the server binds the seat's configured **loopback port**, so protecting only the socket would have left the exact same hazard on the exact population the spec was written without. Port `0` is an ephemeral bind that touches nothing; `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` pointed at the temp dir contains the `.FAILED` marker the child may write. **THE HAZARD WAS DEMONSTRATED ON A LIVE SEAT, BY ACCIDENT, WHILE PROVING THESE GUARDS.** Running the mutations above against the real environment (the tool's own suite spawns a real `node`) left two artefacts in this seat's actual `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: a synthetic bind-witness, and — from the mutations that removed the socket override — a real **`<live-socket>.FAILED` marker**, written by the child when it reached the seat's LIVE socket and hit `EADDRINUSE`. That marker is the FR #2444 operator-facing "this session is deaf to live-wake" signal, and it was FALSE: the socket was bound and accepting connections throughout (verified by connecting to it). A stale deafness marker beside a healthy channel is precisely the confusion `bridge:check` and the launcher exist to prevent. Both artefacts were removed and the channel re-verified healthy. Two things follow, and both are the point rather than an embarrassment. First, the overrides are load-bearing against a hazard that is REAL and reachable on a live box, not hypothetical. Second, **mutation-testing a tool whose purpose is "never touch live state" must itself be sandboxed from live state — so the suite IS sandboxed, in this change, rather than recorded as a known exception.** Leaving it as an exception would have been incoherent: this same DL MANDATES re-running the mutations, so the document would have required the runs and left the hazard live. `setUpModule()` repoints `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET` at a module-scoped `mkdtemp` before any case runs (assignment, not `setdefault` — the same rule the tool follows in `child_env()`), and `tearDownModule()` re-lists the REAL runtime directory and fails the run if it changed, naming what appeared. **That assertion was seen to fail once before being trusted:** with the sandbox disabled and the hazard mutation applied it fired with *added=['agent-webhook-bridge-channel-kanbanboard-agent.sock.FAILED']*. With the sandbox in place, the full mutation campaign leaves `/run/user/<uid>` byte-identical — verified by hashing the listing before and after. **The standing rule for the next transport: enumerate the entry's addressing inputs at SOURCE and assign a throwaway for each one, before shipping it.** `child_env()` is the single place that happens, its FOUR assignments are asserted directly, and each is an assignment rather than a `setdefault` because the seat exports the real values and they must lose. **The "never bound" assertion needed a witness:** the server unlinks the socket it bound, so "no socket file afterwards" is equally true of a path never touched and one bound then **destroyed** — the test's synthetic entry therefore leaves a persistent `<socket>.bound` marker, and that is what goes red when the override is dropped.
- **(f) BUILD REQUIREMENT 2 — the verdict is the EXIT CODE, never "survived the timeout".** The lifecycle is stdin-driven: `process.stdin.on('end', () => shutdown(0))`. With stdin **closed** the server binds, prints its listening line and exits **0 immediately**; with stdin held **open** it is still running at 5s. A survival-based assert therefore **false-FAILs a healthy snapshot** — and, worse, would report a killed process as a pass under the opposite polarity. So stdin is `DEVNULL` and the exit code is the verdict; the timeout is a **backstop** and a timeout is **INCONCLUSIVE** (exit 2), never a pass. One bound, and the two halves of it are now consistent — an earlier revision asserted *both* "the order is not guaranteed, only observed" and "emits its listening line deterministically", which cannot both be true. **The stronger claim is the correct one for the transport this tool pins, and the mechanism is why:** under `http` the listener is a TCP socket, `server.listen()` binds SYNCHRONOUSLY inside libuv and then queues `'listening'` via `process.nextTick`, while stdin EOF on `/dev/null` can only complete in the POLL phase — and the nextTick queue drains before control returns to the loop. So the listening callback runs first by construction on POSIX, not by luck. The 60/60 and 15/15 observations are corroboration of that argument, not a substitute for it; the bound is that it is an argument about *this* entry shape on *this* platform, which is exactly the scope this tool runs in. The verdict does not depend on it, and the PASS message never claims a bind it did not see. **AND THE MARKER IS NOW PART OF THE VERDICT, IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY.** Exit 0 is necessary but not sufficient: a zero-length entry, or one truncated at a valid parse point, exits 0 having started nothing — so an exit-code-only assert printed `LAUNCH OK` while its own message admitted the bind was never observed, i.e. the exit code said the opposite of the measurement. That case is now **exit 2, COULD NOT CHECK** — an unfinished measurement. **It is deliberately NOT exit 1, and the reason is a constraint on the whole tool: the verdict must never rest on matching a log string.** Keying a FAILURE on the ABSENCE of a listening line would couple every deployment on the fleet to the entry's startup prose — reword that line upstream and healthy seats false-fail. So the coupling is ASYMMETRIC by construction: seeing the marker may UPGRADE an exit-0 to a pass; not seeing it may only WITHHOLD the pass. The worst a reworded line can then do is make healthy deployments report *could not check* — visible, annoying, recoverable — instead of declaring the fleet broken. It cannot false-withhold on a healthy snapshot either: the shipped entry emits its listening line deterministically before stdin EOF can close it (15/15 in review, 60/60 in the earlier ordering probe).
- **(g) WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT COVERED — stated here rather than discovered later.** (1) **Steady state.** A launch is not a soak: it proves the module graph resolves and the bind succeeds, at that moment, for that user. The output says so. (2) **Staleness.** The tool has no reference by design, so it cannot know the deployment is three versions behind; that remains `bridge:check`'s version leg — **and a seat whose deployment the bridge cannot traverse still gets no staleness verdict from anywhere, on either side.** That gap is **unchanged by this card and remains open**; `docs/multi-host.md` says so at the point an operator would otherwise assume the new tool closed it. (3) **File contents.** Unchanged from DL-229 (f): a hand-edited copy that still launches is invisible to every check here, and the diff-against-the-reference discipline in `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` is still the only signal. (4) **NOT a per-branch disclosure — an asymmetry that was proposed, CAUGHT IN REVIEW, and REJECTED.** The first shape of this change emitted the finding on the version-EQUAL branch alone, on the reasoning that this is where the completeness leg lived. That is a like-for-like replacement of a leg, and it mistakes what the disclosure is FOR: it does not stand in for the completeness compare, it says launchability was never measured — equally true on STALE, NEWER and REPO-DIRECT. **The repo-direct case is decisive:** that is the topology `examples/channel-servers/README.md` RECOMMENDS, and under the narrow shape it got a fully green run with no disclosure at all — the *green check, dark seat* shape this whole card family exists to end, reintroduced by the fix for it. **DL-229 (h) was weighed as the counter-argument and does not reach it:** (h) rejects a second finding pointing at the SAME single action, and this one points at a different action (run the seat-side assert, not re-copy the directory). The disclosure is therefore uniform across every branch that reached the legs, and exactly-once is asserted per branch rather than on a single representative — which is what the narrow shape's own tests failed to notice.
- **(h) The cross-language ENUMERATION contract goes with the leg — the DL-229 precedent, applied a second time.** DL-229's per-language-lockstep paragraph reasoned that the deleted file-set leg's `SnapshotFileSetLockstep` "went with the leg rather than being left as a guard over a contract nothing reads", and DL-230 (d) brought it back **with** the leg. Symmetry now requires cutting it again: with `referenceFileSet()` gone, nothing in this repo mirrors `_deploy_snapshot`'s `copytree` semantics, so a guard over that conformance would pin an agreement no code depends on. `VersionComparatorLockstep` **stays** — the comparator contract is live and unaffected. The probe is back to **ONE** cross-language contract, as at DL-229.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) Keep the completeness leg *and* add the launch — rejected, and this is the important rejection: two authorities on one question that **silently disagree** (measured: they disagree in both directions on real artifacts) is the exact defect being fixed, and the weaker one would keep FAILing pruned deployments while the stronger one passed them. Retiring it is not tidying, it is removing a second answer. (b) Narrow the completeness leg to a "load-bearing subset" so it stops reddening pruned copies — rejected on DL-229 (g)'s standing ground (a judgment heuristic with no authority behind it) and now on a stronger one: the launch **is** the load-bearing subset, computed by the runtime rather than guessed by us. (c) Run the launch from `bridge:check` — rejected per (b) above; it is the wrong OS user, which makes it a proxy, which is the thing being retired. (d) Have `bridge:check` shell into the agent's account (`sudo -u`, ssh) to launch as the right user — rejected: it needs a privilege or a key the check does not have and should not acquire, on a command whose entire posture is read-only stat; DL-224 already recorded what goes wrong when a probe certifies the wrong account. (e) Keep the leg as a WARN instead of retiring it — rejected: a warn that fires on a correct, working, deliberately-pruned deployment with no action available to silence it is DL-236 (a)'s habituation argument verbatim, and it trains operators past the actionable warns. (f) Emit the `unvalidated` disclosure on every branch (stale / newer / repo-direct too) — **ADOPTED**; it is what shipped, appended once in `probe()`. It is the NARROW per-branch form (version-EQUAL only) that was proposed, caught in review and rejected — see (g)(4). An earlier revision of this line read "considered and narrowed", i.e. the exact reverse of the code, which would have led an auditor of this log to the opposite conclusion. (g) Have the tool read `channel.socket` from the agent YAML so it can avoid the live path — rejected: it would make the tool depend on a bridge config and a config parser, destroying the reference-free property that lets it be copied to a bare seat; the throwaway-by-construction socket needs no knowledge of the live one, and `--live-socket` is there for the operator who wants to assert the disjointness explicitly. **Noted, not taken:** `unverifiedWarn()` now has exactly ONE caller (`visibleOrUnverified()`) since the completeness walk that called it directly is gone, so it is a one-caller indirection whose docblock partly explains a caller that no longer exists. Collapsing it into the guard was raised in review and deliberately left out of this diff as a style call with no behavioral content — recorded here so it is not rediscovered as a finding.
**Tests.** *Python (`bin/test_check_channel_snapshot.py`, 47 cases, real `node` — a mocked launch would assert the mock; every case skips LOUDLY with a stderr banner if `node` is ever absent):* the three shapes above (whole copy ⇒ 0; `channel-lib.mjs` removed ⇒ 1 with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` surfaced; pruned ⇒ 0); the pass message never claims steady state or freshness; an absent entry in a traversable directory ⇒ 1 while an untraversable directory ⇒ 2; a hanging entry ⇒ 2 and explicitly NOT a pass; no `node` on PATH ⇒ 2 naming node; the `main(argv)` seam and the program-as-a-program exit code; `child_env` overrides all four channel-addressing inputs without mutating the parent; the live-socket sentinel is never created **and never bound** (the `.bound` witness); the temp dir is cleaned up; a pre-existing socket path ⇒ refuse, and the file **and its directory** survive; `--live-socket` colliding ⇒ refuse, with a non-colliding one as the positive control; the SHIPPED reference launches (loud skip if `node_modules` is absent) and the shipped entry still imports `channel-lib.mjs`; the tool is stdlib-only and executable. Plus, from review: an **empty** entry and one **truncated at a valid parse point** each ⇒ exit 2, never `LAUNCH OK` and never `LAUNCH FAILED`; **the parent's `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT` never reaches the child** (asserted at the MECHANISM — the Windows EACCES is not reproducible on Linux, so the synthetic entry refuses an unknown transport and the case is pure exit-code evidence, no log-string coupling); **the seat's configured PORT is never reached** (the sentinel port is HELD OPEN for the run, so exit 0 is itself the proof — the `http` leg's behavioural witness, and `http` is the fresh-Windows default, so it gets the unix leg's standard of evidence rather than a dict assertion); **nothing is written into the seat's `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`** (where the entry drops its `.FAILED` marker; the dir must be empty afterwards). **A STRUCTURAL GUARD ON THE SNAPSHOT-PROBE PATH — narrowed, because the first version's stated invariant was FALSE when it was written.** It claimed `bridge:check` never execs anything. It does: `CheckCommand` reaches `ClassifierResolver::probeLoadable()`, which runs `new Process([PHP_BINARY, …])` to load a custom classifier out-of-process, and `SshProbeEnvironment` for the ssh round-trip. A guard whose invariant is already violated by legitimate code teaches the next reader to distrust it — and that one was evadable three ways besides (a fully-qualified `new \Symfony\…\Process`, an aliased import, and the realistic one: **exec in a NEW CLASS**, which is how every other probe in this command is structured). The narrowed form asserts that `ChannelSnapshotProbe` is a final class with no imports, no `new`, no parent, and no static call outside `self::`. **That is a TRIPWIRE, not a proof, and saying otherwise was this guard's SECOND consecutive round of stating evidence broader than what it measures.** The prose claimed those assertions meant the class "cannot delegate to a collaborator that would" exec; review ran five evasions and all five passed GREEN, **two of them literally delegation** — an INDENTED `use LaunchesNode;` (the assertion matched only column-0 imports, while `    use SomeTrait;` is this codebase's own PSR-12 style) and `extends NodeLauncher` with an inherited method still spelled `self::`. Those two, plus the fully-qualified `\shell_exec(` (the lookbehind wrongly excluded `\`), `include`, and a bare dynamic invoke `$f(...)`, are all closed now and each is verified caught against a mutated copy. What CANNOT be closed by an enumerated blocklist — variable-variables, a computed class name, a callable smuggled through an array — is stated outright instead of implied away. A positive control was added to the static-call assertion, whose `or {"self::"}` fallback had made it pass on an EMPTY set, indistinguishable from the regex having misfired. **The rule this produced, and it is the same defect a peer agent self-diagnosed independently on another repo in the same period: state the WEAKEST claim the assertions actually support, and let the code be stronger than the prose — never the reverse.** The value of this guard is not adversarial anyway: the realistic regression is a maintainer adding a launch leg the honest way (`use`, `new`, `extends`, a plain `proc_open`), and every one of those trips it. **The scanner behind it was fixed and its directional promise withdrawn.** It claimed it could only fail into a false NEGATIVE; both directions were reachable, because a mishandled escape does not widen the blanking — it FLIPS the in-string state and desyncs everything after it. PHP's single-quoted `\'` was read as a closing quote, so `'don\'t …'` was CAUGHT (a false positive on idiomatic source) while a real `\'` in `CheckCommand.php` opened a two-line blind window in which an injected `shell_exec()` was NOT caught — inside the file the guard protects. Backslash now consumes the next character in BOTH quote styles (that is what keeps the state machine in sync), `#[` is an attribute rather than a comment, and the primitive list matches whole IDENTIFIERS so `getFilesystem(` is no longer `system(`. Heredoc/nowdoc bodies and `?>` interleaving remain unhandled and are stated as such; neither appears in the scanned file. **Four self-tests pin the exact shapes that broke it**, each red when its fix is reverted — a scanner nobody probes is how the guard it backs becomes decorative. What it backs is called a TRIPWIRE, not a proof. **Proven failable by mutation — every count and name below RE-RUN at the moment this was written, and each entry NAMES THE GUARD that reds rather than a total.** Collateral totals were tried and abandoned: dropping the port override reds 14 or 15 depending on whether port 8788 happens to be free on the box, so a number there is not a fact about the code, and an environment-dependent count reads as coverage. Dropping **`BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT`** reds `test_the_parents_transport_never_reaches_the_child`; **`BRIDGE_CHANNEL_PORT`** reds `test_the_seats_configured_port_is_never_reached`; **`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`** reds `test_nothing_is_written_into_the_seats_runtime_dir`; each also reds the `child_env` dict assertion. **`BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET` reds that dict assertion ALONE** — and read this as a CORRECTION: an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed it also reds the sentinel case, a count taken from a DOUBLE mutation that removed the transport pin as well. Disabling the bind gate reds the two exit-0-without-bind cases plus the customized-entry message case; letting a signal-kill fall through reds `test_a_signal_killed_child_is_an_environment_fact_not_a_verdict`; reporting a timeout as OK reds the hanging case; disabling the pre-existing-socket refusal reds the refusal case; treating any child exit as OK reds the DL-230 case in all three of its forms; giving the probe a collaborator (`new ChannelLaunchProbe`) or a static call outside `self::` reds the structural guard; reverting any of the three scanner fixes reds the scanner self-test; collapsing the dangling-symlink branch reds `test_a_dangling_symlink_is_named_as_one_not_as_a_missing_path`; each of the five exec evasions above reds the structural guard; letting an `OSError` escape either exec site reds the two "not a deployment verdict" cases; stopping the fixture from writing its bind witness reds BOTH witness-presence cases; removing the single output-side `OSError` handler reds `test_a_reader_that_stops_listening_does_not_invert_the_verdict`; dropping the target-ancestor gate reds `test_a_symlink_whose_target_is_invisible_is_not_called_dangling`. **THE GENERATOR, KILLED — and this is the finding that matters more than any instance below.** Rounds 4, 5 and 6 each patched ONE INSTANCE of a single class and left the generator untouched: `OSError` at the exec ⇒ caught; `OSError` at `mkdtemp` ⇒ caught; `BrokenPipeError` at `print` ⇒ caught. The generator never moved — **`main()` had no default, so CPython's exit-1-on-uncaught-exception ALIASES `EXIT_LAUNCH_FAILED`** — and every round added one more entry to an ENUMERATION of exception types. The sharpening worth keeping: the launch mechanism has been stable since commit one because it is a MEASUREMENT, while the guards kept failing because they are hand-maintained enumerations (of exception types, of exec primitives, of addressing env vars, of "six causes"), and enumerations drift and are unfalsifiable at the edges. The single guard here that never came back is the transport pin, and its own comment says why — it *eliminates the hazard class outright rather than defending against it*. Applied to the exit contract, that means three structural moves, none of them a list: `main()` gets a **catch-all default** (`Exception`, scoped exactly to the class that aliases exit 1 — `KeyboardInterrupt` exits 130 and `SystemExit` carries its own status); output is **rendered to an in-memory buffer** so a verdict is always computed before any I/O is attempted, making it impossible BY CONSTRUCTION for a delivery failure to change a verdict; and delivery carries an **in-band flush** so an EPIPE surfaces where a handler can see it. The exit-2 documentation stops enumerating causes and DEFINES itself as "no verdict was reached", with a property test asserting the process exit is always in {0,1,2} across the branch matrix — replacing four prose restatements with one measurement. **AND THE CLASS SURVIVED *IN* THE FIX, which is the sharpest form of it: `_deliver`'s fallback shipped as `except OSError` — a hand-maintained exception list inside the change whose whole argument is that enumerations are the generator — and it was wrong immediately. With fd 1 CLOSED at startup CPython sets `sys.stdout = None`, so the fallback raised `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'fileno'`, escaped to exit 1, and reported a HEALTHY deployment as *LAUNCH FAILED, conclusive, will not come up*. Reproduced with `check-channel-snapshot.py <good dir> >&-`; also reachable under Windows `pythonw.exe`, the population the transport pin exists to serve. No suite case closed fd 1, which is why 46/46 stayed green with it live. **The fix is TOTALITY, not another type:** one `except Exception` around `_deliver`'s entire body, returning unconditionally. Widening `main()`'s `try` to cover delivery was considered and REJECTED — the catch-all there returns COULD NOT CHECK, so it would downgrade a COMPUTED verdict on a delivery failure, the opposite half of the category error already fixed. A total `_deliver` makes both halves impossible at once, and the exception list disappears rather than being extended. **One attribution corrected with it, because an inherited wrong one is how the retracted ">64 KiB, precautionary" claim happened:** the discriminating case for the delivery path is a reader that closes WITHOUT READING, at any size — not a large payload. The fix changed the timing (output is now a single `write()` after the child exits), so for payloads inside the pipe's capacity no pipe breaks at all; instrumented, 4 of 6 read-a-line cells never break one. The regime axis is kept as a BREADTH check and labelled as such, the unread-pipe axis added, and the size table is marked as describing the pre-fix file rather than a live property. **Minor with it:** a fault between `mkdtemp` and the inner `try` leaked the temp directory (observed, one per suite run); the directory is now owned from the moment it exists, via an `except` that cleans and RE-RAISES rather than a `finally` — a `finally` would delete the very thing the two refusal paths deliberately refuse to touch. **And the opposite error, fixed in the same move:** a conclusive `LAUNCH FAILED` was being DOWNGRADED to `COULD NOT CHECK` when piped, because prose could not be handed to a reader who had already stopped reading. Rounds 4–6 fixed this category error pointed one way; that is the same error pointed the other way, and a completed measurement must never be overwritten by a delivery failure. **Two more of the SAME defect the round-4 fix set out to kill — an environment fault reported as a conclusive verdict — at two sites that fix did not audit.** (3) **`BrokenPipeError` IS an `OSError`, and the OUTPUT sites were unguarded**, so `print()` propagated and CPython's exit-1-on-uncaught-exception collided with `EXIT_LAUNCH_FAILED` again. Measured on the exit-2 path with a child emitting ~4000 stderr lines: unpiped **2**, `| head -1` **1** — the verdict INVERTED. This is not an edge case but THE DOCUMENTED USAGE: the whole product is a machine-readable exit code, so `| head`, `| tee` and `| grep -q 'LAUNCH OK'` are how it is consumed, and `grep -q` closes the pipe on first match by design. Caught at `main()`, returning `EXIT_COULD_NOT_CHECK`. **The canon #7 sibling audit comes back justifiably CLEAN rather than empty:** `bin/provision-board-tools*.py` have a binary 0/1 contract, where a broken pipe collapsing to 1 is not an inversion of a distinct verdict — so there is no consolidation item, and this is specific to the only tool in `bin/` with a THREE-valued contract. Recorded because "no sibling found" and "siblings cannot have this defect" are different findings. **[CORRECTED — and the correction is the lesson of round 6, so it stays visible rather than being edited away. The claim that the shutdown-flush 120 was "not reproducible on this platform, precautionary" WAS WRONG, and wrong in the direction that makes a reader stop looking. It is reproducible; it was measured in the one buffering regime that hides it, and the ~4000-line fixture used to "prove" the fix sat at 295 KB — above the 64 KiB boundary, the ONE window where an in-band handler already runs. **The size table that shows this is NOT reproduced here.** It lived in three places, and the third copy went unsynced and became false in the present tense — measured against the CURRENT file, every one of those sizes now exits 2, because the fix changed the timing. That is precisely the failure this bullet exists to record, committed one layer up. The table describes the PRE-FLUSH file and is owned by ONE place, `_deliver`'s docstring in `bin/check-channel-snapshot.py`, which sits beside the code that makes it true or false; read it there. In the 8–64 KiB band no exception is raised in band at all: `print()` succeeds, `main()` returns, and the INTERPRETER SHUTDOWN flush hits EPIPE, so no handler in the file ever executes and the `dup2` inside one never runs. The fix is an explicit in-band `sys.stdout.flush()`, which moves the failure to where a handler can see it; the `dup2` is then reachable and is now falsifiable (removing it reds the short-run case). Both the "not reproducible" and "unfalsifiable" statements are retracted.]** (4) **The round-4 dangling-symlink move was WRONG, and reverting it is not the fix.** The reasoning was that the absence is as proven as the entry-file one because the ancestor's `+x` passed — but that ancestor is the LINK's, not the TARGET's. `lexists() and not exists()` does NOT entail "the target is gone": `exists()` is false for EACCES exactly as for ENOENT, the rule `resolve_entry()`'s own docstring states two branches earlier. Measured on one link over one intact deployment, changing only the TARGET's ancestor mode: `0755` ⇒ exit **0** LAUNCH OK; `0000` ⇒ exit **1** *"the link went dangling, repoint the symlink"* — a confident wrong verdict about a healthy deployment. It also contradicted the sibling branch (a NON-symlink path under the same `0000` correctly reports *not visible to this user*), so the answer an operator running as the wrong user received depended on whether their path happened to be a symlink; and it diverged from `ChannelSnapshotProbe` on the very question the exit code was aligned for (the PHP probe returns `warn` for that shape, `fail` only for a genuinely dangling link). Fixed by resolving the link non-strictly and running the TARGET's nearest existing ancestor through the same `os.access(X_OK)` gate before concluding anything; genuinely dangling keeps exit **1**. Verified after the fix: `0755` ⇒ 0, `0000` ⇒ **2**, genuinely dangling ⇒ **1**, PHP on the same shape ⇒ `warn`. **Two more findings from that round, both the same family as the guard defects above.** (1) **An `OSError` from the exec was uncaught, and CPython exits 1 on an uncaught exception — EXIT_LAUNCH_FAILED exactly.** So a `node` shim that is not a valid executable (ENOEXEC), a `node` on a `noexec` mount (`shutil.which` uses `os.access(X_OK)`, which does not model mount flags), or a fork refused under `RLIMIT_NPROC`/ENOMEM each reported a HEALTHY deployment as conclusively broken. Reproduced with a three-line fake `node`. The third cause settles the routing: a refused fork is the same physical condition as the signal-kill already routed to exit 2, so anything else would make the tool inconsistent with its own principle. Both exec sites (`subprocess.run` and `mkdtemp`) now catch it. (2) **The bind WITNESS was never observed present anywhere** — `${SOCKET_PATH}.bound` and `bound-http-${PORT}` appeared only in the fixture and in two ABSENCE assertions, and `witness()` swallows its own write errors, so if it had ever stopped writing both tests would have passed forever. That is the fourth instance of this family in this card, landing on the very mechanism introduced to end it. Two positive controls added: the witness is produced under BOTH transports (driven directly, since the tool pins `http` and a mechanism proven for one transport is half a control), and it is observed INSIDE the throwaway directory during a real run, before the `finally: rmtree` erases it. **Methodology, because it changed a result:** the mutation must be an ASSIGNMENT OMISSION (delete the `env[...] = ...` line), never a `del env[...]` — the latter is a different mutation (it removes a key the parent may not have set) and produces a false negative. All counts and names above were produced by omission, under the sandbox, at the moment of writing. **One flaky assertion found and fixed while auditing this:** `assertNotIn("-9", text)` on the signal case is path-sensitive — the asserted text embeds a `mkdtemp` path whose random name is drawn from `a-z0-9_`, so 1 name in 37 begins with `9` and the path itself contains `-9` (measured 80/3000, reproduced deterministically by forcing the name). Anchored to the message tail (`killed by -9`) instead; widening the prefix would only move the collision. It is the same family as a fixture that passes for the wrong reason, and the audit of the other 19 absence assertions found no sibling. **One honest layering note, and the rule it produced.** With the transport pinned the entry never reads the socket path, so the unix `.bound` sentinel case reds only if BOTH the pin and the socket override are dropped. That is what belt-and-braces means; each override's own single-mutation guard is the `child_env` dict assertion, and the test says so rather than banking itself as coverage it no longer provides. **The rule, adopted after a stated proof in this very DL was found false: any mutation count or test name written into a DL or a docstring must be one RE-RUN at the moment of writing.** The false claim was not careless arithmetic — it was a count that was true when measured and became false when a later commit renamed the test and changed the layering, which is precisely the shape a reader cannot detect. Prefer naming the guard that reds over stating a total. *PHP:* `ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` — the disclosure is exactly `unvalidated`, names the tool, the seat and the USER, is accompanied by no `fail`, and appears **EXACTLY ONCE** on each of the three version branches (a data provider, so a future branch cannot be added without a row) plus **repo-direct**, which is the case that decided the placement; it survives beside a presence FAIL (asserted, since suppressing it there would couple it to another leg's severity); each of the four EARLY returns asserts `assertCount(1, …)` and no launch line — the (h) shape this must not become; no branch mentions `completeness` / `SKIPPED` / `is MISSING`; an **unreadable reference directory** no longer produces any finding (the structural proof that nothing enumerates it). `BridgeCommandsTest` — through the REAL command against the REAL checkout reference: a version-matched copy missing `channel-lib.mjs` now exits **0** with the disclosure and the tally (the behavior change, asserted rather than left to be discovered); a healthy version-matched copy exits 0 with the disclosure (the exit contract end to end); the STALE and REPO-DIRECT runs each carry it too, `substr_count(...) === 1` on all of them so a per-leg regression is caught; none of the completeness leg's vocabulary survives in the output. **One pre-existing test changed and it is the only one:** DL-236's silent-at-zero case declared a healthy far-future `server_path`, and every such agent now emits the disclosure, so that fixture can no longer produce zero. Its fixture is now an agent with **no `channel:` block** — the honest zero, since the probe is only invoked for an agent with a channel socket, url or `server_path` — and it is renamed `test_check_prints_no_unvalidated_tally_when_nothing_reported_unvalidated` (the old name, *…when every leg ran*, was about to become false regardless: no leg anywhere measures the launch). No test anywhere asserted a finding COUNT on a stale or repo-direct fixture, so nothing was silently absorbed by a loose matcher — checked, not assumed. `bin/test_provision_board_tools.py` — `SnapshotFileSetLockstep` removed per (h); `VersionComparatorLockstep` untouched. CI: the python job is renamed, sets up Node 20, runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in `examples/channel-servers`, and runs the new suite, with the tool + its tests + `examples/channel-servers/**` in its path filter. **The `npm ci` step is not optional and review caught its absence:** `node_modules` there is gitignored, so without it the ONE case that exercises the SHIPPED entry hits its skip on every CI run — and the `examples/channel-servers/**` path filter exists precisely for that case. A check that always skips is worse than one that cannot fail, because the skip reads as coverage. Docs (Rule X1, and the grep was not the audit): `examples/channel-servers/README.md` told operators outright that `bridge:check` catches the cherry-pick — the most load-bearing stale claim of the set, and invisible to `grep -ri completeness` because it never uses the word; found by re-reading the subsystem. Channel-server snapshot `0.8.2` → `0.8.3` for that README edit, per the DL-038 bump guard. **TWO MORE THAT THE FIRST DOCS SWEEP MISSED, AND THEY ARE RELEASED HISTORY — annotated, never rewritten:** the v0.71.0 `docs/CHANGELOG.md` entries for card#5108 and card#5142 still present the completeness leg as live capability, and so does `CLAUDE.md`'s v0.71.0 release row. Each now carries a forward pointer to this DL, following this repo's own precedent for exactly this situation (v0.69.0's *"Precision correction (see [0.69.1] / bridge #5074)"* in the CHANGELOG plus its matching `CLAUDE.md` row, and DL-229's bracketed corrections). A released entry is never edited to say something different from what shipped; it is annotated to say what happened next.
**⚠ Behavior change: a version-matched deployment missing a reference file no longer FAILs `bridge:check` (exit 1 → exit 0).** No migration, no new `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change; an install that never declared `channel.server_path` is byte-identical. Gates: 1426/1426 phpunit, phpstan L7 0 (no baseline file in this repo — the counted-baseline convention is the kanban-board repo's), pint clean, 131/131 provisioner python, 47/47 launch-assert python, `check-doc-refs.php` clean. Card 5143.

## DL-238 — One shared finding primitive (`Severity` enum + `Finding` VO): the four-value vocabulary stops being two private string triples, and an unknown severity becomes UNREPRESENTABLE rather than green

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Context — the vocabulary was implemented twice, and DL-236 had just made the two copies disagree.** `ChannelSnapshotProbe` and `SshTransportProbe` each carried a private helper triple returning `array{severity: string, message: string}`, and `CheckCommand::emitFinding()` rendered both. DL-236 added a fourth severity, `unvalidated`, to the snapshot probe only — so two producers fed one renderer speaking different vocabularies, with nothing in the code expressing which values were legal. A typo'd or newly-invented severity fell through `emitFinding()`'s `else` and printed ANSI-green: an unknown severity reported as CERTIFIED CLEAN, which is card 5170's own defect shape one level further out. DL-236 (f) filed this as card 5178 and recorded that the producer inventory is **three** sites, not the two the card body names. Re-verified live before building by shape-grep `'severity' =>` rather than by class name: **8 construction sites in `app/`** — four in `ChannelSnapshotProbe`, three in `SshTransportProbe`, and the raw array literal in `CheckCommand::checkEventFollowsConsumer()`'s fail-soft catch, minted by DL-236's own second commit ~36 minutes after the card was filed.
**Decision — BOTH primitives, in `App\Bridge\Support`.** A `Severity: string` backed enum (`Fail`/`Warn`/`Unvalidated`/`Ok`) and a `final class Finding` readonly VO (`severity`, `message`) with named constructors `ok`/`warn`/`unvalidated`/`fail` that replace the per-probe private helpers 1:1. All 8 construction sites migrate; every producer return type moves from the repeated docblock literal to `list<Finding>` / `?Finding`; both consumers in `CheckCommand` become exhaustive `match`es over the enum.

- **(a) Why not the enum ALONE — the option the card's question 1 offers first.** An enum fixes the legality question but leaves `array{severity: Severity, message: string}` as an unexpressed shape still re-declared at every producer and consumer docblock, and leaves the two independent helper triples standing. That is most of the duplication the card names, so the enum alone would not remove the defect it was filed for. **Why not the VO alone:** a VO over a `string` severity buys no exhaustiveness, which is the half that turns a fifth value into a compile-time error instead of a green line. Construction cost is unchanged either way — `Finding::warn($m)` is the same call shape as the `$this->warn($m)` it replaces.
- **(b) ONE shared enum, no per-probe subset — decided on evidence, not symmetry (the card's question 2).** A `SshTransportProbe`-specific subset excluding `unvalidated` would hard-code the claim *the ssh probe can never emit it*. That claim is not safe: this probe already has genuine did-not-run legs — the unreadable-`authorized_keys` warn (*the pinned line for agent X is UNVERIFIED*) and the unprivileged `sshd -T` leg its own class docblock describes as *an explicit UNVERIFIED warn … NEVER a false OK*. Whether those belong on the `warn` or the `unvalidated` side is exactly the question (d) leaves open, so a subset would prejudge it in the type system. A shared enum a probe simply never constructs costs nothing and settles nothing. The class docblock was updated to say it constructs Ok/Warn/Fail **today** — a statement about these legs, not a constraint on the vocabulary. (DL-236 (f) deliberately left that docblock's `Severity ∈ {ok, warn, fail}` un-widened while it was still a per-class truth; it is now a per-class *observation* and reads as one.) **[DL-251 (stage 10) VINDICATES THIS BULLET AND RETIRES THREE OF ITS LABELS — the argument is unchanged, the state it describes is not. (i) The subset would indeed have been wrong: `SshTransportProbe` now constructs `unvalidated` at BOTH legs named here, so a type excluding it would have had to be widened one release later. (ii) The two legs are no longer `warn`s — the unreadable-`authorized_keys` leg is limb (a) (the read did not complete) and the no-matching-line-at-an-assumed-path leg is limb (b) (it may have measured the wrong file). (iii) "Exactly the question (d) leaves open" is closed: (d) carries its own `[SETTLED BY DL-251]` marker. (iv) The class docblock no longer says *Ok/Warn/Fail today* — it says **Ok/Fail/Unvalidated**, and that this probe constructs no `warn` at all. Read the `sshd -T` half of this bullet as the state DL-238 shipped for a second reason that is not DL-251's: card#5091 had already RETIRED the sshd password-auth posture leg, and the class docblock sentence quoted here outlived it until stage 10's follow-up rewrote it.]**
- **(c) The card's question 3 DISSOLVES, and that is precisely why this change is UNGATED.** The card asked whether `emitFinding()`'s else-branch should fail loud on an unknown severity, and correctly flagged that answering *yes* changes `bridge:check`'s output/exit and is hard-gate. With `Severity` inside `Finding` there is no else-branch left to make loud: the bad state is unrepresentable at construction, so no reachable input to `bridge:check` produces different output or a different exit than before. Making the state unrepresentable is strictly better than a runtime fail-loud **and** cheaper — it needs no gate, no new error path, and no new operator-facing message.
- **(d) The `warn` ↔ `unvalidated` SEMANTICS are deliberately NOT settled here, and the enum's docblock says so instead of guessing.** A crisp discriminator was drafted — *`unvalidated` = the check did not run and nothing is wrong; `warn` = something is anomalous and a named repair exists* — and it FAILS on a live site: `CheckCommand`'s event-consumer fail-soft catch is a genuine anomaly (a thrown query) that DL-236 assigned `unvalidated`. So `Severity`'s docblock documents the **rendering contract only** — exact, mechanical, and true by construction of `emitFinding()` — and names the open question rather than asserting a when-to-pick rule the code does not obey. Freezing an unargued split into the type every future producer reads would be worse than silence. Filed as **card 5291**, marked hard-gate: any re-assignment changes what `bridge:check` prints for a given condition and whether it enters the closing tally. **[SETTLED BY DL-251 (stage 10). The docblock now carries the rule — `unvalidated` ⟺ the LEG did not answer its own question — and the discriminator drafted here is not it: the failing site named above (the event-consumer catch) is reached by "the measurement did not complete", limb (a), with no clause about whether anything is wrong.]**
- **(e) BOTH consumer arms are exhaustive `match`es, the RETURN included.** `severityMeansSetupIncomplete()` (DL-236 (f)'s positive predicate, was `in_array($severity, ['warn','fail'], true)`; **DL-251 widened it to everything but `ok`, which makes it EXTENSIONALLY the `!== ok` proxy again — the `match` form is what still separates them, and it is the whole difference: a fifth case reds phpstan here instead of being swept in**) and `emitFinding()`'s render arm are the obvious two. The third is `emitFinding()`'s **return**: written as `return $severity !== Severity::Fail` it would silently classify a fifth case as non-failing — the same fall-through shape this card closes, relocated to the exit contract. It is a second `match` over the enum, so a new case reds there too. Verified by mutation, not by reading: adding a fifth case produced **three** phpstan errors, one per `match`.
- **(f) The PHPStan scope was widened by exactly ONE file, because the analyser did not cover the renderer.** Card 5178's premise — *phpstan runs at level 7 on `app/Bridge`, so an enum would make the exhaustiveness real rather than advisory* — is true for the producers and was **false for the consumers**: both live in `app/Console/Commands/Bridge/CheckCommand.php`, outside the analysed paths, where an unhandled case would surface only as a runtime `UnhandledMatchError`. `paths` now names that single file (measured clean at level 7 when added — no baseline, no suppressions). Deliberately not `app/Console` wholesale: the rest of that tree is unanalysed for the reasons in the config header, and widening to it is a separate decision with a separate cost. **The test-side guard is not redundant with this** — `test_every_declared_severity_is_handled_by_the_renderer` iterates `Severity::cases()` and reds on the same mutation, so the property survives even if the renderer ever leaves the analysed paths.
- **(g) The canon #3 watch-item: `'some-future-severity'` was REPLACED, not deleted.** `CheckCommandSeverityContractTest` deliberately pinned *a severity that does not exist yet* → renders green / returns true / is not tallied / does not mean setup-incomplete, protecting DL-236 (c)'s promise that widening the vocabulary cannot change exit codes. That literal became unrepresentable. Deleting the rows to go green would have been loosening a constraint to satisfy the change. Each is now driven off `Severity::cases()`, which is strictly stronger: the string could stand in for exactly ONE hypothetical value, while the enumeration covers every case added later with no list to edit. Measured: the mutation that adds a fifth case reds **four** tests, where the old provider row would have reddened at most one. **[NARROWED, NOT CLOSED, BY DL-251. One of those four — `test_only_warn_and_fail_mean_the_ssh_setup_is_incomplete` — asserted a map the stage-10 sweep had to change, and it was REPLACED rather than deleted: the predicate assertion now reads "everything but `ok`", and a second test pins the severity SET `SshPinnedLineCheck` can emit so an addition reds. That replacement is a tripwire, not a proof — post-sweep `unvalidated` on this path means "could not read authorized_keys" AND would mean the opposite for a future structurally-unmeasurable finding, with the same enum value, and no severity assertion can separate them. The root-cause option — have `probePinnedLine()` report the setup-incomplete FACT instead of the advisory inferring it from a severity — is named in DL-251 and deliberately not built.]**
- **(h) Two honest bounds, stated rather than implied.** (1) DL-236 (f)'s orphaning bound is **unchanged**: nothing pins that `checkSshTransport()` still CALLS `severityMeansSetupIncomplete()` — reverting that call site to an inline `!== Severity::Ok` keeps the suite green, exactly as before, because every call-site test exercises only `warn`, where the two agree. Typing the parameter does not close that; it was not in scope and is not claimed. **[DL-251 makes this bound STRICTLY WORSE and it is recorded rather than quietly inherited: the predicate is now extensionally `!== Severity::Ok`, so the inline revert this bound describes is no longer merely undetected — it is behaviourally identical, and only the `match`'s exhaustiveness would be lost. Same address, same card.]** (2) The exhaustiveness guarantee is over the cases the enum DECLARES. It says nothing about a producer that reaches for the wrong case — that is (d)'s question, and no type can answer it.
**Alternatives considered:** (a) enum only — rejected per (a): leaves the shape and the helper triples duplicated, i.e. leaves most of the filed defect. (b) VO over a plain string — rejected per (a): no exhaustiveness, which is the half that matters at the renderer. (c) a shared `const` list — rejected: gives neither exhaustiveness nor a type, so every consumer still switches on strings and phpstan still sees `string`. (d) per-probe severity subsets — rejected per (b): prejudges (d)'s open semantic question in the type system on the strength of symmetry rather than evidence. (e) runtime fail-loud on an unknown severity — rejected per (c): it changes `bridge:check`'s output/exit (hard-gate) to defend against a state that is now unconstructible. (f) migrate the two probes and leave `CheckCommand`'s raw literal — rejected: that is the hazard surviving its own fix, and it is why the inventory was re-derived by shape-grep rather than trusted from the card body.
**Tests — split by how each was proven failable.**

*Proven by MUTATION* (add a fifth `Severity` case, re-run, restore): three phpstan `match.unhandled` errors, one at each exhaustive site (`severityMeansSetupIncomplete`, `emitFinding`'s render arm, `emitFinding`'s return arm), and four RED tests — the exit-contract provider, `test_every_declared_severity_is_handled_by_the_renderer` (new: every declared case reaches a handled arm AND lands on the buffer, so an arm that silently swallowed a finding is caught too, which no exhaustiveness check would catch), `test_only_an_unvalidated_finding_is_tallied`, and `test_only_warn_and_fail_mean_the_ssh_setup_is_incomplete`. The phpstan leg was additionally given a positive control before the scope widening landed — removing one arm reds `CheckCommand.php` at level 7 — so the widening is measured to be capable of failing, not assumed.

*Carried over unchanged in property, migrated in mechanism:* every existing assertion in `ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` (severity asserts now compare `Severity` cases against `$finding->severity`), `SshTransportProbeTest` (`hasSeverity()` takes a `Severity`), and the DL-236 rendering/tally tests. No assertion was weakened to accommodate the type change; the only removals are the four now-unrepresentable string rows, each replaced per (g).

**No migration, no new `.env`, no exit-code change, no change to what `bridge:check` accepts, rejects, or prints for any reachable input** — the enum's four values are the four strings that existed, and the rendering map is arm-for-arm identical. Gates: 1426/1426 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs.php` clean. Card 5178; the open semantics question is card 5291. **[CLOSED by DL-251.]**

## DL-239 — The card-token accept-set gets an OWNER and the operator sentence is RENDERED from the pattern; the CI lint stops being kept in lockstep by discipline and is tied answer-set to answer-set

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Context — a restatement outlived three grammar moves, and "it has a test" did not catch it.** The card token has moved three times (DL-201 added the dash alias and the leading-`\b`-only boundary, DL-231 froze the digit class to ASCII, DL-233 accepted the glued spelling at a ≥2-digit floor). Every move left prose behind. The one that mattered was **operator-facing and live**: `warnCardTokenNearMiss`'s WARN string told operators the accepted set was `card-<id>` or `card#<id>` — for two releases after DL-233 made glued `card123` correlate — and its own docblock listed `card123` as a *near-miss*. That text is read by humans and by the next agent building an emulator; one built an orientation paragraph from a downstream copy and asserted that `card5086` does not parse. Roundtable #177 leg B. The **discriminator is not "has a test"** — `PrTitleLintTest` executed the real lint bash across all three edits and never once read `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN`, so it stayed green through every grammar move. It is **tied-to-the-authority vs pinned-to-a-past-value**, and that distinction is what this DL implements.

**Decision — one owner, a rendered sentence, and an answer-set tie for the second implementation.** `App\Bridge\Support\CardTokenGrammar` holds the pattern, a shared `VECTORS` example set, and `describe()`, which buckets those examples by RUNNING the pattern. Every surface that tells a human what correlates renders `describe()`. The CI lint — a second implementation of the same grammar, in bash — is held to the PHP authority by comparing computed ANSWER SETS, not by a comment asking future editors to remember.

- **(a) A class, not a `private const` beside the pattern.** The design brief put the examples and the accept-set function inside `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier`. Rejected during the build: the tie that makes this stick is a TEST running the authority, and a `private const` can only be reached by reflection — a reflection-reached authority is a weaker tie than a public one, and it would have made the fix's own guarantee depend on the mechanism the fix exists to replace. `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` is gone from the classifier entirely; both parse sites call `CardTokenGrammar::parse()`.
- **(b) The sentence is DERIVED, and the test reads the RENDERED text.** `describe()` re-buckets `VECTORS` by construction, so the next grammar move rewrites the operator string with no edit. `CardTokenGrammarTest` asserts against `describe()`'s output rather than against `accepted()`/`rejected()` — a `describe()` rewritten to a hardcoded string would pass any assertion phrased in terms of its own helpers, which is precisely the snapshot being made impossible. Mutation-proven: hardcoding `describe()` reds it.
- **(c) `card4` and `card-3` sit in the vector set together, and that pairing is the point.** DL-233 CREATED the single-digit-glued near-miss and no prose named it for two releases. Accepted-at-one-digit-separated (`card-3`) beside rejected-at-one-digit-glued (`card4`) SHOWS the ≥2-digit floor where prose would have to assert it. The examples carry no verdict of their own — which side each lands on is decided by the pattern at render time.
- **(d) The lint is tied ANSWER SET to ANSWER SET, and only the tied half is claimed as tied.** `PrTitleLintTest` extracts the real `good=` and `looks=` regexes out of the workflow YAML (failing LOUDLY if the assignment is gone — a test that quietly stopped comparing would report that as health), drives them under real `bash` + `grep -qE` over `CardTokenGrammar::VECTORS` in three renderings (bare, mid-prose, inside a branch ref — the two boundary spellings `(^|[^0-9a-z_])` and `\b` must agree in all three), and asserts the resulting accepted/rejected lists against `CardTokenGrammar::accepted()`/`rejected()`. Neither side holds a copy of the other's verdicts. The hand-written vector tables that pinned the ASCII near-misses, the single-digit glued case and the accepted spellings are now **derived from the vector set** — shrunk, not deleted, per canon #3.
- **(e) The require step is PINNED, not tied, and the docs now say which is which.** `pr-title-lint.yml` step 2 is a THIRD implementation (`card[-#]?${card_id}`) and it is the one with teeth. It disagrees with the grammar on three MEASURED shapes: single-digit glued `card4` passes the gate but never correlates (**FALSE GREEN** — the gate certifies a silent no-op, which is the exact failure it exists to stop); `card#0123` and `DL-12345` red the gate though the classifier parses both (**FALSE RED**). Repairing either direction changes what a CI gate accepts or rejects ⇒ hard gate, unanswered, tracked as **card#5300**. The divergence is characterized in a named test with its measurements, and the exemption list it excuses from the agreement check is driven by the SAME constant the divergence test asserts against — so a stale exemption reds instead of silently excusing a vector. This file's docblock now labels its two halves TIED and PINNED rather than claiming a uniform lockstep.
- **(f) The prose sweep needed TWO passes, and that is the reusable lesson — it is one layer up from this card.** The site sweep was built by asking *what breaks if the accept-set changes*. That finds every EXECUTABLE site and **under-counts inert prose**, which breaks nothing and so never enters the candidate list; a second pass grepping the accept-set's WORDING found three more stale claims (the branch-create `started` docblock, `docs/writeback.md`'s `started` paragraph, and `pr-title-lint.yml`'s own header — each claiming `card-<id>`/`card#<id>` where the code accepts glued). Sola's leg-A miss on the same roundtable thread was the EXACT MIRROR — a prose grep missing executable sites. Neither method alone is sufficient; a sweep needs both passes. Two further siblings were found by re-reading the subsystem rather than by either grep (the class docblock and `cardToken()`'s own docblock), and the self-review pass on this very diff found **four more of a DIFFERENT shape** in `docs/writeback.md` — not a narrower card-token spelling but the card-token channel **omitted entirely**: the top-of-doc summary said a branch push correlates by `DL-NNN` and that a ref *with no `DL-NNN`* is ignored, across three sub-bullets, plus the same claim in the branch-create bullet. Read against `classifyPush`, the guard is `! $hasDl && $cardToken === null` — a card-token branch with no DL **does** move. That claim has been false since DL-177 introduced the FR-7 native-id channel, i.e. it predates every grammar move this card is about, and it was invisible to BOTH sweep passes because it contains none of the accept-set's wording. Corrected here because encountering a false claim makes it mine (canon #16). All now point at the owner instead of re-listing; `docs/writeback.md`'s grammar blockquote is retitled to say outright that it is the one place the spellings are written for operators, and the narrower restatements point at it.
- **(g) What was deliberately NOT changed, so it is not re-litigated.** `titleAndHead()`'s docblock and the two inline `card#<task-id>` path labels NAME which token kinds share a surface; they do not assert an accept-set. `docs/writeback.md`'s grammar blockquote was already correct and complete (it quotes the regex verbatim and names both the ≥2-digit floor and `card4`) — it is the owner, not a defect. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` and this file are historical records and are excluded from a stale-claim sweep by convention: a released entry naming `CARD_TOKEN_PATTERN` was true as of that release.
- **(h) The near-miss probe at the warn site is untouched, on purpose.** `/\bcard(?:[_:.]|\s#)?\d/i` is a *looks-like* probe, not an accept-set — the `! parses` half of the near-miss predicate is the caller guard. Widening it to the grammar would make it stop detecting exactly the shapes it exists to catch.
- **(i) The one bound worth stating: a prose doc cannot be tied to a PHP const by any mechanism this repo has.** The operator-facing WARNING TEXT inside the YAML is the hardest case — no PHP function can render it. Tied what can be tied: a test asserts that every ASCII shape the grammar rejects is NAMED in that message, so a near-miss cannot enter the grammar and leave the text behind. The Unicode vector is excluded by construction because the message describes that class ("non-ASCII digits") rather than printing a codepoint, which is right for a human-facing string; the leg is scoped to the ASCII half and says so.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) keep the WARN string and add a test asserting it equals an expected sentence — rejected: that is a second snapshot, and the two would drift together silently on the next grammar move. (b) A `private const` accept-set inside the classifier (the brief's own step A) — rejected per (a). (c) Delete the WARN string's accept-set and say only "the token does not parse" — rejected: the near-miss warn exists to tell an operator what to type instead; removing the answer removes the value. (d) Fix the require step's divergences while here — refused: hard gate, and shipping a silent fix to a CI gate's accept/reject behavior is exactly what the gate rule forbids. Pinned instead. (e) Fold the DL-token consolidation in — rejected per the audit below: it is a second defect and gets its own card.

**The other-accept-set audit this card owed (roundtable #177), run and closed.** Nine candidates opened individually, since "has a test" no longer clears a site. **One genuine second instance:** `DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` is a private const with five call sites, no public owner, and an operator-facing restatement that is NARROWER than the code — `pr-title-lint.yml` bounds DL at `[0-9]{1,4}` and its error text says `DL-NNNN`, against the classifier's unbounded `\d+`. Filed as **card#5308** (the consolidation, a pure refactor); the lint's bound itself stays on card#5300's hard gate. The remaining candidates are clean by two different mechanisms, recorded on #5308 with the measurement: `INBOX_LAYOUTS` / `KNOWN_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` / `ALLOWED_METHODS` already render their own const into the operator message (the `describe()` shape, arrived at independently); `OUTCOMES`, the board-tool reserved tags and the `http|ssh` transport are restated only in prose docs and were verified correct member-by-member; `benign_conclusions`, the CI-wake event types and the lint's branch-exemption list are not restated anywhere. Also surfaced and NOT folded in: `WebhookAdapterFactory` enumerates its provider set twice (`SUPPORTED` plus the `match` arms), where a slug added to one and not the other throws at request time rather than at load.

**Tests — every new leg proven failable by mutation, run and read, not assumed.** Eight mutations, each restored: `good=` loses its glued arm → 2 red; `CardTokenGrammar::PATTERN` reverts to pre-DL-233 → 4 red (including the require-step agreement, which proves that step is genuinely tied for the vectors it agrees on); the warn step drops its `tr` fold → the case leg reds; the warning text stops naming `card:123` → the message leg reds; the `looks` probe loses its glued-digit arm → 2 red; the require step's DL bound widens to `[0-9]+` → the divergence pin reds; the require step's separator becomes mandatory → 2 red; `good=` renamed → the extraction fails loudly rather than skipping. Card#5267.

## DL-240 — The DL token gets its own public grammar owner (a SIBLING, not a merged one); the consolidation's vector loop immediately found a fourth CI-lint divergence, and it is a LOCALE-dependent false green

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Context — the second instance the DL-239 audit found, and why it could not be folded in.** DL-239 gave the card token a public owner because a restatement had outlived three grammar moves. The other-accept-set audit it owed opened nine candidates and returned exactly one genuine second instance: `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::DL_TOKEN_PATTERN`, a `private const` with four call sites and no public owner. Two consequences, both measured before this card was filed. (1) `PrTitleLintTest` — the file whose entire job is comparing the CI lint against the authority — could reach that authority only by **reflection**, which is the weaker tie DL-239(a) rejected on the card side. (2) Its one operator-facing restatement was **narrower than the code**: `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` spelled the token `DL-NNNN` and bounded it at `[0-9]{1,4}` against an unbounded `\d+` — measured, not inferred (`dl-12345 fix` on `fix/999-slug` reds the gate; the classifier parses it; `dl-1234` passes). Card 5308. **[card#6025:** there is no `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::DL_TOKEN_PATTERN` in the tree today — this entry is the one that moved it to `DlTokenGrammar`.**]**

**Decision — a sibling `App\Bridge\Support\DlTokenGrammar`, with the coupling made executable instead of co-located.**

- **(a) Sibling, not a rename of `CardTokenGrammar` into a combined correlation-token owner.** The card filed the choice as genuinely open, because the two grammars are coupled by ratification (DL-201 widened the card token's boundary to MATCH this one's) rather than merely adjacent. Decided with the code open: they share a *shape*, not a line of code — different return types (`?int` vs `?string`), different arms (the card token has a glued form with a ≥2-digit floor; the DL token has a mandatory separator and no floor), and different operator surfaces. A merged class would have had to prefix every member (`cardVectors`/`dlVectors`, `describeCard()`/`describeDl()`) — a namespace wearing a class's clothes — and would have conflated two accept-sets that answer different questions. The coupling is instead expressed as a TEST (`test_both_grammars_share_the_ratified_boundary_shape`) that drives one fixture shape through both grammars, so the ratification reds if either boundary moves alone. That is a stronger tie than co-location, and it is the first time that claim — asserted in two docblocks since DL-201 — has been run by anything.
