- **(b) `parse()` + `sole()`, because the four call sites were asking two different questions.** Two sites wanted *the first DL token* and two wanted *the token only if exactly one appears* (the card#4852 guard: a title carrying 2+ DLs is bundled/release-shaped, so its DL is foreign to any one card and must never be stamped). That distinction was re-spelled as a bare `preg_match_all(...) === 1` at each stamping site. It is now named once. `DlTokenGrammarTest` asserts the pair on the SAME fixture — `parse()` returns the first of two, `sole()` returns null — because either alone would pass a test that conflated them.
- **(c) NO `describe()`, and the omission is stated in the class rather than left to be noticed.** The card's brief specified "the same three parts as `CardTokenGrammar` — pattern, shared vectors, derived operator sentence". The third part was dropped on inspection: `CardTokenGrammar::describe()` exists because a *runtime near-miss warning* renders it to operators, and the DL token has no such PHP surface — its only operator-facing restatement is in YAML, which no PHP function can render into. A renderer whose sole caller is its own test is a decoration (canon #6/#9). The class docblock says so and says what would justify adding it later.
- **(d) The vector loop is the deliverable, not the class.** The card half has been driven over `CardTokenGrammar::VECTORS` since DL-239; the DL half was three shapes checked by hand, so a fourth divergence could enter unobserved — and one already had. Both require-step arms are now driven over their authority's whole vector set, with named exemptions that are each pinned by their own test, so a stale exemption reds rather than silently excusing a vector.

**The fourth divergence, found the day the loop was written: `[0-9]` in bash is a COLLATION range, and the gate is locale-dependent.** Under `en_US.UTF-8`, `[[ "$title_lc" =~ …dl-[0-9]{1,4}… ]]` **matches** `dl-٣` (U+0663 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE) — so the gate GREENS a PR title carrying a DL that the classifier, whose `\d` is ASCII by DL-231's ratification, correlates to **nothing**. Same FALSE-GREEN shape as `card4`: the gate certifies a silent no-op. Measured across four locale NAMES but **three distinct locales** — `POSIX` is glibc's alias for `C` (identical `LC_COLLATE` keyword set, identical charmap), while `C.UTF-8` *is* genuinely distinct from `C` (UTF-8 collate-codeset, multibyte-aware), so the count is neither four nor two. `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `POSIX` reject it (the gate agrees with the grammar there), `en_US.UTF-8` accepts it — and GNU `grep -E` rejects it in **all** of them, which identifies bash's regex engine as the cause and is why the warn step is unaffected by the identical bracket expression. This is a direct breach of DL-231's fleet-wide clause that *any* other engine implementing this grammar matches ASCII digits only: the CI gate is such an engine, and it does not.

- **PINNED, not fixed.** Widening or narrowing the gate changes what a CI check accepts or rejects — the hard gate **card#5300** already owns, alongside the three shapes DL-239 characterized. Recorded there, not repaired here. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-272 — this row alone is now FIXED (the arm enumerates its digits), on the user's 2026-07-27 approval of the Unicode/locale row only. The three DL-239 shapes are still pinned and still card#5300's, exactly as stated here.]**
- **Pinned as a MEASUREMENT, not a claim.** `test_the_require_steps_digit_class_is_a_locale_collation_range_unlike_the_authority` asserts both locale answers plus the grep control, so the C-family half proves the vector is otherwise ordinary and the divergence is attributable to the engine. If the `en_US.UTF-8` locale is absent the leg reports **incomplete** — it never passes silently on a box that could not measure it. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-272 — that leg is renamed `test_the_require_steps_dl_arm_matches_ascii_digits_only_in_every_locale` and inverted: post-fix the vector reds in BOTH locales, so "both locale answers" would no longer discriminate. It now mutates the real script back to `[0-9]` to show the pre-fix spelling green where the shipped one reds. The absent-locale incomplete branch is retained.]**
- **Scope of the locale sensitivity, verified rather than assumed.** The full `PrTitleLintTest` was run under `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8`: all pre-existing legs return identical answers in all three. Only the Unicode-DL vector is sensitive, so `runStep()` gained an optional `LC_ALL` pin used by the characterization alone rather than a blanket locale pin that would have decoupled every other leg from the runner CI actually uses.

**The prose sweep is TIED, not merely corrected (the DL-239(i) bound, applied to the DL half).** `DL-NNNN` is gone from the workflow header and from both operator-facing error lines, replaced by the delimited `DL-<number>` — a placeholder that asserts no width. What can be tied is tied: `test_the_require_steps_operator_text_never_restates_the_dl_digit_grammar` collects every `DL-<alnum>` spelling in the step's real script and requires `DlTokenGrammar` to accept it, so a letter-run standing in for the digits (which necessarily encodes a count) reds. A **positive control runs first** — the collector is fed the historical `'DL-NNNN'` sentence and must return exactly it — because a collector that silently matched nothing would report a defect-bearing step as health. Also corrected: the require step's inline comment asserted "the lint must accept everything the classifier correlates, or it reds a title that would have moved the card" as an unqualified invariant, which the `[0-9]{1,4}` bound already violated; it now names the exception and points at card#5300.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) rename `CardTokenGrammar` to a combined owner — rejected per (a). (b) Add `describe()` for symmetry — rejected per (c). (c) Fix the locale divergence here, since `[0-9]` → an explicit ASCII enumeration looks trivial — rejected: it changes what the gate accepts, which is a hard gate regardless of how small the edit is, and the narrow-vs-widen direction is genuinely undecided (narrowing makes the gate agree with the classifier; widening the classifier would breach DL-231). (d) Pin `LC_ALL` for the whole test file — rejected per the scope note: it would make every leg measure a locale CI may not use.

**What was deliberately NOT changed, so it is not re-litigated.** The `DL-NNN` placeholder used throughout `app/` docblocks, `docs/writeback.md` and `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` is left alone. It is the fleet's established spelling for *a DL number* and is not adjacent to a bounded regex — what made `DL-NNNN` a defect was that it sat beside `[0-9]{1,4}` and told an operator what would satisfy a **gate**. The new prose tie is therefore scoped to the require step's own script, not applied repo-wide; widening it to every doc would be a sweep this card does not own.

**Tests — each new leg proven failable by mutation, run and read, not assumed.** Eight mutations, each restored, full suite green before and after (1444 tests): `DlTokenGrammar::PATTERN` bounded to `\d{1,4}` → **only** the ratified-rows floor reds, and the reason is worth recording — `parse('DL-12345')` then returns `'DL-1234'`, which is non-null, so the FALSE-RED pin's `assertNotNull` still passes; the exact-value row is what actually holds that bound. `/u` added to the pattern → the Unicode row and the locale characterization's ASCII premise red. `sole()` rewritten to return the first match → the sole/parse pair reds. `DL-12345` dropped from `VECTORS` → the ratified-rows floor reds. `DL-NNNN` restored to the workflow's error line → the prose tie reds. The gate's `[0-9]{1,4}` widened to `[0-9]+` → the FALSE-RED pin reds. A trailing `\b` added to `CardTokenGrammar::PATTERN` → the cross-grammar coupling leg reds. `DlTokenGrammar::sole()` swapped for `parse()` at the stamp site → `test_card_fallback_does_not_stamp_a_dl_when_two_or_more_are_present` reds, which is what proves the migration preserved the card#4852 guard rather than merely compiling. Card#5308.

## DL-241 — The `getCard` permanent-refusal reason names its hypothesis: 404 (no such card) and 403 (exists, not visible to this token) stop sharing one opaque `getcard_4xx`

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Context — the reason string is the DL-009 guard's only voice for the case the guard cannot reach.** `KanbanMoveCardHandler` reads the card, then refuses it if `board_id !== $mapping->boardId` (the belongs-to-mapped-board security guard, DL-009/DL-020). That guard reads `board_id` **out of the `getCard` result**, so it can only fire for a card this writeback token was able to READ. *[Additive annotation, 2026-08-21 (card#7138, DL-292): the SPELLING quoted above is no longer the code — the predicate is now `is_numeric($card['board_id'] ?? null) && (int) $card['board_id'] === $mapping->boardId`, and it lives in `MappedBoardGuard` rather than in `KanbanMoveCardHandler`, shared with the `kanban_block_reason` and `kanban_coord_card_move` arms. It accepts strictly MORE than `!==` did (a numeric-string or float `board_id` naming the mapped board), so DL-292 widened this guard on this handler. **Nothing this entry decides moves**: the guard still reads `board_id` out of the `getCard` result, is still structurally unreachable for a card the token cannot read, and that is still why the 404/403 split below is the operator's only signal for the tenancy case. The original sentence stands as written, per this log's frozen-original convention (DL-277).]* A card on a board the token *cannot* see returns one branch earlier, at the `getCard` 4xx refusal — the guard is structurally unreachable for exactly the tenancy case it exists to refuse. That earlier branch emitted a single reason value, `getcard_4xx`, over two unrelated operator hypotheses: **404** (no such card — deleted, or an id that never existed) and **403** (the card EXISTS and is not ours — a foreign install's card id correlated onto this bridge, or this token's scope missing the card's board). An operator investigating a live cross-install token hijack saw a generic 4xx pointing at nothing. Sourced from roundtable #178 (aimla-pm), second separable defect; card#5288.

**Decision — split the reason by status; leave every other behaviour byte-identical.** `getcard_404_no_such_card`, `getcard_403_not_visible_to_this_token`, and `getcard_4xx` retained as the catch-all for other 4xx. The 403's *operator-facing log line* names both hypotheses explicitly (the reason slug is a key, not an explanation). **Hard-gate approved by the user 2026-07-27** — the vocabulary above is the approved one, verbatim. **[SUPERSEDED by DL-314 as to the 403 SLUG only: `getcard_403_not_visible_to_this_token` was renamed to `getcard_403_foreign_card_id_or_token_scope` and no longer exists in this tree. The old spelling named the TOKEN as the thing at fault, which is only one of the two causes a 403 cannot choose between — the operator who hit the other one live went auditing their own token's board scope for a card that was never theirs. `getcard_404_no_such_card` and the `getcard_4xx` catch-all are untouched, and everything this decision settles otherwise — the split itself, the byte-identical exit behaviour, the single status read, the log line naming both hypotheses — stands. The original sentence stands as written, per this log's frozen-original convention (DL-277).]**

- **No status-code or exit-behaviour change.** All three are still `RefusalContext::isPermanent` ⇒ log + no-op ⇒ the dispatch acks. Nothing that was swallowed now throws, and nothing that threw now swallows.
- **Additive on ONE event kind, not a new one.** `WritebackAlertNotifier::notify()` carries `reason` as a *field* of the single `writeback_move_failed` type (DL-171), so new values need no new type and no body-shape change. A consumer switching on `reason` sees two new values; one switching on `type` sees nothing new.
- **The status is read ONCE, from the context the log line already builds.** The match keys on `RefusalContext::from($e)['status']` rather than a second `$e->response->status()` read, so the branch has exactly one notion of what the server answered.
- **The reason values stay string literals, matching the five siblings in this handler.** A named constant set for three of eight values would be a half-migration that reads as a distinction where there is none. If a second caller ever needs this mapping (the `moveCard` refusal below is the candidate — see the follow-on), it hoists then, at the second real caller (canon #5).

**This also FIXES a silent loss the collapse caused — dedup, not diagnosis.** Alerts dedup per `sha1(repo \x00 outcome \x00 reason)` (DL-171). With one shared reason, a 404 and a 403 on the same `(repo, outcome)` produced the **same** signature: whichever arrived second was suppressed as "already alerted" and reached the operator **zero** times. Distinct reasons are distinct signatures. The card's acceptance asked this be *verified*, not assumed, so it is asserted directly — two deliveries with different statuses, two pushes, two distinct reasons, in that order — rather than inferred from the hashing.

**Tests — mutation-proven, not merely green.** Three new legs: the distinct-reason/no-collapse assertion above, the 422 catch-all, and the two log lines (403 names *both* hypotheses; 404 says *no such card*), each asserting the reason/text, never just the no-op. Reverting the match to the single collapsed `['getcard_4xx', …]` pair was run: the distinct-reason test fails on the reason list AND on its length (one push, not two — the dedup half), and both log tests error on the never-received warning. Restored; class green 73/73, full suite green. Note that the *pre-existing* `test_kanban_4xx_on_get_is_permanent_noop` stayed green under that mutation — it asserts only the absent PATCH, which is precisely why the card required asserting the reason.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) add a `status` field to the alert body instead of splitting the reason — rejected here: it is a report-**shape** change (a new key every consumer must learn) where the approved change is additive within an existing field, and it would leave the dedup collapse in place, since `reason` is what the signature hashes. (b) Widen the split to the `moveCard` and `stampCorrelationRefs` 4xx branches in the same change — rejected as out-of-scope scope-creep; see the follow-on, which is a different defect (no alert at all), not a wider version of this one.

**Follow-on filed, not fixed (canon #7 sibling audit).** The sibling audit over "an operator-facing signal that collapses distinguishable causes" found no second instance in the `reason` vocabulary — the other five values each name exactly one cause. It DID surface an adjacent, different defect: the `moveCard` 4xx refusal and the `stampCorrelationRefs` 4xx refusal are `Log::warning` permanent branches that emit **no alert at all**, so a token with read-but-not-write scope 403s on the PATCH and is live-silent — the same rotated/degraded-token scenario DL-171 was built to surface. DL-171 enumerated "the 5 `Log::warning` branches" and those two were not among them; whether that was deliberate is not recoverable from the record. Filed as **card#5312** rather than folded in: it changes *which* failures signal, which is a separate hard-gate question from *what a signal is called*.

**Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Handlers/KanbanMoveCardHandler.php` (the `getCard` catch branch only — every other path byte-identical); `tests/Feature/Handlers/KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest.php` (+4 tests); `docs/writeback.md` (the signal table splits into three rows + a "why the split" subsection naming what to check on each). No migration, no new `.env`, no token-scope change, no change to what the receiver accepts or rejects.

## DL-242 — `bridge:check`'s growth is a MISSING ABSTRACTION, not a busy command: the diagnosis, the Check-registry target, and the ruling that the receiver core is NOT the problem

**Decision:** adopt `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` as the reasoning owner for the `bridge:check`
consolidation program, and rule that the **receiver / dispatch / adapter core is explicitly out of
scope** — the card pressure this repo has been absorbing does not originate there.

**Why.** The prompting hypothesis was that bug cards were outpacing fixes because the core design
was accumulating symptom-fixes. Measured over 448 commits since 2026-06-01, the core is small and
static: `WebhookController` 77 L / 2 commits, `VerifyHmacSignature` 130 L / 2, `KanbanAdapter`
42 L / 1, `GitHubAdapter` 89 L / 2. DL-001 is holding. The churn is `CheckCommand.php` — **74 →
1767 lines in two months**, 50 commits (2× the next-highest file), `handle()` at **891 lines**
nesting 11 deep, **129 check-site emissions of which only 4 (~3%) route through the
`Finding`/`Severity` primitive** built for that purpose by DL-238.

The mechanism is what makes this a design decision rather than a cleanup: a silent-failure card is
closed by adding a leg to `bridge:check`; the leg is a raw `warn()` because there is nothing else
for it to be; **raw `warn()` cannot represent "did not run"**, so the new leg's not-run state is
indistinguishable from its pass state — which mints the next card. `CheckCommand.php:961` already
prints a five-line apology for exactly this (*"a floor, not an inventory"*). A registry makes the
inventory exact and deletes the apology.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) patch the three open cards individually — cheaper, and explicitly
recorded as a legitimate call in the plan, but leaves the ~125 unmigrated sites to re-mint the
shape; (b) rewrite `bridge:check` — rejected, an operator-facing command with 103 test invocations
against it is not a rewrite candidate; a **strangler migration under a byte-identical golden-output
contract** keeps every stage revertible; (c) restructure the classifiers too — rejected on the
data: `CoordinationClassifier` and `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` are properly decomposed and their
churn is feature accretion, with all three cards against them already closed.

**Bounds, stated rather than implied.** The plan closes **3 open cards** (card#5229, card#5291,
card#5292) — it does **not** close card#5170 (released) or card#5178 (shipped), which are the
*precedent* whose fixes created `Severity::Unvalidated` and `Finding`, nor card#5310 / card#5312,
which are the same silent-degrade shape at a different address (`GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier`,
`WritebackAlertNotifier`). The justification is recurrence prevention and must be argued on that
basis. Stage 0 is the plan's own falsifier: if byte-identical capture proves impossible, the
approach is re-planned rather than half-executed, and the golden test's guarantee is bounded by
fixture coverage, so the fixture set is derived from `handle()`'s branch predicates with any
uncovered predicate disclosed as a named gap.

**Consequences:** documentation only — **no code change, no migration, no new `.env`, no receiver
accept/reject change, no token-scope change.** `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` (new) + the
`CLAUDE.md` subfile index. Stages 8–10 are hard-gate and unstarted; **no new `bridge:check` leg
should be added until Stage 8 lands**, since each one added first is another site to migrate.

**[AMENDED 2026-07-28 — the open question DL-242 recorded is now RESOLVED.]** DL-242 left one fork
for Stage 8: do the opt-in probes (`--probe-tools` / `--probe-tools-ssh`) report `unvalidated` when
their flag is absent? **Ruled: neither `unvalidated` nor `ok` — the choice is not a severity.** The
discriminator is whose fact the not-running is: a fact about the **install** the operator cannot
know (undeclared `channel.server_path`, an untraversable dir, no `node` on PATH) is `unvalidated`
— card#5170's case, and what the severity is for; a fact about the **invocation**, which the
operator necessarily knows because they chose not to type the flag, is not. `ok` is worse than
either, asserting a pass for something never executed. **"Not requested" is therefore a third
DISPOSITION living in the inventory/renderer split, not a new `Severity` case:** the runner records
every registered check's disposition (so constraint (a) holds and nothing is invisible), the text
renderer stays silent on not-requested (today's output preserved byte-identical, no noise on the
common path), and the JSON renderer emits it (card#5229's consumers get the full inventory
including what was never asked for). `unvalidated` keeps exactly one meaning — *I should have
measured this and the install stopped me*. The exhaustive-`match` property and the exit contract
(only `fail` flips) are untouched by construction. **Scope: the opt-in axis ONLY** — card#5291's
re-assignment sweep over the ~dozen couldn't-probe `warn` sites stays open and stays hard-gate.
**[LANDED 2026-07-31 by DL-251 — the sweep ran (21 sites, plus 3 legs that emitted nothing at
all, a count DL-251 records as a floor) and `unvalidated` now carries a stated rule. This scope
note is historical from here.]**
Full reasoning also recorded on card#5291, the SoT for that sweep.

## DL-243 — A whole-suite coverage claim is only writable from a MUTATION; a grep cannot support one in either direction, and a claim of membership in `check-golden-coverage.md` is false by construction for any migrated check

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Context — the DL-242 program kept minting a claim its own evidence did not support, and awareness of the rule was measured to be insufficient.** Check-package comments repeatedly stated a coverage claim MEASURED at golden-fixture scope ("no golden fixture renders X") at WHOLE-SUITE strength ("...so `XCheckTest` is its whole measurement"). The second clause does not follow from the first, and `BridgeCommandsTest` — which drives `bridge:check` through ~130 scenarios — reaches many of those arms. Fifteen instances accumulated across stages 4–7 (card#5551 is the SoT and carries the per-instance attribution). Two things make this more than a tidy-up. **(1) The rule as first written did not hold.** A stage-6 pass, whose entire purpose was correcting this class, stated its selector — a grep of `tests/` for `validateInboxConfig` and `BRIDGE_INBOX_GROUP` — and was still WRONG, because the covering tests reach those refusals through a CONFIG KEY (`config(['bridge.inbox_layout' => 'bogus'])`) that names neither symbol. The grep was clean AND the behavior was covered. **(2) The defect was re-minted by the act of fixing it**, by an author holding the rule in mind, which is why the replacement is mechanical rather than a matter of care.

**Decision — two rules, both mechanical, recorded in `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` § the golden harness (the one place that owns them; the 15 sites POINT rather than restate).**

- **Fixture scope** — "no golden fixture renders X" — comes from a grep of `tests/Fixtures/check-golden/`, because that corpus IS text. It licenses nothing about the rest of the suite, and saying so is the whole content of the claim.
- **Whole-suite scope** — "nothing else asserts X" — comes ONLY from a MUTATION: change the arm, run the whole suite, and the set that goes RED *is* the measurement set. This is the same discipline the program already enforces for absence claims in shell (positive-control it in the same command), applied to prose.
- **A comment asserting membership in `docs/check-golden-coverage.md`'s disclosed-gap list is FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION for any migrated check**, not merely stale: that file is generated from and bounded to `CheckCommand::handle()`, a migrated check is by definition no longer in `handle()`, and no regeneration can make the claim true again. The fix is to DELETE the membership claim, never to re-sync it. NEGATIVE claims stay correct and stay ("absent from that list ENTIRELY", "does not speak for it in either direction") — absence there was never protection.

**The measurement, because the ruling rests on it and not on argument.** `~/.cache/coord/claimmutate.py`: 12 arms mutated in one run, each to its own severity-preserving sentinel, one full-suite execution. Baseline at `origin/dev` 1735 pass; under the 12 mutants 1681 pass / 54 red. Attribution is by each failing test's EXPECTED STRING, never by grepping the sentinel — the sentinel token over-counts (a token inside a dumped-output diff is not an assertion) and under-counts (truncated diffs). Result: **six claims false** (`CiFailureFilterCheck`'s `catch`, `WakeMembershipCheck`'s `catch`, `InboxSurfacingConfigCheck`'s two refusals, `AgentIdentityCollisionsCheck`'s walk, BOTH `ChannelTransportCheck` liveness probes, `InstallProviderAdaptersCheckTest`'s exclusivity parenthetical), plus `AgentTreatAsSignalCheck`'s throw confirmed false; **five hold** (`AgentWebhookSecretCheck`'s insecure-perms arm, `InstallSuffixDsnCheck`'s mismatch branch, `DatabaseConnectivityCheck`'s failure arm, `ChannelTokenPathCheck`'s `catch`, `AgentClassifierResolvableCheck`'s `for()` catch). The five that hold now SAY they were mutation-measured, so a later reader can tell a proven claim from a guessed one.

**The discriminator that predicts which is which — and why it does not replace measuring.** Every FALSE claim is an arm reachable by writing a YAML or setting a config key, which is exactly what a command-level test does cheaply. Every HOLDING claim needs host state the command-level suite cannot stand up (a group-readable secret, a crosstalking DSN, an unreachable database, a bad token file, a class that loads out-of-process but throws in-process). The channel probes are the case that refutes using the heuristic INSTEAD of the instrument: they need a live listener, and `BridgeCommandsTest` stands one up anyway.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — card#5551's site list was a FLOOR, not a ceiling: 4 named, 15 found.** The broadened selector (`unobserved|coverage table|observed verdict|golden-coverage|gap list|disclosed` over `app/` + `tests/`, then a re-read of each hit) added `InstallSuffixDsnCheck`, `InstallConfigDirCheck` + its test, three writeback unit tests, `GoldenChannelEnvironment`, and `ChannelTransportCheckTest`'s class docblock plus four method docblocks. **Why the count quadrupled is the durable part:** stage 7 completing migrated essentially every remaining leg AT ONCE, so a claim family that was true site-by-site as it was written went false wholesale on one merge. A defect class whose truth value flips on an unrelated event is one a periodic re-read cannot be relied on to catch. Live-verified while auditing: `check-golden-coverage.md`'s disclosed-gap table holds exactly ONE row (the `$configs !== [] && $ctx->configDir !== null` guard — cited by construct, never by the generated offset id, which moves whenever anything above it does), positive-controlled against its result table.

**Follow-on filed, NOT built (canon #2 — filing is the floor, not the discharge).** Nothing gates a prose coverage claim in a source comment: `bin/check-doc-refs.php` reads `CLAUDE_*.md` and `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` only, and has no concept of a membership claim — which is how 15 instances arrived unnoticed. **card#5564** proposes extending it with a membership-claim rule over `app/Bridge/Check/` + `tests/Unit/Bridge/Check/`, using the in-tree correct sentences as the guard's negative fixtures. Raised to the user with a recommendation rather than built: adding a CI rule changes what the pipeline REJECTS, which is the always-ask class. Until it lands, the class stays re-mintable, and stages 8–10 are the next exposure.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) keep the wording rule from card#5551's first two appends ("apply the rule before writing the claim") — REJECTED by measurement, not by argument: it was applied, by an author with the card open, and produced two more false claims. (b) Re-sync the membership claims to the current disclosed-gap list — rejected: the list can never again contain a migrated check's predicate, so the re-synced sentence would be false the moment it was written. (c) Restate the two rules at each of the 15 sites — rejected as the duplication card#5547 exists to remove; the rules live in `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` and the sites point.

**Consequences:** comments + docs only, **zero behavior change** — no `app/` logic touched, no golden fixture regenerated, no predicate added or removed. `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` (the two rules + the fixture-count restatement dropped in favor of the property), `CLAUDE_ARCHITECTURE.md` (the Check package gains the section it never had — card#5549), `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` (the stage-5c "the unit tests are the whole measurement" sentence corrected in place), 9 check classes, `CheckCommand`'s two count-bearing fail-soft comments (card#5547), and 11 test/support files. No migration, no new `.env`, no token-scope change, no change to what the receiver accepts or rejects.

## DL-244 — The coverage-membership claim gets a MECHANICAL gate, and it is a whitelist: a check docblock naming the generated gap list must state what naming it does not buy

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Context — DL-243 ruled the claim class false by construction and filed the gate as a follow-on it deliberately did not build** (adding a CI rule changes what the pipeline REJECTS, which is the always-ask class). The user ruled BUILD on 2026-07-29. DL-243's own follow-on paragraph stands as written — this log is append-only and that paragraph was true at that version; this entry supersedes it.

**The gap being closed.** `docs/check-golden-coverage.md` is generated from and bounded to `CheckCommand::handle()`, so once a check migrates into the registry a comment claiming its predicate is one of that file's disclosed gaps is false BY CONSTRUCTION. Nothing gated it: phpstan does not analyse `bin/` or `tests/`, pint excludes `bin/`, and a false comment is valid PHP that passes every assertion. Fifteen instances arrived that way, and — the part that decides the shape of the fix — they went false *in one merge*, stage 7 completing, without a character changing in the files holding them. A defect class whose truth value flips on an unrelated event cannot be caught by a periodic re-read; it needs a gate that runs every time.

**Decision — a THIRD rule in `bin/check-doc-refs.php` (the existing CI step), whitelist and fail-closed.** A comment block under `app/Bridge/Check/`, `tests/Unit/Bridge/Check/`, `tests/Support/CheckGolden/` or `tests/Feature/Console/Check/` that mentions `check-golden-coverage` — or the bare phrase "disclosed gap" — must ALSO carry one of four licences: the bound named in the SAME SENTENCE as the mention (that the file is generated from `handle()`), or, anywhere in the block, the consequence drawn ("absence … is not protection"), the two-way denial ("in either direction"), or an explicit negative membership ("never a disclosed gap").

**Whitelist, not blacklist, and the asymmetry is the whole argument.** An unrecognised WRONG sentence passes a blacklist silently; an unrecognised RIGHT one fails a whitelist loudly and is fixed by naming the bound — which the author owed the reader anyway. This is the same trade the line-citation rule already made when it bounded the name→offset distance instead of enumerating quoting forms.

**The design was WRONG first, and a planted claim — not a review pass — found it.** The rule initially licensed a mention whenever the bound appeared within a measured distance window of it (~100 chars in the corrected corpus, against 579–811 for a block that merely points at the file: a decisive-looking gap). Then a membership claim planted into a real check docblock walked straight through. Cause: **every migrated check opens "…migrated out of `CheckCommand::handle()` (DL-242 stage N)"**, so the boilerplate opener sits inside the window of anything written beneath it. The window was measured honestly and the measurement was sound — the corrected corpus simply contained no example of the shape that defeats it, which is the same "the evidence never covered this half" failure the citation rule's own test file was built against. Proximity was a proxy for a GRAMMATICAL link; the sentence is that link, so the bound now counts only where it shares a sentence with the mention. The regression is pinned as a test, and the mutation matrix (6 arms, each red on its own named vector) is what stands behind the rule rather than a green run.

**What it does NOT prove, stated because an unstated bound is how this class began.** A marker is a phrase, not a semantics: a false membership claim that also carries a sanctioned sentence still passes, and a licence in one sentence licenses the whole block. What the gate closes is the path that actually minted the fifteen — a docblock written from a neighbour's wording. It is not a truth prover, and must not be cited as one.

**Three in-tree blocks were corrected to green it, and they are the gate working rather than churn.** `ChannelTokenPathCheckTest` stated absence ("absent from the disclosed-gap list ENTIRELY") without drawing the consequence its sibling `ReconcileRepoTokensCheckTest` draws; `GoldenCapture` pointed at the file with no bound at all, from the very block that states the harness's own bound; `CheckGoldenTest` said the file "names those gaps individually" without saying it names nothing belonging to a migrated check. Each now states the bound. All six sentences DL-243 identified as the correct forms pass unmodified.

**Scope, and its stated bounds.** `docs/` is deliberately OUT — `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` narrates the gap list at length and a whitelist over narrative prose is churn, not a gate. Because the surface is a root allow-list rather than a repo-wide scan, this rule needs no exclusion twin like `$citeExcluded`: neither the script nor its test lives under those roots, so both quote rejected claims freely. The unit is a PHP COMMENT, so a non-`.php` file placed under those roots is not scanned — there are none today and the repo's prose lives in `docs/`; that is a stated bound, not a claim the surface is airtight.

**Mechanics.** Blocks are TOKENIZED, not pattern-matched, so a comment delimiter inside a string literal cannot open a phantom block (a fixture string in the rule's own test is exactly that shape). The unit is the BLOCK, not the line — these claims run three to six wrapped lines and the mention routinely wraps away from its verb — and consecutive `//` lines merge into one block for the same reason. Findings report the SENTENCE the mention sits in: a fixed byte window splits an em-dash and emits invalid UTF-8 into the CI log, and a fragment is harder to locate than the sentence it came from.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) a blacklist of membership verbs (lists / discloses / is one of), as card#5564 originally proposed — rejected on the asymmetry above; it is the losing half of the trade. (b) A per-file exemption for `GoldenCapture`'s bare pointer — rejected: that block genuinely owed the reader the bound, so the exemption would have encoded the defect as an allowance. (c) A line-scoped rule — rejected by the corpus: it would reject nearly every correct sentence in the repo while accepting a claim whose mention wrapped away from its verb. (d) The distance window — tried, measured, and refuted by a planted claim; recorded above because the measurement looked decisive and was not.

**Consequences:** CI now REJECTS a comment shape it previously accepted — the only behavior change, and it is confined to the pipeline. **Zero runtime change:** no `app/` logic touched, no golden fixture regenerated, no predicate added or removed, no migration, no new `.env`, no token-scope change, nothing altered in what the receiver accepts or rejects. The three corrected blocks are comments only. `tests/Support/DocRefGateHarness.php` extracts the synthetic-tree harness at its second real caller (canon #5); `DocRefCitationLintTest` moves onto it unchanged in behavior (8/8, its vectors untouched). Neither pint nor phpstan covers `bin/`, so the rule's own gates are its phpunit vectors, the real-surface mutation proof, and the 6-arm rule mutation matrix.

## DL-245 — `board_my_cards` gains an opt-in `include_description`: the card becomes a DELIVERY surface, and the minimal-disclosure allowlist is widened by exactly one field

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Context — a card could not carry scope to the seat that had to implement it.** `board_my_cards` projected exactly `id, name, stage, tags, dl_number, pr_number, updated_at`, and its docblock stated the allowlist deliberately ("nothing else leaves the bridge"). Under the ratified card-first standard a PM writes scope onto a card — and the impl seat reading its own board through this tool structurally could not see it. A peer install measured the consequence: 240 cards visible, 0 with a readable description, while one of their cards carried a 7,805-byte scope statement the seat it was written for could not read. The failure is quiet in the worst way: a cold session reads a title with no body and implements from the title alone. The mitigation in use — compressing scope into the card TITLE and pointing at a second thread — caps scope at ~170 characters and splits authority across two surfaces, which is a drift generator.

**Three facts were verified before the design, and each removes an objection rather than answering one.** (1) **Isolation is not the projection's job.** `filterSwimlane()` runs fail-closed on every row BEFORE `groupByStage()` → `projectCard()`, so a row reaching the projection is already proven in-scope for the caller; adding a field cannot widen *who sees which card*. (2) **`description` is ALREADY FETCHED and thrown away** — `KanbanClient::swimlaneCards()` reads `/tasks/search.json`, whose rows carry the full field. This is a projection change: no extra API call, no N+1. (3) **Response size is therefore the only real cost, and it is the whole reason the field is opt-in** rather than stylistically so.

**Decision — a per-CALL `include_description` argument, plus a per-card byte cap and an explicit truncation flag.** Absent argument ⇒ **both keys are ABSENT, not null** — the default response is byte-identical to the DL-217 shape, which is what lets this land without touching any existing caller. Passed ⇒ every projected card (own lane, shared lane, and coord cards alike) carries `description` cut to `board_tools.description_max_bytes` (default 16384) and `description_truncated`. A non-boolean argument is REFUSED (422) rather than coerced: a truthy string would silently switch on the expensive projection the opt-in exists to gate.

**The allowlist widening is scoped to THIS field and must not be cited as a general opening of it.** The DL-217 minimal-disclosure posture stands for every other column on a card row. What was actually ruled is narrower than "the projection may grow": the card body is the one field whose absence defeats the tracking surface's stated purpose, and it is already inside the bridge's process when the projection discards it. Any future field starts the same argument from the beginning.

**Per CALL, not per agent — the property belongs to the call.** A seat wants scope when it is *starting* a card and does not want it when polling; a config key would make a call-shaped property seat-shaped and pay the cost on every poll forever. The bearer/identity model is untouched either way — the argument cannot change board, lane, or which cards are returned.

**The truncation flag is load-bearing on its own, and the cut is on a CHARACTER boundary.** A seat must never be able to mistake a truncated scope for the whole scope — that is the same failure class as reading a title with no body, which is what this card exists to close, so a silently-short body would have reintroduced the defect one layer in. The cut uses `mb_strcut`, not `substr`: the cap is a byte budget (response size is what it bounds), and a raw byte cut can split a multi-byte character — the resulting invalid UTF-8 fails `json_encode` for the WHOLE response, so a single emoji at the cut point would blank the caller's entire board window rather than trim one card.

**The cap is configurable because the right value is a property of the install, not of the code.** 16384 carries the 7,805-byte motivating case whole while bounding a pathological body; an install whose scope statements run longer, or whose lanes are much larger, needs a different number and the bridge cannot know which. A non-int or a value < 1 fails like every other `board_tools` malformation (explicit ⇒ throws at load, default-class ⇒ suppresses with a reason `bridge:check` FAILs on) — never a silent fallback to the default, which would read as honored.

**Stated bound — the cap bounds ONE CARD, not the response.** The total is `cards in the lane × their bodies`, and nothing caps that; a seat with a large lane that opts in gets a large response and the argument's own description says so. This is deliberate for v1: the caller is asking explicitly and the per-card cap removes the unbounded-single-body case. If a lane grows large enough that the aggregate is the binding cost, the fix is a single-card read (below), not a second cap here.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) **a per-agent `board_tools` config key defaulting off** (the filer's shape 2) — rejected above: seat-shaped knob for a call-shaped property. (b) **Always include, truncated** (shape 3 alone) — rejected: it changes the default response for every existing caller, and the opt-in is the only thing that keeps that byte-identical. (c) **Untruncated opt-in** (shape 1 alone) — rejected: it reintroduces the unbounded response the opt-in exists to avoid, one card at a time. (d) **A hardcoded cap** — rejected: it bakes an install-specific number into shared code, and the two installs that motivated this card differ by 4× on it. (e) **A single-card `board_card <id>` read** — not built: it is the right shape if the aggregate becomes the binding cost, but it does not answer the "show me my lane WITH scope" call that motivated the card, and building both now is speculative. Filed as a follow-on.

**Consequences:** `BoardMyCardsTool` (the argument, the cap thread-through, `capDescription`), `BoardToolsConfig` (`description_max_bytes` + `DEFAULT_DESCRIPTION_MAX_BYTES` + `optionalPositiveInt`), the reference channel server's advertised `board_my_cards` input schema (a `tools/list` change — the argument is unreachable over MCP without it; snapshot `0.8.3` → `0.9.0` per DL-038). **No migration, no new required `.env`, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change**, and no change to which cards a caller can see. The one behavior change to an existing surface is the new 422 on a non-boolean argument, which no pre-existing call can trigger. Docs: `docs/board-tools.md` (arguments table + a § on reading scope), `docs/config-schema.md` (the new key).

## DL-246 — A source tripwire pins to the CALL, not to the FILE; and a job whose path filter cannot see the change that breaks it is a decoration

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Context — a security tripwire had been guarding nothing, and the job that would have said so was structurally unable to run.** `bin/test_check_channel_snapshot.py` carries two assertions about `app/` PHP SOURCE SHAPE: that `ChannelSnapshotProbe` has no reachable way to execute a process, and that the SNAPSHOT leg's call into it stays a pure string-in/findings-out call. The DL-242 stage-7 migration moved that call from `CheckCommand::handle()` into `ChannelSnapshotCheck`. The call-site assertion went on scanning `CheckCommand.php` — a file that no longer held its subject. `dev` was red from that merge until an unrelated PR (#441) happened to touch `examples/channel-servers/**` and made the job fire.

**The near-miss is the finding, not the red.** The assertion survived as a failure only because it was written as an exact equality against one literal argument string. Written the way such a guard is usually written — "no call site passes a non-string" — it would have been **GREEN over an empty result set**, guarding nothing, indefinitely. That is the card#5552 shape (a fixture that does not exercise its named subject) reappearing in a different language on a security guard, and it is why the rewrite below leads with an existence assertion.

**Decision (1) — the guard is pinned to the CALL, wherever it lives.** It now walks every `.php` under `app/`, collects every `ChannelSnapshotProbe::` call site, **asserts at least one exists** (naming the "this guard has lost its subject" failure explicitly), and judges each site's arguments against a GRAMMAR — a variable, a property-read chain, a quoted string, or a class constant. Anything containing `(` fails by construction, so a smuggled call cannot match however it is spelled. The previous revision pinned the literal argument TEXT of one call site in one named file; that is what a refactor orphans. A tripwire pinned to where code lives dies at the next migration.

**Decision (2) — the no-exec assertion gets an allow-list with a TRANSITIVE scan, not a second entry.** The probe now legitimately calls `Finding::` (the same-namespace value object it returns — which is why it still imports nothing and the no-`use` assertion still holds). Adding `Finding::` to the permitted statics alone would have widened the trust boundary to a file this test never reads, so every allow-listed collaborator now gets the SAME exec-primitive scan as the probe. `_ALLOWED_PROBE_STATICS` is compared by exact equality in BOTH directions, so a permission nothing uses fails too — a trust grant must not outlive its reason. `_PROBE_COLLABORATORS` is deliberately WIDER than the allow-list: `Severity` is never named in the probe, only inside `Finding`'s constructors, and a hop the scan skips is a hop nothing guards. **Stated bound: ONE HOP over a declared list, not a call-graph proof.**

**The design was caught being wrong by its own assertion, which is the argument for the exact-equality form.** The first cut of `_ALLOWED_PROBE_STATICS` included `Severity::` on the assumption the probe named it. It does not. The both-directions equality reddened immediately and the list was corrected to `{self::, Finding::}` with `Severity` moved to the collaborator scan where it belongs. A subset assertion would have accepted the wrong list silently.

**Decision (3) — `app/**` joins the workflow's path filter (a change to what the pipeline REJECTS; user-approved 2026-07-29).** `provision-tools-python.yml` filtered on `bin/*.py` + `examples/channel-servers/**`, while the tests it runs assert about `app/`. **No `app/`-only PR could ever run this job** — so the migration that invalidated the guard could not be caught by the guard, and the `push:` filter had the same gap, which is why `dev` stayed red unseen. This is the "[a green analyser says nothing about files outside its paths]" failure one layer up: a workflow path filter instead of an analyser's `paths:` key. A check that cannot run on the change that invalidates it is a decoration. The workflow file itself was also missing from its own `push:` filter (present on `pull_request:` only) and is added for symmetry. **Cost: this job runs on `app/` PRs — seconds — and that is the correct price.**

**Decision (4) — `CLAUDE.md` rule 5 stops ENUMERATING the CI workflows.** It named four; `bin/ python unit tests` was added later and never joined the list, so a reader following the rule literally self-merges over exactly this red — which is the decision this session actually faced. A named list of checks is a second copy of `.github/workflows/` and drifts the moment a workflow is added. The rule now says to read the workflow list from the Actions API for the head SHA rather than from memory.

**Sibling audit (canon #7), and it is an honest NEGATIVE.** The shape hunted was *an assertion about file A gated by a path filter that does not include A* — not a grep for `app/`, since the defect is a mismatch between what a test READS and what its workflow WATCHES and shares no search term. Only two workflows carry path filters at all: this one, and `channel-server-supply-chain.yml`, whose every step runs under `working-directory: examples/channel-servers` and reads nothing outside its own tree. `laravel-tests.yml`, `security.yml`, `pr-title-lint.yml`, `release-promote-cards.yml` and `auto-tag-version.yml` have no path filter, so a phpunit test reading `bin/` is always covered. `test_provision_board_tools*.py` make no repo-root-relative reads. One instance, now closed; no second.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) add `Finding::` to the permitted statics and stop — rejected: it goes green by widening trust to an unscanned file, which is the "don't loosen a constraint to make a failure go away" case, and `Finding` reaching `Severity` means the unscanned surface is two files, not one. (b) Repoint the call-site scan at `ChannelSnapshotCheck.php` by name — rejected: it fixes this instance and re-arms the identical trap for the next migration, and the whole finding is that a file-pinned guard is the defect. (c) Narrow the path filter to the specific `app/` files the tests read, rather than `app/**` — rejected: the call-site scan is deliberately repo-wide (any `app/` file could introduce a call site), so a narrow filter would re-create the exact blindness in a subtler form. (d) Delete the two tripwires as too fragile — rejected: they are the only assertions standing behind "the snapshot path cannot execute", and the one that failed did its job.

**Consequences:** `bin/test_check_channel_snapshot.py` (two tests rewritten, three module constants added), `.github/workflows/provision-tools-python.yml` (path filters), `CLAUDE.md` (rule 5). **Zero `app/` change, zero runtime change** — no migration, no `.env`, no token-scope change, nothing altered in what the receiver accepts or rejects. **CI now runs one more job on `app/` PRs**, which is the intended behavior change. 5 positive-control arms, each red on its own named test and each mutating the SUBJECT rather than the assertion — including one that recreates this card's own defect (the call site removed) and proves the rewritten guard now says so instead of passing empty. 47/47 `bin.test_check_channel_snapshot`, both other `bin/` modules green, `bin/check-doc-refs.php` clean.

## DL-247 — A golden fixture must PROVE it reaches its subject: a corpus compared only against itself cannot tell a measurement from a decoration

**Date:** 2026-07-29
**Context — three of the 33 `bridge:check` golden fixtures did not exercise the subject they were named for, by three unrelated mechanisms.** Found by MEASURING the rendered corpus rather than reading the builders (card#5552): 33 files, 30 distinct hashes. `board-tools-http-enabled` carried `channel.auth.token_path` with no `channel.url`, so `AgentConfig::load` threw, the agent was skipped, `$configs` was empty and the entire board-tools plane was unreachable — its two `Http::fake` stubs were never called. `writeback-board-unreadable` registered its 500 with a second `Http::fake()` AFTER `moveLegInstall()` had already registered a `'*'` catch-all; Laravel matches stub callbacks in registration order, first non-null wins, so the fixture captured the fully HEALTHY output and sat byte-identical to `writeback-move-leg-coord-config-unset`. `retention-last-pass-failed` set the retention marker in its builder and `PinnedHost::apply()` cleared it one step later — `apply()` necessarily runs AFTER the builder, because the builder is what tells it which pins to set — so it was byte-identical to `minimal` **from the single commit that created it**.

**The root cause is one missing invariant, not three mistakes (canon #7).** Three unrelated mechanisms converging on one symptom is a structural gap: **nothing asserted that a golden fixture MEASURES anything.** A golden file is captured once and thereafter only ever compared against ITSELF, so a fixture that never reached its install shape is indistinguishable from one that works — it silently pins some other, healthier output forever. The program already refuses a check that cannot fail and an empty result standing in for a measurement; it had never applied that bar to the FIXTURES those instruments run on, which is the layer everything else rests on. This is also why no earlier review pass caught it: there was nothing to notice.

**Decision (1) — each repair is scoped to its own subject, not to the largest change that goes green.** The board-tools bearer moves to `board_tools.auth.token_path` (a first-class shape the config's own error text recommends as the cure when there is no HTTP channel) rather than adding a `channel.url`: that keeps the fixture channel-free, makes it the http TWIN of the ssh fixtures — differing in the transport and nothing else — and leaves *"no golden fixture reaches a channel probe"* TRUE, which `GoldenChannelEnvironment`'s stage-5b reasoning still rests on. The writeback 500 passes THROUGH `moveLegInstall()` ahead of the defaults (the only ordering that works) and is scoped to the KANBAN board reads rather than blanketed over `'*'`: a blanket 500 also fails the github token probe, so the fixture would carry a second unrelated diagnosis and a later diff could not say which leg moved. The ambient-cache reset becomes `PinnedHost::resetAmbientState()`, called BEFORE the builder — the fixture is NOT made to re-set the marker afterwards, which would have hidden the ordering defect for the next fixture needing ambient state.

**Decision (2) — every fixture declares what its render must CONTAIN, and the declaration is mandatory.** `CheckGoldenTest::subjects()` maps each of the 33 fixtures to one or more substrings, asserted against the capture in the same data-provider run and deliberately AFTER the golden compare — including under `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`, where the compare returns early, so **a regen cannot mint a fixture that measures nothing.** A fixture named for two things declares both (`agent-missing-secret-and-token`, `agent-ci-failure-patterns-and-wake-membership`, `writeback-half-configured-triggers`), because a one-string subject lets the other half rot silently. The lookup is STRICT rather than `?? []`, so a missing declaration fails at the fixture itself and does not depend on `test_every_fixture_declares_a_subject` continuing to exist — a guard that silently asserts nothing when its declaration is absent is the very shape being removed.

**Decision (3) — an ABSENCE subject never stands alone.** Three fixtures exist to pin a leg printing NOTHING (`minimal-fpm-present`, `no-opt-in-probes-requested`, `event-consumer-nothing-arrived` — the card specified two; the fpm pair is the third, and its whole effect is the REMOVAL of a line). They declare that in `absentSubjects()` **in addition to** a positive subject, never instead: a notContains alone is satisfied by an empty capture, so silence would be assumed rather than asserted.

**Decision (4) — byte-identical golden files red unless declared, and the allow-list is asserted BOTH ways.** `CONTROL_PAIRS` holds the one legitimate duplicate (`no-opt-in-probes-requested` ≡ `minimal`, whose value is the DIFF against `probe-tools-with-no-enabled-agent`, not its own bytes). A declared pair that has quietly stopped being identical also fails — a stale pairing is a defect in the other direction, which keeps the list load-bearing instead of an escape hatch.

**Positive controls — 7 arms, every one RED as required, each mutating the SUBJECT rather than the assertion.** A guard for *"a check that cannot fail"* must not itself be one. A: a subject pointed at text the fixture cannot print. B: an absence-subject pointed at text the fixture does print. C: one fixture's bytes copied over another's. D: a fixture's declaration removed. **E1/E2/E3 re-introduce the three REAL defects and regenerate the golden files** — the exact scenario the guard exists for (a fixture silently stops reaching its subject and someone regenerates) — and each reds on its own named fixture. The tree was restored and verified clean after every arm, and the cleanliness check was itself positive-controlled.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — one instance, honest NEGATIVE on a second.** The shape hunted is *an artifact captured from the system and thereafter compared only against its own prior capture*. `tests/Fixtures/check-golden` is the only one in the repo; the remaining `tests/Fixtures` entries are hand-authored INPUTS (classifiers, `kanban-webhook-events.json`) and the other tests reading committed files assert about repo contents rather than about a stored capture of their own output. Adjacent but deliberately NOT swept in: a hand-authored fixture input that has stopped representing its subject is a different shape and no fixture-subject guard would see it.

**Two doc claims this falsifies, corrected in the same change.** `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` § Disproved claims gains **claim 8**: stage 2's `is_array($lastError)` mutation was cited among six that "each red the suite", which reads as evidence that the retention marker-PRESENT branch is covered — no fixture reached that branch at all, so the arm red on the marker-ABSENT rendering. **The coverage table's `observed` verdict is NOT affected** — `observed` is a distinguishability claim under the instrument's own negation and never a claim that a branch was reached. The stage-7b board-tools measurement is re-measured from the RENDERED corpus (six fixtures print a `board_tools` line, five of those lines belong to stage-7b code) with its ZERO-coverage list re-checked and unchanged: the repaired fixture carries a working bearer and a satisfied block, so it buys reaching the plane at all, not coverage of any leg past it.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) fix the three fixtures and stop — rejected, that is three instance fixes leaving the N+1th to re-mint the bug, and the whole finding is that nothing would say so. (b) Pairwise distinctness alone (~5 lines) — rejected as the whole answer: it catches instances 2 and 3 exactly, and is blind to instance 1, which was UNIQUE and still measured the wrong thing. Kept as a second, cheap guard because it catches a shape subjects cannot (two fixtures both reaching their subjects but rendering identically). (c) Give `board-tools-http-enabled` a real `channel.url` — rejected: it drags the fixture into the channel plane, couples it to the probe seam, and falsifies the stage-5b "no golden fixture reaches a probe" property for no gain in what the fixture is for. (d) A `mustNotContain` alone for the silent fixtures, as originally specified — rejected: an empty capture satisfies it.

**Consequences:** `tests/Feature/Console/Check/CheckGoldenTest.php`, `tests/Support/CheckGolden/PinnedHost.php`, three regenerated golden files, `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` (two new rules), `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`. **Zero `app/` change and zero runtime change** — no migration, no `.env`, no token-scope change, nothing altered in what the receiver accepts or rejects; `bridge:check`'s output for every unrepaired fixture is byte-identical. **The corpus baseline MOVES**, which is why this lands after stage 7 and before stage 8 rather than inside a stage PR: stages 4/5a/5b/5c/6/7a all refused a corpus change mid-migration for that reason. 1768/1768 phpunit, phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `bin/check-doc-refs.php` clean.

## DL-248 — A stage row is a hypothesis until the stage measures it: `bridge:check`'s registry is now ACCOUNTED FOR, not ">=1 finding per check"

**Date:** 2026-07-30
**Context — the DL-242 plan's stage-8 row specified an invariant that measurement falsified before any code was written.** The row read *"every registered check emits ≥1 finding"*. Instrumenting `CheckRunner` and re-running the whole suite plus all 33 golden fixtures gave, for `minimal` — the healthy baseline install that exits 0 in 11 output lines — **37 registered checks, of which 13 are NEVER INVOKED** (the writeback plane's 9 and the board-tools plane's 4; their slots sit behind conditional envelopes in `handle()`), **13 are invoked but silent**, **2 opt-in probes are never asked**, and **9 speak**. (**Corrected in the third pass below** — this first read *"15 are invoked but silent"*, a PRE-taxonomy count taken before the stage separated `NotRequested` from `Silent`, which folded the 2 un-requested probes into the silent population and called both *invoked*, which neither is. The four figures are now the four `CheckDisposition` cases.) Across the corpus **26 of 37 yield nothing on at least one run**, and **no fixture invokes all 37** (max 33, min 16, median 24). The instrument was positive-controlled: 47 distinct ids minus 10 `CheckRunnerTest` synthetic doubles = exactly 37, matching the registration list counted independently.

**Enforcing the row literally would have been a behavior change wearing a refactor's clothes.** It requires dissolving the conditional envelopes stages 3a and 7b deliberately preserved *as behavior* — running board-tools checks against an install with no `board_tools` block — and adding an `ok` line to 26 checks, taking a healthy run from 11 output lines to ≥37. That contradicts the row's own operator-visible column (*"disclaimer text changes; opt-in probes may gain lines"*), and a diagnostic printing 37 lines of mostly-`ok` prints nothing.

**This is the second time a stage-0-authored row has been falsified by the stage that built it** (the `6–7` row was the first, corrected at stage 6). The generalisable rule: **a stage row is a hypothesis, the measurement belongs before the code, and a falsified row gets corrected in the open rather than quietly built around.** Both corrections are now recorded in the plan.

**Decision (1) — the enforced invariant is ACCOUNTING, not emission.** *Every registered check is accounted for on every run that COMPLETES: it either ran (findings recorded, possibly none) or was deliberately skipped with a recorded reason.* The qualifier is the one `CheckRunner` imposes by deliberately not catching (stage 3a's preserved behavior): a check that throws aborts `bridge:check` before the inventory renders, so the operator gets no accounting rather than a partial one. Stated without it — as this entry and four code/doc sites first did — the property is pitched above what the code implements. `CheckDisposition` has four cases — `Reported`, `Silent`, `NotRequested`, `NotRun` — and they are deliberately **not** a `Severity`: severity answers *how bad is what this check found*, a disposition answers *did it get to look at all*. No new `Severity` case, so the exhaustive-`match` property and the exit contract are untouched by construction, as the resolved opt-in-probe decision required.

**Decision (2) — `NotRun` is DERIVED from the registration list, never declared by the caller.** Anything the run recorded no disposition for did not run; `CheckRunner::noteNotRun()` attaches only the human-readable reason. **The rejected alternative — the caller declaring each skip — would have made the mechanism's correctness depend on remembering to call it, which is the same shape as the bug it closes.** A forgotten reason therefore degrades a message (disclosed at runtime, listed by `CheckInventory::unexplainedNotRun()`); it cannot open a hole. This is also what makes it safe for `CheckCommand` to note the three per-agent slots' reasons unconditionally after the loop: a reason for a check that DID run is inert, and that inertness is asserted.

**Decision (3) — `not requested` is DECLARED via `OptInCheck::wasRequested()`, never inferred from an empty yield.** A check that looked and found nothing and a check nobody asked to look are different facts and only one says anything about the install; inferring the disposition would be exactly the collapse the resolved decision refuses. **The axis is the flag's ABSENCE only** — a requested probe with nothing to certify still owes an answer and keeps its `warn`. Two golden-fixture comments predicted otherwise and **conflated the two axes**; both are corrected here. The control pair got sharper instead: passing `--probe-tools` makes that probe run, so the fixture reports one opt-in probe not requested where its control reports two.

**Decision (4) — the inventory line ALWAYS prints, and the `unvalidated` tally SURVIVES narrowed.** A coverage statement an operator gets only sometimes is one they cannot rely on. The tally is not deleted as redundant because it answers a *different* question that stage 8 did **not** settle: severity assignment is still imprecise (a leg that could not measure may report `warn`), which is card#5291's separately-gated sweep. Conflating those two claims is precisely what the old *"floor, not an inventory"* wording did. **[DL-251 LANDED THAT SWEEP AND THE TALLY SURVIVES A SECOND NARROWING rather than being deleted — the same call for a different reason. What it discloses now is that the rule the vocabulary follows is keyed on what a leg CONCLUDED, so a leg that never noticed it measured nothing is not counted there — and is not reliably silent either: it may say nothing, or say what it would have concluded (card#5698).]**

**What the inventory deliberately does NOT claim,** stated because a coverage claim pitched above its evidence is this program's recurring defect (DL-243): it accounts for the **registered set** and cannot see a leg nobody wrote as a check; a not-run **reason** is the **envelope's** claim about itself, so a wrong envelope condition makes the reason confidently wrong; the counts are keyed by **check id**, so a per-agent check that ran for two of three agents counts once as having run with nothing scoping it to the agents it reached; and a `Silent` disposition is **not yet distinguishable** from a check falling off the end of its generator by accident. **The not-run population is labelled `N did not run`, corrected in place from the `N not applicable here` this entry's stage first shipped:** five of the recorded reasons are COULD-NOT-LOOK rather than does-not-apply (a malformed agent YAML, an unloadable `writeback.json`), so the stronger label was a false claim on exactly the installs that most need the line — and the parenthetical carries the cause either way. Making a check *declare* its silence is a strictly-additive strengthening, deferred as **card#5596** — legitimately, because stage 8 makes the silence visible and counted rather than absent; had stage 8 left silence unaccounted it would not have been deferrable, and the card records that.

**Positive controls — the plan demanded one and it needed TWO,** because measurement showed the un-invoked slot is the larger population. `CheckInventoryTest` carries both (a deliberately non-emitting check; a registered slot deliberately never invoked). **Five single-arm mutations** — one mutation, one named test, a restore and a `cmp` between each, so every proof is individually attributable rather than attributable-as-a-batch — each RED as required: `NotRun` not derived, a silent check recording nothing, `NotRequested` collapsed onto `Silent`, `Reported` unable to upgrade a `Silent`, last-reason-wins. The corpus-wide conservation assertion was separately controlled by corrupting one golden file's arithmetic. **phpstan's green was controlled on the new files specifically** (a deliberate `strlen(array)`, observed red, restored byte-identical) rather than assumed from `app/Bridge` being in `paths` — the DL-246 trap.

**The arithmetic is the operator-facing line's own control:** the dispositions sum to the registered total, asserted across all 33 committed golden files rather than spot-checked, because a disposition leaking on one install shape only would survive a per-fixture check.

**Measurement note worth carrying forward: `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` and an asserting run report DIFFERENT assertion counts, and the gap is the proof the regen skipped the compare.** **CORRECTED — the numbers first recorded here (regen 107 / asserting 140) were FALSE, and were "derived from source" rather than observed, which is how they got that way.** The derivation omitted `assertFixtureReachesItsSubject()` (added by DL-247, and it runs under `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` too, so the regen figure shared the falsified premise) and this stage's own `test_every_golden_file_carries_a_self_conserving_inventory_line`. **OBSERVED**, on `vendor/bin/phpunit tests/Feature/Console/Check/CheckGoldenTest.php`, 43 tests either way: **asserting 466** (`UPDATE_GOLDEN` unset, on the branch) and **regen 433** (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` on a throwaway copy of the repo outside the branch — a regen rewrites tracked fixtures — with the branch's fixtures confirmed untouched afterwards). The gap is **33**: one fixture's `assertFileExists` + `assertSame` pair collapsing to the regen path's single `assertTrue(true)` sentinel, times 33 fixtures. The DEVICE is sound and is kept; **an arithmetic derivation is not a measurement**, which is the same lesson as this program's disproved-claims section one level down.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — the stale-claim family was larger than the files changed.** The claim *"stage 8 turns this into a returned disposition"* appeared in **17 inline comments across 15 check classes** plus 6 docblocks; three docblocks asserted a ">=1-finding invariant" that does not exist. All corrected. **A uniform grep found 12 of the 17 and would have read as complete** — five carried a preamble (`// no absolute secret dir ⇒ …; stage 8 turns this into…`) and needed a second pass. The moratorium in DL-242 (*"no new `bridge:check` leg until Stage 8 lands"*) is **LIFTED**; a new leg is now a registered `Check` whose id must join `CheckCommandRegistrationTest`'s pinned list in the same commit.

**Closes the plan's disproved-claims item 7** (*"nothing pins which checks `CheckCommand` registers"*): `CheckCommandRegistrationTest` asserts the exact id set in registration order against the command's own builder — reached by reflection rather than rebuilt, so the test cannot agree with a copy of itself. `CheckCommand::registry()` was extracted for that, and stays a private method precisely because the fuller `CheckContext`-as-builder restructure belongs to the final stage making it deliberately.

**Alternatives considered:** (a) the literal row — rejected above. (b) Inventory internally and keep the operator surface silent — rejected: it satisfies the invariant while leaving the operator exactly where they started, and is *strictly worse than the status quo*, because today's disclaimer at least warns that the tally is a floor and this deletes it giving nothing back. (c) A new `Severity::NotRequested` — rejected by the resolved decision (dilutes `unvalidated`'s one precise job, and touches the exit contract). (d) A new `CheckRegistrations` class instead of a private method — deferred to the final stage for the reason above.

**Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Check/{CheckDisposition,OptInCheck,CheckInventory}.php` (new), `CheckRunner`, `Check`, `PerAgentCheck`, `CheckResult`, both opt-in probe checks, 15 check classes' comments, `CheckCommand`, `tests/Unit/Bridge/Check/CheckInventoryTest.php` + `tests/Unit/Console/CheckCommandRegistrationTest.php` (new), `CheckGoldenTest` (3 tests), `BridgeCommandsTest` (one premise), all 33 golden files (+1 line each; 35 insertions / 2 deletions, fully accounted), `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. **OPERATOR-VISIBLE — this is the gate stage, and the gate was granted.** Every run gains one inventory line and the `unvalidated` tally is reworded. **No migration, no new `.env`, no token-scope change, and no change to what the receiver accepts or rejects; exit codes are untouched by construction** (only `fail` flips the exit, and no disposition emits a finding). **Stages 9 and 10 remain HARD GATE.**

**Correction pass, same stage and same branch — every finding was one class: a claim pitched above the evidence supporting it.** The not-run label weakened to `did not run` (above); a `! is_readable($configDir)` arm added to the per-agent skip reason, because a dir that exists but cannot be read passes `is_dir()`, globs empty, and made the line assert *"this install has no agent config files"* about an install that may hold a dozen (reproduced before fixing); the two writeback not-run reasons re-pitched at their ENVELOPE's strength rather than at one thrower inside it, which otherwise contradicts the warn printed beside them; the `notRunReasons()` order docblock corrected to registration order (the code walks the registration-ordered disposition map, not a record-order list); the per-agent granularity bound added to all three *does-not-claim* lists; and the inventory line's composition extracted to a pure private seam — the one stage 9 splits anyway — so `tests/Unit/Console/CheckInventoryLineTest.php` can witness every arm. **That last one closes an absence assertion with no presence witness:** the only statement about the `bridge:check internal:` disclosure was `assertStringNotContainsString(...)` on one fixture, so deleting the whole block or changing its text **reds nothing** — and the corpus renders neither zero-arm nor the reasonless not-run arm at all. Eleven single-arm mutations (one mutation, a run, a restore, a `cmp` between each) each RED the test named for that arm; the ones that alter the whole line also RED the two exact-string tests, which is the intended overlap, not a smear. Golden fixtures regenerated: 33 files, 33 insertions / 33 deletions, one inventory line each.

**Re-verification pass, same stage and same branch — re-running this stage's mutations against the WHOLE suite found TWO that SURVIVE, and the shape they share is the entry's real lesson.** Both are observed green with the guarded code deleted (**1798/1798, 4688 assertions — identical to the unmutated baseline**), and the run has to be the whole suite for that to mean anything: a run scoped to the tests written for the mutated code answers a question nobody asked, since those are the tests that cannot be absent. **(1) CORRECTED IN PLACE — the seam above first shipped as TWO methods (`inventoryLine()`, `inventoryInternalDefectLine()`), and testing them left the CALL SITE unproven:** every one of the eleven proofs above mutates one of those two renderers and none mutates the call site, so the set was exhaustive over what was already covered and silent about the one thing that was not — replacing `emitInventory()`'s call to the disclosure renderer with `null` deletes it from every operator's output and reds nothing. **Extracting a pure method and testing it exhaustively proves the COMPOSITION and says nothing about whether anything still CALLS it** — a seam closes a gap only if the DECISION TO EMIT lives inside the tested surface. The two are now one `inventoryOutput()` returning `[channel, message]` pairs, with `emitInventory()` a dispatch loop over it; every case ported, plus two asserting the disclosure is included on the `warn` channel when a not-run check is unexplained and absent otherwise. **(2) The `! is_readable($configDir)` arm was REPRODUCED before fixing but never ASSERTED after** — deleting it restores the confidently-false *"this install has no agent config files"* claim, with the suite green. Shipping a fix with nothing asserting it re-mints the class one layer down; a check that cannot fail is a decoration. It now carries a feature test that constructs the state (`chmod 0000`), asserts the three facts the arm rests on, guards the precondition with a skip for a root runner rather than assuming a non-root one, and restores the mode in `tearDown`. Each fix's own proof was re-run as mutation → FULL suite → named failing test → restore → `cmp`, and each RED. **The residual is stated rather than rounded up:** the `warn` channel's DISPATCH is proven at the seam only — ~~the corpus exercises the `line` channel on all 33 fixtures and the `warn` channel on none~~ **[FALSE — corrected in the third pass below: `GoldenCapture` reads an UNDECORATED buffer, so the corpus exercises NEITHER channel]** — and no install shape can reach it, since every conditional slot in `handle()` records a not-run reason by design. Both survivors were found by re-running the mutation set against the full suite rather than by reading the test file — the same device that found the `ran()` locus gap, now twice in one stage.

**Third pass, same stage and same branch — the pattern is now the entry's subject, not an incident in it: every finding in all three passes is one class, a claim pitched above its evidence, and this pass found the class in the SENTENCE THAT DISCLOSED THE PREVIOUS RESIDUAL.** Four findings, two of them un-witnessed code. **(1) The residual above was NARROWER THAN THE TRUTH.** `GoldenCapture` reads `Artisan::output()`, an undecorated `BufferedOutput`: the formatter strips `<warning>`/`<error>`/`<info>` to bare text, so `line()`, `warn()`, `error()` and `info()` write byte-identical output there. The corpus does not exercise the `line` channel — it is blind to the channel axis entirely. **Observed:** mutating the inventory head's `'line' => $this->line(...)` to `warn(...)` leaves all 33 golden files unchanged and renders a yellow warning on every healthy operator run. A residual stated narrower than the truth is worse than one left unstated, because it reads as a measured bound — and this one had been copied to four sites before the read that falsified it. **The sibling was one method away** (canon #7, audited on the SHAPE): `emitFinding()`'s severity→channel `match` sits behind the same undecorated capture, so its `fail`/`warn`/`ok` render arms were equally invisible (the RETURN arm is witnessed by exit codes, the `unvalidated` arm by the tally line two fixtures render). **Closed for both by ONE instrument rather than per-site** — `CheckOutputChannelTest` drives each dispatch through a DECORATED buffer and asserts the ANSI attribute's presence/absence and that the channels are DISTINCT, never the colour name, so an upstream scheme change moves a colour while a channel collapsing into another still reds. **(2) The `$agentNames === []` arm of the per-agent skip `match` had no presence witness** — the canon-#7 sibling of the `! is_readable` arm the second pass added, and missed because that pass fixed the instance and did not audit the shape. Arms 3 and 4 are BOTH true on a config dir that exists, is readable, and holds no `*.yml`; arm 3 wins by POSITION alone, so deleting or reordering it tells a FRESH INSTALL — `bridge:check`'s primary first-run audience — *"no agent config parsed (see the errors above)"* on an exit-0 run with no errors above, suite green. Closed by a feature test that constructs the state and pins the three facts the arm rests on. **(3) The `unvalidated` tally counted FINDINGS and said `check(s)`.** `emitUnvalidated()` increments per finding and a per-agent check yields one per agent, so a two-agent install with no `channel.server_path` prints *"2 check(s)"* directly beneath an id-keyed inventory line that counts that same check ONCE. Now `finding(s)`; two golden fixtures regenerated. **(4) *"15 more run and report nothing"* was a PRE-TAXONOMY count, in SEVEN sites** — and the count of sites is itself a finding: a first grep over the paths the review named returned four, and the two that a repo-wide grep added (`CLAUDE.md`'s subfile-index row and this entry's own measurement paragraph) are the two furthest from the code, which is where a restated number rots unread. A clean grep is not a clean audit when the grep's PATH LIST came from the report rather than from the repo — it folded the 2 un-requested opt-in probes into the silent population, so nothing reconciled it with the `13 with nothing to report · 2 opt-in probes not requested` the stage shipped.
