## DL-263 — A file this process cannot READ is not a file that is absent: the `is_file()`-gated read is hoisted to one primitive and the third state reaches every caller

**Card:** #5789 · **PR:** #463

**Context.** DL-262 fixed ONE member of a class and filed the rest. The shape is `if (! is_file($path)) { return <benign>; }` followed by an unguarded read: on a file that is PRESENT and unreadable, the benign early-return never fires (`is_file()` is TRUE) and the read's warning becomes an uncaught `ErrorException` — an outcome none of the sites documented and three were explicitly designed NOT to produce.

**The audit found FIVE, not the four on the card, and how the fifth was found is the point.** `BridgePaths::readJsonl` uses `file()` rather than `file_get_contents()`, so the grep that produced the card's list could not have surfaced it — it came from re-reading the subsystem (canon #7: a clean grep is not a clean audit). It is also the worst member: it backs the inbox itself, so the degraded answer is *"no intents staged"* for a file the process cannot see into. Its `?: []` fallback was **already dead code** under the console and HTTP kernels, where the warning becomes an exception before the fallback is reached; it ran only under a logging-only handler. DL-262's sibling-audit paragraph is corrected in place to say five.

**Measured, not inferred**, under the console kernel's bootstrap (`tinker` remains an invalid harness here, DL-262): `BridgePaths::readSeen`, `AgentRegistry::loadSharedIdentities`, `WritebackConfig::load` and `BridgePaths::readJsonl` each THREW `ErrorException`; `bridge:provision --reconcile` against an unreadable secret printed `[prod-agent] kanban:5 API error: file_get_contents(…): Failed to open stream: Permission denied`.

**Decision — one primitive, and the discrimination is hoisted rather than re-derived.** New `App\Bridge\Support\FileContents::read($path, $subject)`: bytes when present, `null` when absent, `UnreadableFileException` when present-but-unreadable. `TokenFile::readTrimmed` — which owned the only correct copy — now layers trimming and the secret subtype ON it instead of holding a second implementation. **`UnreadableSecretException` is retained as a SUBCLASS rather than collapsed into the base**, because six callers catch it to map a secret fault onto their own surface (a 401, a `ConfigException`, an `unvalidated` finding) and those catches must not silently widen now that non-secret readers throw too. The subclass also means zero edits at those six sites and their tests — the wider rename was considered and rejected as a larger diff whose only benefit was deleting a type that costs nothing.

**Per-site disposition turns on ONE question — what does the caller's benign answer CLAIM?** Four propagate and one degrades, and the split is not a matter of taste:
- `BridgePaths::readSeen` and `readJsonl` **propagate.** Fail-soft is strictly worse, not merely less tidy: `bridge:inbox` filters on both, so `[]` re-surfaces every already-seen intent (or hides the whole inbox), and `updateSeenLocked` then opens the same file `c+` and throws regardless — a duplicate inbox followed by a crash. Aborting is the outcome these paths ALREADY had; only the diagnosis is new.
- `WritebackConfig::load` **raises `ConfigException`.** `null` means *"writeback is off"*; answering it for a permissions fault would silently disable every card move on the receiver's dispatch path. Outcome unchanged (it already threw), type and message honest.
- `AgentRegistry::loadSharedIdentities` **degrades to `[]` with a warning** — the one exception, and its own documentation is the authority: its other caller is the receiver, which must not 5xx over an optional policy file. **This makes existing docs TRUE rather than requiring a doc edit:** `SharedIdentitiesCheck`'s docblock, DL-259, and `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest`'s comment all already stated that this loader answers `[]` for a file it could not read. It did not. Now it does.
- `WebhookProvisioner` reuses `TokenFile::readTrimmed` (the `ChannelToken` shape — its own perms gate already ran) and maps the throw to `cannot_reconcile`.

**A pre-existing defect found in passing and fixed with it (canon #16).** `ProvisionResult::cannotReconcile($kind, $secretPath)` hardcoded `"{$kind} (secret missing at {$secretPath})"` — but one of its two existing callers already passed a full perms message, so a present, `0644` secret was being reported as **missing**. The parameter is now a `$reason` rendered verbatim; adding a third cause to a template that asserts absence for all of them would have compounded a wrong-but-specific cause (canon #10).

**⚠ AN `@`-SUPPRESSION SWEEP WAS THE REJECTED FIX and the card recorded it as such.** Silencing each warning converts every one of these into the "absent" answer — card#5698's defect minted five more times. The suppression is load-bearing ONLY inside the primitive, where the throw on the next line re-raises the state as a type; the class docblock says so, because that is the line a future caller would copy.

**Tests — every new assertion was watched go RED against the un-fixed code.** The control reconstructs the pre-fix tree by stashing only the tracked `app/` changes: 5 reds, each for the right reason — four raw `ErrorException`s naming `Failed to open stream: Permission denied`, and the provisioner test failing on the literal pre-fix output `API error: file_get_contents(…)`. Every unreadable-state test carries a **skip-if-still-readable** guard (root reads through mode 0000; a test that cannot fail must not report as a pass), and each propagating site has a discriminating control asserting the outcome directly rather than only the exception type, so no arm can be satisfied by collapsing it onto another.

**A test-harness trap worth recording, because it cost a false red.** Laravel's `expectsOutputToContain` registers a Mockery `doWrite` expectation per substring, and **Mockery dispatches each call to the FIRST expectation whose matcher passes** — so two substrings of ONE rendered line cannot both be satisfied (the later reports as missing), and a `doesntExpectOutputToContain` registered after them never sees a line an earlier matcher consumed, i.e. it silently cannot fail. The provisioner assertions run against captured `Artisan::output()` instead.

**Consequences.** New `app/Bridge/Support/FileContents.php` + `app/Bridge/Exceptions/UnreadableFileException.php`; `UnreadableSecretException` now extends it; five call sites migrated; `ProvisionResult::cannotReconcile`'s message template corrected. **No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, no exit-code change in the fixed direction** — the four propagating paths already aborted, and the one that degrades can only turn a 5xx into a served request. `--format=json` `schema` stays **1**.

## DL-264 — A directory this process cannot STAT is not a directory it certified: the shared permission verdict gates its own stat, and the filed mechanism was wrong

**Card:** #5774 · **PR:** #464

**Context.** `DirectoryPermissions::warnIfInsecure()` is the one group/world-accessible verdict (DL-014) behind both install dir checks. It ran `clearstatcache(); $perms = fileperms($dir);` with nothing in between, and treated a `false` return as indistinguishable from a clean mode. `InstallSecretDirCheck` never existence-checks its directory — its guard is only `is_string() && str_starts_with('/')` — so a `BRIDGE_SECRET_DIR` pointing at an absent or unseeable path reaches that stat. **[card#6025:** there is no `DirectoryPermissions::warnIfInsecure()` in the tree today — the entry records the code as it stood.**]**

**⚠ THE MECHANISM ON THE CARD WAS WRONG, AND THE FIX THE CARD SPECIFIED WOULD HAVE BEEN DEAD CODE.** The card (filed by the DL-259 audit) predicted a SILENT false-clean: a green `secret dir: /nope` line followed by silence from the perms leg, "both halves read as certified." The `?Finding` return makes that reading look obviously right. **It is not what happens.** `fileperms()` on an unstattable path RAISES `E_WARNING`; it does not return `false`. Under Laravel's error handler that becomes an uncaught `ErrorException`, so the real pre-fix behaviour is that **`bridge:check` ABORTS** — stack trace, exit 1, and **no report rendered for any subsystem**, not just this leg. Measured on the real command, not inferred:

```
$ BRIDGE_CONFIG_DIR=$T/cfg BRIDGE_SECRET_DIR=$T/nope php artisan bridge:check
   ErrorException
  fileperms(): stat failed for /tmp/…/nope
  at app/Bridge/Check/DirectoryPermissions.php:32
```

The card's prescribed fix — an arm on `$perms === false` — is **unreachable**: control never returns from that line. Written as specified it would have passed review, passed CI, changed nothing, and left the abort in place. This is the same class DL-262/DL-263 closed for the READ family (`file_get_contents` on a present-but-unreadable file), now found in the STAT family; the card's own filing predates that pair's finding that the degraded outcome is a THROW, not a false answer.

**Decision — gate before the stat, and split the failure by cause.** `file_exists()` (silent on an unstattable path, verified) gates the stat. When it is false the two causes get different findings, because they ask the operator for different actions: an untraversable ancestor is `PathVisibility::unverifiedUnlessVisible()` → **`unvalidated`** (the leg could not ANSWER — `Severity` limb 2); a traversable ancestor makes the negative stat conclusive → **`warn`** naming the directory as absent. Neither flips the exit code this primitive has never flipped, so the DL-014 warn-not-fail posture is preserved (an absent dir cannot be chmod'd either, and the DL-010 point-of-use gate is fail-closed over it exactly as over a loose mode).

**Fixed at the primitive, not at the one reachable caller.** `InstallConfigDirCheck` cannot reach the gate (its own `is_dir()` runs first, barring a race), so the arms are live via one caller today — but the false return value is the primitive's, and a third caller would inherit the raise. That is how this class keeps being re-minted (card#5698, DL-262, DL-263).

**⚠ `file_exists()` IS THE GATE, NOT `is_dir()`, and the difference is a deliberate refusal to widen scope.** A `secret_dir` pointing at a REGULAR FILE stats fine and still reports that file's mode through the warn — the wrong subject, but pre-existing and LOUD rather than silent. `is_dir()` would have quietly reclassified it as *"does not exist"*, which is a new false claim, in exactly the class this fix belongs to. Left byte-identical and tracked as **card#5796**, which records the rejected `is_dir()` gate as the reason. **[Superseded by DL-265, which closes the wrong-subject report with a NESTED `is_dir()` arm rather than the gate swap rejected here — the rejection above still stands.]**

**Sibling audit (canon #7), by reading each site rather than trusting the grep.** Every stat-family call in `app/` — `fileperms`, `filetype`, `readlink` — was checked for a pre-gate: `ChannelSnapshotProbe::resolveNonStrict` (gated by `is_link`), `ChannelToken` (behind `is_file && is_readable`), `SocketEndpoint` (behind an early throw on `! file_exists && ! is_link`), `ChannelTransportCheck` (behind `file_exists` in the same short-circuiting `&&`), and `SecretFile` ×2 (`@`-suppressed — confirmed under the console kernel to return `false` without throwing). **`DirectoryPermissions` was the only unguarded one.**

**Tests — watched RED against the un-fixed code**, reconstructed by stashing only the tracked `app/` changes. Both new assertions errored, and the error is itself the evidence for the paragraph above: `fileperms(): stat failed for …`, not an assertion failure about a missing finding. The unseeable-path case carries the skip-if-still-readable guard (root reads through mode 0000). The absent and unseeable arms are each other's control: the point is that an identically-failed stat must NOT be reported as the measured fact "does not exist" when the cause is this process's own blindness.

**A duplication found in passing and consolidated rather than extended (canon #5/#7).** The skip-if-root helper these tests need existed as **six** private copies, in two wordings ("directory" vs "file" permission checks) already diverging for no stated reason. Adding a seventh was the alternative. It is now `Tests\Support\SkipsAsRoot` — a **trait, not a method on `Tests\TestCase`**, because `ChannelSnapshotProbeTest` extends PHPUnit's base directly and a method on the Laravel base would have left exactly one file holding a private copy.

**Consequences.** `bridge:check` completes and renders its full report on an install where it previously aborted; the secret-dir leg reports `warn` (absent) or `unvalidated` (unseeable) instead of taking the command down. **No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.** The exit code changes only in that a run which previously died at exit 1 with no output now exits on the merits of its findings. `--format=json` `schema` stays **1** (`unvalidated` and `warn` are existing severities at an existing check id). `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest`'s pinned adopter set gains `DirectoryPermissions.php`; `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` is unmoved (the construction stays inside `PathVisibility`).

## DL-265 — A path that is not a directory is not a directory with bad permissions: the shared permission verdict names the fault instead of reporting a mode for the wrong subject

**Card:** #5796 · **PR:** #465

**Context.** DL-264 gated `DirectoryPermissions`'s stat on `file_exists()`, which is true for a regular file, a socket, a fifo — anything that stats. So `BRIDGE_SECRET_DIR` pointing at a regular file reached `fileperms()`, succeeded, and rendered that file's real mode under the secret dir's label. Measured on the real command before any code was written:

```
$ BRIDGE_CONFIG_DIR=$T/cfg BRIDGE_SECRET_DIR=/etc/passwd php artisan bridge:check
   secret dir: /etc/passwd
   secret dir /etc/passwd is group/world-accessible (mode 0644) — chmod 700 (it holds secrets)
   EXIT=0
```

**The mode is real and the subject is wrong**, which is worse than it looks: the remedy the line gives would be actively harmful if followed (`chmod 700 /etc/passwd`), and the operator's actual fault — *this setting does not point at a directory* — is never named. **This card's filed mechanism was accurate**, unlike DL-264's; it was still re-verified against the running command first, because DL-264 is the standing reason not to trust a filed mechanism.

**Decision — a `! is_dir()` arm NESTED INSIDE the existence gate.** Not a replacement of the outer gate: `is_dir()` alone answers false for an absent path AND for a present non-directory, so promoting it to the outer gate would report a regular file as *"does not exist"* — a new false claim in the class DL-262/263/264 exist to close, which is precisely why DL-264 rejected it and left the wrong-subject report standing. Nesting is what makes the third state expressible without that trade: absent (or unseeable) is answered above, non-directory below. Inside the gate `is_dir()` is conclusive — the stat already succeeded, so a false answer is the file type and never an unreadable ancestor.

**⚠ Severity is `fail`, and this is the primitive's first — it flips the exit code where the run previously exited 0.** The card filed severity as genuinely open rather than assuming the primitive's warn-only posture, and the posture does not carry: **DL-014's warn-not-fail rationale is about a loose MODE**, where the bridge still works and is merely less safe, so operator-owned perms can stay advisory with the DL-010 point-of-use gate as the hard backstop. A path that is not a directory is not a weaker version of that state. Every secret and token resolves *underneath* it (`<dir>/<provider>/…` — `SecretPath` / `TokenPath`), so not one can be opened and no inbound webhook can be verified (`VerifyHmacSignature` reaches `unknown_scope` 401 for every delivery). That is `Severity` limb 1 — the leg answered its question and the answer is a fault proven about THIS install — which is the same ground `InstallConfigDirCheck` stands on when it calls its own unusable-dir state a `fail`, and the same call `ChannelSnapshotProbe` already makes for a `channel.server_path` that names a file rather than a directory. **No healthy install newly reds:** the only state that flips is one that already rejects every webhook.

**Renamed `warnIfInsecure()` → `verdictFor()`.** The old name had already stopped being true when DL-264 gave the method an `unvalidated` arm; a `fail` behind a name promising a warn is a trap for exactly the third caller the primitive's own docblock exists to protect. Two call sites, and the class docblock already called this "the shared permission verdict," so the name was available.

**Sibling audit (canon #7), by reading each site.** The shape is *acting on a path whose type was never established*. Every `file_exists()` in `app/` was read: `SocketEndpoint` asserts `filetype($path) !== 'socket'` and throws; `ChannelTransportCheck` requires `filetype($socket) === 'socket'` and says why in a comment; `ChannelSnapshotProbe` already splits not-a-directory from a dangling symlink and **fails** on the former. Every `is_file()`-gated read (`SecretFile`, `ChannelToken`, `AgentApiTokenCheck`, `WritebackTokenCheck`, `AgentWebhookSecretCheck`, `FileContents`) is type-correct by construction. **`DirectoryPermissions` was the only site that acted on a path without establishing its type** — consistent with DL-264 finding it the only unguarded stat.

**A doc-defect class found in passing and closed (canon #16).** DL-261 through DL-264 all carried `**PR:** #TBD` — the placeholder was never resolved after each merged. Corrected to #461/#462/#463/#464 from the merge commits. The DL-264 CHANGELOG entry's claim that the wrong-subject warn is deliberate was accurate when written and is stale as of this entry; both ship in the same release, so it now points forward to this one rather than contradicting it.

**Tests — watched RED against the un-fixed code.** The new case asserted `Warn` where `Fail` was expected before the arm existed. It asserts the exact message AND that the message does **not** contain `group/world-accessible`: a message naming the right fault would still be wrong if it kept reporting a mode for a subject that has none worth reporting, and only the negative assertion catches that. It lives on `InstallSecretDirCheckTest` for the reason that file already documents — this is the only caller that reaches the primitive without an `is_dir()` of its own.

**Consequences.** A `secret_dir` that exists and is not a directory now **fails** `bridge:check` naming the real fault, instead of exiting 0 with a mode for the wrong subject and harmful advice. **No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change.** `--format=json` `schema` stays **1** (`fail` is an existing severity at an existing check id). `PathVisibilityAdoptionTest` and `UnvalidatedCallSiteTest` are both unmoved — the arm constructs neither a `PathVisibility` call nor an `unvalidated`.

## DL-266 — A check must DECLARE its silence: the deliberate empty yield stops being inferred and becomes a `Silence` yielded on the path that produced it

**Card:** #5596 · **PR:** #467

**Context.** DL-242 stage 8 made a check's silence **visible and counted** — `CheckDisposition::Silent`, with the whole registry accounted for on every completing run. It could not say what that silence MEANT. Two different things produced the identical row: a check that looked and correctly had nothing to report, and a check falling off the end of its generator through a path its author did not intend. The stage disclosed that bound as open in `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` and filed it as card#5596, recording the deferral's reasoning so it would not later read as arbitrary. This is that landing.

**Decision — the declaration is YIELDED at the path, and the card's own recommended shape was rejected.** A check declares a deliberate silence by yielding `App\Bridge\Check\Silence::because('<reason>')`. `CheckRunner::materialize()` is the ONLY place it is stripped, so no renderer can be handed one to print; an execution that yields neither a finding nor a declaration is named in `CheckInventory::undeclaredSilent()`. Same direction as the not-run accounting — the runner trusts a DECLARATION and never an inference from an empty yield — for the same reason `OptInCheck` exists.

**Rejected: a second contract method (the card's recommendation), by analogy with `OptInCheck::wasRequested()`.** The analogy breaks exactly where it matters. `wasRequested()` answers about the INVOCATION and is a constructor-time fact, correct however many times `run()` is called; *"was this silence deliberate"* is a fact about the EXIT PATH of ONE execution. A method consulted after the fact would need the check to record which path it took — **per-execution mutable state on an object `PerAgentCheck::runFor()` re-invokes once per agent** — making correctness depend on every check resetting that state per call. That is the shape stage 8 rejected for the not-run accounting, in its own words: it *"would have made the mechanism's correctness depend on remembering to call it, which is the same shape as the bug it closes"*.

**Rejected: a `return;`-keyed static analyser (the card's third option).** Structurally blind. The commonest silent path in this registry has no `return` at all — a `foreach` over a collection that is empty, of which `AgentIdentityCollisionsCheck` is the plain case — so an analyser keyed on `return` sites cannot see the majority of the population. Same blindness DL-251's sweep had when it keyed on the sites that REPORT.

**The idiom is a TRAILING UNCONDITIONAL yield, and that is what makes the tripwire survive.** A declaration does not assert *"I am silent"* — the check cannot know that while running — it states what the silence WOULD mean, so the runner IGNORES it when findings were also yielded. Two placement rules: one immediately before each explicit early `return;` (reasons differ per path; a single trailing one would launder them into one sentence), plus one for the fall-through. **An early `return;` added later sits BEFORE the trailing declaration, so it skips it and the execution is recorded undeclared** — a new silent path cannot inherit an old path's judgement. A check with no zero-finding path at all needs neither, and adding one would claim a state it cannot reach.

**The reason is a required constructor argument and is rendered nowhere, and both halves are deliberate.** Nothing prints it — the change is output-neutral by requirement, and it is read by the maintainer at the call site. It is an argument rather than a comment because that is what makes a blind sweep visible in review: `Silence::because('…')` cannot be inserted across 37 files without someone writing 37 sentences, which is the per-site judgement the card exists to force. An empty or whitespace-only reason throws, mirroring `CheckRunner::register()`'s empty-id guard.

**`undeclaredSilent()` is recorded per EXECUTION, and that CLOSES the per-agent granularity bound rather than disclosing it.** It is the one accessor on `CheckInventory` that is not a fold over `$dispositions`. A per-agent check that reports for agent A and is undeclared-silent for agent B ends the run `Reported`, so the `unexplainedNotRun()` shape — filter `disposition === Silent` — would have hidden exactly the execution that went unjudged. It remains a list of check **ids**: an id appears at most once however many of its executions were undeclared, because it names the unjudged path and not the size of the roster.

**No new `CheckDisposition` case and no new `Severity`.** Declaredness rides ALONGSIDE the disposition exactly as `notRunReasons` rides alongside `NotRun`. `--format=json`'s four `disposition` values, the exhaustive `match` and the exit contract are untouched **by construction**, not by inspection.

**⚠ THE ONE DEVIATION FROM THE CARD'S BYTE-NEUTRALITY CLAUSE, taken deliberately: `inventory.undeclared_silent` is added to `--format=json`.** `unexplained_not_run` is already there, and a machine consumer blind to an internal defect the text consumer can see is this program's own recurring defect re-minted at the new surface — the same argument stage 9 made for putting the fail-soft envelopes' findings in the document. Per `docs/check-json-contract.md` §2 an ADDED key does not bump `schema`, which stays **1** on the added-key row alone.

**A second `bridge:check internal:` warn, and unlike the first one it IS reachable on a real install.** The stale `emitInventory()` docblock claiming *"NO INSTALL SHAPE CAN REACH IT"* of the `warn` channel was corrected in the same change: true of the not-run half (every conditional slot in `handle()` records a reason by design, so `unexplainedNotRun()` is empty on every real run), false of this one — **whether a given silent path executes is a fact about the OPERATOR'S install.** That is why it is worth printing at runtime rather than only asserting in CI. No fixture reaches it because every path the corpus exercises is declared, which `CheckJsonContractTest` **asserts** rather than assumes.

**What a declared silence does NOT establish, stated because an unstated bound reads as a guarantee.** It says the author INTENDED this silence, **never that the silence is CORRECT**. The author who wrongly returns early will equally wrongly declare that path. What the mechanism buys is a forced review moment over the existing population, once, and an un-bypassable tripwire on every zero-finding path added after it — not a detector for a wrong judgement. Written on `Silence`, `CheckDisposition::Silent`, `Check::run()` and `CheckInventory::undeclaredSilent()`.

**The forced review moment found NO wrong path, and that is reported rather than rounded up.** The card predicted *"expect to find ≥1 path that should have yielded something"*. Reading all 37 check bodies, **no path was judged wrong.** What the reading did produce: a trailing declaration written on `ChannelSnapshotCheck` claiming `ChannelSnapshotProbe::probe()` can return nothing was **false** — every path returns ≥1 finding (an undeclared `server_path` is answered with `unvalidated`) — so it was removed and a comment says why there is none. The same verification was applied to `SshTransportProbe::probePinnedLine()`/`probeLive()` and to `WritebackSourceCoverage` / `WritebackByRef` / `BoardToolsBoardState`. **A declaration on a path that cannot be silent is a false statement about the code**, and it is the failure mode a bulk sweep produces — as a scripted docblock widen proved by over-reaching onto five private helpers that never yield a `Silence` (caught and reverted per-method: a bulk regex over docblocks needs a per-method control). `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheck`'s defensive `continue` is **deliberately left undeclared** — it is unreachable by construction, so if every enabled agent took it the run SHOULD disclose an undeclared silence rather than have a declaration vouch for an impossible state.

**Tests — the positive control is the only reason the green means anything.** Removing the trailing declaration from `AgentIdentityCollisionsCheck` reds **35 of 84 `CheckGoldenTest` cases**, the diff naming `agent.identity_collisions` verbatim; restored, `cmp` byte-identical, 84/84 green. Three further single-arm mutations (one mutation, one named test, restore + `cmp` between each) each RED: dropping `materialize()`'s `continue` reds the strip-containment test; recording unconditionally instead of behind `! $declaredSilence` reds the declared-silence test; re-deriving the list by disposition instead of by execution reds the per-agent test. Pristine negative control green.

**⚠ THE MECHANISM BROKE 110 ASSERTIONS ACROSS 22 TEST FILES, AND THE DUPLICATION THAT LET IT IS ITS OWN FINDING (canon #7).** Every per-check unit test ended in its own copy of `iterator_to_array($check->run($ctx), false)` — **43 sites across 30 files**. Harmless while a check yielded nothing but `Finding`s; wrong at all 43 the moment a check could also yield a `Silence`, because a raw `iterator_to_array` hands the test the sentinel. **This was NOT caught by the mechanism's own commit**, which ran `CheckGoldenTest` only — a filtered run is structurally incapable of seeing it, and the whole-suite run is what named it. That is the same measurement lesson stage 9 recorded when a whole-suite run exposed two cross-test defects invisible to `--filter`.

**The fix is the primitive, not the 43 call-sites — and the tempting fix was REJECTED for loosening the design's own constraint.** A test-local strip helper would have been a **second implementation of `CheckRunner::materialize()`**, whose entire safety argument is that it is the ONLY strip site; a copy would falsify that claim on the day it was written and would then be free to drift. Instead `tests/Support/MaterializesChecks` registers the check in a **real `CheckRunner`** and returns what the runner built, so the tests measure the production path rather than an imitation of it — the same lesson stage 8 recorded as *"a seam tested only at the callee leaves the call site unproven"*. All 43 sites converted, including the ~14 that were still green (a file whose check happens to yield on every tested path would break the day a declaration reached one, so leaving them would have left the defect armed). **The sweep script REFUSED 3 of 43** — a multi-line `false,` form it could not parse — rather than mangling them; they were fixed by hand. A bulk regex over source needs a per-site control, which is the same discipline the docblock widen above needed and initially lacked.

**Consequences.** `bridge:check` text output is unchanged on every install whose silent paths are declared — which is all of them today. `--format=json` gains one key. **No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change, no exit-code change.** The population this was audited over is every check body, re-derived per pass by command (`grep -rl 'implements \(Check\|PerAgentCheck\|OptInCheck\)\b' --include=*.php app`) with three controls, never quoted — the first form of that derivation omitted `OptInCheck` and silently under-counted by two.

## DL-267 — A run that could not apply its mutation is a DESTROYED run, not a measurement: the coverage instrument stops laundering a failed write into a verdict

**Card:** #5548 · **PR:** #468

**Context.** `bin/check-golden-mutate.php` is the instrument the whole DL-242 program's evidence rests on — every stage's disclosed-gap count, and the `## Verification` method's items 1 and 3, are its output, quoted into this plan doc as the program's measured record. It could not distinguish a destroyed run from a completed one. A regen whose copy tree was deleted underneath it had every `file_put_contents($target, $mutant)` fail, so **no mutation was ever applied**; the golden run then aborted for the unrelated reason that the repo was gone, which sets `$aborted` and `$red`, which the `match()` scored as `observed-via-abort`. All 35 predicates scored identically in about two seconds and the run printed `observed-via-abort 35 · UNOBSERVED 0` at **exit 0** — read at face value, the strongest possible outcome. It was caught only because someone checked the artifacts' mtime.

**Decision — one write primitive that THROWS, and it must throw rather than exit.** All four write sites (the mutant, the `finally` restore, the `.md` report, the `.json` artifact) route through a single `$writeOrThrow()` that compares `file_put_contents`'s return against `strlen($contents)`. **`exit()` does not run `finally` in PHP**, so a guard that exited from the mutation loop would leave a mutant on disk — the exact poisoning the file's own header warns about, caused by the guard written to prevent it. Throwing keeps the restore on every path. Three consequences fall out for free: the loop dies at predicate 1 instead of manufacturing N verdicts, a failed restore becomes loud instead of silently poisoning the next run's `$original`, and `wrote <path>` is printed only after a write that happened.

**The restore-failure message READS THE FILE BACK rather than inferring.** A failed mutant write and a failed restore write address the same file, so whatever stops one stops the other and they normally co-occur — but in that case nothing was ever written and the file is pristine. Reporting *"a mutant is live"* there would be a wrong-but-specific cause, which is worse than a generic one. The message compares the on-disk bytes to `$original` and states which is true; both branches were exercised against the real file before the guard was trusted. Both failures are also reported together, because reporting only the restore would drop the cause.

**A degenerate corpus is a measurement failure, not a finding.** Two whole-run signatures are refused rather than rendered: every predicate `observed-via-abort` (the destroyed-run shape above — refused because it reads as the STRONGEST outcome), and every predicate `UNOBSERVED` (the suite provably never went red, so it is not running — a `--filter` matching no test exits 0). **All-`observed` is deliberately NOT refused:** every flip being caught is a legitimate strong result, and refusing it would be the instrument declining to report good news. The guard is bounded to a full run — under `--only` a single predicate shares one status trivially.

**A narrowed run no longer writes the artifacts, which is the same defect with a different cause.** The generated header claims the measurement covers *"the {$total} branch predicates in `handle()`"*. Under `--limit 3` that sentence rendered as "the 3 branch predicates in `handle()`" over a rewritten full-corpus doc — a false denominator committed to the repo. Narrowed runs now print their verdicts to stdout and leave the artifacts alone. No consumer breaks: the script has no caller in CI or any workflow, and is run by hand.

**Scope, and the one thing NOT built.** `json_encode` gained `JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR` because `false."\n"` is `"\n"` — an encode failure would have written a syntactically fine, entirely empty artifact, the same laundering one layer down. This was found by re-deriving the write-site population after the first fix, not by the original card, whose sibling audit named four sites; the fifth is why the population is re-derived per pass rather than quoted. The `fwrite(STDERR, …)` diagnostics are deliberately left unchecked: each sits on a path that exits non-zero on the next line, so the exit code is the failure channel and a failed advisory write is not laundered into a reported outcome.

**The audit that found the rest is worth more than any single guard: enumerate the EMISSION SITES, not the failure signatures.** Reviewing by reading kept finding one more degenerate case per pass — a report over zero predicates (a `--only` typo exits 0 having printed nothing, and on a full run would have written a doc covering *"the 0 branch predicates in `handle()`"*), and an artifact-failure message asserting *"the files still hold the previous run"* when the report had already been rewritten and only the JSON failed. Two passes in a row adding members is the signal that the LOOP is wrong, not the work: the population *"degenerate signatures I notice"* is unbounded. The bounded restatement is that all of them are **one shape — a claim about the run whose precondition was never checked** — over a population that is finite and greppable: every `printf` / `fwrite` / `fprintf` / write in the file, each asked what its claim asserts. That sweep found exactly those two and no third, and a repeat pass found none. The instrument's own defect and the method that finds it are the same idea one level apart, which is why this is recorded here rather than left in the PR.

## DL-268 — The channel-server snapshot version is only a signal while every file that states it agrees: `version-bump-guard` asserts lock↔manifest agreement, and the lockfile stays IN the trigger set

- **Date:** 2026-08-04
- **Context (card#5232):** DL-038 made `examples/channel-servers/package.json` `version` the staleness signal a copied snapshot compares against canonical, and enforced it with the `version-bump-guard` job. That job reads **one** of the **two** committed files that carry the version. Measured on `dev`: the lockfile's root `version` sat at **`0.7.1`** while the manifest went `0.7.2 → 0.8.3` — roughly a dozen bumps, every one of them green, because the guard cannot fail on a field it never reads. DL-038 itself asserts the two move together (*"`npm version --no-git-tag-version` moves `package.json` + `package-lock.json` together"*) — true of that command (re-measured 2026-08-04: it moves the manifest and **both** lockfile version sites), but nothing enforced that the command was the one used, so a hand-edited manifest drifted the lock silently. **The drift is no longer live and was never fixed:** it closed at `6c4f504` when an `npm` run resynced the lock as a side effect. Agreement was luck, which is the argument for the guard rather than against it. Not an outage at any point — `npm ci` validates the dependency tree, not the root `version` field (verified during card#5143's review).
- **Decision — tighten; do not weaken (three parts, ruled by the user):**
  1. **Leave the trigger set alone.** A lockfile change keeps demanding a version bump. Excluding `package-lock.json` would buy convenience on a handful of PRs by making the guard blind to real artifact drift: a transitive bump changes what `npm ci` installs, so the deployed snapshot genuinely differs and the signal must move with it.
  2. **Add the agreement assertion.** A new step requires `package-lock.json`'s `.version` **and** `.packages[""].version` to equal the manifest's. Both sites are read, because the defect class being closed is exactly a guard that reads one of N fields that must agree — covering only the root would re-mint it one level down. It is **not diff-gated** the way the bump step is: agreement is a property of the tree, so no shape of diff earns an exemption from it. It is **not** unconditional in the absolute sense, and the distinction is worth stating because it is where a reader would over-trust the guard — the whole workflow carries a `paths:` filter (`examples/channel-servers/**` plus the workflow file), so a PR touching neither never runs this job. Coverage is nonetheless complete for the entry path: drift can only be INTRODUCED by a PR that edits one of those two files, and every such PR trips the filter. An absent manifest `version` **fails** rather than comparing jq's `null` to `null` — the compare alone would pass a tree carrying no drift signal at all, the guard's own blind spot.
  3. **A lockfile-only dependency PR gets a one-command maintainer commit.** Dependabot structurally cannot bump the manifest, so `version-bump-guard` is red by construction on those PRs (measured on #472; the same shape consolidated #343/#353/#354 by hand at v0.65.0). The remediation is documented **in the guard's own error output** — the surface the maintainer actually reaches — rather than in a runbook that must be found first.
- **Alternatives considered:** (a) **exclude `package-lock.json` from the trigger set** — rejected as above; it inverts the guard's purpose to buy ~monthly convenience, and `channel-server-deps` separately gates the same directory on `npm audit --audit-level=high`, so the two legs would be in open contradiction. (b) **Assert agreement only when the diff touched the directory** — rejected: the drift that motivated this entry entered through PRs that *did* change the directory and still passed, so a second diff gate inside a job the `paths:` filter has already selected adds a way to be exempt without adding any protection. (c) **A cron leg re-checking agreement between PRs** — rejected (canon #6): every path into `dev`/`main` is a PR, so a PR-time assertion catches drift at entry; a scheduled re-check could only find drift that predates the guard, and there is none.
- **Validation:** the assertion is driven by `tests/Feature/Workflows/ChannelServerVersionAgreementTest.php`, which extracts the step's real `run:` block from the YAML and executes it under `bash` (same shape as `PrTitleLintTest`) — so it cannot drift from what CI runs. Its positive control is **real history, not invented JSON**: the pair as it stood at `4abe8e3`, the last commit at which the defect was live. Mutation-proven, 4/4 killed against a 5-test / 17-assertion baseline, both control axes asserted (the edit changed the file; the suite still ran the full baseline): dropping the `packages[""]` site, dropping the null-manifest guard, turning the mismatch into `exit 0`, and renaming the step all go red. Harness `~/.cache/coord/5232-mutate.sh`.
- **Consequences:** `.github/workflows/channel-server-supply-chain.yml` (new agreement step, `shell: bash` pinned on both steps so a test can drive them, dependabot remediation line, job comment); one new test file. **This changes what CI accepts — a PR whose lockfile and manifest disagree now fails.** No app code, no migration, no runtime change. Also deleted in passing: the bump step's comment claimed the filter excludes *"the CI workflow itself"*, which it does not — the workflow was never inside the pathspec, so the clause described a protection that was not being performed and, worse, read as an invitation to add `package-lock.json` to that same exclusion list.
- **Sibling audit (canon #7) — one confirmed, one refuted, filed as card#5910.** The shape is *a guard reading one of N files that must move together*. **Confirmed:** `VERSION` vs `docs/CHANGELOG.md` — `auto-tag-version.yml` is the only automation reading both, and on a missing `## [<VERSION>]` section it WARNs and publishes the GitHub Release with a placeholder note, defeating that job's own stated purpose; no PR-time guard asserts the section exists. Left unfixed deliberately: it adds a check that can reject a PR, which is a hard gate. **Refuted, and recorded so it is not re-derived:** `composer.json` + `composer.lock` in *both* this repo and kanban-board looked identical in shape (no `composer validate` in either CI), but `composer install` in the shared `setup-app` composite refuses an out-of-sync pair itself — measured two-sided on the real files, rc 4 mismatched vs rc 0 restored. Every installing job is already the guard.

## DL-269 — A suite that spawns the marker-writing channel server sandboxes the addressing env AND asserts the seat's real runtime dir did not move: the redirect is not the guarantee, the assertion is

- **Date:** 2026-08-05
- **Context (card#5233, the canon #7 half of DL-237(e)):** mutation-testing `bin/check-channel-snapshot.py` — a tool whose entire purpose is *never touch the seat's live channel endpoint* — wrote a synthetic witness AND a real `<live-socket>.FAILED` deafness marker into a live seat's `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. The marker was FALSE: the socket was bound and accepting throughout. DL-237 answered it for that one python suite (`setUpModule` repoints all four channel-addressing inputs; `tearDownModule` snapshots the real runtime dir and raises if it moved). The open question was whether the answer belongs to that suite or to the shape.
- **Audit — the population is TOOLS that can address seat-live state, not test files that mention one.** The file-side grep is a candidate-finder and is provably lossy: a test reaching live state through a shared helper carries no token of its own (`bin/test_provision_board_tools_samebox.py` and `tests/Support/CheckGolden/GoldenSshEnvironment.php` both fall out of it). Derived tool-side, then measured — every suite run under `~/.cache/coord/5233-tripwire.py` on a **live** seat (`/run/user/1006/agent-webhook-bridge-channel-kanbanboard-agent.sock` bound, so the measurements are not vacuous):
  - **python (3 suites) — clean, and structurally so.** `test_check_channel_snapshot` 47 tests, `test_provision_board_tools` + `_samebox` 131 tests: `NO CHANGE`. The latter two never reach the filesystem (every fs/exec seam patched; a `FakeFs`), so their exclusion from the exec set is correct rather than a false negative.
  - **node (3 files, 27 tests) — clean, by two DIFFERENT disciplines and no assertion.** `clear-context.test.mjs` builds its child env as an **allowlist** (safe by construction); `marker-refusal.test.mjs` uses a **denylist** (`{...process.env}` then delete two keys); `channel-lib.test.mjs` is pure. Both are correct today. Neither notices a new test that forgets them — and the seat exports `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_SOCKET` pointing at its LIVE socket, so a plain `{...process.env}` spawn reaches it: bind → `EADDRINUSE` → a `.FAILED` marker beside a healthy socket. `markerPath()` (`agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs`) is the named mechanism: `${SOCKET_PATH}.FAILED` under `unix`, else `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR || os.tmpdir()}/…FAILED` — an ambient-environment fallback either way.
  - **PHP (2008 tests, 6002 assertions, 419s) — clean, and ACCEPTED without a guard, on the record.** The one class that touches `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (`ChannelTransportCheckTest`) redirects it in `setUp` and restores in `tearDown`; `tests/Support/CheckGolden/PinnedHost.php` already pins `PATH`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`COORD_CONFIG`/`GH_TOKEN` for the golden corpus; every other live-state-adjacent test reaches its subject through `config()` overrides and `sys_get_temp_dir()`. **No PHP test was measured to write the seat's real runtime dir, and no reading found a path to it** — bounded claim: one whole-suite tripwire run plus a reading of the candidates the tool-side derivation named, not an exhaustive proof over 2008 tests. On that evidence a cross-cutting extension would be mechanism without a named mechanism to defend against (canon #6); if one is ever found, this is the entry it reopens.
- **Decision:** the contract generalises to **any suite that spawns the marker-writing server**, and node gets it — `examples/channel-servers/tests/live-state-guard.mjs`, imported first by every file in that directory. It neutralises all four addressing inputs at import (before any case runs) and registers an `after()` hook that fails the run if the real `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` moved. **The generalisable part is the ASSERTION, not the redirect:** every harness already redirected in some form; only python could tell you when its redirect stopped holding.
- **One contract, one authority per language — deliberately not one shared implementation.** python and node cannot share code, so they are separate authorities that must move together (the per-language guard-lockstep policy); a third hand-rolled copy inside a single language would be the duplication defect this entry exists to avoid (canon #5/#7).
- **Alternatives considered:** (a) **fix `marker-refusal`'s denylist into an allowlist and stop there** — rejected as the downstream patch (canon #2): it converges the two node files on one discipline but still leaves nothing that notices the next file. The harness redirect subsumes it. (b) **a PHPUnit extension mirroring the guard suite-wide** — rejected as above; recorded as accepted-with-reason rather than skipped, so it is not re-derived. (c) **`node --test-global-setup`** — unavailable on Node 20 (the pinned runtime); a `--import` preload would be skipped by anyone running `node --test tests/` directly, which is what the README tells them to do.
- **Validation — the assertion was seen to fail, twice, at two levels.** (1) **The python teardown assertion, which had never been positive-controlled** (DL-237 shipped it untested against a real escape): with the harness sandbox removed **and** `child_env()`'s four overrides mutated away — the incident configuration, aimed at a fake runtime dir so nothing live was touched — it raised `THIS SUITE TOUCHED LIVE STATE`, naming the two sockets and the `.bound` witness the escape created. Removing **either** layer alone changed nothing: the protection is genuinely two independent sufficient layers, not one layer with a decoration. (2) **The new node guard:** a temporary escaping test wrote a marker into a fake real-runtime-dir; the run failed with the same message while the test body itself PASSED — i.e. the `after()` hook, not a test assertion, is what caught it. `live-state-guard.test.mjs` is the permanent comparator control, including the **overwrite-in-place** case a name-set compare misses (the incident wrote over an existing path; a previously-deaf seat is exactly where a stale marker already sits). (3) **A reachability probe, because a hook proven in one file proves nothing about the others:** making the guard's `after()` throw unconditionally failed **4 of 4** files, so the hook is genuinely registered per test file rather than only in the file that happened to be controlled. (4) **The CI-shaped environment was run, not assumed:** with `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and every `BRIDGE_CHANNEL_*` var unset — the state CI runs in, where the guard's assertion is deliberately inert — the suite is 33/33 green.
- **Consequences:** `examples/channel-servers/tests/` gains two files and one import line per existing file; snapshot version `0.9.1 → 0.9.2` (DL-038 bump-guard, lock in agreement per DL-268). **No app code, no migration, no runtime change, and no change to what the receiver accepts or rejects.** The suite goes 27 → 33 tests. `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` gains the contract; the supply-chain workflow's header comment described the node suite as *only* the marker-refusal regression suite, which was already false before this change (it has held `channel-lib` and `clear-context` since v0.69.x) — corrected in passing (canon #16).

## DL-270 — A `card#` token is not authorization by itself: the head branch outranks the PR title, and a title-only token is corroborated against the card's own `pr_number`

- **Date:** 2026-08-04
- **Context (card#5287, roundtable #178 R3):** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` matched the card token over `titleAndHead()` = `$title.' '.$head` with a single non-global `preg_match`, so the **leftmost** match won. The head branch ref is minted by this install's own tooling (`board-card-start` → `card-<id>-slug`) and is the authoritative referent for what a PR is work *on*; the title is prose, where a `card#NNNN` is as often a **descriptive citation of another card** as a claim about this PR — and the title sits FIRST in that concatenation. So a foreign/descriptive title token **silently outranked the branch's own correct token**. This is the exact sibling of the foreign-DL hijack DL-218 closed, one layer over: DL-218's conflict predicate covers `DL`-vs-`card#` and does not reach across the title/branch boundary.
- **The reachable input is a same-board citation, not a cross-tenant collision — and it needs no second instance.** There is ONE kanban instance, multi-tenant, one id allocator, so ids cannot collide across tenants (roundtable #55/#178) and `KanbanMoveCardHandler`'s DL-009 guard is **board-scoped, not install-scoped**. Measured: (1) another tenant's card → `getCard` **403**, refused at the 4xx arm; (2) another board of the same tenant → 200, `board_id` mismatch, refused; (3) **another card on the SAME mapped board** → 200, board matches, **the wrong card moves, silently**. Case 3 is a toolkit PR title descriptively citing another toolkit card — ordinary practice.
- **Decision (a) — the DL-218 SHAPE applied to (title token, head-branch token), defined ONCE.** New `cardTokenResolution()` parses the two surfaces separately and returns `{token, uncorroborated, foreignTitleToken}`. Branch present ⇒ branch is the token; a **disagreeing** title token is foreign → `Log::warning` naming both cards and the ruling, then the **branch's** card moves. Agreeing or absent ⇒ unchanged. The move path and the draft overlay both consume the one resolver (canon #5); the branch-create `started` push parses the ref alone and is corroborated by construction. The conflict is logged at the move site only — the overlay resolves the same tokens on the same event and would double-log, the same split DL-218 made.
- **Decision (b′) — corroboration is WIDER than selection, and measuring the real branch convention is what kept this guard from breaking ordinary work.** The head ref corroborates a title token when it carries a full `card-<id>` token **or simply the card's bare id**. The first implementation required a full token, and a check of merged PRs killed it: the dominant convention here is `<type>/<id>-slug` (`fix/5915-…`, `test/5233-…`), which carries **no** card token — so nearly every real PR would have been uncorroborated, and the handler gate below refuses any **second** PR against a card that already tracks a first. Three merged PRs (459/460/461) track card 5698, so that is routine work, not an attack. The approved residual says *"no BRANCH CORROBORATION"*, and a ref naming the id plainly corroborates it. A bare number can only **confirm** a token the title produced, never **select** a card — keeping the `card`-prefix requirement in the grammar (else `chore/2026-cleanup` would correlate) and adding no correlation channel. Accepted bound, stated rather than discovered later: a numeric branch can accidentally corroborate a very low-id card (`chore/bump-1-2-3` vs `card#2`); that only relaxes a guard which did not previously exist and never widens selection (canon #6).
- **Decision (b) — the residual (a title token the ref does not back) is settled at the HANDLER, on evidence the card already carries.** The classifier flags the target `card_token_uncorroborated`; `KanbanMoveCardHandler` accepts it only when the card's `pr_number` is **unset** or **already this PR**, else refuses with `card_token_uncorroborated` (log + alert + no-op). Rationale as approved: a foreign card almost always already carries its own PR ref, so this closes the hijack without breaking legitimate title-only PRs, and it reads **no field the handler's existing `getCard` did not already return**. The gate sits BEFORE the already-in-stage self-heal, because that branch still *stamps* — a refused move must write nothing at all. "Tracks no PR" reuses the stamp's own emptiness test so the two cannot disagree. Fail-closed on a non-numeric `pr_number` or an event with no PR number.
- **Decision (c) — on a conflict the sole-DL stamp derives from the head ref alone.** Once the title is established foreign, a DL sitting in it is foreign to the branch's card too; stamping it would re-mint the DL-218 correlation poison at the new surface. This is the `$conflictDl` exclusion applied to the SURFACE rather than to one already-resolved token.
- **Alternatives considered (both offered by roundtable #178, both rejected — the axis was wrong):** **namespace the token** helps only if the BARE form is rejected, which breaks every existing title and every emulator and leaves the hole open until the last emitter migrates; **convention-only** ("never cite a foreign card with `card#`") is an unenforced restatement. The defect is not the token's grammar — it is that `card#` was read as **authorization without corroboration**. On the residual specifically, **(a) refuse every uncorroborated title-only token** and **(b) accept-but-alert** were put to the user and declined in favour of the corroboration gate.
- **This CHANGES WHAT THE BRIDGE ACCEPTS and was gated.** User-approved 2026-07-27 (residual option (c) + the conflict-predicate shape + the comment correction). Card#5288's 403/404 split was landed first, by that gate's own build note, so an operator hitting the new refusal is not reading an opaque one.
- **The false-delegation claim it also fixes, and its sibling audit (canon #7/#16).** The classifier's `card#`-fallback comment asserted *"the durable handler rejects a card not on the mapped board"* as one guarantee — false for the unreadable-card case (the 4xx arm returns first) and, on the same mapped board, false as a bound on this hijack. **It is the sentence that hid the whole finding: an auditor reads it and stops.** Swept by re-derivation (a vocabulary grep across `app/` + `docs/` with a named-member control, plus a re-read of the subsystem, because the wording grep and the behavior grep under-count differently — DL-243(f)); `docs/CHANGELOG.md` and this file are excluded as historical records (DL-243(g)). Corrected: the classifier comment (both the PR and push paths), `docs/writeback.md`'s **Card-token correlation** delegation sentence, the top-of-doc handler summary, the alert-reason table, the permanent-refusal enumeration, and the **Security notes** bound — where *"nudge a card that genuinely sits on the mapped board"* was stating a real bound that was doing less work than it read, since "sits on the mapped board" is satisfied by every other card on your own board.
- **Known NOT closed, filed rather than silently widened:** the draft-overlay path inherits the title-vs-branch rule (shared resolver) but **not** the handler-side corroboration gate — its target carries no flag — so a title-only `card#` can still overlay a `block_reason` onto a merely-cited card. Same shape, strictly lower harm (one add-if-missing field, cleared on `ready_for_review`, never a stage move); extending the gate there changes what the bridge accepts on a second surface and the approved answer named the move path. Recorded in `correlatedCardIds()`'s docblock and carded. **[Closed for the overlay SET path by card#5953 — user-approved as "extend the move path's gate to the overlay SET" (that card's option (a), not the refuse-all (a) this entry records as declined): the target now carries the flag and both handlers share the extracted `CardTokenCorroboration` gate. The `ready_for_review` CLEAR is deliberately NOT gated — clear-if-ours can only null the exact marker string, and gating it would strand markers on cards now tracking a different PR; the constant-sentinel bound and the accepted pin-release residual are stated in docs/writeback.md.]**
- **Validation:** 5 mutations run, all killed — pre-fix leftmost-match resolution (reds the conflict, overlay-conflict and uncorroborated-flag tests), un-narrowed stamp surface, **bare-id corroboration removed**, gate removed, and **gate moved below the self-heal**. That last one initially **survived**, which exposed the first version of its own test as a decoration: the card carried a `pr_number`, so the add-if-missing stamp had nothing to write and no PATCH could ever be sent whatever the gate did. Fixed by giving the self-heal real work (a `stamp_dl` against a card with no `dl_number`) — the assertion can now fail, which is the only thing that makes its passing evidence (canon #9).
- **Consequences:** `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` (new `cardTokenResolution` + `refCorroborates` + `prTitle`/`prHead` split out of `titleAndHead`, `cardToken()` retired into the resolver, `isDependabot` reuses `prHead`), `KanbanMoveCardHandler` (the gate + `corroboratedByCardPr`), `docs/writeback.md` (6 sites), 8 new classifier tests + 6 new handler tests. **No migration, no new `.env`, no token-scope change, no change to what the RECEIVER accepts** — the change is what the writeback authorizes a card write against.

## DL-271 — A comment that names WHICH component performs a check is a restatement with a lifetime: it survives the arrival of a second caller, and the audit for that shape found the door set restated twice

- **Date:** 2026-08-04
- **Context (card#5289, canon #7 sweep off roundtable #178):** DL-270 corrected one comment that DELEGATED a check to a callee which could not run it for the cited case, and flagged the shape as unswept. This is the sweep. Population re-derived rather than recalled: every comment block in bridge-owned code (`app`, `bin`, `config`, `database`, `routes`, `tests`, `examples/channel-servers`), filtered by a delegation vocabulary, **all 1324 candidates read and classified.** Method + per-pass trend in the card; the reusable half is below.
- **The instrument was wrong first, and that is the load-bearing part.** The first extractor opened comments with a REGEX, and `'/*.yml'` — a real glob inside a string literal in `CheckCommand` — opens a block comment to a regex. That injected code into the candidate set AND masked real comments inside the false span: the denominator was under-counted by 585 blocks. Its negative control (a method-signature regex over extracted text) passed the whole time, because the leaked line contained no method signature — **a control that cannot fail for the failure it is placed against is a decoration** (canon #9). Replaced with each language's OWN tokenizer (`token_get_all`, python `tokenize`+`ast`, a JS state machine), and the negative control re-pinned to the exact line that broke v1 and **shown to discriminate** (v1 leaks it, v2 does not) rather than merely to pass.
- **Finding (a) — ONE class, TWO instances: the door set restated per-consumer.** `BoardToolsRegistry` justified having no opt-in gate with *"the route is loopback-gated and the controller refuses an unresolved token"*, and `Tool` described the invocation path as *"the Node MCP server forwards … to POST /agent-tools/call, the controller resolves the caller's agent from the bearer"*. Both are true of the HTTP door and of nothing else since DL-223 added `bridge:tools-call`, which reaches the SAME registry through {@see BoardToolDispatcher} with no route and no bearer (identity is the pinned `--agent`). **The timeline is evidence, not inference:** both files have exactly ONE commit in history (`ce8ce28`, DL-217), and the ssh door landed later at `68327be`. The CONCLUSIONS still hold — `ToolsCallCommand` refuses any `--agent` that is not an enabled ssh board-tools agent — so nothing was insecure; what was wrong is that an auditor asking whether the always-on registry is safe reads two named guards and stops, which is the DL-270 harm exactly.
- **Decision — do not re-sync N copies; delete the restatement and point at the owner (canon #16).** `BoardToolDispatcher`'s docblock ALREADY owns the two-door fact, so both sites now say that each door gates before dispatch on evidence of its own and name the dispatcher, rather than enumerating doors. The rule this generalizes: **a comment may name that a check happens; naming WHICH component performs it is a second copy of the call graph, and it goes stale the next time a caller is added.** Rejected: updating both docblocks to say "the HTTP door … and the ssh door …", which is the same defect with a longer lifetime — it would go stale at door three.
- **Finding (b) — a delegate that has never existed.** `ValidatorsTest` claimed its two patterns *"must stay character-for-character identical to the Python provisioner side (lib/validators.py)"*. `git log --all --diff-filter=AD -- '*validators.py'` is EMPTY and `a856940` (the v0.12.0 Laravel rewrite) is this repo's ROOT commit: the reference arrived with the rewrite pointing at a file that did not come across, and no Python source here carries either pattern. It has read as a live cross-language lockstep guard for 561 commits. The method NAME carried the same claim and was renamed with it. Corrected to the true rationale — the two patterns are a RECEIVER-BOUNDARY accept-set, and `ScopeId`'s `..` / `//` rejections are the path-traversal defense for the per-scope secret filename — with an explicit *do not restore a mirror claim without a mirror to name*.
- **Verified truthful, delegate opened and reachable on the cited path (8), so they are recorded as CHECKED rather than left implicitly clean:** the classifier-socket `..` gate before the prefix compare; the channel-URL SSRF gate on the agent's own `channel.url` and not only `payload.url`; the spawn allowlist before the `setsid` resolve; the `supports()` pre-check gating BOTH `WebhookAdapterFactory::for()` callers; `assertFieldLengths` reached from both adapters; the `[EnvelopeSizeLimit, VerifyHmacSignature]` route order; `LoopbackOnly` on the board-tools route; and `parseStringList`'s empty-entry throw licensing an absent per-entry guard.
- **What this did NOT close, stated rather than left to be discovered.** The sweep stopped on its STATED BOUND, not on convergence: the sibling audit added a member the vocabulary never saw, which by the card's own criterion means the pass did not converge. Every member whose delegate was not opened is named individually in the card, as are the two strata (`bin/`, `examples/`) read for the shape but not verified. A clean result over an unnamed population would report where the searcher stopped, not the state of the code.
- **Consequences:** comment-only. `BoardToolsRegistry`, `Tool`, `ValidatorsTest` (docblock + one method rename). **No behavior change, no migration, no `.env`, no token-scope change, no change to what the receiver or either board-tools door accepts.**

## DL-272 — The PR-title gate's DL arm enumerates its digits: a bracket RANGE in bash is resolved by COLLATION, so `[0-9]` was a locale-dependent second engine that greened a token the authority correlates to nothing

- **Date:** 2026-08-04
- **Context (card#5300, the one row of four the user approved).** DL-240 found and PINNED a fourth divergence between `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml`'s require step and the token authorities: under `en_US.UTF-8`, `[[ "$title_lc" =~ …dl-[0-9]{1,4}… ]]` matches `dl-٣` (U+0663), so the gate GREENED a PR title carrying a DL that `DlTokenGrammar`'s ASCII `\d` (no `/u`, DL-231) correlates to nothing — the gate certifying the exact silent no-op it exists to stop. It was pinned rather than fixed because repairing it changes what a CI check accepts, which is a hard gate. **The user approved this row only, 2026-07-27, on the stated ground that its DIRECTION was already ratified fleet-wide by DL-231 — so building it implements an existing decision rather than making a new one. The other three rows (`card4` false green, leading-zero and 5-digit-DL false reds) stay pinned and untouched.**
- **Decision — enumerate, do not narrow-the-range.** The arm is now `dl-[0123456789]{1,4}`. `[[:digit:]]` was measured and behaves identically here, and was still rejected: it trades one piece of locale data for another, where an enumerated set depends on **no** locale data at all. Given the defect is precisely a bracket construct silently consuming locale data, removing the dependency beats re-pointing it. DL-231's clause is "matches ASCII digits only"; the enumeration states that literally.
- **Nothing else in the step was touched, and the reason is a direction, not a scope preference.** The step's REMAINING bracket expressions are collation-sensitive too — measured, in this build — but they are all NEGATED classes (`[^0-9]`, `[^0-9a-z_]`) or the branch-shape test `^[a-z-]+/[0-9]+-`, where a collation-wide range REDS a title the authority correlates instead of greening one it does not. Narrowing them would make this gate **more permissive**, which is its own hard gate and is not what was approved. They are characterized in `test_the_require_steps_negated_classes_are_still_collation_sensitive_pending_a_gate` and appended to card#5300.

*[Annotation, 2026-08-18 (card#6822, DL-289) — ADDITIVE.] DL-289 widened the BRANCH predicate and deliberately left its `[0-9]` a bracket RANGE: enumerating it there would make the gate more permissive, the opposite of this entry's direction. The token arms this entry governs are untouched, and this entry's collation pin was observed green throughout that change.*
- **THREE further divergences, measured during this build and appended to card#5300 (canon #7 sibling audit of the shape being fixed).** Each row was run through real bash under both locales AND through the authority — never reasoned. `card-4<U+0663>` on `fix/4-slug`: authority parses card 4, gate reds under `en_US.UTF-8` and greens under `C.UTF-8` (trailing `([^0-9]|$)`). `fix dl-1234<U+0663>` on `fix/999-slug`: authority parses `DL-1234`, same split (trailing boundary, DL arm). `<U+00E9>card-44` on `fix/44-slug`: authority parses card 44, same split — and here the collation-wide range is **`a-z`, not the digits**, which is why the digit fix provably does not move it (measured: narrowing only the digits in that class leaves the row unchanged). A fourth site differs in KIND rather than direction: the branch-shape test decides whether the step enforces AT ALL, so `fix/<U+0663>-slug` is skipped under `C.UTF-8` and enforced under `en_US.UTF-8` — the step's SCOPE is locale-dependent, not just its verdict.
- **The pin became a regression anchor, and its control had to be re-pinned to survive that.** The old leg asserted the vector red under a C-family locale and green under `en_US.UTF-8`. Post-fix the vector reds in BOTH, so a same-shape assertion would pass whether or not the fix were present — a check that cannot fail. The leg now MUTATES the real workflow script back to `[0-9]` and re-runs it: the pre-fix spelling must GREEN under `en_US.UTF-8` where the shipped one REDS, same locale, same vector, same process. The mutation's application is asserted (`str_replace` count `=== 1`), so a rename or a re-spelling can never leave a control that silently re-runs the unmutated script. The `grep -E` control is retained — GNU grep's `[0-9]` is ASCII in every locale measured, which is what identified bash's engine rather than the bracket expression as the cause.
- **Proven failable, not merely green.** With the fix reverted in the real file, two legs red: the mutation assertion (`0 !== 1`) and — because this box's ambient locale IS `en_US.UTF-8` — the DL agreement loop, on `DL-<U+0663>`. That second red is why the vector left the exemption list rather than being re-exempted: it now rides the same loop as every other vector. Restored, `PrTitleLintTest` 18/18, 316 assertions.
- **Consequences:** `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` (one regex + the comment stating why an enumeration and why the remaining ranges stay), `tests/Feature/Workflows/PrTitleLintTest.php`. **This DOES change what a CI gate accepts — strictly narrowing, on the approved row only: a title whose only DL token spells its digits in non-ASCII now reds where it used to pass. No migration, no `.env`, no token-scope change, and no change to what the receiver or either board-tools door accepts.**

## DL-273 — A DL-token near-miss stops being silent, and the probe that finds one becomes a shared primitive rather than a second grammar inside a second grammar

**Date:** 2026-08-05
**Context — DL-234's argument was made about the DL token by name, and the DL token is the half that never got the fix.** A branch ref or PR title that APPEARS to name a DL but does not parse was a complete no-op: `feat/DL_239-slug` (underscore, not the separator), `feat/DL239-slug` (glued — the DL token has no glued arm, unlike the card token), and every plural spelling (`DLs-239`, `DLs239`, …, silent by the identical mechanism DL-250 measured: `\bDL` matches inside `DLs`, the optional separator group cannot consume the `s`, and `\d` then fails against it with no second word boundary to retry from). Each of those publishes, moves nothing, and tells nobody. `warnCardTokenNearMiss()` only ever fired on card-ish text (`\bcards?…`), so there was no DL near-miss probe of any kind. DL-234 shipped exactly this for the card token on the argument that an unparsed token is *"as high-value a miss as an unresolvable DL"* (roundtable #48) — an argument about the DL token, applied only to the other one. Card#5310.

**MEASURED ON THIS REPO'S OWN HISTORY, not argued from examples.** Evaluating the 400 most recent PRs (all states) against the shipped grammars: **12 head branches use the glued `dlNNN` spelling** — `feature/dl207-4483-promote-on-release`, `docs/dl204-live-witness`, `feature/dl200-4352-coord-issue-card-move`, `feat/dl189-classifier-config-knobs`, `docs/pm-consumption-standard-dl170`, `feature/dl161-dependabot-archive-on-close`, and six more down to `dl028` — and carry no card token, so each branch-create `push` correlated to nothing, emitted no target, and warned nothing. **In all 12 the PR TITLE carried a properly-spelled `DL-NNN`**, so the PR-path move worked and the board looked right; what was silently lost every time was the DL-160 `started` move — the card never advanced when work BEGAN, only when the PR opened. That is the same failure mode DL-233 recorded for the card token (*"the board looks right until the merge that should have advanced it does nothing"*), inverted onto the other end of the lifecycle. **Stated bound: this is a static evaluation of branch NAMES against today's grammar, not a replay of delivered events.** Roughly half the 12 carry DL numbers below 160 and so predate the branch-create leg entirely, meaning they could not have been processed at all — so 12 is an exact count of the SPELLING the probe now catches and an UPPER bound on events actually missed. The spelling is the thing being fixed; the count is not asserted as an incident total.

**Decision (1) — the probe MECHANISM moves to `NearMissProbe`, bound to a stem; it is not copied into a second grammar.** This is the second real caller, which is where a shared primitive is extracted rather than sibling-ed (canon #5). DL-250 put the mechanism on `CardTokenGrammar` when cards were its only stem, and none of its reasoning was ever about cards: the separators are DATA, `matches()` assembles the pattern from that list, `vectors()` derives one text per cell of {singular, plural} × {no separator} ∪ that list, so the pattern and the corpus that covers it remain two consumers of ONE definition. Copying ~15 lines of rule-shaped logic into `DlTokenGrammar` would have re-created, one level up, the exact restatement shape DL-250 removed one level down. **This supersedes DL-250(1) as a code-state claim** (`NEAR_MISS_SEPARATORS` no longer lives on `CardTokenGrammar`) and reverses none of its reasoning; DL-239(h)'s refusal to widen the probe *to* the grammar stands untouched — the probe is still a *looks-like* predicate whose `! parses` half is the caller guard, and it is still not derivable from any `PATTERN`.

**Decision (2) — ONE separator list serves every stem, and that is a claim about authors, not about tokens.** `NearMissProbe::SEPARATORS` is the set of characters an author types where a real separator belongs. That is one human behaviour, so a card-side edit to it deliberately moves the DL probe too. The consequence is stated rather than discovered: widening the list widens both warning sets at once. It can only ever ADD warnings — the probe is consulted solely where `parse()` returned null, so no text that correlates can reach it, and no accept-set moves. The alternative, a per-grammar copy of the same six members, is two lists someone must keep in step, which is the defect and not the safeguard.

**Decision (3) — the accepted-separator inertness is re-proven per grammar, because it is a property of the PATTERN, not of the list.** `-` and `#` sit in the shared set although `-` is the DL grammar's only accepted separator and both are the card grammar's. That looks like it should make the probe fire on every real token and does not: every text matching `\bDL-\d` parses, so no such text reaches a probe consulted only where `parse()` returned null. `DlTokenGrammarTest` pins that implication for the DL pattern exactly as `CardTokenGrammarTest` already pinned it for the card one — a comment cannot red when a pattern moves, and one class's proof says nothing about the other's.

**Decision (4) — `DlTokenGrammar` gains `describe()`, which its own docblock said to add "the day a PHP surface needs it".** That day is this one: the warning renders the accepted set from the grammar rather than spelling it out (the DL-239 ruling, now applied to the token that motivated it). Pinned by the same anti-snapshot assertion the card side uses — read the RENDERED sentence, never the helpers that built it, because a `describe()` rewritten to a hardcoded string passes any assertion phrased against `accepted()`/`rejected()`.

**Decision (5) — WARNING, never a failure, matching DL-234(c) exactly.** No accept/reject change: which text correlates to which card is untouched, and nothing that moved a card before moves differently now. Only which NON-correlating text gets a log line changes.

**Decision (6) — the warn stays behind the both-null guard, so DL-234(e)'s whole-subject limit governs the new stem too.** A subject carrying a parsing `card#` beside a malformed `DL_239` moves its card, so it is not in the silent-failure class the probe exists to catch — and the message's own "no move" clause would be a false statement about it. **The bounded cost is real and is filed, not absorbed:** that subject also loses its `dl_number` stamp with no signal at all, because `correlationRefs()` asks `DlTokenGrammar::sole()` and gets null. Naming a lost STAMP is a different signal from naming a lost MOVE and needs its own site — card#5961, which also carries the second thing left silent here. **[card#5961 BUILT that site: the warning is now emitted in `stampRefs()`, where the DL result is consumed, guarded on `parse() === null && looksLikeDlToken()`. `correlationRefs()` in the sentence above names no method that has ever existed in this repo — the site that asks `sole()` and gets null is `stampRefs()` itself (original preserved per the freeze rule; card#6025 tracks the phantom-reference class). This decision (6) is UNCHANGED — the near-miss probe still sits behind the both-null guard and this subject still draws no near-miss line from it (the CI lint's per-stem DL arm does warn there); what closed is the CONSEQUENCE, at its own site, with its own message. Read "with no signal at all" as the state at DL-273, not as current.]**

**Two warnings, not one merged line.** A subject that is a near-miss on both stems warns once per grammar, each line naming its own accept-set. A merged line would have to pick one grammar's sentence or restate both; the shape is pinned by a test so a later "de-duplicate the warnings" edit reds instead of silently choosing.

**STATED BOUND — the Unicode-digit DL is silent on BOTH surfaces, which is worse than the card token's position and is why card#5961 exists.** The probe's digit class is ASCII by ratification (DL-231, upheld by DL-250), so `DL-<U+0663>239` — one of the three shapes card#5310 named — does not warn at runtime. For the CARD stem that is acceptable because `pr-title-lint.yml`'s DL-234 step covers the class BY NAME in its operator text. **There is no DL arm on that step at all**, so for the DL stem nothing covers it anywhere. Scoping this build to the runtime surface therefore shipped the half DL-234's own alternative (d) called insufficient (*"the author-facing gate is the PR check"*) — deliberately, on scope, and named here rather than left for the next reader to discover as an absence. **[SUPERSEDED as a code-state claim by card#5961: that step now carries a `looks_dl=`/`good_dl=` arm beside its card one, same step, same severity, with the non-ASCII-digit class named in its operator text. The runtime half of the bound STANDS — the probe is still ASCII, DL-231 is not reopened — so what changed is that the DL stem reached the card stem's position rather than the bound being lifted.]**

**Alternatives considered:** (a) **Duplicate the probe into `DlTokenGrammar`** — rejected per (1); it is the restatement shape one level up, and a future separator-semantics fix would then have to be made twice.
