For the subject `Guard against DL-9 (card_4811)` / head `fix/4811-guard`: `card_4811` does not parse (underscore separator), so both surfaces resolved null; the near-miss probe was skipped because a DL DID parse (its both-null guard); `DL-9` correlated; `cardConflicts(null, [7])` returned **false**; and the DL-218 arm — which exists precisely to stop a descriptive or foreign DL outranking an intentional `card#` — never ran. **The DL's card moved and was stamped with this PR's `pr_number`/`pr_url`, with zero warnings.** The stamped `pr_number` then feeds DL-270 corroboration and release-promote on a card the PR never touched. A near-miss spelling of the card token switched the guard off; that is the whole bug.

**Decision 1 — the card token is THREE-state: absent / parsed / unreadable(id).** The predicate is replaced by one that returns a `CardTokenVerdict` (`DlWins`, `CardTokenAuthoritative`, `NearMissRedundant`, `NearMissRefusal`) rather than a bool, and every one of the **three** consumers of it — the move path, the branch-create `started` push, and the draft overlay — reads that verdict. One predicate, as DL-218 established (canon #5): the blindness was in the predicate, so a fix at any one call site would have left the other two carrying it.

**Decision 2 — the near-miss id comes from the EXISTING probe, as a capturing sibling; never a fourth pattern.** `NearMissProbe::id()` captures the digit run `matches()` already had to match, and `matches()` is now DERIVED from it (`id($text) !== null`), so the two cannot disagree about what a near-miss is. `CardTokenGrammar::nearMissCardId()` binds it to the card stem beside `looksLikeCardToken()`. DL-239(h) / DL-250(1) stand: the near-miss SET is unchanged, and a fourth hand-written regex was the alternative that mints the drift those entries exist to remove.

**Decision 3 — an unreadable token that names one of the DL's own cards is REDUNDANT, not a refusal.** This is the leg that separates the shipped rule from "refuse on the bare shape" (candidate B, rejected): B refuses on SPELLING, so a prose-ish `card_4811` mention in a title would block an otherwise-correct DL move **even where it names the DL's own card**, and recovery would need `bridge:replay` (a title edit re-fires nothing). The redundant arm logs `info` and lets the DL win, mirroring the agreeing-arm precedent the parsed token already had. Everything else — a differing id, or an id the probe cannot pin to a resolved card — refuses. **What the redundant arm rescues is bounded, and stating it as "the leg that keeps ordinary prose citations working" OVERSTATES the separation from B:** it keeps a prose citation of **the DL's own card** working, and nothing wider. A near-miss-spelled citation of a DIFFERENT card — the ordinary "see also `card_4811`" in a title whose DL resolves elsewhere — is refused by the SHIPPED rule too, identically to B, so B's own cost statement above (`bridge:replay` is the recovery; a title edit re-fires nothing) applies unchanged to the shipped rule for that input class. The two rules differ over WHICH citations survive, not over whether prose citations survive at all; the shipped one is narrower than B by exactly the redundant set.

**Decision 4 — the refusal is HANDLER plumbing over the classifier's predicate, so it ALERTS.** The classifier emits its move target(s) carrying `card_token_near_miss: true` and `KanbanMoveCardHandler` refuses them through `WritebackAlertNotifier::warnAndNotify` — the one primitive every permanent refusal uses (DL-274 / DL-285). Dropping the target at classify time was the alternative and was rejected on exactly that ground: it would be a third **log-only** refusal branch, the shape DL-274 spent a card removing. The gate sits before the client is built — a refused move needs no card read, and a missing/insecure token must not 5xx-retry an event that is permanently refused. It carries no stamp refs: a refused move writes nothing at all.

**Decision 5 — HARD BOUND, written into the code: the recovered id may REFUSE or WARN, never SELECT.** It is read only as a member test against ids the DL resolved on its own. The precedent is `refCorroborates` / DL-270(b'): corroboration is deliberately wider than selection, and a bare id can confirm a token but never produce one. Same rule here — otherwise every spelling the grammar rejects becomes a correlation channel through the back door, which is what `CardTokenGrammar::PATTERN` decides against. The redundancy arm is written as the narrow POSITIVE test, so anything the probe cannot pin to a resolved card lands on the refusing side rather than the permissive one.

**OPERATOR GATE — the refuse half was APPROVED (2026-08-13), asked before any code was written.** Refusing changes what the bridge accepts, so it is a hard gate (canon #14). The ask carried the blast radius below and a recommendation to approve; the ruling approved refusing a move when a DL resolves beside an UNREADABLE card token naming a different card. The warn half needed no gate and would have shipped either way.

**BLAST RADIUS — 0 of 1,118 historical PRs, measured through the shipped grammars via the dev autoloader (never a re-implemented regex), with a positive control.** 520 PRs on this repo + 598 on the kanban repo: card-shaped-but-unparsed = **0**, so this refuses nothing that has ever happened here. Control: 3 synthetic rows including the repro were all caught while the historical count stayed 0, so the instrument could see one. **Bounds, stated rather than left implied:** "a DL RESOLVES" was approximated by "a DL PARSES" (an upper bound, and it measured 0, so it is exact); deleted branch names are un-enumerable, so the push surface is only partially covered (9 live branches, 0 hits); and only the 2 writeback-mapped repos were measured.

**STATED BOUNDS — recorded, deliberately not "fixed".** (a) A malformed TITLE token beside a PARSING BRANCH token stays invisible: the branch is authoritative (DL-270), so the question of which card is named is already settled and a misspelling beside it changes nothing. (b) A pure-overlay event (`converted_to_draft` / `ready_for_review`) inherits the refusal through the shared predicate, with **no** diagnostic — the same no-double-log split DL-218 made for its own conflict, on the lower-harm surface that ruling was about. **It suppresses BOTH directions, and the one-directional wording this bound originally carried ("no `block_reason` lands on the DL's card") hid the second:** `correlatedCardIds()` returns `ids: []` for `ready_for_review` exactly as for `converted_to_draft`, so a marker SET under an earlier title is also never CLEARED. Reachable, on a `draft_overlay` mapping: a PR opened-as-draft titled `DL-9 fix` sets `PR is in draft` on the DL's card; the title is then edited to `DL-9 fix (card_4811)`; `ready_for_review` now reads NearMissRefusal and emits no overlay target, so the card keeps the marker for as long as that title stands. The residual is not inert — `PinGuard::isPinned()` reads a non-empty `block_reason` as a human pin, so a later `started` promotion of that card is refused (loudly, `pinned_no_automove`) on a pin the PR left behind; the refusal is signalled, its cause is not. **Disclosed, not fixed:** giving the overlay a diagnostic here re-opens the DL-218 double-log ruling, and the harm is a stale marker rather than a wrong write. (c) The digit class stays ASCII (DL-231 is not reopened); a Unicode-digit near-miss is invisible to the probe and covered by name in the CI PR-title lint. (d) The design's "or no recoverable id" arm was **not built**: with the capturing sibling, a probe match implies a captured digit run, so an unreadable-token-with-no-id state is unreachable and a branch for it would be defending against a state that cannot happen (canon #6). The refusing side is the negation of the redundancy test, so if that ever became reachable it would refuse, not select. (e) **The BARE-SPACE spelling is a live residual of exactly the harm this entry closes, one separator away from the shipped repro.** `NearMissProbe::SEPARATORS` excludes `' '` deliberately — DL-201 ruled prose ("supports card 2") warns nowhere and DL-250(6) recorded that ruling ON the data so no later stem could widen into it — so for `Guard against DL-9 (card 4811)` on head `fix/4811-guard` the probe answers null: `token=null`, `nearMissId=null`, verdict `DlWins`, and DL-9's card moves and is stamped with this PR's refs with no warning of any kind, which is the defect at the top of this entry with a space where the underscore was. Measured through the shipped grammars rather than inferred (`CardTokenGrammar::parse()` and `nearMissCardId()` both return null on that subject; the `card_4811` spelling recovers `4811` as the positive control). It is left open because closing it means adding the bare space to the ONE shared separator list, which reopens DL-201/DL-250(6) for every stem and widens the warn surface far beyond anything this card measured — a ruling-level change, not a bound this entry may take. `docs/writeback.md` discloses the bare-space near-miss silence where the near-miss set is written for operators; this bound is what that silence now costs at the DL-win sites.

**Sibling audit (canon #7) — one open instance of the same shape, NOT fixed here, because closing it is a separate gate.** The shape is *"a card-shaped token that does not parse is invisible to the guard that would have used it."* Re-read rather than grepped: a malformed token in the **head branch** beside a **parsing title** token — `Fix card#5287` on `fix/card_4811-slug` — is the reverse of bound (a) and is NOT covered. The authoritative surface is the unreadable one there, and the title's card is selected (marked uncorroborated, so DL-270's handler gate is the only thing between it and a move). Refusing it would be a NEW validation change beyond the approved gate, and its shape is not the one that was measured, so it is disclosed here and reported to the card rather than widened in silently.

**Adjacent honesty fix, shipped with this.** The FR-7 **no-move** arms (a DL that resolves to nothing with no `card#` fallback, on both the move and push paths) now call `warnTokenNearMiss()`. Nothing moves on those arms, so the near-miss line's own "no move" clause is TRUE about them — which is the DL-234(e) whole-subject condition, satisfied, not widened. To make that safe the probe helper now asks each grammar's `parse()` before probing its stem: at the both-null call site that is implied by the caller's guard (byte-identical answer), and at the new call sites it is what keeps the line from telling an operator that a DL which parsed does not parse.

**Tests — every leg was watched fail, and each states HOW.** **10 new legs:** 7 in `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` (the repro end-to-end with a TOTAL-warning-count assert; the push mirror through the shared predicate; the redundant arm on each surface — `info`, no warning, no flag; the pure-overlay inheritance; and both no-move arms) and 3 in `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` (refused before any read; the refusal ALERTS with `reason=card_token_near_miss`; and an unflagged target unaffected). **8 were written first and observed red against the unfixed code**, each on the defect's own signature — `Undefined array key "card_token_near_miss"`, the DL's card emitted clean, the missing `info`, `Requests were recorded`. The other **2 were green when written and were made to fail by mutation instead**, which is the same evidence obtained the other way round and is stated rather than glossed: the push-surface redundant leg (its arm removed ⇒ red) and the unflagged-target negative control (the gate made unconditional ⇒ red). **11 mutations, each applied singly and restored by `cp`+`cmp` (never `git checkout --`), measured over the subset that can see them** (`tests/Feature/{Classifiers,Handlers,Support,Writeback,Workflows}` — 796/796 green as the control): the recovered id SELECTS the card ⇒ **10 red**, including DL-250's grammar-driven corpus leg (`'card4' must not correlate`) — the hard bound is enforced by the suite, not by this prose; the predicate reads unreadable as absent again (the shipped defect) ⇒ 4 red; the push consumer left unfixed ⇒ 1 red; the overlay consumer left unfixed ⇒ 1 red; the handler ignoring the flag ⇒ 2 red; refuse on the bare SHAPE (candidate B) ⇒ 1 red — the redundant arm, which is exactly the leg that should object; each no-move probe removed ⇒ 1 red each; the push redundant arm removed ⇒ 1 red; dropping the per-stem `parse()` check ⇒ 3 red, one of them the DL-corpus leg's exact warning COUNT; and the refusal gate made unconditional ⇒ **58 red**, the negative control among them. **Pins re-run and green:** the DL-234(e) whole-subject suppression, the DL-201/DL-250(6) prose silence (`card 2` warns nowhere), the DL-218 conflict legs' single warning, the overlay silence legs, and `PrTitleLintTest` (untouched — no grammar and no lint changed). **2223/2223 phpunit (6819 assertions)** — 2213 before, +10 — phpstan L7 0, pint clean, `check-doc-refs` clean.

**Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Writeback/CardTokenVerdict.php`; `NearMissProbe` (capturing sibling, `matches()` derived from it); `CardTokenGrammar` (`nearMissCardId()`); `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` (three-state resolution, the verdict predicate at all three consumers, the refusal warning + flag, the honest no-move arms, the per-stem probe guard); `KanbanMoveCardHandler` (the `card_token_near_miss` refusal arm); `docs/writeback.md`; `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **No config key, no migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change** — the only behaviour change is that a move which today happens onto the wrong card is refused and alerted. Card #6027; DL-218, DL-231, DL-234, DL-250, DL-270, DL-273, DL-274, DL-285.

## DL-288 — the changelog gate's CI half takes composer.json, composer.lock and .env.example; the npm pair beside them is DISCLOSED, not inherited (card#6137)

- **Date:** 2026-08-17
- **Status:** implemented (card#6137). **Extends DL-280/DL-282; supersedes neither.** The CI-half criterion at `changelog-gate.yml` — *what CI ACCEPTS OR REJECTS, which is shipped behaviour for a contributor* — is unchanged; what changes is which files are measured against it. **No claim of criterion-completeness is made here either**, and DL-282's withdrawal of that claim stands.

**What DL-282 left, and why it could not stay.** It recorded three files as DISCLOSED ACCEPTED GAPS rather than verified exclusions, because their real mechanisms were named rather than denied. One of the two reasons offered for `composer.json` — *"no CI step runs a composer script"* — was **already withdrawn as false in the same commit that shipped the entry**; that half was never in force. The surviving reason — *a dependency change alters the subject under test rather than the gate's own rule* — is not an application of the criterion but a proposed **amendment** to it, and the operator ruled against the amendment: `composer.json:14-23` pins `larastan/larastan`, `laravel/pint` and `phpunit/phpunit`, which ARE the analysers `laravel-tests.yml` runs, and `composer.json:9`'s platform constraint fails `composer install` outright. A change to those changes what CI accepts, directly and by four independent mechanisms.

**Decision 1 — three members join the anchored group; the branch exemption is untouched.** `composer.json`, `composer.lock`, `.env.example`, anchored `^…$` like every other root-file member. `changelog-gate.yml`'s `dependabot/*|release/*|sync/*|revert-*` exemption is deliberately not touched and is what keeps the cost at one PR shape.

**BLAST RADIUS — one commit in 125, re-derived independently by the reviewer rather than trusted.** Over `v0.70.0..dev` (125 first-parent): `composer.json` **0** commits, `.env.example` **0**, `composer.lock` **12**, of which **11** are `dependabot[bot]` on `dependabot/*` branches and therefore already exempt. The single human-authored one is `a864bd9` — a `league/commonmark` **GHSA** bump touching `composer.lock` and nothing else, with no card/DL token in its title and no `docs/CHANGELOG.md` change — i.e. the one PR this catches is a security bump that shipped undocumented. A premise the measurement silently rests on was checked separately: `.github/dependabot.yml` sets no `pull-request-branch-name` prefix override, so all 11 really are on `dependabot/*`. Independently confirmed: **0 of those 11 touches `docs/CHANGELOG.md`**, which is why the branch exemption is load-bearing rather than incidental — that fact is now pinned by a test instead of living in prose.

**⛔ Decision 2 — the npm manifest pair is recorded as a NEWLY DISCLOSED CI-half gap, in this same change, and is NOT inherited from DL-282.** `examples/channel-servers/package.json` and `examples/channel-servers/package-lock.json` meet the CI-half criterion on the identical mechanism used to justify `composer.lock`: `channel-server-supply-chain.yml:66` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (failing the PR on manifest/lock drift), `:72` runs `npm audit --audit-level=high` reading the lockfile as **that gate's own rule input**, `:102`/`:108` run a version-bump guard reading the `version` field of **both** files and failing on disagreement, and `provision-tools-python.yml:88` runs a second `npm ci` against the same lockfile.

⚠ **This is the defect shape DL-282 itself named** — *"fixing 2 of 5 IS the guard-reads-a-proper-subset defect shape … re-minted one directory down"* — and without this disclosure the change would have discharged a card-owned gap list while the repo demonstrably knew of another gap, leaving the CI half's recorded gap set empty and false. **The exposure is not theoretical and this repo has already measured it:** `.github/dependabot.yml`'s header records that security updates are disabled here, that **17 of 19 lifetime alerts (89%) were npm on that exact lockfile**, and that the surviving path is *"anything urgent is hand-cut as a PR to `dev`"* — a human, hand-cut, lockfile-only security bump on a non-exempt branch, which is `a864bd9`'s shape exactly, one directory over.

⭐ **Recorded because it is the more useful lesson: DL-282 HAD the evidence and used it in the other direction.** Its *Verified exclusions* paragraph disposes of the ROOT `package.json` with *"the two `npm ci` steps run with `working-directory: examples/channel-servers`, against that directory's own manifest, not the root one."* The sentence is still literally true and is annotated rather than contradicted — but it points straight at the nested pair and never turns the question around on it. **An exclusion argument that names the file it is not about is where the next gap hides.** Widening to reach the pair is a separate operator ruling and is deliberately NOT taken here.

**Controls — four, each observed RED, each restored by snapshot + `cmp`, never `git checkout --`.** Dropping `composer.lock` from `VERSIONING.md`'s scope row → 38/39 naming it (the one that mattered: the round's own rewording of that cell could have broken the leg's field extraction and made it vacuous — it did not, the failure message shows the cell isolated at 317 chars). Deleting the `composer.lock` row from the `PATH SCOPE` table → 38/39. Moving `pint.json` into the prefix alternation, and `bin/` into the anchored alternation → each reds the new regime assertion. ⚠ **A fifth attempt silently DID NOT APPLY and the suite came back green at 39/39** — caught by the harness's per-replacement applied-check, not by the result. A mutation that does not apply reports as a passing control; only the applied-check separates the two.

**Decision 3 — the scope's two-regime invariant is now DERIVED, not counted.** The surfaces previously carried the numeral *"seven root files"*, the only scope fact `test_every_scope_enumeration_is_derived_from_the_predicate` did not cover — a future widening would have left it false at green, and this change had to hand-edit it. Both surfaces now state the **rule** (every prefix-group member ends in `/`, every anchored-group member does not), and the derivation leg asserts it (+11 assertions, so provably non-vacuous), pinning the invariant DL-282 Decision 2 rests on and nothing previously covered.

**Log annotations — three, all ADDITIVE, zero words removed (`git diff --word-diff` verified).** Appended to DL-282's *surviving argument* paragraph (scoped to the whole DISCLOSED ACCEPTED GAPS block: records the discharge, withdraws the surviving argument, carries the npm gap forward), a standalone supersession line after the fenced predicate literal (which deliberately does NOT restate the current predicate — a fifth hand-maintained copy is the defect DL-282 closed), and a count-only supersession on *Decision 2 — the four root files*. ⚠ **Correction to the precedent as it was briefed:** two of the three prior annotations (DL-280 *Stated bound*, DL-281 *Consequences*) close with the frozen-original formula attributed to DL-277; the third (DL-276 Decision 4) carries no such formula and states the opposite — that rewriting in place was *"a convention set HERE, not one this log already had."* All three blocks here are original prose and take the additive form.

**Tests — one stale pointer repaired by re-pointing, per DL-276 Decision 4.** DL-282's *Controls* paragraph names `dl282InScopeMemberProvider` and *"5 of 8, as fixture paths"*. That provider is renamed `rootCiConfigMemberProvider` (ruling-specific names go stale, which is the reason for the rename) and the figures are now **8 of 11**. Recorded here rather than as a fourth annotation.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **The rename escape is still open and untouched:** the gate reads `git diff --name-only`, so its verdict depends on git's rename detection — a file moved into or out of an in-scope path can be recorded as delete+add. Real, on this same card, deliberately out of scope. (b) The MariaDB matrix leg was not run locally (SQLite only here). (c) No criterion-completeness claim is made or reintroduced; every `complete`/`exhaust` in the new prose is a negation, and the npm pair is cited by name as the live instance of the difference.

## DL-289 — the PR-title gate inspects every branch that NAMES a card id, and one regex both decides and extracts it (card#6822)

- **Date:** 2026-08-18
- **Status:** implemented (card#6822). **Corrects DL-182 in exactly one clause — its accept-set — and supersedes nothing.** The token grammar, the `edited` trigger, the unconditional near-miss warning (DL-234) and the digit-class narrowing (DL-272) are all untouched and re-confirmed.

**What DL-182 established, and the half that stopped being true.** DL-182 made a card-id branch's PR title carry a `card#<id>` / `DL-NNNN` token, because that token is the ONLY key the writeback has. It defined "card-id branch" as `^[a-z-]+/[0-9]+-`. **The rule survives; the accept-set does not.** The house branch style drifted to the `card`-prefixed spellings, and a guard whose accept-set no longer describes the population it guards **passes green having enforced nothing** — the same silent-success shape DL-182 was written to abolish, re-minted one layer up, in the classifier instead of the token arm.

**Decision 1 — the accept-set is "a run of ASCII digits followed by a hyphen, optionally prefixed `card`/`card-`, optionally preceded by a `<type>/` segment."** So `fix/6100-slug` (DL-182's shape, unchanged), `card6027-slug`, `card-5538-slug`, `fix/card6371-slug` and `chore/card-5913-slug` all name a card id. **⚠ This is an accept/reject change:** a PR on either newly-reached spelling whose title carries no token now REDS where it passed.

**Decision 2 — the predicate and the id EXTRACTION become one regex (`BASH_REMATCH`), and this is not a tidy-up.** The extraction was a second parse — `${branch_lc#*/}` then a `%%-*` chop — that agreed with the predicate on exactly the one shape the predicate accepted. **Widening the predicate alone would have yielded `card6371` for the prefixed shape and the WHOLE BRANCH NAME for the segment-less one**, i.e. a gate that fires and then compares against a malformed id: loudly wrong instead of quietly absent, which is worse than the defect being fixed. Two copies of one decision is DL-182's real residue here (canon #5). Side effect worth naming: the old chop could place arbitrary branch text into the token arm's regex; `([0-9]+)` structurally cannot.

**MEASUREMENT — and ⚠ the two derivations disagree for a reason that was MEASURED, not assumed.** Over the merged subset of the newest 100 closed PRs, minus `dependabot/*`/`release/*`/`sync/*`/`revert-*`: on the newest **60 merged**, 35 branches — 16 old-reached, 6 segment-less, 7 prefixed, 6 card-less ⇒ **13 of 29 card-bearing PRs (45%) merged with nothing enforcing the writeback's only key**; over the full **96 merged** refs, **33** branches move skipped→enforced. card#6822 recorded 18/7/7/6 over a **different** window: `gh pr list --state merged --limit 60` orders by MERGE recency (oldest merge `2026-08-04`), while the derivation above is ordered by PR number and reaches back to a merge of `2026-07-29`. **Both reproduce exactly over the population each names — re-running the card's command returns the card's figures unchanged.** This is not window drift and was not left as one; ⇒ **any future re-count must state which window it used.** The shapes and the conclusion are identical either way.

**⛔ The prefixed shape is the finding, not the segment-less one.** `fix/card6371-…` and `chore/card-5913-…` DO follow the `<type>/…-slug` convention and read as compliant to a human reviewer. Only the literal `card` sitting between the slash and the digits put them outside the regex. A convention violation you can see is not the dangerous kind.

**Decision 3 — the guard moved, the branch names did not.** Renaming the offending branches would satisfy the old regex and leave the next `fix/card<NNNN>-` branch free to re-mint the silence (canon #2/#5). The header no longer restates WHICH spellings qualify — that set is owned by the require step's own predicate, for the same reason the token grammar is not restated there, and now with the same measured history: the set this header used to name is precisely the one that went stale while nothing noticed.

**Controls — 7 mutations of the real workflow, each applied, measured, and restored by snapshot.** The pre-fix predicate+extraction pair (6 legs red); **the named trap — predicate widened with the old extraction kept (5 legs red, exactly the `card`-prefixed rows)**; the `tr` case-fold removed (2); the exemption `case` removed (2); the trailing `-` dropped (3); the `^` anchor dropped (4); `BASH_REMATCH[3]`→`[2]` (9). Assertions read the **extracted id out of the step's own output**, so a malformed id cannot pass a leg that merely fired: the desync leg pins `card6371`/`card`/`card6027`/`card` against `6371`/`5913`/`6027`/`5538`.

⚠ **Two of the builder's own premises were falsified by its own checks and corrected before ship**, which is why they are recorded rather than the conclusions alone: (a) the trailing `-` was claimed to exclude `feat/oauth2-login` — measurement showed the `^` anchor does, and the leg is now split into two axes each paired with rows it actually flips; (b) the digitless rows were claimed as negative controls — they cannot flip under ANY widening, so they are population coverage, not controls. The real negative controls are `fix/cards-123-thing` (plural), `feat/oauth2-login` and `fix/2fa-enrollment`, each swallowed by a specific over-widening. Separately, *"every real exempt branch fails the predicate anyway"* is now **measured** (0 of 29) rather than asserted, which is why the `skip:exempt` rows are synthetic.

**Case-folding is preserved and now PINNED.** DL-182's `branch_lc`/`title_lc` fold (bridge #4384 — the classifier's regexes are `/i`, so a title the classifier correlates must never red here on case alone) is a real divergence from the co-vendored kanban-board copy. A leg removes the `tr` and watches an upper-case card branch go unreachable; `FIX/CARD6371-Stage-Aware-…` → `6371` and `Card-5538-…` → `5538` are asserted.

**⛔ DISCLOSED NEW FALSE RED, characterized rather than discovered later.** With both optionals empty the shape is a bare leading `<digits>-`, so `2026-08-18-notes` is enforced as card 2026. Absent from the corpus, as is a bare `5538-slug`. **Taken deliberately: the failure it risks is LOUD and the defect it closes is SILENT**, and that trade only runs one direction. Pinned as a test row so the choice is legible rather than latent.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) **Nothing ran on a GitHub runner** — the require step's bash was executed by the repo's own harness against the real `run:` body; per the repo's testing doc nothing local validates Actions YAML *as* a workflow. The first real exercise is this PR's own run, and ⚠ **that run cannot exercise the NEW shapes**: the branch `fix/6822-…` satisfies the OLD accept-set too, so a green there proves no-regression, not the widening. **The new shapes' first real exercise is the next `card<NNNN>-` PR on this repo.** (b) The kanban-board copy is the same class (kanban card#6820, DL-244, shipped) and is a separate repo, board and gate — deliberately not touched here.
