## DL-295 — the DL number is ALLOCATED from the board counter and vetoed against local checkouts; CI refuses a number already in use, and says out loud what it cannot see (card#7157)

- **Date:** 2026-08-21
- **Status:** implemented (card#7157). **⛔ Operator-approved.** Adds a contributor tool (`bin/decision-log.py`) and a new CI gate (`.github/workflows/dl-collision-gate.yml`) — **it changes what CI accepts for a contributor**, and nothing about what the receiver accepts or rejects. No migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change, no `app/` file touched.

**The defect.** This repo had no DL-minting tool. `next-dl` lives in the toolkit repo and is not vendored here, so the only in-repo way to pick a number was the maximum `DL-` header in `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md`, plus one. **That method structurally cannot see a mint that has not been pushed.** Two agents cutting branches off the same `dev` tip read the same maximum and write the same number; neither tree contradicts the other until merge, and by then the loser's number is already in a decision entry, a CHANGELOG line, several commit messages and a PR title. The failure is **silent, permanent and cross-cutting**: nothing rejects it, review cannot see it (each PR's log is internally consistent), and once both land the log has two entries claiming one identifier — an identifier cited across repos, in card titles, and by the writeback's own card-correlation grammar. Measured near-miss 2026-08-21: `card-7127-…` and `card-7138-…` both read max 290; the second only avoided minting 291 because the first's in-flight remediation string surfaced in an unrelated test failure during a mutation run. **The correct outcome there was luck, not method.**

**Decision 1 — the number comes from the board's counter, and the tool REFUSES rather than falling back to a scan.** `bin/decision-log.py next` shells out to the toolkit's `next-dl bridge`, which claims atomically from the board's DL sequence **when that endpoint answers** — the only source that can see a number claimed by another allocator moments ago. ⛔ **When it does not answer, `next-dl` falls back to a `max + 1` scan silently, at rc 0 with an empty stderr, and this tool prints that guess as an allocation** — bound (e) below states it verbatim, with the measurements, and the fix is filed upstream as toolkit card#7214. When that allocator is not on PATH the command **exits 3 and prints nothing on stdout**. It was tempting to fall back to the header scan so the tool always answers; that is precisely the method this entry exists to retire, and performing it under a tool's name would launder the same hazard rather than fix it. The board project (`bridge`) is pinned in the tool, because the bridge sequence is per-board and a caller who has to remember the argument can mint out of the kanban-board sequence instead.

**Decision 2 — the tool VETOES the allocated number against every decision log this host can reach, which is the half the counter cannot do.** An entry written on a branch that was never pushed is invisible server-side, so the counter can hand back a number another agent is already writing. The veto enumerates **this clone's worktrees** (`git worktree list`) plus anything matched by `BRIDGE_DL_CHECKOUT_GLOBS` (default `~/agent-webhook-bridge-*`), and refuses with exit 4 naming the file. **The worktree leg is what the incident needed and no existing tool had:** the three branches involved lived in two throwaway worktrees plus the main checkout, and the toolkit's own offline glob (`~/agent-webhook-bridge-*`) matches only the last of those. **The veto was not exercised on a planted case — it refused a LIVE one.** Run on this branch while the card#7157 dispatch was in flight, `next --peek` reported the counter's next number as 294 and then refused it, naming the `~/agent-webhook-bridge-dev` checkout's `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md`, which already carried an unpushed `DL-294` entry. Without the veto the next agent to allocate would have been handed a number another agent had already written — the card's incident, reproduced without being staged. When git cannot enumerate the worktrees the tool **warns that the veto is narrower than it looks** rather than degrading quietly — a clean result over an unnamed population reports where the searcher stopped, not the state of the world. Separately, when a local log carries a number at or above the one the counter returned, the tool warns that the counter is BEHIND this host: that allocation is still free, but the *next* one will collide. It is a warn, not a refusal, because the predicate for a refusal is "this number is in use" and nothing wider.

**Decision 3 — the CI gate refuses a number already in use, and its stated scope equals its predicate.** `.github/workflows/dl-collision-gate.yml` runs `bin/decision-log.py check` on every PR and makes exactly two assertions: the log at head uses no number twice (which catches a mint colliding with the PR's own base, because the log is append-only), and no number the PR *adds* is already in use at the **live tip** of the target branch (which catches a number `dev` took after the branch was cut — read by fetching, since neither snapshot the gate already holds contains it). **The snapshot it calls the base is the FIRST PARENT of the merge commit the job is standing on — `HEAD^1`, read by `bin/pr-base-snapshot.sh`, deliberately NOT the merge base and — since card#8527 measured it lagging — deliberately NOT the event's `base.sha` either** — and "present at head, absent at base" means "this PR minted it" only because the head it is paired with is `github.sha`, that same merge. The pairing is the invariant; it is owned by the workflow's own comment, and it is now true BY CONSTRUCTION rather than on GitHub's word, because the base end is the commit the head end records as its parent (bound (f), and the amendment below it). **⛔ STATED BOUND, and it is the one people assume away: it does NOT catch two OPEN PRs that each mint the same new number.** Neither number is on `dev` yet and neither PR's file contains the other's entry, so both are green; the second reds only when it is re-checked *after* the first merges, which is a re-run, not a consequence of the merge — a PR last checked before that merge carries a stale green. Both halves of that bound are pinned by tests rather than left as prose. The gate is also **not a required status check** until an operator adds it to branch protection; until then it reds visibly but does not physically block a merge.

**Decision 4 — one grammar for `DL-` headers, owned by one file.** The allocator's veto and the gate's predicate ask the same question, so they read headers through the same function. A DL entry is an H2 whose text begins `DL-` and digits — deliberately not a search for the token anywhere, because this log embeds kanban-board cross-references ("Mirrors kanban-board DL-196") that a bare grep counts as bridge entries (measured returning 197 when the real maximum was 188). Headers inside a fenced code block are skipped: an entry that shows what a header looks like is documentation, and treating it as a second entry would refuse the very change that documents this file.

**⚑ Operator-facing note — this hazard is CREATED by parallel dispatch, and the cheap mitigation is legitimate.** A single agent working serially cannot hit it; it appeared the first session two agents were dispatched at one repo, and during the card#7157 dispatch itself the operator had to **hand-assign 294/295/296** to three agents to prevent exactly this. **"Do not run two DL-minting agents at once" is a real resolution and is written down here as one** rather than left as an unstated assumption the next parallel dispatch violates. What this entry buys is that the hazard is no longer *silent* when that assumption is broken — which is the part hand-assignment cannot provide, because it depends on the operator remembering.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Vendor the toolkit's `next-dl` into `bin/`** — rejected: it is 336 lines plus a shared library, and a second copy of an allocator that already exists is the divergent-duplication defect this repo keeps filing. Delegating to it keeps one implementation and adds only what this repo needs (the pinned project, the local veto, the refusal to fall back). (b) **A CI gate alone** — rejected as sufficient: it is a backstop that fires after a number is already written into four artifacts, and it cannot see a number claimed but unwritten. (c) **The tool alone** — rejected as sufficient: it is bypassed by anyone who types a number by hand, which is the current default. (a)+(b) together is what the card recommended and what shipped. (d) **Mint from the board's `dl` custom field instead of the counter** — rejected, and it is the reason (a) is not enough on its own: that projection returned null on all 264 board-8 cards when it was checked as a cross-source, so a caller treating it as authoritative would read a confident zero. (e) **Assert that a minted number EXCEEDS the target branch's maximum** — rejected: the operator hand-assigns blocks, so the PR carrying 295 legitimately lands after the one carrying 296. The predicate is "already in use", never "must be highest", and a test pins that a lower-but-free number passes.

**STATED BOUNDS.** (a) The gate reads three files and knows nothing about a number **claimed from the counter but not yet written** into any log, and nothing about a checkout on **another host**; `next` covers the first and neither covers the second. (b) The veto's population is this clone's worktrees plus one glob — a checkout outside both is not covered, and the tool says so when it cannot enumerate them. (c) `next` was exercised against a **fake allocator** on PATH: what is tested is what this tool does with the number it is handed, not the toolkit's claim path or the board endpoint behind it. (d) Appending entries at end-of-file means two agents minting concurrently will hit a **git merge conflict** in this file. That is deliberate and is the good failure — visible, at merge, before either number is final.

(e) ⛔ **THE ATOMICITY IS THE ALLOCATOR'S AND IT IS CONDITIONAL — and its condition fails SILENTLY, which is the one silent failure mode left in a change whose whole thesis is that the retired method failed silently.** The bound is `next-dl`'s own, recorded verbatim rather than paraphrased. Its header: *"If the endpoint is absent (older kanban / not deployed) or unreachable, it falls back SILENTLY to the offline max+1 scan"*, and *"the offline path is NOT atomic — safe for single-stream allocation; concurrent allocators on a shared board need the claim endpoint (the default) to avoid duplicates"*. Its transport says the same at the two arms that take that path: `resp="$(curl …)" || exit 1` — *"connection failure → benign fallback"* — and `kb_is_uint "$val" && [[ "$val" -ge 1 ]] || exit 1` — *"2xx but no positive value → benign fallback"*. Only a non-2xx other than 404 aborts. On the benign arm `next-dl bridge` prints a `max + 1` guess, **exits 0, and writes nothing to stderr**, and `bin/decision-log.py next` prints it as an allocation: two agents there get one number, which is this card's own defect wearing a tool's name. **Both halves measured, 2026-08-21, not inferred.** The live board answers `GET /boards/8/dl-sequence.json` with HTTP 200 `{"board_id":8,"last_value":289,"live_max":296,"next":297}`, so the endpoint IS deployed and today's primary path is genuinely atomic — the silent path needs a 404 or a connection failure on the CLAIM route. Against a stub board answering 404 there, `next-dl bridge` printed `DL-0294` at rc 0 with an empty stderr and `decision-log.py next` printed `DL-294`. **Recorded here, deliberately not cross-checked in this repo**, and the alternative was measured rather than argued: under the same stub `next-dl bridge --peek` printed `DL-0294` too, because both routes degrade to the SAME offline scan — a claim-vs-peek compare would therefore agree exactly when the hazard is present, which is a decoration, not a check. Reading the endpoint directly from here would mean re-implementing the toolkit's board-config resolution and auth — alternative (a), already rejected above. The distinction exists only inside `next-dl`, which knows which arm answered, so the fix is filed where it can be made: **toolkit card#7214** (`--require-counter` strict mode plus a loud fallback). Until that ships, this is the bound, and `cmd_next`'s docstring and its refusal text carry it where an author meets the tool.

(f) ⛔ **SUPERSEDED BY THE CARD#8527 AMENDMENT BELOW — this bound was MEASURED TRUE and is now closed. Kept verbatim because it is the disclosure that made the incident legible, and deleting a bound that fired is how the next one gets waved off.** The gate's base WAS the PR's `base.sha`, and its correctness rested on a pairing GitHub supplies, which nothing in this repo could verify. Head is the working tree at `github.sha` — the merge of the PR head into that same `base.sha` — and only that makes `added` the PR's mints. Should the two ever disagree, a `base.sha` OLDER than the merge commit's base parent makes entries the base branch already carried read as this PR's mints (a loud, visible false refusal), and a NEWER one drops entries from `added` (a silent missed catch). `DlCollisionGateTest` pins the invariant on the inputs the step is handed — a fixture whose head is a real merge commit, with the fork point as the control that reds — but it cannot pin what GitHub hands it. Measured on this repo, 2026-08-21: `base.sha` is genuinely not the merge base — PR #542's `fe562910` is not even an ancestor of its head branch `270c236f`, whose merge base is `61e40d85` — which is why nothing in this change calls it one. Rewriting the step to derive its base with `git merge-base "$BASE" HEAD` is inert while the pairing holds (`$BASE` is then an ancestor of the merge, so `merge-base` returns `$BASE`; measured — every case stays green), and that is exactly what makes it dangerous: the first caller whose head is not that merge gets the fork point and the false refusal. The workflow comment says so at the line.

**⊕ AMENDMENT 2026-09-02 (card#8527) — BOUND (f) FIRED, WAS MEASURED, AND THE GATE NO LONGER TAKES THE CLAIM FROM THE PAYLOAD.** (f) said a `base.sha` older than the merge commit's base parent would make entries the base branch already carried read as this PR's mints, "a loud, visible false refusal", and that nothing in this repo could verify the pairing. **It happened, in the direction (f) named, twelve days later.** On PR #640, run 33598959720 (2026-09-02 06:28Z), the event carried `base.sha` `549c894` — the base tip when that branch was cut — while the merge commit `642decf` GitHub built for the SAME event has first parent `7a11085`, `dev`'s tip once #639 had merged. The step read `dev`'s own **DL-335** as a number the PR had minted and refused an innocent PR at rc 6. Reproduced from a clean checkout: `check --head <the merge ref's log> --base <549c894's log> --target <dev's log>` returns 6, and the same head against `7a11085` returns 0. **The mechanism is GitHub's, not this repo's: `pull_request.base.sha` is not refreshed on every `synchronize`, so it can lag the base tip the merge commit was actually computed against.**

**What changed.** The base is no longer an INPUT. `bin/pr-base-snapshot.sh` reads `HEAD^1` — the base commit the checked-out merge itself RECORDS — after asserting that HEAD is a two-parent merge whose second parent is the PR head sha the event names; failing either leg it prints no sha and exits non-zero, so a step that cannot say what its base IS reports no verdict rather than a wrong one. That closes (f) at the root: the pairing is true by construction instead of on GitHub's word, because the two ends are one commit's tree and that commit's own parent. **It is NOT the `git merge-base "$BASE" HEAD` rewrite this entry rejected, and that rejection stands** — `merge-base` RE-DERIVES a base from whatever head it is handed and hands the fork point to the first caller whose head is not the PR merge; `HEAD^1` derives nothing. Measured, and it is why the distinction is worth the paragraph: substituting `git merge-base` for the derivation is INERT on most of the workflow harness and red on a minority of it — the cases that pin the pairing, and card#8339's pre-fold diagnosis, which reads the base as well — the inertness (f) warned about, now with tests that catch it — including in the PRIMITIVE's own harness, which was itself inert to the substitution until this round: every `PrBaseSnapshotTest` fixture was linear, where `HEAD^1` and the fork point are the same commit, so the discrimination lived only in the callers' harnesses. `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` § *The PR base snapshot* owns the figures and the recipe that re-derives them (which mutation, which cases red, out of which denominator, at which head); they are not restated here because the denominator moves with every merge and the first copy of one drifted within one merge round. ⚑ **And the two-parent requirement's obvious worry — a PR whose branch has already merged the base — was MEASURED rather than argued: GitHub never fast-forwards `refs/pull/<n>/merge`.** Checked 2026-09-02 against the two open PRs on this repo in exactly that state (#635, merge `570d1dc`; #630, merge `6286dc9`): both are two-parent merges while `git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <head>` is true for each. A plain `git merge` in a FIXTURE does fast-forward there, which is why the workflow harnesses pass `--no-ff`; a fixture without it tests a shape GitHub would never hand a gate.

**Three gates beyond this one took the same field and were fixed in the same change (canon #7 — the class, not the instance):** `changelog-gate.yml` (both steps), `channel-server-supply-chain.yml`'s version-bump guard, and `release-artifacts-gate.yml`, which feeds a composite action's `base-sha` input and therefore derives the sha in its own step and passes it through a step output — the action is pinned by sha in another repo, so the derivation belongs at the call site. ⚠ **That fourth call site had NO live red on the PR #640 shape, and is moved for one derivation (canon #5), not for a defect — corrected here after R1 read the far end's contract.** The action's `action.yml` at the pinned sha consumes `base-sha` only to resolve `merge-base(base, head)`, and a lagging base cannot move that fork point unless the PR branch has itself merged the base: measured, a branch cut at B0 while the base advanced to B1 has `merge-base(B0,H) == merge-base(B1,H) == B0`; only a branch that merged B1 differs (`B0` vs `B1`), and there the stale sha puts the base's own `B0..B1` commits inside the asserted range. Three of the four callers had the live defect; this one had the narrow shape. `changelog-gate.yml`'s two SCOPE diffs also stop diffing against `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` and diff the WORK TREE instead: moving only the base end would have paired a fresher base with an independently-sourced head, which is the same defect on the other operand. **`$HEAD` remains an input there and is a DIFFERENT question, not a second spelling of the same one** — card#8339's pre-fold diagnosis asks where the branch STARTED and what the branch ADDS to the base's text, properties of the branch's own history that a merge commit's first-parent chain does not carry. ⭐ **card#8441 (the scope predicates' two-dot-vs-three-dot ruling) is CLOSED by this derivation, and PR #642's three-dot spelling is SUPERSEDED rather than merged.** `HEAD^1` is an ancestor of `HEAD`, so `merge-base(HEAD^1, HEAD) = HEAD^1` and `"$BASE...HEAD"` ≡ `"$BASE..HEAD"` on the pairing the steps now have — three dots would be a no-op spelling. That is NOT the same set as #642's `"$BASE...$HEAD"` against the branch tip, and the one cell where the two differ decides for the merge's delta: a branch that made the same edit the base already shipped is inside the branch-tip three-dot range and outside the merge's delta, and the merge lands nothing for that file, so no entry is owed for it — pinned (`ChangelogGateTest::test_a_change_the_base_already_carries_identically_is_not_in_scope`, watched red under the three-dot spelling; `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` records it). **Direction, stated both ways:** merge delta ⊆ branch-tip three-dot ⊆ retired two-dot, so newly ACCEPTED is a PR whose merge lands no in-scope file — card#8441's two cells (a branch cut before a release fold no longer reads as a release PR; a docs-only branch is no longer pulled into the entry requirement by the base's own `app/` change), both carried here as forked fixtures under the derived pairing, plus the identical-change cell — and newly REJECTED is nothing. card#8441's operator ruling approved exactly that accepting direction. DL-329's *"A SIBLING IS FILED, NOT FIXED"* note is discharged in place; **no DL-337 is minted** — the ruling lives here because the mechanism that closes it is this one, and `VERSIONING.md`'s gate table now says what *"the PR changes …"* means. **Cross-repo siblings, reported not fixed, and NARROWED:** `release-artifacts-gate.yml` on `agent-board-toolkit` and on `kanban-board` pass the same `base-sha` from the same field into the same action, so by that action's contract their exposure is the branch-merged-the-base shape only, not the PR #640 shape; each is its own repo's card, to be filed at that narrower shape.

**⛔ Operator-approved (always-ask: what CI rejects).** This removes a false refusal and adds one: a job standing on something other than this PR's merge commit now fails loud where it previously ran against whatever it was given. It cannot make the gate more permissive — the live-target collision leg is untouched, and `added` can only SHRINK when the base moves forward.

**Consequences:** new `bin/decision-log.py` (`next` + `check`, stdlib-only) and `bin/test_decision_log.py` (29 cases, wired into `bin/ python unit tests` by discovery — no enumeration to update); new `.github/workflows/dl-collision-gate.yml` with **no `paths:` filter**, deliberately, since a filter that stopped covering this log would make the gate absent rather than red (DL-283's measured failure mode); new `tests/Feature/Workflows/DlCollisionGateTest.php` executing the real workflow bash against a throwaway origin + clone, so the fetch of the live target tip is genuinely exercised and the CI pairing is built from a real merge commit rather than approximated (card#8527 made every fixture's work tree that merge, added `bin/pr-base-snapshot.sh` plus `tests/Feature/Workflows/PrBaseSnapshotTest.php`, moved `changelog-gate.yml`'s two scope predicates to the merge's delta with three forked cells in `ChangelogGateTest` and the *"the PR changes …"* paragraph in `VERSIONING.md`); this file's header gains the minting method; `CLAUDE.md` standing rule 2 and the quick-start block point at it.

## DL-296 — an ARCHIVED coord card is a RETIRE the create leg honours, read on kanban's own archive axis, partitioned exactly as the consumer partitions it (card#7169)

- **Date:** 2026-08-21
- **Status:** implemented (card#7169). **⛔ Hard-gate approved by the operator 2026-08-21** — it changes what the bridge accepts: an `issues.reopened` that creates a card today stops creating one when the thread's only card is archived. Extends DL-198 (`create_coord_cards`); no change to what the RECEIVER accepts or rejects, no config key, no migration, no token-scope change.

**The defect, OBSERVED and not inferred.** `KanbanClient::cardsByTag()` sends `q=board_id=<b> tags:"<tag>"` and **no `archived` parameter**, and kanban's `TasksController::search` applies `whereNull('archived_at')` unless one is passed. So the create leg's tag pre-check in `KanbanCoordCardHandler` structurally **cannot see an archived card**, a thread whose only card was retired reads as un-carded, and `COORD_CARD_CREATE_ACTIONS = ['opened','reopened']` puts every reopen on the create path. The card that filed this marked the COMPOSITION inferred from two source reads; it was **reproduced on the live sandbox board (1162) before any code was written** — card 521 created with `id:QUERY-7169` and archived, an `issues.reopened` for that thread replayed through the real classifier and the real handler against the real API, and **card 522 was minted over the retire**. The same replay after the fix creates nothing and pushes `coord_card_archived_twin`.

**Decision 1 — the fix is a SECOND read, because kanban's `archived` is a SWITCH and not a widening.** `?archived=1` is `whereNotNull('archived_at')`; absent is `whereNull(...)`; the endpoint offers no both-sides mode. There is therefore no way to "widen" the live pre-check, and no existing caller's read changes: `cardRowsByTag` gains an `$archivedOnly` parameter (default `false` ⇒ the `archived` key never reaches the query string, byte-identical to every read it served before) and the create leg calls it with `true`. **`cardsByTag` is untouched, and its other four callers stay live-only** — but for two different reasons, and the first cut of this decision gave only one of them. **Correct as live-only:** the two post-create collapses (a collapse reduces the LIVE set to one survivor; a read that saw archived rows would re-archive an already-retired card) and the coord-move correlation (a move that resolved an archived row would RESURRECT a retired card into a stage). **NOT correct, and left unfixed here:** `BoardCreateCardTool`'s `idem:<agent>:<key>` pre-check. It is a CREATE decision, not a move, so the same defect this DL fixes is live on it — archive the card a key minted, call again with the same key, and it mints a second card and answers `"created": true`. `docs/board-tools.md` promised that repeat unconditionally; this PR gives the claim its archived bound, and the code is unchanged. Not fixed here because the mechanism is inherited but the DECISION is not: a tool-minted card has no reroute partition, and both candidate answers (report the archived card as the hit vs. refuse and signal) change what the tool ACCEPTS — an operator gate, not a review call.

**Decision 2 — the read is placed on the LAST branch before the create, so its cost is one search per card the handler was about to mint.** Not beside the live pre-check (which would pay it on every redelivery skip), and not in the client (which has no way to know the caller's intent). A delivery that skips on the live tag, or on the by-ref key, issues nothing extra.

**⛔ Decision 3 — the fork the consumer already made is INHERITED, not collapsed: a human retire suppresses, a reroute-archived twin does not.** `kanban_common.archived_stable_ids()` exists for exactly this hazard and its own docstring states it verbatim (*"a source whose ONLY card is archived would look un-carded and be RE-CREATED on the create path"*), with `reroute_archived_stable_ids()` subtracted from it on the create path — the reclass pass archives a coord twin whose source re-routed to another board and stamps `coord:reroute-archived`, which is FRAMEWORK bookkeeping, not a human decision, so a reroute-BACK must card again. One hazard, two movers, and now one rule: the bridge pins the same tag literal (a shared contract like the `id:<sid>` adoption key) and applies the same partition **at the same granularity** — see Decision 3b, which is where the first cut of this got it wrong. **Suppressing on "any archived card exists" was refused explicitly** — it would silently stop carding legitimately-reopened work, which is a worse defect than the duplicate.

**Decision 3b — the exemption is per THREAD, because the consumer's is; a mixed archived set CREATES.** The consumer subtracts SETS OF STABLE-IDS, not cards: `archived_stable_ids()` and `reroute_archived_stable_ids()` both project the card rows down to sids before the difference, so a sid holding one reroute-tagged archived card and one untagged one is a member of BOTH sets, the subtraction removes it, and `reconcile_simple_board` **creates**. `retiredTwins()` therefore returns `[]` as soon as any row carries the tag — every row it sees carries one `id:<sid>` tag by construction (they came from a search on it), so *any tagged row* IS that sid's membership in the subtrahend. Both row orders are asserted, because the implementation returns early and an order-sensitive one would answer differently depending on what kanban returned first.

**⛔ Corrected in review (card#7169, review R-M1): this shipped first as a per-CARD partition, and that made Decision 3's "one hazard, two movers, one rule" FALSE in the one cell where the two spellings differ.** Reachable: reroute away (the reclass pass archives + tags) → route back (a fresh card) → hand-retire that card. The per-card reading refused the create, alerted the operator *"unarchive that card if the thread is live again"* — and the reconcile's very next pass minted a fresh card anyway, because the sid is in its difference. So the refusal was not a stricter honouring of the human decision; it was a **refusal the other mover undoes**, with a remedy line that points the operator at a card unarchiving which fixes nothing. Matching the consumer is also the cheaper claim to keep true: one sentence stays honest instead of a divergence that has to be restated, and kept in sync, on three surfaces. The alternative considered and rejected was to KEEP per-card and record the divergence + its consequence in all three places — rejected because it buys a suppression that does not survive one reconcile pass, and it would have had to be raised with the consumer's owner as a live cross-system disagreement.

**Decision 4 — the refusal SIGNALS; it is not a quiet skip.** It routes through `WritebackAlertNotifier::warnAndNotify` with reason `coord_card_archived_twin` (log + push, `card_id` null + `issue_number` per DL-285), not `Log::info` like the "a card already exists" arms. The difference is what the operator is left with: those arms end with the thread TRACKED, this one ends with a reopened thread **untracked**, and card#7133 is the standing precedent for a real refusal written at info level staying invisible for its whole life with the level-keyed coverage guard green over it. The `Log::warning` names the archived card ids, so the remedy — unarchive that card — points at a specific card. Dedup is the usual `(repo, outcome, reason)`, i.e. told-once-per-repo; that bound is stated in `docs/writeback.md` beside the row.

**⛔ STATED GAP — the by-ref (`issue_population: all`) path is NOT covered, and cannot be closed from this side.** A non-prefixed issue has no `id:<sid>` tag, and kanban's `by-ref.json` **hard-excludes** archived rows with no parameter to include them (`TasksController::byRef` → `whereNull('archived_at')`, unlike `search`). So there is no archived-visible correlation key on that path and a retired by-ref card is still re-created on reopen. It is pinned by a test asserting the handler issues **no** tag search there (so a later change cannot half-close it silently) and recorded on card#7169; closing it needs a kanban-side `archived` parameter on `by-ref.json`, which is a cross-system ask, not a bridge change.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Have `cardsByTag` return archived rows too** — impossible as stated (the switch, Decision 1) and wrong if it were possible for three of the four other callers (the two collapses and the move correlation, per Decision 1) — and the fourth, `BoardCreateCardTool`'s idem pre-check, needs a DIFFERENT read, not a widened shared one, since a widened `cardsByTag` would break the collapses to fix it. card#7222. (b) **A new `archivedCardsByTag` method** — REJECTED (canon #5): `cardRowsByTag` already issues this exact query and returns the rows the tag partition needs; a sibling method would be a second implementation of one read. (c) **Skip whenever any archived card exists** — REJECTED, Decision 3. (d) **Un-archive the card instead of refusing the create** — REJECTED: archival is the reconcile's and the operator's (DL-198's *"archival remains the reconcile's alone"* stands), and a bridge that un-retires a card overturns a human decision on a webhook. (e) **Report at `Log::info`** — REJECTED, Decision 4.

**Proven the way it fails.** Six legs, each watched red before it was green: the **positive** (archived untagged twin ⇒ no create + the push) reds with *"Unexpected request was recorded"* when the guard is removed; the **negative** (no card at all ⇒ still creates, and the `archived=1` read is asserted on the wire) reds the same way, so "stops the duplicate" cannot pass as "stops carding"; the **fork** (reroute-tagged twin ⇒ still creates) reds against the naive mutant with the carve-out deleted; the **mixed cell** (a reroute-tagged twin beside a hand-retired one ⇒ still creates, both row orders) reds on both data sets against the per-CARD mutant — the spelling this shipped with before review, restored by hand and watched fail; the **multi-retire signal** (two hand-retired twins ⇒ BOTH ids in `archived_card_ids`) reds against a `retiredTwins` that returns after its first untagged row, the shape the thread-level early return makes easy to reach for; the **by-ref gap** pin reds against the mutant that drops the `$tag !== null` condition. **Scope of the live-board leg, stated rather than absorbed:** the first FOUR (positive, negative, fork, by-ref gap) also ran end-to-end against the live sandbox board and were asserted on BOARD STATE (a GET re-read of both sides of the archive axis) and on the alert body captured off a real localhost channel — never on an exit code. The two legs added in review (the mixed cell, the multi-retire signal) were proven by **mutation under phpunit only**; they were not replayed on the board, and this DL does not claim they were.

**A test-harness defect this exposed, fixed here.** `Http::fake([...])` **invokes every stub for every request** and keeps the first non-null answer, so a `*/tasks/search.json*` stub carrying `Http::sequence()` is POPPED by the new `archived=1` read as well — the post-create re-read then gets the archived read's element. Two collapse tests were affected: one red, and one **green for the wrong reason** (it asserted only that nothing was archived, which is also true when the create is suppressed). Both now go through one closure fake that answers each read for what it is, and the second carries a positive create assertion so it cannot pass on a suppressed create again.

**⛔ The SIBLING CLASS is filed, not asserted away — card#7222.** Decision 1's first cut disposed of every other correlation read in one sentence (*"they all mean live when they say card"*), which is true of the collapses and the move and false of two members. The class — *a LIVE-ONLY correlation read answers "no card" for an ARCHIVED one, so the create it gates re-mints over the retire* — now has one item with a per-member disposition and a re-derivable denominator (grep the correlation-read methods under `app/`, keep the sites whose result decides a CREATE; today 4 create-deciding sites, 3 non-create). Members: **M1** this handler (CLOSED, here); **M2** `BoardCreateCardTool`'s idem pre-check (OPEN, live defect, hard-gated on what the tool accepts); **M3** `KanbanDependabotCardHandler` — it archives its own card on `closed_unmerged` (DL-161), `pull_request.reopened` collapses to `opened` (`GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier`, deliberately), and by-ref hard-excludes archived rows, so a reopened dependabot PR re-creates over the bridge's own retire; that may well be INTENDED (a bridge-set churn archive is bookkeeping, the same argument the reroute carve-out makes) but nothing records the reading, and a hand-archived dependabot card gets the identical re-create — it needs a ruling, possibly only a written rationale beside DL-161; **M4** the by-ref coord path (OPEN, cross-system — the STATED GAP above, blocking M3 too); **M5/M6/M7** the collapses, the coord-move correlation and `BoardMyCardsTool`'s listing, disposed correct-as-live-only. **Adjacent, same hazard:** the consumer marks its bookkeeping archive and the bridge marks neither of its own (`CardCollapse::toSurvivor`, the DL-161 retire), so a bridge artifact is indistinguishable from a hand retire to `retiredTwins()`. Bounded in prose here (the `REROUTE_ARCHIVED_TAG` docblock + `docs/writeback.md`), not fixed — a bridge marker tag is a new cross-system contract the consumer would have to partition on too. Reachability of the collapse case is nil while its survivor is live (the live pre-check answers first); it needs a later hard delete of that survivor.

**Consequences:** `KanbanClient::cardRowsByTag` (`$archivedOnly`) + `cardsByTag`'s docblock (live-only, stated as the contract); `KanbanCoordCardHandler` (the archived-twin branch, `retiredTwins()`, `REROUTE_ARCHIVED_TAG` + its bridge-archive bound); `docs/writeback.md` (the create-precondition bullet, the signal-table row + its bound, the marker bound); `docs/config-schema.md` (the `create_coord_cards` clause's granularity); `docs/board-tools.md` (the `idempotency_key` promise's archived bound); `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` (the tag-search row: the archive axis and the `by-ref` asymmetry); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **Tests:** 2 client (the default sends no `archived` key; `archivedOnly` sends `archived=1`), 6 handler executions across 5 methods (positive, negative, fork, the mixed cell over **both** row orders, and the multi-retire signal), 1 by-ref gap pin, plus the two collapse tests re-harnessed and one strengthened. No new config key, no migration, no `.env` change, no token-scope change; `create_coord_cards` remains opt-in, so an install that cards no coord issues is byte-identical.

## DL-297 — an ARCHIVED card under an `idem:` key is a RETIRE that REFUSES the create; `board_create_card` reads both sides of kanban's archive axis (card#7222 M2)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7222, member M2). **⛔ Hard-gate approved by the operator 2026-08-22** — it changes what the tool ACCEPTS: a `board_create_card` call that creates a card today is refused (422) when the only card its `idempotency_key` correlates to is archived. Extends DL-198's idempotency pattern and DL-217's tool contract; no config key, no migration, no token-scope change, no change to what the RECEIVER accepts or rejects.

**The defect, DEMONSTRATED before it was fixed.** `BoardCreateCardTool`'s `idem:<agent>:<key>` pre-check called `KanbanClient::cardsByTag()`, which sends `q=board_id=<b> tags:"<tag>"` and **no `archived` parameter**, and kanban's `TasksController::search` applies `whereNull('archived_at')` unless one is passed. So a key whose card was archived read as un-carded and fell through to the create. Demonstrated by asserting the broken behaviour green against the unmodified tool: board state *card 77 exists and is archived under `idem:me:k3`*, one call with that key ⇒ HTTP 200, **a second card (88)**, `"created": true`, `"idempotent_hit": false`, and **no read of the archive side on the wire at all**. That demo assertion was then inverted into the refusal test, watched red against the same input, and made green by the fix. This is DL-296's defect on the agent-facing surface — the second of the four create-deciding members on card#7222's class item, and the one DL-296 left open because the mechanism was inherited and the DECISION was not.

**⛔ Decision 1 — the answer is REFUSE-AND-SAY-WHY, not "hand back the archived card as the hit".** Both shapes were live options and they give a caller very different answers, so the caller-visible delta is enumerated here rather than described:

| Board state under `idem:<you>:<key>` | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a LIVE card | 200, `idempotent_hit: true`, that card | **unchanged** (and the archive side is never read) |
| a LIVE card beside an archived one | 200, `idempotent_hit: true`, the live card | **unchanged** — the live read answers first |
| **only ARCHIVED card(s)** | **200, a SECOND card, `"created": true`** | **422, no card created**, the message naming the archived ids |
| no card on either side | 200, created | **unchanged**, plus one extra search per card actually minted |
| no `idempotency_key` | 200, created, no reads | **unchanged** (byte-identical, no probe exists to extend) |
| the archive-side read itself errors upstream | n/a (no such read) | **502, nothing created** — fail-closed *[Additive annotation, 2026-09-02 (card#8486, DL-339): the STATUS in this cell moved and the OUTCOME did not. A permanent board 4xx (401/403/404) on either idempotency read is now a **422 refusal naming the install fault**; only a fault that may clear still answers 502. Nothing created, fail-closed, unchanged — which is what this row decides.]* |

The rejected alternative (b), *report the archived card as `"idempotent_hit": true`*, was refused on what it hands the caller: a **retired** card id, presented as a success, for a card the same agent's own `board_my_cards` window does not show (that read is live-only, and correctly so — card#7222 M7). The agent would then comment on, cite, or report progress against a card the operator deliberately took off the board, and nothing in the response would say so. A refusal costs the caller one round trip and tells it exactly which card to unarchive; there is no state in which (b)'s answer is more actionable. **Archival is not the bridge's to undo** — DL-198's *"archival remains the reconcile's alone"* and DL-296 Decision 3 both stand, so un-archiving instead of refusing was never a candidate.

**Decision 2 — a 422 refusal, not a 200 carrying a new field.** The tool already has one refusal channel (`ToolRefusalException` → 422 through `BoardToolDispatcher`), the caller is answered synchronously, and the message is the remedy. A 200 with `created: false, idempotent_hit: false` and no `card_id` was rejected: it invents a third result shape for a contract whose documented return carries a `card_id`, and an LLM caller that sees a 200 moves on — which is the silent-success failure this exists to prevent. **No `WritebackAlertNotifier` push, unlike DL-296 Decision 4:** that handler has nobody to answer (a webhook reaction ends with a thread untracked and no one told), while this refusal is delivered to the caller in the response. The bridge-side record is a `Log::warning` naming `archived_card_ids` — warning, not the `Log::info` the two "a card already exists" arms use, because those arms end with the caller holding a card and this one ends with none.

**⛔ Decision 3 — the consumer's `coord:reroute-archived` carve-out is deliberately NOT carried here, and the reason is the mechanism, not the surface.** DL-296 Decision 3b exempts a whole thread when any archived twin carries that marker, because the consumer's reconcile is a **second mover** that re-creates the exempted thread on its next pass — so refusing there would be a refusal the other mover undoes, with a remedy line pointing at a card whose unarchiving fixes nothing. **No second mover creates a tool card.** An `idem:<agent>:<key>` card is minted only by this tool, by that agent's own call; nothing reconciles it, nothing re-routes it between boards, and the consumer's reclass pass partitions coord threads keyed by `id:<sid>`, a tag this tool refuses from callers and does not stamp. So the refusal here is durable and its remedy is accurate. The two spellings are the same rule — *a retire suppresses* — applied to populations with different movers; `BoardCreateCardTool::archivedIds` therefore returns every archived row's id and `KanbanCoordCardHandler::retiredTwins` keeps its exemption.

**Decision 4 — a second read, on the last branch before the create, reusing the client method DL-296 already shipped.** Kanban's `archived` is a SWITCH, not a widening (`archived=1` returns archived rows ONLY; the endpoint offers no both-sides mode), so there is nothing to widen: `cardsByTag` is untouched and its other callers are unchanged. `cardRowsByTag(..., archivedOnly: true)` is the read DL-296 added and is called here as-is — no `archivedCardsByTag` sibling (canon #5, the same rejection DL-296 made). Placing it after the live pre-check rather than beside it is what keeps the hit path free: a repeat that hits pays nothing, and the extra search is bounded by cards actually minted.

**⛔ STATED BOUND, inherited unchanged from DL-296 — the bridge marks none of its own archives.** `CardCollapse::toSurvivor` retires the losers of a same-key create race, and those losers carry the very `idem:` tag this probe searches. That is bridge bookkeeping, indistinguishable here from a hand retire. It is unreachable while the collapse's survivor stays LIVE (the live pre-check answers first and this branch is never reached) and bites only if that survivor later leaves the live search by hard delete — the same reachability argument, and the same non-fix, as DL-296's: a bridge marker tag is a new cross-system contract the consumer would have to partition on too. Card#7222 carries it.

**Second stated bound — a 200 whose body carries no card collection reads as "nothing archived" and the create proceeds.** `cardRowsByTag` returns `[]` for a body it cannot descend, so an upstream that answers 200-with-a-strange-shape fails OPEN on this branch (a non-200 throws and 502s, which fails closed). That is the pre-existing posture of the read, shared with the coord create leg; it is stated rather than changed, because changing it belongs to the client and to every caller of that read, not to this branch.

**Proven the way it fails.** Five mutants, each watched: (1) **the fix removed** — the refusal test, the multi-id test and the archive-side wire assertion all red, which is the pre-fix demo above; (2) **`archivedOnly: true` → `false`** (the probe reading the live side) — 4 red, including the collapse test, so the archive AXIS is load-bearing and not merely a second call; (3) **`archivedIds` returning after its first row** — the multi-retire test reds on a message naming only card 77 when 77 and 91 are retired, the shape that would send an operator to unarchive the wrong card; (4) **the probe hoisted ABOVE the live pre-check** — the paired witness and the lowercase-key test red, so "honours a retire" cannot pass as "stopped being idempotent". (5) **the probe hoisted OUTSIDE the `idempotency_key` guard** — the no-key test reds, so a caller that supplies no key still issues ZERO reads and the *byte-identical* row of the caller-visible table is pinned rather than asserted. The **paired witness** (a LIVE twin still returns the same card, no create, and no archived read issued) and the **negative control** (no card on either side ⇒ still creates, with `archived=1` asserted on the wire) are what separate the fix from a tool that simply stopped creating. All legs are phpunit-level against a faked kanban; **no live-board replay was run for this member**, unlike DL-296's first four legs.

**A test-harness trap re-encountered, fixed the same way.** `Http::fake([...])` invokes every stub for every request and keeps the first non-null answer, so a `Http::sequence()` on a single wildcard `tasks/search.json` pattern is POPPED by the archive-side probe — `test_idempotency_raced_duplicate_is_collapsed` would have handed its post-create re-read the archived element. The tool's idempotency tests now go through one closure fake (`archiveAxisFake`) that answers each read for what it is, keyed on `archived=1` and on the request method, and the collapse test carries a positive `created: true` assertion so it cannot pass on a suppressed create. This is the same defect DL-296 fixed on the coord tests; this file inherited it the moment the tool grew a second read.

**Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Tools/BoardCreateCardTool.php` (the archived-twin branch, `archivedIds()`, class docblock); `docs/board-tools.md` (the `idempotency_key` bullet — the DL-296 "known, not fixed" bound becomes the new behaviour and the caller's two remedies; the 422 row); `examples/channel-servers/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs` (the `idempotency_key` tool description a PROGRAM loads inline — it carried DL-296's *"re-using a key whose card was ARCHIVED creates a second card"*, which this makes false; snapshot **0.9.5 → 0.9.6** per DL-038); `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (a new entry, plus an annotation on the DL-296 entry in the same `[Unreleased]` block, whose *"the code is unchanged"* clause would otherwise ship contradicting this). **Tests:** 3 new (`refuses_and_creates_nothing` with the `archived=1` read asserted on the wire, `every_archived_twin_is_named`, `no_card_on_either_side_still_creates`), **3** strengthened (the correlate-before-create witness now also pins that a live hit issues NO archived read; the collapse test re-harnessed off `Http::sequence()` with a positive create assertion; and `test_legitimate_caller_tag_is_accepted` gained the no-key `Http::assertNotSent(/tasks/search.json)` — the assertion that pins the table's *no `idempotency_key` ⇒ byte-identical* row), 1 new helper. **Corrected in this same branch, after the fix landed:** `KanbanClient::cardsByTag`'s docblock named this pre-check as the open member (*"That is open, with its siblings, on card#7222"*) and was stale the moment this change closed it. The file sat outside the fix's file scope (concurrent agents partitioned by file), so it was corrected separately in `2c6ef22` — it now reads *"WAS such a caller … DL-297 … closed it"*. **No correction item is owed on card#7222 for it.** ⚠ An earlier revision of this entry recorded that line as still-stale-and-deferred; that was true when written and false by the time this shipped, which is why it is restated here rather than left to a reader to reconcile. **Also not done, and filed rather than smuggled in:** hoisting the read-then-decide sequence M1 and M2 now spell twice into one primitive both call (card#7222's consolidation note) needs an edit to `KanbanCoordCardHandler`, the same out-of-scope file; a shared primitive with one caller would have been a third spelling, not a consolidation.

## DL-298 — a card resolved from a board-scoped SEARCH is re-checked against the mapped board before it is written to, through the guard the token path already owns (card#7211)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7211, fix #2 of two). **⛔ Hard-gate approved by the operator 2026-08-22** — it is a fail-closed tightening on a write path: a card the writeback moves or archives today stops being written to if the row kanban returned does not name the mapped board. **The newly-refused set is EMPTY on a correctly-scoped instance, and that is the design intent, not a hedge.** No config key, no migration, no token-scope change, no change to what the RECEIVER accepts or rejects. Fix #1 (the call-construction pin, `BoardScopedReadConstructionTest`, PR #557) shipped first and is untouched here.

**The defect.** Four writeback paths resolve card ids from a **board-scoped search** and then write to those ids — archive, move, collapse — without ever re-checking each returned row's own board. `MappedBoardGuard` (DL-292) covers only the five TOKEN-path sites, the ones that parse `card#NNNN` / `DL-NNN` out of a PR title or branch: those read the card and refuse it if it is not on the mapped board. These four parse no token, so nothing runs. **An audit keyed on "where is the guard?" is structurally blind to a site that never had one** — it returns nothing to the search and reads as clean.

**⛔ Why it is a defect even though the scope IS honoured today.** Measured on the live instance (rt#327), with the control that makes a zero mean something: a token planted only on board B returned `total:1` scoped to B and `total:0` scoped to A, holding past page 1; `tags:"…"` is likewise enforced and does not fall through to free text. So `q=board_id=<id>` works and these sites are **not** on a live cross-tenant write path. But the harm class is one parameter-name away: the same endpoint **silently drops an unrecognised TOP-LEVEL query parameter and answers 200 with an UNFILTERED result set** — a bogus `?<key>=xyz` returned 21 cards spanning every board the token could reach. ⚑ **And `board_id` ALSO works as a bare top-level parameter and filters correctly there**, so hoisting it out of `q` filters in a manual test, reviews as equivalent, and takes the next filter hoisted beside it silently out of the query. Nothing in a 200 distinguishes a dropped filter from an honoured one. Card ids are allocated GLOBALLY on this multi-tenant instance. ⇒ **Correct by luck, not by construction.**

**Decision 1 — the check is on the RESULT, and it is the SAME primitive as the token path, never a second copy.** Each site calls `MappedBoardGuard::refuses()` with its own arm name: it owns the DL-292 predicate (`is_numeric` + `(int)` cast), the `card_not_on_mapped_board` reason code and the warn+notify report together, and `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest`'s kind-keyed leg reds on any handler that spells `board_id` itself. So a third writeback family cannot mint a fourth predicate, a fourth log level, or a fourth reason string. The three new arms share the one reason code and stay apart in the `(repo, outcome, reason)` dedup tuple by their `outcome` — `dependabot_card`, `promote_on_release`, `coord_card_create` — exactly as DL-274(3) intends.

**Decision 2 — the board is taken from the row the read ALREADY returned; no site pays an extra request on its ordinary path.** The trilemma the card posed (carry the board through / switch to the row-returning twin / re-read per card) dissolves once you notice **every one of these searches returns full task rows and the projection to ids happens client-side inside `KanbanClient`** — it is the projection, not the request, that was discarding the board. Concretely: `KanbanDependabotCardHandler::cardsForRepo` already `getCard`s each id for its repo attribution, so the row is in hand (0 extra requests); `KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler` scans `readBoardCards`, which is rows (0 extra); `KanbanCoordCardHandler`'s post-create collapse switches from `cardsByTag` to its row-returning twin `cardRowsByTag` — **the same single GET**, rows instead of ids (0 extra). **The one place a read IS added, stated rather than hidden:** the coord handler's by-ref collapse arm projects to ids and carries its board in the URL PATH, so there is no row to re-check; it pays one `getCard` per correlated card — but only inside `count($liveRef) > 1`, i.e. only on a create RACE, never on the ordinary single-card path. That trade was taken deliberately: a collapse is where the cost is already anomalous and where the consequence is worst (below).

**Decision 3 — the refusal is PER ROW, and the delivery continues.** A refused row is dropped from the card set and reported; the rest of the delivery proceeds. Not an abort: a foreign row is evidence about the READ, and abandoning the mapped cards beside it would turn one bad row into a stranded delivery that is never retried (a permanent refusal is deliberately not redelivered). The refusal shape is the token path's, unchanged — `warnAndNotify` (durable `Log::warning` first, then the additive push) with `card_not_on_mapped_board`.

**⛔ Decision 4 — why a COLLAPSE needs this more than a stray write does.** `CardCollapse::toSurvivor` keeps the **lowest id**, and ids are global across the instance. So a single foreign row in a collapse set does not merely add an archive: if its id is lower it **WINS the tie-break**, and the card this handler just created is the one retired — a cross-board read costing us the card we minted, with the foreign card left as the "survivor" nothing on our board tracks. The dependabot move path has the same shape (the survivor is what gets moved). Both are pinned by tests that red exactly that way without the guard.

**What stops being written, enumerated before the code was written.** (a) `kanban_dependabot_card`: a correlated card whose `getCard` row does not name the mapped board is no longer archived on `closed_unmerged`, no longer archived as a collapse loser, and no longer eligible to be the survivor that is moved. (b) `kanban_promote_released`: a Shipped candidate whose board row does not name the mapped board is no longer promoted. (c) `kanban_coord_card`: such a row is excluded from the post-create collapse, so it is neither archived nor allowed to survive. **In all three, a row with an ABSENT or unreadable `board_id` is refused like a foreign one** — fail-closed, and it is what a `q=`→top-level hoist against a trimmed projection would actually look like. **On a correctly-scoped instance that set is EMPTY**: every one of these reads is board-scoped (by `q=board_id=` or by the by-ref URL path), and that scoping is measured to hold. This is a no-op guard by design — it converts a call-construction convention into a property of the data.

**⛔ NOT changed, and deliberately: the READ-decision sites.** `KanbanCoordCardHandler`'s live tag pre-check, its by-ref pre-check and its DL-296 archived-twin read all resolve rows and then decide **not to create**; they write nothing. A foreign row there suppresses a create, and board-scoping them would make the handler create where it previously skipped — a change in the **permissive** direction, on a different gate, needing its own ruling. Named on card#7211 rather than folded in.

**⛔ STATED GAP — the fourth site of card#7211 is NOT covered.** `bridge:reconcile --fix` reads the board (`ReconcileCommand`, `readBoardCards`) and calls `moveCard` on its plan with no board re-check. It was out of this change's file scope and is left OPEN on card#7211. It is the least exposed of the four (operator-invoked, report-first, `--max-moves` capped, and it prints every planned move) but it is the same defect and this DL does not claim otherwise. **[CLOSED by DL-301 — the fourth site now calls the same guard, before its GitHub read. Read this paragraph as the disclosure it was, not as current state.]**

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Filter inside `KanbanClient`** (drop any row whose board disagrees with the `$boardId` argument) — REJECTED: the client has neither the `WritebackMapping` the shared predicate compares against nor the `(repo, outcome)` tuple the refusal report needs, so it would have had to mint a second, quieter compare — the exact duplication DL-292 removed. It would also have silently dropped rows from `bridge:check`'s diagnostic reads, where a foreign row is a finding, not noise. (b) **A new `MappedBoardRowFilter` primitive over lists of rows** — REJECTED (canon #5 read the other way): `MappedBoardGuard` already owns this behaviour and is called directly from five sites; a second entry point over the same rule is a divergence waiting to happen, and the three call sites differ in input shape anyway (ids+`getCard`, board rows, tag rows). (c) **Abort the delivery on any foreign row** — REJECTED, Decision 3. (d) **Rely on fix #1 alone** — REJECTED, and it is the reason both shipped: a construction pin catches the bad CALL and is blind to a bad RESULT from any other cause (a server-side scoping regression, a proxy rewriting the query, a kanban upgrade). (e) **Do nothing, since the refused set is empty** — REJECTED: an empty refused set is a measurement of today's server, not a property of the code, and the measurement's own author recommended this fix unprompted.

**Proven the way it fails.** Five methods in `tests/Feature/Writeback/ResolvedRowBoardGuardTest.php`, **all five watched RED before the guard existed** and each red for its own reason: promote — the foreign row WAS promoted (`Unexpected request was recorded`); dependabot move — the mapped card was NOT moved, because the foreign row won the collapse tie-break and was moved instead; dependabot `closed_unmerged` — the foreign card WAS archived; the absent-board row — it WAS written to; the coord collapse — a write reached a card the guarded path leaves alone. **Every method feeds a MIXED set** (one mapped row, one foreign row) and asserts both directions in one measurement, because the happy path refuses nothing: a method asserting only that the foreign row is unwritten cannot tell *refuses foreign rows* from *stopped writing*, and one asserting only the mapped write cannot tell the guard from its absence. Assertions are on the WIRE (`Http::assertSent` / `assertNotSent` on the PATCH, and the alert body captured off the fake channel), never on a return value. The coord leg uses a request-keyed closure fake, not `Http::sequence()`, for the DL-296 reason: Laravel invokes every stub for every request and a sequence is popped by the `archived=1` read as well.

**A fixture class this exposed, fixed here.** Every existing card fixture in the three handler tests carried no `board_id` — 16 `getCard` responses, 20 board rows, 3 tag rows. Kanban returns `board_id` on every task row, so those were never realistic responses; the guard simply made the unrealism observable. They now carry it, with the reason recorded at each test class rather than at each fixture.

**Consequences:** `KanbanDependabotCardHandler` (`cardsForRepo` gains the board gate, ordered BEFORE the repo gate so a foreign-board card that also fails repo attribution cannot be dropped silently); `KanbanPromoteReleasedHandler` (the gate is applied where a row BECOMES a candidate, so the refused set equals the write set); `KanbanCoordCardHandler` (`onMappedBoard()`, the collapse re-read switched to `cardRowsByTag`, the by-ref arm's per-card read); `KanbanClient` (`cardsByTag` / `cardRowsByTag` docblocks: the ids-vs-rows projection is what the caller's re-check needs back); `docs/writeback.md` (three new signal-table rows + the bound they share); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **Tests:** 5 new methods (3 arms × control + paired presence witness, plus the archive arm and the unreadable-board arm), 39 fixtures made realistic. **⛔ TWO doc edits this change OWES and could not make — both outside its file scope, both recorded on card#7211 rather than left implicit.** (i) `MappedBoardGuard::refuses()`'s docblock enumerates the three arms that call it (`kanban_move_card`, `kanban_block_reason`, `kanban_coord_card_move`); there are now **six**. (ii) `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`'s §3 invariant row ends *"the client-side re-check of each returned row's own `board_id` is **not** in place"* — that clause is now false for three of the four sites and needs rewriting to name the one that is still open (`bridge:reconcile --fix`). **[Discharged by DL-301 — both edits are made: the docblock says SEVEN arms and the §3 row says ALL FOUR. Read this clause as the disclosure it was, not as an outstanding debt; card#7211 carries no correction item for it.]**
