## DL-299 — `board_create_card` reports the placement it READ BACK from the card, never the one it was configured to write (card#7225)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7225, instance **B** of that class — the tool-response instance). **⛔ Operator-ruled FIX 2026-08-22.** It is a **contract change on a tool response** and was therefore gated before any code, per the card's own closing note. No config key, no migration, no token-scope change, and **no change to what the tool accepts, refuses, or writes** — the POST body is byte-identical; only what the response *means* changed.

**The defect.** Both arms of `BoardCreateCardTool::call()` ended in `'board_id' => $boardId, 'swimlane_id' => (int) $cfg->swimlaneId`. Those are `BoardToolsConfig` values — **where this agent is configured to write** — returned on keys a calling agent consumes as **where its card is**. `KanbanClient::createCard()` returns an id and nothing else, so the created card's placement was never read; and on the idempotency-hit arm the id came out of `cardsByTag()` — a tag SEARCH, a Group-B resolution (card#7211) with no membership re-check — so the tool asserted the configured board for a card it had **not** created and had **not** checked. ⛔ **The two readings differ only when something has gone wrong, so the record was silently correct exactly until the moment a reader needed it, and silently wrong from then on.** It failed in the direction that reads as safe.

**Why this instance ranks above its log-line siblings, which are NOT fixed here.** The same shape sits on `kanban_coord_card: created`, `kanban_dependabot_card: created`, this tool's own `created` log line, and on the `stage` axis of five move records (card#7225 §A/§C). Those are **diagnostics**: a log line is read by an operator who is already hunting a problem, and who can read the next line. A **tool response is consumed by an agent as fact** — it is the only channel that answers, it is answered synchronously, and nothing downstream re-derives it. That ranking is the operator's, recorded on the card, and it is why one instance shipped alone rather than the class.

**Decision 1 — read the CARD back (`GET /tasks/{id}.json`), not the POST echo and not the search row.** One primitive (`placement()`) serves both arms, and it reads **the card the tool is about to name** — after the DL-198 duplicate collapse, so when the survivor is a card another worker minted, the response describes *that* card. Cost: **one extra GET per successful call** on an agent-initiated, interactive surface that already makes 1–3 (and none at all on any refusal path). ⚠ **State the payload, not just the round trip:** `tasks/{id}.json` is kanban's `show`, the FULL task aggregate — `subtasks, comments, attachments, outgoingLinks.toTask.board, incomingLinks.fromTask.board, externalReferences, lastStageMoveChangelog` eager-loaded plus a `TaskLinkProjector` pass (read in kanban's `TasksController::fullTaskResource()`) — all to obtain two integers, and on the idempotency-hit arm the card can be old and comment-heavy. The request count is right; "one small read" would not be. `board_id` is the anchor: kanban's `TaskResource` carries `board_id` and `swimlane_id` at the top level of `data`, both **unconditional** (no `when()`/`whenLoaded()` wrapper — re-read in `app/Http/Resources/V3/TaskResource.php`), and every task row carries a board.

**Decision 2 — `placement_observed`, because a bare null cannot say which null it is.** A card legitimately in **no** lane reports `swimlane_id: null`, so a null alone conflates *"the card is in no lane"* with *"the bridge could not look"*. `true` ⇒ the two ids are that card's own values; `false` ⇒ **both are null and the response claims no placement**. Without the flag, the fail-soft path below would re-mint this card's own defect one level down: an unreadable state rendered as a confident reading.

⛔ **The flag only discriminates if the READ does — corrected in the fix round.** The first cut gated the board axis on `is_numeric($card['board_id'] ?? null)` but let the lane axis fall out of the same `?? null`, and `?? null` cannot tell a PRESENT null from an ABSENT key. Measured on the shipped code: a read-back body `{"id":42,"board_id":10}` answered `{"swimlane_id": null, "placement_observed": true}` — *"your card is in no lane"*, offered as an observation the calling agent may act on, for a card sitting in lane 4, plus a spurious divergence warning on every such create. That is this DL's own defect one level down, exactly as the paragraph above predicts, and the two halves of ONE change disagreed with each other: this branch's own first commit (`a0665e3`) had already written `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` §2 the other way (*"or the tool reports an unobserved placement"*) while shipping code that did the opposite. ⛔ **That sentence is NOT independent authority and must not be read as one.** The fix round's first draft of this paragraph appealed to it as a pre-existing published contract the code had violated; measured, `git show origin/dev:docs/kanban-integration-contract.md | grep -c "unobserved placement"` returns **0** — the phrase is this branch's, an hour old, and no repo state has ever held that doc without the corrected code. Post-merge a maintainer reading the appeal would credit a contract that never existed and could cite it as prior authority. The measured pre-fix body above is the whole of the evidence and needs no doc to stand on. `array_key_exists('swimlane_id', $card)` is the discrimination: a **present** null is a real no-lane reading; an **absent** key, or a present non-numeric, means the body answered nothing about the lane and unobserves the **pair** — `placement_observed` answers for the placement, not per axis. One warning arm covers both axes (its `unusable` context field names which), so the count of distinct messages stays at three rather than growing a near-identical sibling per axis.

⛔ **ONE flag for the PAIR here, one flag PER AXIS on `board_my_cards` (DL-302) — deliberate, and recorded because a divergence that is deliberate but unrecorded is indistinguishable from drift to the next reader.** ⚠ DL-302 is a SEPARATE change on a separate branch (card#7295), not depended on here — on a tip carrying only this one it is not yet in this log and `board_my_cards` still echoes its configured board. Both entries land in `docs/board-tools.md`, in one release, for one reader, so the difference will be read as one of the two being wrong unless the reason is on the record. The reason is structural, not stylistic: `board_my_cards` reads **two independent populations** — the agent's own+shared rows, and the coord rows, each from its own request against its own board — so either can be observed while the other is not, and one flag could only answer for both by lying about one. `board_create_card` derives **both axes from ONE read-back of ONE card**: `board_id` and `swimlane_id` arrive in the same body or neither does, so they are observed or unobserved together, and a per-axis flag would advertise an independence that does not exist — a caller could then write a branch on `board_observed && ! swimlane_observed`, a state this tool cannot produce. The shared rule is the same in both: **a flag exists per unit that can independently fail to be read**, and the two tools differ in how many such units they have. (The three-spellings/two-shapes duplication that let this question be answered twice is filed as its own class item — see Consequences.)

**Decision 3 — fail-SOFT, and never back to config — but the REASON differs per arm, and the first cut stated only one of them.** On the **create** arm the read-back runs after the create has already landed, so throwing would answer a failure for a card that exists and whose id the caller would then never see — and, with no `idempotency_key`, its retry double-creates. ⛔ **That argument is false for the other half of the callers this shared primitive serves:** on the **idempotency-hit** arm no create happened and a retry is idempotent by construction, so nothing double-creates and nothing is lost by throwing. What carries the hit arm instead is the contract of a shared primitive — **a caller cannot tell which arm answered it**, so the response shape must not vary by arm; a hit that threw where a create degrades would make the tool's failure mode a function of board state the caller cannot see. The decision (uniform fail-soft) is unchanged; the justification is now true for both arms. Losing the placement is strictly cheaper than losing the id, so an upstream failure — or a 200 whose body carries no usable `board_id`, no `swimlane_id` key, or a non-numeric one — yields `placement_observed: false` + two nulls. ⛔ **Falling back to `$cfg` on that path was rejected outright: a fallback that restores the config value is the defect wearing a different hat**, and it would be reachable precisely when the bridge knows least.

**Decision 4 — a divergence WARNS; it does not refuse.** When the observed board/lane disagrees with the agent's configured scope the bridge logs a `Log::warning` naming both pairs (`observed_*` beside `configured_*`) and the tool still answers 200 with what it saw. What a card's placement should make this tool **do** — refuse the hit, decline to answer, alert — is a change to what the surface accepts or rejects, i.e. a separate gate with its own ruling. This change is scoped to the **report**, and says so.

**Decision 5 — the configured scope stays in the response, under its OWN name, on BOTH arms (operator-ruled in the second fix round).** `configured_board_id` / `configured_swimlane_id` are present whether `placement_observed` is true or false, sourced from `$cfg`. ⛔ **This is not Decision 3's rejected fallback and the difference is the whole point:** a fallback writes the config value onto the OBSERVATION key, where the caller cannot tell an observation from a restatement — that is the defect wearing a hat. A separately named key answers a question the observation cannot, *"what scope was this agent aiming at?"*, and answers it precisely when the observation is gone. The first cut of this change DROPPED the config values entirely, and the cost of that is legible against its sibling. ⚠ The two tools lose the observation by different mechanisms — here a read-back that fails or answers nothing usable; there an empty window or a row whose own `board_id` is unreadable — but the caller-visible state is the same one: *the bridge could not take the reading*. In that state `board_create_card` answered **nothing at all** about scope, while `board_my_cards` (DL-302) answered `board_id: null` **plus** `configured_board_id: 10` — same state, same page of `docs/board-tools.md`, same release, two different answers, with the calling agent holding no other channel to its own configured scope. The precedent is the one DL-302 cites: `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext` (card#7212) puts **both keys on both arms**, because a record carrying only one can answer *"did we stop it?"* and never *"did this happen?"*. Additive, so no existing caller breaks. **Alternative rejected — leave the tool silent about config and let the caller read its own YAML:** the caller is an agent behind a loopback/ssh proxy that has never seen the bridge's config, which is why the tool was echoing those values in the first place; removing the question is not answering it.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Drop `board_id`/`swimlane_id` from the response** ("stop naming placement the tool did not verify") — REJECTED: the keys are documented and useful, and an agent that has just captured a card legitimately wants to know where it landed; removing them answers the defect by removing the question. (b) **Have `createCard()` return the created ROW** (the `POST` echo already carries the full task, so zero extra requests) — REJECTED **here**: it is instance **A**'s primitive change, whose value is the three *log* call sites, and it cannot serve either of the two paths this instance is actually about — the idempotency **hit** (no create happened) and the **collapse survivor** (a card this worker did not create). Fixing the primitive for one consumer that still needs a second mechanism is the worse trade; A stays open with that fix named. (c) **Switch the hit arm's `cardsByTag()` to `cardRowsByTag()`** and read placement off the search row (also zero extra requests) — REJECTED: `cardsByTag` runs its result through `correlationIds()`, which makes an unreadable-body degradation **loud** (DL-026); `cardRowsByTag` treats the same body as an ordinary empty and would mint a second card in silence. Trading a durable warning on the idempotency probe for a saved round trip is a bad exchange, and a card's own `GET` is stronger evidence than a row from the search whose scoping is the very thing in doubt. (d) **Re-check the hit card against the configured board and REFUSE a foreign one** — REJECTED here as Decision 4: correct-looking, and a permissiveness/refusal change that is not this card's ruling. (e) **Do nothing, since placement disagrees only when kanban misbehaves** — REJECTED: that is the argument for every record in this class, and card#7211 has already MEASURED the mechanism on this install (a top-level query parameter kanban does not recognise is dropped, answering 200 with an unfiltered set). (f) **Read `GET /tasks/{id}/preload.json` instead** — the lightweight twin, same `TaskResource` with only `lastStageMoveChangelog` loaded (kanban `TasksController::preload()`, routed at `tasks/{task}/preload.json`), which would carry the same two integers without the aggregate Decision 1 now costs. **REJECTED here on availability, not on merit** — and it is the strongest of the six: this is a live-surface behavioural dependency on an endpoint whose presence across the kanban versions deployed against this bridge is UNVERIFIED, and the fix round declined to spend one. Recorded rather than left unexamined; a later pass that first establishes the version floor (as `byRefAvailable` does for `by-ref.json`) should take it.

⚠ **Count reconciliation:** this list is **six**, lettered (a)–(f). Card#7225's fix comment records **three** — the subset that had been proposed on the card at the time — and is the surface to correct, not this one; the DL is the log of record.

**Proven the way it fails.** In the first cut, seven methods in `tests/Feature/AgentTools/AgentToolsCallTest.php` were watched **RED against the unmodified tool**, each red for its own reason: the create arm reported the configured lane 4 for a card kanban placed in lane 99 (`Failed asserting that 4 is identical to 99`); the idempotency hit reported the configured board 10 for a search-resolved card on board 77 (`10 is identical to 77`); an unreadable read-back and a body with no `board_id` both still reported board 10 (`10 is identical to null`); a lane-less card reported lane 4 (`4 is identical to null`); and the two pre-existing idempotency legs lacked the flag entirely (`null is identical to true`). **The absence assertions are paired with presence witnesses** — the unreadable-card method asserts `created: true` + `card_id: 42` + the POST on the wire beside the two nulls, so *"reports no placement"* cannot pass as *"stopped creating"*, and the lane-less method pins `placement_observed: true` beside the same `swimlane_id: null` the failure path emits. ⛔ **"Both `Log::warning` messages are asserted" was FALSE as written — `placement()` emits THREE, and a grep of `tests/` for the third (`no usable board_id`) returned empty.** Corrected in the fix round: **all three** are now asserted by pattern, each watched red under a message mutation, with a `Log::shouldNotHaveReceived` control on the in-scope path keyed on the messages themselves and never on `warning` at large. The third one is not decoration — `test_a_read_back_carrying_no_board_id_reports_no_placement` asserts a body **byte-identical** to the one the throw branch produces, so before the log leg it could not distinguish the branch it is named for from the branch beside it; the message discriminates it from the throw arm and the `unusable` context field discriminates it from the two swimlane-key cases, whose bodies are identical again.

**Fix round (same branch, after an adversarial review returned CHANGES REQUESTED on `a0665e3`).** Re-derived and re-measured, each leg watched fail-first:

- **The lane axis was not observation-gated** (Decision 2). Two new methods — an ABSENT `swimlane_id` key and a present non-numeric one — both RED against the shipped code with `Failed asserting that 10 is identical to null`, over a measured pre-fix body of `{"created":true,"idempotent_hit":false,"card_id":42,"board_id":10,"swimlane_id":null,"placement_observed":true}`. The PRESENT-null method (:610) is the control: it passes on both sides and now carries a `shouldNotHaveReceived` on the unusable-axis message, so the fix cannot pass by unobserving every null.
- **Two tests were issuing a REAL outbound request on every suite run.** `test_loopback_peer_is_admitted` and `test_loopback_peer_with_external_xff_is_admitted` stubbed `*/tasks.json` but not `*/tasks/*.json`, so their `assertStatus(200)` passed **through** the fail-soft catch rather than the stubbed happy path. Proven by temporarily re-throwing from `placement()`'s catch under `Http::preventStrayRequests()`: **2 strays before, 0 after** (`StrayRequestException: Attempted request to [https://kanban.example.com/api/v3/tasks/1.json] without a matching fake`), with the deliberate 500-stub test failing under the same instrumentation as the control that the re-throw was live. **The population was re-derived, not asserted:** throwing unconditionally at the top of `placement()` makes every test that reaches a success arm red, which enumerates them — **17 of the 83 cases in `tests/Feature/AgentTools` (15 methods; 14 cases on the create arm, 3 on the hit arm)**, and no test outside that directory constructs the tool (the only other mention is a docblock in `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`). ⚠ **The figure the fix round first wrote here was 15 of 81 / 13 methods — measured BEFORE that same commit added the two lane-axis methods above, and shipped stale by exactly those two.** Re-derived by the method rather than re-counted: the probe now also appends `$arm` to a file, so the create/hit split is read off the run instead of assigned by test name; the instrumentation was reverted from a snapshot copy and the tree re-checked for leftovers. **Read the method, not the number** — the population moves with every test added to that directory, so a written figure is stale the next time anyone touches it. ⛔ **`preventStrayRequests()` was deliberately NOT adopted in `tests/TestCase.php`** — that is a suite-wide posture change with an unmeasured full-suite blast radius, filed as its own card.
- **The collapse-survivor read-back was advertised but unguarded.** `test_idempotency_raced_duplicate_is_collapsed` asserted the survivor id and nothing about which card the read-back targeted — and could not have, because its fixture made this worker's create id and the survivor id both 8. The fixture now returns **9** to this worker with survivor **8**, and the test asserts `GET /tasks/8.json` sent and `/tasks/9.json` not sent; RED under a mutation that names the survivor in the response while reading back the pre-collapse id (`An expected request was not recorded`).

**Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Tools/BoardCreateCardTool.php` (the shared `placement()` reader + both arms; the fix round adds the `array_key_exists` lane gate and folds the two unusable-axis reports into one warning arm carrying an `unusable` context field; the second fix round adds the Decision 5 `configured_*` pair to both returns); `docs/board-tools.md` (the return shape + what each value now claims + the aggregate-payload cost + the `configured_*` bullet and the one-flag-vs-per-axis note); `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` (the `GET /tasks/{id}.json` row gains `swimlane_id` and its first reader outside the writeback — a cross-system dependency on `TaskResource` keeping that key top-level); `examples/channel-servers/agent-webhook-bridge-channel.mjs` (the `board_create_card` MCP description — the only documentation the CALLING AGENT actually reads, and a doc surface a program loads inline, so it gains the read-back/`configured_*`/`placement_observed` clause; snapshot **0.9.6 → 0.9.7** per DL-038); `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` (the card#7225 stray-request note's *"74 tests in the three board-tools suites"* now names the three and the commit it was counted at, because the directory holds four files and 83 cases today). **A caller reading `swimlane_id` as "my configured lane" must stop** — it is the card's lane now, and it can be `null`; `configured_swimlane_id` is where that reading moved.

**⛔ The naming/shape duplication behind this entry is filed as its own class item — card#7319, and it is NOT attempted here.** Three spellings of one concept now exist in the repo: `observed_board_id`/`configured_board_id` (this entry's warning context), `observed_board`/`configured_board`/`row_board` (`BoardMyCardsTool`, DL-302), and `card_board`/`mapped_board` (`MappedBoardGuard::boardContext`, the oldest and the only one already hoisted, which neither newer instance reused). Two response-shape conventions sit on top of them. That duplication is what let the pair-vs-per-axis question and the drop-vs-keep-`configured_*` question each be answered twice without anyone disagreeing out loud, and it is what will mint a fourth spelling at the next instance of the card#7225 class — so the consolidation (one convention, hoisted, copies migrated, with a drift guard) is the class item, and fixing three call sites without it would leave the fourth to re-mint the divergence. **⛔ The siblings stay OPEN on card#7225 and are named rather than folded in:** the three `created` log lines (§A, incl. this tool's own, which still logs the requested placement at POST time), the five move records whose `stage` is the target (§C), and the residual non-success board-axis records. **One sibling this audit ADDED, found by reading rather than by the card's predicate: `BoardMyCardsTool` answers `board_id` from `$cfg` for a row set whose own `board_id` is never re-checked** — the same shape, on the same TOOL-RESPONSE surface this DL ranks highest (its swimlane axis is sound: every returned row is filtered against the configured lane, which is what makes the board axis the exception rather than the rule there).

## DL-300 — a writeback board DIVERGENCE is persisted; the happy path is not, and retention never touches it (card#7212)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7212, the second and final half). **Operator-approved 2026-08-22, in the narrow form only:** persist a row when `card_board != mapped_board`, nothing on the happy path. A row per successful writeback was explicitly NOT approved. **One new table, no existing table/column/index touched, no backfill, no config key, no token-scope change, and no change to what the bridge accepts, refuses, writes or retries.** The first half (PR #556) put the pair on every record of a write kanban accepted and is untouched here.

**The defect this closes, and why #556 did not close it.** #556 made the pair *visible* on both arms — until then a successful write logged the board it INTENDED to hit while only a refusal logged the board the card was actually on, so a write that LANDED on an out-of-mapping card was byte-identical in the log to a correct one. What it did not do is make the pair *survive*. The log is retention-bounded: 14 days, and since DL-199 the receiver prunes on its own gate. ⇒ **"Has a cross-board write ever landed here?" became answerable for a fortnight and unanswerable again after it.** An absence of record is not a record of absence — and **a record that expires is an absence on a timer**. This is the same generalisation rt#327 R4 recorded, applied to the time axis rather than the arm axis.

**Decision 1 — the row is minted inside `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext()`, the rendering itself.** That method is the one place holding BOTH the card and the mapping, so the durable row and the log line are the SAME observation, tested by the SAME predicate (`! belongs()`), with no second rendering and no second compare. It is also the only placement under which the **N+1th write site** is covered the day it is written: a `record()` call beside each of the eleven records would be one more thing to remember, and forgetting it is the exact shape of the defect being fixed. A renderer with a side effect is the cost, and it is paid deliberately and documented at the method.

**Decision 2 — the disposition comes from the caller, and only the guard passes anything but the default.** `refused` (the guard stopped the write; nothing was written to that card) vs `recorded` (the pair was rendered for a record of a write the bridge MADE, i.e. no gate stopped it). The vocabulary deliberately does not claim more than the site knows: `recorded` says *a divergent card reached a site that reports a write*, not *this exact write landed* — the one site that renders the pair before its write (`kanban_promote_released`, at scan time, because the row is out of scope two calls later) would otherwise make the stronger reading false.

**Decision 3 — the trigger is the PREDICATE, not an inequality of the two rendered values.** The accepted set is an INTERVAL (DL-292): `'8'` and `8.9` both belong to a mapping of 8. A ledger keyed on `card_board !== mapped_board` would mint a permanent, unprunable row every time kanban spelled the same board differently — noise in the one table whose emptiness is its signal — while saying nothing new about the case that matters. A test leg pins exactly this and reds under that mutation alone.

**Decision 4 — nothing on the happy path, `bridge:prune` never touches this table, and a REPEAT counts on the row it already has. ⛔ RE-DERIVED at review: the bound this decision first rested on was FALSE.** A row per writeback would put the bridge's whole write rate into the DB to record the one thing every other row's absence already implies. So the healthy state is EMPTY and **growth is the signal**. Retention is the mirror of that: a window on the record that exists to outlive a window is the same defect with a longer fuse. That much stands. What did not is the sentence that made the accepted risk sound small — *"it is bounded by the webhook rate"*. **`bridge:reconcile` is the seventh arm of this record (DL-301) and is not webhook-driven at all**: it is an operator CLI documented for an **hourly cron** (`docs/writeback.md § Scheduling`), it renders the pair on **every** run including the report-only one (the guard sits before the run decides anything, so a run with no `--fix` still writes to this table), and the row had no dedup — the ALERT dedups on `(repo, outcome, reason)`, the row did not. Measured: the same foreign card over three consecutive report-only runs gave **1, 2, 3** rows. ⇒ on a board read that has stopped being scoped, an append-only table takes **N rows per hour, indefinitely**, in the one table nothing prunes — and `bridge:stats`'s count becomes a measure of how long the cron has been running rather than of how many divergences there are. That is the signal degrading into noise in exactly the failure mode this table exists for.

**The fix is at the row's IDENTITY, not at its lifetime.** One row per DISTINCT observation: `observation_key` (a hash of the whole stored observation) is UNIQUE, and a repeat bumps `observations` and `last_seen_at` in place. The table is then bounded by the number of distinct divergences the install has ever had — which is the quantity being recorded — instead of by uptime, and the row answers *when did this start* (`created_at`, never rewritten), *is it still happening* (`last_seen_at`) and *how often* (`observations`): the three questions N identical rows made the reader count for themselves. **A hash rather than a composite `UNIQUE` over the columns**, because `card_id` and `site` are NULLABLE and both MariaDB and SQLite treat NULLs in a unique index as distinct — the bound would have leaked on precisely the unreadable responses that accompany this failure. It is derived from the row's own stored attributes, so a column added to the observation joins the identity with no second column list to keep in step, and the two board spellings the model deliberately stores identically (`12`, `'12'`) are one observation here too. **Rejected instead:** *pruning or capping the table* — the row a cap drops is the OLDEST, i.e. the first sighting, the single most valuable one; *special-casing the reconcile arm* — a webhook redelivery repeats an observation too, and the N+1th arm would re-mint the vector, so the dedup belongs in the ledger (canon #5). **Accepted, stated:** the timestamps of the 2nd…Nth sighting are not kept, only the first, the last and the count; `site` carries a line number, so moving the code mints a new row (the observation genuinely moved); and two processes first-observing the same divergence concurrently can race the insert, where the loser's unique-key violation lands in the never-throw catch and costs one sighting off a counter, never the row.

**Decision 5 — the call site is read from the stack, not passed in.** `Class::method (File.php:NN)`, resolved by walking past the guard's own frames, with `DEBUG_BACKTRACE_IGNORE_ARGS` so no card payload can ride into an audit row. An `$arm` argument would have to be spelled at eleven call sites, beside a message string that already names the arm — and the site this table exists to catch is the one that would omit it.

**Decision 6 — `bridge:stats` prints the counts on EVERY run, zero included — and says so when it could not take them.** A line that appeared only when the table was non-empty would make *"no cross-board write was ever recorded"* indistinguishable from *"nothing measured it"* — this card's own defect, one level up. The zero is the measurement. **Three states, not two, for the same reason:** an install that upgraded without running `php artisan migrate` has every other table and not this one, so that case prints `NOT MEASURED — table missing` rather than a `0` that would assert something nobody checked. Until the review it printed neither: the missing table threw through `guardDatabase()` and took the whole report — including the event and dispatch counts the command had always printed — down with it, under a message blaming `DB_HOST` for a server that had just answered. `guardDatabase()` now probes the connection and reports which of the two it is (the branch is measured, never sniffed off a driver's SQLSTATE — a missing table is `HY000` on SQLite and `42S02` on MariaDB). The counts are of ROWS, i.e. of distinct divergences (Decision 4); `observations` on the row is where a repeat shows up.

**Schema, and who reads it.** `writeback_board_divergences`: `disposition` · `card_id` · `card_board` (the card's own board VERBATIM, as a string — a string value is stored as-is so one board has one spelling, anything else through `json_encode` so a non-board value cannot masquerade as a board id; NULL when the row carried no readable board, which is an observation and not a missing field) · `mapped_board` · `site` · `created_at`, indexed `(disposition, created_at)`. The reader is an operator or agent asking, months later, *"did a cross-board write ever land here?"* — so the row must answer **whether** (disposition), **which card and boards** (to open the card), **where** (to read the code), and **when**. There is no `repo` column: `boardContext()` is not given one, and inventing it from the card payload would be a guessed value in an audit row. There is no `updated_at`: the rows are immutable observations.

**A persistence failure is logged, never thrown.** This runs mid-writeback — after kanban has already been written to, and on the refusal arm whose contract is a permanent no-op (never a 5xx redelivery storm; the DL-020 posture). A missing table or an unreachable DB is deterministic, so retrying it would only re-run the write it audits. The `Log::error` carries the same rendered pair, so the observation still lands in the record that has 14 days.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **A `Log::listen` tap persisting any record whose context carries a divergent pair** — attractive (zero call-site edits, the message names the arm) and REJECTED on evidence: `Illuminate\Log\Logger::writeLog()` returns early when the channel's handler is not handling that level, so `MessageLogged` never fires. An install with `LOG_LEVEL=warning` would durably record refusals and silently lose every success-side observation — the defect re-minted, controlled by an unrelated config knob. (b) **A row per writeback, filtered at read time** — REJECTED by the operator's ruling and on the merits (Decision 4). (c) **A `persist()` call beside each of the eleven records** — REJECTED: eleven duplicated arm strings, and the N+1th site omits it (Decision 1). (d) **Re-deriving the divergence in the ledger from the rendered pair** — REJECTED: it needs the DL-292 compare, and a fourth copy of that predicate is what `MappedBoardGuard` and `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` exist to prevent. The ledger is handed the verdict and the already-rendered pair instead. (e) **Alerting on a `recorded` row** — NOT done: the alert channel is for live wake-ups and this state is unreachable on today's code; `bridge:stats` and the table are the reader's surface, and adding a push is a separate ruling.

**⛔ Bound, stated.** A `recorded` row is unreachable on today's code — every writeback arm inside the mapped-board regime is gated by `MappedBoardGuard::refuses()` (DL-292 + DL-298 + DL-301), so a divergent card cannot reach a write record. That is not an argument against the table; it is the argument for it. This is a tripwire for the N+1th write site and for a gate that regresses, and it is the only instrument that can answer the question at all once the log has rolled. **⚠ `bridge:reconcile` is INSIDE the regime and inside this record.** This paragraph first said the opposite — *"remains outside the regime entirely (card#7211) and therefore outside this record too — it renders no pair, so it mints no row"* — which was true of the tree it was written against and false of the merged one: DL-301 landed on `dev` in the same window and made the command the **seventh** `refuses()` arm, which is where a `refused` row is minted. It mints one per refused card per run, on report-only runs as well as `--fix` ones (measured: two rows, cards 6 and 7, sited at `ReconcileCommand->reconcileCard`), and it is the growth vector Decision 4 was re-derived against. **The correction is recorded rather than quietly applied, because a textually clean merge is what produced it** — no line was lost from either parent, and each parent's claims were true; only their conjunction was false. Nothing in a merge diff can show that.

**Consequences:** `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext()` (a third, defaulted `$disposition` parameter and the persist; `refuses()` passes `refused`); new `app/Bridge/Writeback/BoardDivergenceLedger.php` (the disposition vocabulary, the insert, the call-site resolver, the never-throw envelope — and it names no column, spreading the rendered pair straight into the insert, which is what keeps `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`'s one-rendering leg true and makes a key rename a migration); new `app/Models/WritebackBoardDivergence.php` (`card_board` mutator; identity fields immutable, with `observations`/`last_seen_at` the only columns a row ever rewrites); new migration; `StatsCommand` (three always-printed rows, plus the table-absent state) and `BridgeCommand::guardDatabase()` (which of missing-schema / unreachable-server it was, measured); `CLAUDE.md` / `CLAUDE_ARCHITECTURE.md` / `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` (the third store and its retention posture) and `docs/writeback.md` (the durable half of the card#7212 section). **Tests:** 9 new methods in `tests/Feature/Writeback/WritebackBoardDivergenceLedgerTest.php`, each happy-path leg PAIRED with a witness that the write really happened and the pair really rendered — an absence asserted alone certifies whatever replaces it, including nothing. **Seen to fail (9 mutants, each restored):** no persist (3 divergence legs + the never-throw leg red); persist unconditionally (both happy-path legs + the mixed refusal leg red); the raw-inequality trigger (the INTERVAL leg alone, which is the leg's whole reason to exist); `refuses()` not marking its disposition (the refusal leg); a null call site (both site legs); rethrowing instead of logging (the never-throw leg errors); a stringifier that drops a non-numeric board (the verbatim leg — this one initially passed and the leg was ADDED because of it); the stats row removed (the reader-surface leg); and a renamed column in the migration (the key-drift leg). The presence witnesses were watched red under a collapse that makes no write.

**Added by the pre-merge review (same card, same PR).** `observation_key` / `observations` / `last_seen_at` on the migration and the model (Decision 4, re-derived), with the identity computed once in the ledger; `BridgeCommand::guardDatabase()` and `StatsCommand`'s third state (Decision 6); a sentence in `RetentionService`'s docblock, which is the file a maintainer adding retention would edit and the one place the never-prune ruling was not stated; and the test isolation this record's own write exposed — `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext()` made six test classes touch the database transitively for the first time (`ReconcileCommandTest`, `ResolvedRowBoardGuardTest`, `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`, `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest`, `KanbanBlockReasonHandlerTest`, `KanbanCoordCardMoveHandlerTest`), none of which declared `RefreshDatabase`, because before this change none of them needed one. On SQLite `:memory:` every one of those inserts threw `no such table` and was swallowed by the ledger's own never-throw envelope; on the shared MariaDB of the CI matrix they COMMITTED, and 26 rows were waiting for the first test that asserted on the table — which is how a change with a green SQLite suite came back red on both MariaDB legs, two directories from its cause. The traits are added, `ReconcileCommandTest` (the arm with the growth vector and no ledger assertion at all) now pins both refused rows, and `Tests\TestCase` fails any test that leaves rows in this table with no isolation trait, naming the class that did it. ⛔ That backstop is **blind on SQLite by construction** — an un-isolated test there has no table to leave rows in — so it is the MariaDB legs that enforce it, which is the same asymmetry that hid the defect and is now the thing that catches it.

**Tests seen to fail (this review's five, each restored):** the identity made unique per observation ⇒ the repeat leg reds with 3 rows where 1 is required; the identity collapsed to a constant ⇒ the control leg reds with 1 row where 2 are required (without that control, a degenerate key passes the repeat leg perfectly); the repeat routed through the base query builder so it does not touch the timestamp ⇒ the same leg reds on `last_seen_at` still naming the first sighting; `StatsCommand`'s table-absent arm removed ⇒ the stats leg reds on exit 1, which is the reported regression exactly; and the persist disabled ⇒ `ReconcileCommandTest`'s new ledger assertion reds on an empty table. **⛔ One mutant came back GREEN and is recorded rather than dropped:** making the ledger `save()` unconditionally still leaves one row with the right count, because the UNIQUE key refuses the second insert and the never-throw catch swallows it — the dedup is enforced by the index, and the code path above it only decides whether the failure is normal or noisy. **The isolation backstop was proven the same way, and only on MariaDB:** with `RefreshDatabase` removed from `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest`, that class reds naming itself; the identical run on SQLite stays green, which is the asymmetry stated above.

## DL-301 — `bridge:reconcile --fix` re-checks each board-read row against the mapped board before it moves it, and records the board a landed move actually hit (card#7211)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7211, the fourth and last search-resolved write site — the one DL-298 disclosed as an open gap and this closes). **⛔ Hard-gate approved by the operator** — like DL-298 it is a fail-closed tightening on a write path: a card `bridge:reconcile --fix` moves today stops being moved if the row the board read returned does not name the mapped board. **The newly-refused set is EMPTY on a correctly-scoped instance, and that is the design intent.** No config key, no migration, no token-scope change, nothing about what the receiver accepts.

**The defect, and it is DL-298's verbatim.** `ReconcileCommand::reconcileBoard` reads a board through `KanbanClient::readBoardCards` — a `q=board_id=<b>` server-side search — and `finish()` calls `moveCard` on the ids that read produced, with no client-side re-check. The scoping IS honoured today (measured with a control, rt#327), but the same endpoint silently drops an unrecognised **top-level** parameter and answers 200 with an unfiltered result set, and `board_id` happens to filter correctly as a bare top-level parameter too — so the `q=`→top-level hoist that breaks the scope reviews as equivalent and tests green. Nothing in a 200 distinguishes a dropped filter from an honoured one. DL-298 fixed the three handler sites and recorded this one as a stated gap; a disclosed defect is not a closed one.

**Decision 1 — same primitive, seventh arm, no second predicate.** The command calls `MappedBoardGuard::refuses()` with the arm name `bridge_reconcile` and the synthetic outcome `reconcile` (a CLI run has no PR outcome of its own; the constant is what keeps this arm's dedup marker from sharing one with the event arms, DL-274(3)). It therefore inherits the DL-292 predicate, the `card_not_on_mapped_board` reason code, and the paired warn+notify report — a CLI cannot mint a fourth compare or a quieter log level.

**Decision 2 — the gate sits where a row becomes a card the run will DECIDE about, not at the write.** It runs immediately after the card's `(repo, mapping)` resolves and **before** the per-card GitHub read. The promote handler's rule ("refuse where the row becomes a candidate, so the refused set equals the set we would otherwise have written to") lands here differently, and deliberately: whether a given card gets written is not knowable until its PR is read, so *every reconcilable card* is a potential write. Gating earlier also stops a foreign card's `pr_url` being dereferenced with this repo's GitHub token, and keeps foreign rows out of the `in sync` / `backward` counts — a run that reconciled another tenant's board and reported it as in-sync would be a false green in the shape this card is about.

**Decision 3 — the refusal is LOUD, and the run exits non-zero.** Per refused card: a `REFUSED` console line naming it, the durable `Log::warning` and the alert from the primitive; and `hadError`, so the process exits 1. This is the posture the command already takes for its other degradations (unreadable stage order, a mid-run 401/403) rather than a new one — a `bridge:reconcile` on a timer reading exit 0 over a cross-board row in its board read would be reporting a clean reconcile over an unfiltered result set. **Dedup is unchanged** (`(repo, outcome, reason)`): one push per run carrying the first refused card, with the console lines and the per-card log as the enumeration.

**Decision 4 — the DURABLE move record carries the OBSERVED pair; the console report does not.** `driftRow()` carries `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext($card, $mapping)` alongside the mapped board id, so a row reaching `finish()` still has the card's own `board_id` (raw) in hand long after the row itself is out of scope. **The applied move writes `Log::info('bridge_reconcile: moved', …)` with that pair** — this is the part that is not merely bookkeeping. The refusal is durable (it goes through the alert primitive); the success was `$this->info(...)` only, i.e. wherever the operator's cron happens to redirect stdout. Recording only the refusal answers *"did we ever stop it?"* and never *"did this ever happen?"* — the exact asymmetry card#7212 closed for the six handler arms, and it would have been re-minted here by fixing the guard alone. The console `MOVED` line is unchanged beside it. **Ruled in scope rather than filed**: without it, threading the pair into the record would render a value nothing durable ever reads.

**⛔ The DRIFT / SKIP-DRIFT console lines keep printing the MAPPED board, and the review that asked for the card's own value there is the reason this says so.** A first revision of this change rendered `card_board` on those lines through a `boardText()` helper with an `'unknown'` arm for a non-scalar value. That helper was DELETED before the change shipped, on the review's measurement plus canon #6: after the guard, `belongs()` has already established `(int) card_board === mapped_board` on every row that can reach a report line, so the helper rendered a divergence that cannot occur and defended a state — an absent or unreadable `board_id` — that the guard refuses two hundred lines earlier. The pair still lives where it does work: the durable record, which is the half that answers *"did this ever happen?"*. Deleting it also removed the only `card_board` literal in the command, which is what let `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`'s census widen onto the bridge CLI with no predicate split (Decision 5).

**Decision 5 — TWO class guards' populations widened onto the bridge CLI, and the second one only because Decision 4 removed what blocked it.** `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest`'s KIND leg (the level-independent one: no file may spell `'board_id'` or `'card_not_on_mapped_board'` itself) now also globs `app/Console/Commands/Bridge/*.php` — the new arm is the first caller of the primitive outside the handler files, so without it the newest copy of the rule would sit exactly where that leg cannot see. Empty today; **proven able to fail** by planting a compare in the command and watching it red on `ReconcileCommand.php:<line>`. The LEVEL-keyed leg (bare `Log::warning`/`Log::error` against an allow-list) is unchanged and still handler-only, so the two legs no longer share a population — recorded in the class docblock. **`WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`'s write census was widened too — a file glob, not a residue.** A first revision left it alone and named `ReconcileCommand::moveCard` as a stated residue, because leg 2 forbids spelling `card_board`/`mapped_board` as a literal and the report line then READ `card_board` off the rendered pair; splitting that predicate into render-vs-read looked like the only way through. The review dissolved the conflict rather than paying for it: deleting the report-line render (Decision 4) leaves the command spelling neither key, so `app/Console/Commands/Bridge/*.php` joins the file axis with **no predicate change at all**. Cost measured with the test's own `writeMethodsOf`/`writeSites` derivations over that glob: **exactly one** new entry, `ReconcileCommand.php:moveCard => 1` — every other `bridge:*` command is read-only. Legs 2 and 3 come back empty over the new files and were seen to fail (below). **A second kanban write added to that command, or a first one added to any other bridge command, now reds** — which is what the residue would have cost, and no longer does. *[Additive annotation, 2026-09-02 (card#8530) — **the KIND leg no longer globs anything.** The widening minuted here was the right direction and too small a step: its population is now the whole of `app/`, derived on the tokenizer through `Tests\Support\SourceScan::sitesInApp`, the same primitive the pre-read enforcer uses, with a per-site disposition list in place of the empty expectation. `bridge:reconcile`'s arm is still in the population — it is inside `app/` — and still comes back with nothing of its own to disposition. `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest`'s three axes are UNCHANGED and still glob-derived; only this leg moved.]*

**Proven the way it fails.** Two methods in `tests/Feature/Console/ReconcileCommandTest.php` (beside the command's own harness — the console fixture is not re-derived in `ResolvedRowBoardGuardTest`, which now points here). The guard leg feeds a **MIXED** set in one measurement: a mapped row that drifts forward, a row naming board 12, and a row with no `board_id` at all — identical in every respect but the board. **Watched red with the guard disabled: the foreign card WAS PATCHed** (`Unexpected request was recorded`). It asserts the presence witness (the mapped card still moves), both controls (neither refused row is written, neither PR is fetched), the alert body, the dedup bound (card 7's refusal is log-only), and the non-zero exit. The record leg pins `card_board === '8'` on a mapped board of `8` — the divergence forced through the DL-292 accepted INTERVAL, because the guard now makes a genuinely foreign row unreachable on that path; a record echoing the mapping gives int `8`. **Watched red twice:** once with the pair replaced by a mapped-board echo, once with the `Log::info` removed (the pre-fix, console-only state).

**Four more mutants, all watched, from the review that removed `boardText()`.** (1) **The new ACCOUNTED entry dropped** — the widened census reds naming `ReconcileCommand.php:moveCard => 1` and nothing else, which is simultaneously the proof that the new file axis is live and the re-derivation of the widening's cost. (2) **A hand-rolled `['card_board' => …, 'mapped_board' => …]` planted in `StatsCommand`** — leg 2 reds on `StatsCommand.php:<line>`, so the one-rendering rule now reaches every `bridge:*` command and not only the one this change touched. (3) **`driftRow`'s board argument replaced by a constant** — both report legs red, because the DRIFT and SKIP-DRIFT assertions were tightened from a bare `DRIFT` / `SKIP-DRIFT` keyword match to the whole line including the board column. That column was asserted by NOTHING before the review: a mutant restoring the pre-fix report line left `ReconcileCommandTest` 21/21 green, which is what made the console render look load-bearing when it was not. (4) **The guard disabled** re-run after the removal — still red: the run exits 0 where the method requires 1, because the foreign row is reconciled instead of refused. (The exit assertion fires before the wire assertions, so this run's message names the exit code where the pre-removal run named the unexpected PATCH; the mutant is the same one.)

**⛔ One review finding measured and CLOSED rather than fixed: the alert dedup directory is not a cross-user exposure on this install.** `ReconcileCommand` is the first `app/Console/` caller of `WritebackAlertNotifier`, whose dedup markers live under `<state_dir>/writeback-alerts` at mode 0700 — so a cron running as a different OS user than the PHP-FPM pool would lock one of the two out of the other's markers. **Measured on this host:** the bridge's PHP-FPM pool runs as `kanban`, the cron runs as `kanban`, and `~/.config/agent-webhook-bridge-prod/state/` is `kanban`-owned mode 0700 with the receiver's `inbox.jsonl` written there as the same user. Same user; the exposure does not exist here, and no code changed for it. Recorded so the next reader does not re-open it — it is a claim about THIS install's user model, not a property of the notifier, and an install that splits those users would have to re-answer it.

**Consequences:** `ReconcileCommand` (the guard, the `reconcile` outcome constant, an injected `WritebackAlertNotifier` on the handlers' own optional-argument shape, the board pair carried to `finish()` for the durable move record, the class docblock's safety-posture list, and `$boardId` dropped from `reconcileCard` — the loop's board id no longer travels anywhere; the report line takes `$mapping->boardId`, which is the same value by construction); `MappedBoardGuard` (docblock: three arms → six → **seven**, in three families, with the pointer to where a missing arm actually reds rather than another restatement); `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` (KIND-leg population + both docblock bounds); `WritebackSuccessBoardRecordTest` (the file axis widened to `app/Console/Commands/Bridge/*.php`, one new ACCOUNTED entry, and the Console-command bound rewritten from *"outside the population"* to what it now is); `ReconcileCommandTest` (the two DL-301 methods, plus the pre-existing forward/backward drift methods tightened onto the whole report line); `KanbanBlockReasonHandler` (a call-site comment claiming the primitive serves *"all three arms"* — a live-state count with no owner, replaced by a pointer at the one that has the list); `ResolvedRowBoardGuardTest` (its stated BOUND was *"the fourth site … is NOT covered here and is NOT guarded"* — now false in its second half, so it names where the cover lives); `docs/writeback.md` (the "one site of that class is still open" paragraph, the shared dedup bound, the signal table's new CLI arm, the reconcile section's safety posture and move record, the census's file-glob sentence, and two live-state *"all three arms"* counts the DL-292 era left behind); `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md` (the `bridge:reconcile` safety-posture enumeration — the THIRD hand-synced copy of one list, which the new refusal reached in none of its siblings; collapsed to a pointer at `docs/writeback.md § Reconciliation` rather than re-synced, canon #16's DELETE case); `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md` (§3: three of four → **all four**); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`; `CLAUDE_DECISIONS.md` DL-298's stated gap AND its *"two doc edits this change OWES"* clause, both marked discharged in place.

## DL-302 — `board_my_cards` reports the board its ROWS are on, the coord block stops inheriting a board that does not describe it, and the live probes read the scope header under its own name (card#7295)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7295 — the sibling the card#7225 audit found; same tier, same surface, different tool). **No refusal, no drop, no config key, no migration, no token-scope change, and nothing about what the receiver or the tool ACCEPTS.** Caller-visible: the meaning of `result.board_id` changes and three (own) + three (coord) keys appear.

**⚠ HARD-GATE CLASS — recorded, not waved away.** The paragraph above is accurate about what does NOT change, and it is not the whole disposition. This is a **breaking change to the meaning of a key in a shipped cross-seat response contract**: an agent reading `result.board_id` gets `null` on the common empty-window path after upgrade, where it previously got the configured board. That is hard-gate class on the same reading DL-223 applied to the HTTP-relay corrupt-body flip — a change to what an outward-facing surface reports, ratified there as *"hard-gate class … covered by the standing autonomous-dev-branch authorization"* and surfaced as its own item rather than buried. Same disposition here: it ships on a **dev-targeted** PR under the operator's standing dev authorization (2026-07-18 — dev-targeted PRs carry no per-change merge gate; the gate is the release→`main` PR), and it is called out in the PR body and in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`'s ⚠ UPGRADING bullet, not folded into "no behaviour change". The honest record is **hard-gate class, authorized** — not *not hard-gate*.

**The defect.** `BoardMyCardsTool::call()` stated `'board_id' => (int) $cfg->boardId` — where this agent is CONFIGURED to read — for a row set whose own `board_id` nothing had looked at. A calling agent reads that key as *"these cards are on board N"*, and nothing established it. The same file already filters the LANE axis fail-closed (`filterSwimlane` drops + logs a row whose own `swimlane_id` does not match), so one tool carried two standards for the two axes of the same claim: one verified, one asserted. That asymmetry is what makes it a defect rather than a design choice — the pattern the board axis was missing was already in the file. **Measured, not assumed:** kanban's `TaskResource` emits `board_id` on every row `/tasks/search.json` returns and `tasks.board_id` is a non-nullable FK, so the reading was already in the tool's hand and cost nothing to take.

**Decision 1 — report the reading; do NOT drop and do NOT refuse.** `board_id` is now the board the returned rows carry, `board_observed` says whether one was read, and `configured_board_id` carries what the key used to hold, under a name that says what it is. Dropping a foreign row or refusing the call is an accept/reject change and is ask-gated; it also trades one wrong answer for another — a silently dropped row is as invisible to the caller as a mislabelled one. The board is not the isolation boundary here (kanban scopes reads by the token user's BOARD membership; the LANE is what the bridge must enforce, and that filter is untouched), so a report is the whole of what was wrong.

**Decision 2 — the pair, not the observation alone.** An empty window observes nothing, and an agent with no cards is the common case; answering only `board_id: null` there would delete a datum the response used to carry. `MappedBoardGuard::boardContext` already ruled this shape for the writeback record (card#7212: BOTH keys on BOTH arms, because a record carrying one can answer *"did we stop it?"* and never *"did this happen?"*), and this follows it: observed and intended are both present, both named, neither dressed as the other. `swimlane_id` gets no flag and needs none — every row is filtered against it before projection, so the lane axis is verified by construction.

**Decision 3 — unobserved on ANY row unobserves the SET, and there is no key-absent/value-null discrimination on this axis.** The response states ONE board for a row set, so a set that does not unanimously answer has no honest single value: a non-numeric/absent/null `board_id` on any row, or two boards across the set, yields `[null, false]` — never a majority, never the configured board. ⛔ **This is the one place the card#7225 shape must NOT be copied.** That fix (card#7225 — a SEPARATE change that may not be in your build, and not depended on here; it corrects BOTH axes of that tool's reported placement, and only its LANE axis has a legitimate null) has to tell a PRESENT `swimlane_id: null` (a card really is in no lane) from an ABSENT key; `tasks.board_id` is non-nullable, so a card is always on exactly one board and all three spellings mean *unread*. The accepted set of the compare is `is_numeric` + `(int)` — deliberately the same one `MappedBoardGuard::belongs()` applies — but it is **not routed through that primitive**, and the card's suggestion to do so was measured and declined: `belongs()` takes a `WritebackMapping` (a repo→board WRITE mapping this read path does not have and must not invent), it answers a membership DECISION that ends in a refusal, and its predicate is pinned VERBATIM by `WritebackRefusalSignalCoverageTest` against DL-292's minuted vector table — reshaping it to serve a read projection is a gated change to a security guard, not a refactor. That guard's KIND leg globs the handlers and `app/Console/Commands/Bridge/`, so a read tool naming `board_id` does not red it; widening it onto `app/Bridge/Tools/` would forbid the very reading this change exists to take. *[Additive annotation, 2026-09-02 (card#8530) — **the RULING stands and is now what the guard implements; the MECHANISM sentence is superseded.** The KIND leg globs nothing any more: it walks the whole of `app/`, so `BoardMyCardsTool::observedBoard()` IS in its population — and it does not red, because the leg dispositions each site rather than forbidding it. This entry's decision is the disposition's stated reason, verbatim in kind: report-only on a READ path, `BoardToolsConfig` axis and not `WritebackMapping`, reshaping `belongs()` to serve a read projection being a gated change to a security guard. What "widening onto `app/Bridge/Tools/`" would have cost — a false red pushing the author to launder a non-refusal compare through the refusal primitive — is exactly why the population was widened with a disposition list instead of an empty expectation.]*

**Decision 4 — the coord block carries its own board pair (the card's appended second member, verified at source).** `coordCards()` projected rows from `cardRowsByTag($cfg->coordBoardId, …)` with **no board key at all** — confirmed by reading, as the append asked. It is the same surface in the MISSING-KEY variant rather than the wrong-value one, and it needed a different answer, decided on the record rather than by symmetry: nothing false was asserted there, so this is an ADDITION, and the case for it is that Decision 1 sharpens the ambiguity it lives in. Once the top-level `board_id` means *where these cards are*, a second card list sitting under it from a DIFFERENT board with nothing saying so is the reading a caller will make. `coord_board_id` / `coord_board_observed` / `configured_coord_board_id` appear on exactly the condition `coord_cards` does; the list itself is unchanged, so no consumer of it breaks.

**Decision 5 — the two live probes read the scope header under its own name, and their claim about what it proves is corrected.** `bridge:check --probe-tools` and `--probe-tools-ssh` compared `result.board_id` against config. Left alone, that compare would fail every agent whose lane is EMPTY (`board_id: null`) with an ISOLATION finding — a false failure on the commonest state. Both now read `configured_board_id` through the new `BoardToolsScopeHeader`, which owns the two spellings in ONE place. **NEITHER leg is guaranteed to be talking to the install it runs inside:** `--probe-tools-ssh` round-trips to another HOST outright, and `--probe-tools` POSTs to an operator-supplied vhost that rule 7's co-resident prod/dev installs can serve at an independent version — so both can meet a responder predating this entry, which answers only the old key. Read strictly, that version skew would be reported as a scope violation, a specific WRONG cause. **The claim was the other half.** The probe's `ok` line said the header matching config *"is the observable that the bridge-side isolation filter ran"*, and DL-217 recorded the probe as verifying *"the swimlane isolation property"*. **Both are false, and were false when written:** the header is an identity ECHO of whatever agent the bearer resolved to, so config compared against config is true whatever the rows held. What it does certify — that this bearer reached THIS agent's window, which a token collision or a mis-pinned key breaks — is real. **All FOUR operator-facing strings say it, not just the docblocks:** both `ok` lines carry the identity-echo caveat, and both fail tails name an identity/bearer-resolution cause (*this key/bearer resolved to a DIFFERENT agent's window — look for a token collision or a mis-pinned key*) instead of the lane-scoping cause they used to assert. A first pass corrected the docblocks and the HTTP `ok` line and left the two fail tails and the ssh `ok` line saying the false thing — the review caught it, and it is the sibling sweep (canon #7) of the very claim this entry exists to correct: **the surface an operator actually reads is the message, not the docblock.**

**The LABEL moved with them.** `ISOLATION` (ssh) / `ISOLATION MISMATCH` (HTTP) carried the same overclaim as the tails, in the loudest word on the line: it sends an operator hunting a read-isolation breach that this probe structurally cannot see. Both legs now emit one shared **`IDENTITY MISMATCH`** — one label for one condition across the two probes, which is also what the condition is. `bridge:check` `message` strings are explicitly outside the `--format=json` write contract (`docs/check-json-contract.md`), so no machine consumer is broken; the ssh golden fixture and three in-repo assertions moved in the same change.

**The skew tolerance is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, and the other direction is an upgrade-order constraint, not a code one.** The fallback lives on the READING side, so it covers old-responder → new-prober only. An old `bridge:check` on host B probing a NEW responder on host A reads `result.board_id` strictly and, on the commonest state (an empty lane ⇒ `board_id: null`), reports a mismatch and exits 1 — naming the wrong cause, exactly the failure the fallback exists to prevent in the other direction. No code can fix that from this side; `docs/CHANGELOG.md`'s ⚠ UPGRADING bullet owns the rollout order (prober first) and the signature of the false failure, and this entry deliberately does not restate them.

DL-217 stays as written (the log is append-only); this entry corrects it. **The probes deliberately do NOT assert on the new observation:** a fail arm there changes what `bridge:check` rejects, which is gated, and it is filed on card#7295 rather than taken here.

**Proven the way it fails.** The pre-existing `ToolsCallCommandTest` happy path is the defect's own witness: it fakes an EMPTY window and asserted `board_id === 10`, and it went red on `Failed asserting that null is identical to 10` — the tool had been reporting a board it had read nothing about, and one test had been pinning that. **Ten new test METHODS** in `AgentToolsCallTest` — 13 executed CASES, because one of the ten is a four-case data provider; the diff adds 13 functions in all, those ten plus two fakers and the provider, so the population has to be named with the number (`git diff origin/dev...HEAD -- tests/Feature/AgentTools/AgentToolsCallTest.php | grep -c '^+    public function test_'` ⇒ 10). The ten: own-board reading, a foreign board reported as the row's own, four unreadable-board spellings (the provider), a two-board set, the empty window, a foreign SHARED lane unobserving the whole window, three coord-board cases, and the absent coord keys. Each was watched red under a mutant of the thing it guards — the pre-fix `'board_id' => $boardId` restatement, `board_observed` hard-wired true, `observedBoard` returning unobserved, the coord keys dropped, and the coord gate forced on. Probe side: a window whose rows are on a foreign board still certifies OK (the probe asserts identity, not rows), an unobserved board still certifies, and the old-key responder is accepted on BOTH legs — the HTTP probe can meet a skewed responder too (its endpoint is an operator-supplied vhost, and rule 7 puts prod + dev installs on one box at independent versions), so the tolerance is unit-covered once per leg and both tests are deleted with the fallback. The ssh GOLDEN fixture feeds the CURRENT envelope shape (an empty window: `board_id: null`, `configured_board_id: 10`) rather than the pre-DL-302 spelling it was first written with — the only end-to-end witness of the `ok` line must exercise the live shape, not the fallback, or deleting the fallback later would silently re-pin a mismatch as that fixture's correct output.

**Consequences:** `BoardMyCardsTool` (`observedBoard`, `coordCards` → `coordBlock`, the shared-lane read hoisted out of the result literal so the top-level reading covers own+shared, class docblock; the coord block is spliced PER KEY rather than by `+=`, whose array-union would silently discard a right-hand key a future result literal grew — phpstan reds a wrong key against `coordBlock()`'s declared shape, which `+=` gave no way to check; and the top-level `observedBoard` leg label is `own` when no shared lane is configured, so a diagnostic never names a leg that did not run); new `BoardToolsScopeHeader`; `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheck` + `SshTransportProbe` (header read, both class/method docblocks, both `ok` lines, both fail tails, and the `ISOLATION`→`IDENTITY MISMATCH` relabel — the old text named a response key that now means something else and a cause the probe cannot see, both of which send the operator to the wrong field); `AgentToolsCallTest`, `ToolsCallCommandTest`, `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheckTest`, `SshTransportProbeTest`, `BridgeCommandsTest`, `CheckGoldenTest` + the regenerated `board-tools-ssh-live-probe` golden; `docs/board-tools.md` (the return shape + a new § on `board_id` vs `configured_board_id`, and the § 6 verify step's claim); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
