## DL-303 — the test suite blocks a stray HTTP request instead of letting it reach the network, and the blast radius was derived by turning it on rather than estimated (card#7300)

- **Date:** 2026-08-22
- **Status:** implemented (card#7300, which absorbed the independently-filed card#7322 as the same shape). **Tests and docs only** — no file under `app/`, `bin/`, `config/`, `routes/` or `database/` is touched, no config key, no migration, no token-scope change, and **no change to what the bridge accepts, refuses, writes or retries**. What moves is what the suite PROVES about a release, which is why it carries a CHANGELOG entry a test-only change would not otherwise need.
- **Discharges** the bound DL-299 recorded on itself — *"`preventStrayRequests()` was deliberately NOT adopted in `tests/TestCase.php` — that is a suite-wide posture change with an unmeasured full-suite blast radius, filed as its own card."* This is that card. The log is append-only, so DL-299's sentence stays as written; this entry is where it is answered.

**The defect.** `Http::fake()` does not BLOCK a request no stub answers. `PendingRequest::buildStubHandler()` invokes every registered callback, takes the first truthy result, and when there is none falls through to the **live** handler. A bare `Http::fake()` and a `'*'` closure answer everything and hide this; the URL-pattern array form — the majority form in this suite (`grep -c 'Http::fake('` over `tests/` against the same grep for `Http::fake(\['`) — does not. Nothing here called `Http::preventStrayRequests()`. ⇒ **an outbound call on an already-covered path left the process on every suite run, and the suite stayed green**, because the caller's fail-soft `catch` (the correct production posture) swallowed the connection failure and the test's own assertions passed *through the degradation arm* while naming the happy path.

⛔ **The green was a property of the RUNNER'S NETWORK, not of the code.** Those legs passed because DNS failed. Two different causes — *a stub answered* and *the host did not resolve* — produced the same pass, and nothing distinguished them. On a box where the host resolves, the same test asserts against whatever answers.

**Decision 1 — `Http::preventStrayRequests()` in `Tests\TestCase::setUp()`, suite-wide, with the strays FIXED rather than exempted.** The factory flag is read at request-construction time (`Factory::createPendingRequest()` copies it onto each `PendingRequest`), so setting it before a test's own `Http::fake()` calls is not shadowed by them, and it covers a class that never calls `Http::fake()` at all — the stub handler is pushed onto the stack unconditionally. An unmatched request then raises `StrayRequestException` naming the exact URL.

**Decision 1b — the refusal is PAIRED with a recorder, because refusing a request does not make it visible.** This is alternative (f) below, and it is the half that makes the change worth more than its stub count. `Http::globalMiddleware()` registers a Guzzle middleware on the factory; `PendingRequest::pushHandlers()` pushes the global middleware FIRST and Guzzle resolves its stack in reverse push order, so that middleware is strictly OUTSIDE `buildStubHandler()` and sees the `StrayRequestException` on its way out. It records the url and re-throws the exception unchanged — the loud path is byte-for-byte what it was — and `Tests\TestCase::tearDown()` fails the test naming every recorded url the test did not declare with `expectStrayRequest()`. ⇒ **the 47 stubs this change adds that no assertion witnesses are load-bearing after all: drop one and the test reds.** The discriminator is the exception CLASS, which is why this works where the DL's own first reading said it could not (see (f)).

**Decision 1c — the report is made inside a `finally`, because a guard that throws out of `tearDown()` aborts `parent::tearDown()` and poisons the rest of the run.** `fail()` throws, and the throw skipped `tearDownTheTestEnvironment()` — `Mockery::close()`, `HandleExceptions::flushState()`, `$app->flush()` and every `beforeApplicationDestroyed` callback. `RefreshDatabase` registers its ROLLBACK as one of those and caches the PDO in the STATIC `RefreshDatabaseState::$inMemoryConnections`, which outlives the test case: one skipped rollback leaves an open transaction on the suite's default connection for the rest of the PROCESS. Measured on this entry's own mutant (drop one `fakePreload()` from `BridgeCommandsTest`), three runs, one variable: unmutated **527** assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors; mutated without the `finally` **76** / 1 / **158** — every later test in the class erroring `cannot start a transaction within a transaction`, 451 assertions never executed; mutated with it **528** / 1 / **0**. ⛔ **It is not noise, it falsifies Decision 1b's own claim.** With two strays in two `RefreshDatabase` classes, the first names its url and the second dies in `setUp()` before it can name its own — *the reds are a SAMPLE again*, sized by run order, which is the defect card#7300 was filed on, re-minted inside its own fix, and it lands on the shape holding 51 of the 57. `tests/Feature/Support/StrayRequestGuardCascadeTest.php` is the witness — two throwaway `RefreshDatabase` classes in a nested `phpunit` run, asserting each names its OWN url, read from phpunit's JUnit log rather than a printer's stdout. ⚑ The residual the `finally` creates is stated rather than hidden: an exception thrown BY `parent::tearDown()` replaces the guard's, which is the third under-report in Decision 2's note.

**Decision 1d — a declaration is witnessed by the refusal it declares, or it fails.** `expectStrayRequest()` is the only thing that silences the reporter, and nothing made one expire: a declared url the test stops straying to passed silently while still covering whatever strayed to that url NEXT — a declaration witnessed by nothing, i.e. the shape this card was filed on, minted in the card's own exemption. `tearDown()` now fails an otherwise-SUCCEEDING test that declared a url no refusal matched. Gated on success deliberately: a test that already failed usually stopped before the request it declares, and reporting the stale declaration on top of the real failure would name a consequence as a cause. Population today is 3 call sites, all inside the guard's own witness, so the measured impact is nil and the value is that the exemption cannot rot. Witnessed by a discriminating pair in a nested run — a fixture that declares AND strays must PASS, or the guard would just be failing every declaring test.

**Decision 2 — the population is DERIVED by instrumenting the throw site, not read off the red list.** This is the load-bearing methodological point of the card, and the obvious method would have missed 96% of it. `StrayRequestException extends RuntimeException`, and `PendingRequest::makePromise()` re-throws it ahead of the `ConnectionException` wrapping — so it reaches the caller unchanged, and a caller that degrades on `catch (Throwable)` swallows it **exactly as it swallowed the connection error**. The test stays GREEN and the guard is silent about it. Measured, at the branch point: turning the guard on and running the full suite reds **2** tests; recording every URL at the throw site over the same run records **57 stray requests across 53 test legs in 5 classes**. ⇒ *"enumerate the newly-red tests"* is not a derivation of this population, it is a sample of the callers that happen not to swallow. The instrument used to MEASURE that was a temporary edit to the vendored throw site, reverted before commit; the reproducible statement of that method is: enable the guard, record `<test>\t<uri>` where `StrayRequestException` is constructed, run the whole suite, and read `sort -u` of that file — **running the control FIRST**, because an instrument that records nothing and a suite with no strays produce the same empty file (it fired before it was trusted: the pre-known `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` strays appeared on a filtered run first).

⚑ **With Decision 1b in the tree, that vendor instrument is the FALLBACK and not the method.** The recorder makes every refusal fail its own test, so the derivation becomes *turn the guard on, run the whole suite, read the reds* — the sentence that was 96% wrong before it existed. It is stated this way round deliberately: `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` is the live surface a reader is routed to, and it must not carry a method that is only true while a mechanism is present, so it says which method belongs to which tree. The reds under-report in THREE known ways, all disclosed there: a test that declares a stray; a test that registers a catch-all and therefore never produces one; and — narrow but real — a test whose `parent::tearDown()` also throws (`Mockery::close()` on an unmet expectation), where the `finally` in Decision 1c lets that exception replace the guard's, so the test is red but the url is not in it. ⛔ **A FOURTH way existed and was unbounded, and it is why Decision 1c exists** — see there; an earlier draft of this sentence read *"exactly two"* while that one was live.

**Decision 3 — every stray is a FINDING, and the fix is the stub plus, where the call is the point of the test, the request asserted on the wire.** The five, each carrying BOTH units the header uses — the request figures sum to 57 and the leg figures to 53, and an earlier draft of these bullets labelled the request figures as legs, which is what made them contradict the header:

- **`KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` — 22 requests in 22 legs, `/boards/8/preload.json`.** The no-regression guard's stage-order read. `noRegression()` fails OPEN inside `catch (Throwable)`, so those 22 asserted a move the guard was never able to weigh, and the class's own `fakePreload()` helper had existed all along. All 22 now pass through it, and the happy path additionally pins the GET on the wire — the one assertion in the class that reds if the stub is dropped, since the move itself succeeds either way.
- **`BridgeCommandsTest` — 29 requests in 28 legs, the same URL.** `WritebackBoardStateCheck` reads it unconditionally per mapping, and the whole per-mapping block sits inside ONE `catch (Throwable)`: the unstubbed read did not make one leg quieter, it replaced every later line that block would have produced with a single `could not read board 8 … with the writeback token`. A class-local `fakePreload()` now carries the stage order, registered through the `$stubs + $defaults` order G-020 requires so a case that needs a MISSING id still stubs its own.
- **`InstallGuardTest::test_bridge_check_fails_on_crosstalk` — 4 requests in 1 leg, and the worst of them.** It ran `bridge:check` with **no** config-dir override, so it read `bridge.config_dir` from the `BRIDGE_DIR` a deployed checkout's own `.env` sets — `phpunit.xml` overrides neither that nor the kanban API base — and issued four **token-bearing** requests to the operator install's LIVE board and to `api.github.com` on every suite run. On CI the same test reached a fixture directory that does not exist and exercised none of it. **Same test, two different subjects, decided by the host the runner sits on.** Now hermetic (its own temp dir, which it already created for other reasons), and asserting the crosstalk message rather than a bare exit code — `1` alone cannot say which check produced it.
- **`KanbanPromoteReleasedHandlerTest::test_the_github_token_is_resolved_with_the_configured_repo_spelling` — 1 request in 1 leg, `api.github.com`.** The test drives the PAYLOAD spelling `Owner/repo` while the fixture stubs are keyed `owner/repo`, and `Str::is` is case-SENSITIVE — so the read was unstubbed and went to the real GitHub API with the test's Bearer attached, and the test's own `assertSent` passed on whatever GitHub answered. `fakeBoard()` grew a caller-first `$extra` parameter; the assertion now pins the exact URL rather than only its host, which is what makes the stub the thing that answers.
- **`ChannelPushUdsTest::test_posts_intent_body_over_unix_socket` — 1 request in 1 leg, and the one allowance.** See Decision 4.

**Decision 4 — exactly one URL is allowed to stay stray, and the bar is what the test's SUBJECT is, never how loud the class is.** `ChannelPushUdsTest` calls `Http::allowStrayRequests(['http://localhost/'])`. That test forks a child which binds a Unix-domain socket, and the parent pushes the real handler through it: the live curl/Guzzle UDS transport IS the thing under test, so a stub would replace it. Nothing escapes the process — the destination is a socket the test creates and deletes, and `http://localhost/` is curl's placeholder authority for a UDS transfer, never a TCP connection. `Factory::allowStrayRequests(array $only)` keeps the guard ON and allowlists only that URL, so anything else this test reaches is still a red. ⛔ **A per-CLASS opt-out was refused** — turning the guard on and exempting the loud classes re-mints the defect with a note attached, and the two loud classes here (51 of the 57) were exactly the ones with real findings in them.

**Decision 5 — the guard gets its own test, because nothing else in the suite reds if it is deleted.** `tests/Feature/Support/StrayRequestGuardTest.php` exercises four cases: an unstubbed request throws and NAMES the url; a request matching no pattern of an ARRAY fake throws (the form that hides the fall-through — a bare fake would pass a broken guard); a stubbed request is still answered and still recorded, which is the presence witness the two absence assertions need — without it a guard that refused *every* request, faked ones included, would satisfy them both; and — the fourth, added with Decision 1b — a refusal SWALLOWED by a `catch (Throwable)` — the shape all but the 2 that reached a red test had — is still reported as a finding. That last one asserts the reporter's own verdict (`undeclaredStrayRequests()`) BEFORE declaring the url, because declaring first would empty the list it exists to witness; and the answered-request case doubles as its control, asserting the verdict is empty when a stub answered.

**Decision 6 — `bridge.config_dir` / `bridge.secret_dir` get a hermetic DEFAULT in the base `TestCase`, not a sixth copy of the workaround.** F1 was possible because the default resolved from `BRIDGE_DIR` in a deployed checkout's own `.env` and `phpunit.xml` cannot override it (`<env>` does not reach the `getenv()` layer `env()` reads). Five of the six artisan-invoking classes pinned a temp dir in `setUp()`; `InstallGuardTest` was the one that did not, and that is a guard-shaped residual, not a closed finding — the NEXT class to invoke artisan re-mints it. `Tests\TestCase::setUp()` now defaults both keys to a path that does not exist, so **the default on every host is the shape CI already had**, and a class that forgets the override reads an empty install instead of the operator's live one. Tests that need a populated config dir override both keys after `parent::setUp()` exactly as before; nothing may depend on the default resolving to a real directory, which is why it is a fixed non-existent path rather than a created temp dir. ⚑ Spelled under `/dev/null/`, not `/nonexistent/`: `BridgePaths::ensureDir()` is a RECURSIVE `mkdir` from `/`, so the first spelling refused only with `EACCES` — a permission verdict, and permission is what root bypasses — while a non-directory path component refuses with `ENOTDIR` for every user, which is what makes *cannot be created by accident* true by construction on a suite that supports root runners. The constant's own docblock holds the measured errnos and says which leg is inferred. ⚑ It is a floor and not a substitute for the per-test pin: it makes the failure mode *empty install* rather than *someone else's install*, and it does not make a test that reads config hermetic by itself.

⚑ **It closes more than the HTTP half, and the entry under-claimed it.** `BridgePaths::stateDir()` falls back to `config('bridge.config_dir').'/state'` when `bridge.state_dir` is empty — which the base `setUp()` makes it — so on a deployed checkout the suite's default STATE dir was the operator install's real one, the directory holding its live `inbox.jsonl`. An unpinned test that staged an intent would have appended to it. ⛔ **Stated as a hazard and not as an observed write, because it was measured and the measurement says otherwise:** instrumenting all four state-write primitives (`ensureDir`, `writeFile`, `updateSeenLocked`, `filterJsonlLocked`) over the whole suite records **173 calls, NONE of them through the default** — every one resolves to a `sys_get_temp_dir()` path the test pinned itself. So the default closes the next unpinned stager, not a write today's suite makes. ⚑ Bound, because it is the one this measurement cannot answer: it was taken WITH the default in place, so it does not cover a path that a POPULATED `config_dir` would have unlocked; reproducing that needs a run pointed at the operator's real install or a copy of its secrets, and neither was done.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) **Leave the guard off and fix the instances** — REJECTED: the instances were found only BY the guard; a grep for `Http::fake` cannot bound the population, because `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` calls it and escapes on the URLs it did not name. (b) **Per-class opt-in (adopt it in the three board-tools suites already measured clean, and file the rest)** — REJECTED: that is the state card#7225 shipped, and it leaves the escape live everywhere it was not looked at — which is where ALL 57 turned out to be: not one of them was in `tests/Feature/AgentTools`, the directory that measurement covered. (c) **Opt the loud classes OUT of the guard** — REJECTED, Decision 4. (d) **`Http::fake()` with a `'*'` catch-all in the base `setUp()`** — REJECTED and it is the trap, not the cure: a catch-all registered in `setUp()` is registered FIRST, and first-match-wins (G-020), so it would answer every request in the suite and shadow every per-test stub — a green suite in which no per-test stub is ever consulted. (e) **Make the fail-soft callers re-throw `StrayRequestException`** so every stray reds — REJECTED: teaching production code about a test-only exception is a worse trade than the wire assertion the standing rule already requires, and it would change the behaviour of a `catch` on the writeback's most load-bearing degradation path. (f) **Record strays and fail in `tearDown()`**, which makes a swallowed stray loud without touching app code — **TAKEN, and it is Decision 1b. The reason first recorded for not taking it was wrong, and is corrected here rather than left standing:** it read *“a global request middleware cannot tell a stray from a stub that deliberately threw (this suite has several).”* It can, because the discriminator is the exception CLASS, not the fact of throwing: the middleware catches `StrayRequestException` and nothing else, and that class is constructed at exactly one site — `PendingRequest::buildStubHandler()`, the fall-through. The suite's deliberately-throwing stubs are three, and all three throw `ConnectionException` (`GitHubRepoProbeTest:128`, `ReconcileRepoTokensCheckTest:130`, `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheckTest:229`); nothing anywhere in `tests/` or `app/` constructs a `StrayRequestException`. The second clause — *“there is no public hook at the throw site”* — is true and is not the obstacle it was read as: the middleware does not need a hook AT the throw site, only a frame OUTSIDE it, and `Http::globalMiddleware()` is a public API that provides one (`PendingRequest::pushHandlers()` pushes global middleware before the stub handler, and Guzzle's `HandlerStack` resolves in reverse push order, so global middleware is strictly outer). **No vendor file is touched.** ⚑ What (f) genuinely does NOT close is unchanged and is stated in `CLAUDE_TESTING.md`: a catch-all fake answers every request it will ever make, so it produces no refusal for anything to record.

**Proven the way it fails.** Every assertion this change adds was watched RED before it was trusted:

- `StrayRequestGuardTest` — the two absence legs go red with the `preventStrayRequests()` call removed from `Tests\TestCase`, and the message is the mechanism itself: `ConnectionException: cURL error 6: Could not resolve host: kanban.example.com`, i.e. the request leaving the process. The third leg (a stubbed request answered and recorded) passes under the same mutant, which is what makes the pair discriminating rather than a check that refuses everything.
- The `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` happy path's new preload assertion — red with the stub dropped (`An expected request was not recorded`) while the PATCH assertion beside it still passes, which is precisely the blindness being closed.
- `InstallGuardTest`'s crosstalk expectation — red on a known-absent string (`Output does not contain …`), and red on exit code with the suffix cleared. Its hermeticity leg is measured, not asserted: with the config-dir override removed, the four live-host strays reappear on the instrument and the test stays GREEN, which is why the fix is the dir and not an assertion.
- The GitHub URL pin — red under a stub key lowercased to the spelling the request does NOT use (`Attempted request to [https://api.github.com/repos/Owner/repo/pulls/100] without a matching fake`).
- The `ChannelPushUdsTest` allowance — red with the allowance removed, which is what shows it is load-bearing rather than decoration.
- **The `tearDown()` reporter (Decision 1b) — watched red on one of the 26 stubs that no assertion witnesses.** Dropping `+ $this->fakePreload()` from `BridgeCommandsTest::test_check_warns_when_the_writeback_token_sees_zero_cards` — GREEN at `68d82d0`, which is the whole complaint — now fails with `made 1 outbound request(s) no stub answered: …/boards/8/preload.json`. Its control is the same leg unmutated (green) and `StrayRequestGuardTest`'s answered-request case, which asserts the reporter's verdict is EMPTY when a stub answered, so a reporter that fired on every request could not pass. The two deliberate strays stay green through their declarations.
- **The `finally` (Decision 1c) — watched red on the witness itself.** `StrayRequestGuardCascadeTest` fails with the `finally` removed on exactly the second-class assertion (`Failed asserting that '' … contains …/second-class-stray.json`) while the FIRST-class assertion beside it still passes — which is what makes the pair discriminating rather than a test that would red on any broken guard.
- **The stale-declaration guard (Decision 1d) — watched red twice, one leg each.** With the `tearDown()` call removed, the declares-and-never-strays fixture goes green and the finding assertion reds; with the guard's `array_diff` against the recorded strays removed so it fires on EVERY declaration, the control fixture (declares AND strays) reds instead.
- **`AgentToolsCallTest::test_loopback_peer_is_admitted`'s two stubs, re-measured because the comment describing them was false.** Dropping `'*/tasks/*.json'` reds on the `placement_observed` pin; dropping `'*/tasks.json'` returns **500** — the create arm does not swallow, so `StrayRequestException` propagates out of the controller. The comment had claimed both were droppable-and-green.

**Consequences:** `tests/TestCase.php` (the refusal, the recorder, `expectStrayRequest()` + `undeclaredStrayRequests()`, the `tearDown()` report, the hermetic `config_dir`/`secret_dir` default, and the docblocks that say what each does NOT close); `tests/Feature/Support/StrayRequestGuardTest.php` (new); `tests/Feature/Support/StrayRequestGuardCascadeTest.php` (new) and `tests/Support/NestedSuite.php` (new — the nested-`phpunit` harness, hoisted at its second real caller: both properties it serves are *what the runner reports for a test case that has already finished*, which no in-process assertion can observe, and a test that fails on purpose cannot assert its own failure from inside itself); `tests/Support/PreloadStub.php` (new — the `/preload.json` stub body hoisted at the second real caller, canon #5: `KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest` and `BridgeCommandsTest` had grown one fixture shape twice and the two had DIVERGED on `swimlanes`, the field whose absence `WritebackBoardStateCheck` reads as *carried no swimlane collection at all* — so presence/absence is a parameter there and `null` omits the key; both callers keep a named local `fakePreload()` over it and both bodies were proved byte-identical to what they replaced, with a control showing the comparison distinguishes an absent `swimlanes` from an empty one); `tests/Feature/Handlers/KanbanMoveCardHandlerTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Console/BridgeCommandsTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Config/InstallGuardTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Handlers/KanbanPromoteReleasedHandlerTest.php`, `tests/Feature/Handlers/ChannelPushUdsTest.php`, `tests/Feature/AgentTools/AgentToolsCallTest.php` (comment only); `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` (the stray-request paragraphs now state what the refusal does, what the recorder adds, which derivation belongs to which tree, what the wire assertion still answers that neither mechanism can, the bar for a second allowance, and the new hermetic config-dir default); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **⚠ Stated because it bounds every claim above: a test that registers a catch-all — `Http::fake()` with no arguments, or a `'*'` pattern — has answered every request it will ever make, so the guard is structurally unable to say anything about it, and those tests are not in the 57. That is a different class from this one and is not fixed here.**

**⚑ Left standing, named so the next toucher finds the owner rather than minting an eighth.** `tests/Feature/AgentTools/AgentToolsCallTest.php` repeats ONE byte-identical inline `*/boards/10/preload.json` stub body **7 times**. It is a third shape — its stages carry a `name` — so it is not an instance of `PreloadStub` as built, and folding it in would mean widening the builder for one file's benefit inside a change that otherwise only edits a comment in that file. Reported as a class (canon #7/#18), not fixed here.

## DL-304 — the version-skew fallback's removal condition is a MEASUREMENT the probes report, not an instruction in a docblock (card#7325)

- **Date:** 2026-08-23
- **Status:** implemented (card#7325). **No behaviour change: the fallback is kept, no severity moves, no exit code moves, no config key, no migration, no token-scope change, and nothing about what the receiver, the tool or `bridge:check` ACCEPTS.** Operator-visible: every `board_tools` probe finding gains one closing sentence.

**The defect is the OWNERSHIP, not the code.** `BoardToolsScopeHeader`'s docblock ended *"Drop the fallback once no supported install can answer a probe without `configured_board_id`."* — a deletion instruction addressed to nobody, with no trigger anyone watches, that will next be read by whoever edits the file, i.e. at the moment they are least willing to reason about supported install versions. Canon #18: an item with no owner and no queue position is not filed, it is abandoned. **The sibling audit found the same shape three more times** (canon #7): both skew-tolerance tests said *"Delete both with the fallback, not before"* / *"delete both with the fallback"*, and DL-302's own Proven-the-way-it-fails paragraph says *"both tests are deleted with the fallback"*. The two test docblocks are corrected here; **DL-302's copy is frozen by the append-only rule and this entry supersedes it** — that clause is now a pointer to card#7325, not a standing instruction.

**Why it is load-bearing rather than housekeeping.** The fallback is the ONE place a **row-derived** `board_id` is still read as an **identity** header. Those are different quantities since DL-302: `configured_board_id` is an identity echo (which agent the bearer resolved to), `board_id` is an observation of where the returned rows are. Reading the second as the first is exactly the conflation DL-302 exists to remove, surviving here **by design** as version-skew tolerance. It is unreachable from this repo today — but only because `BoardMyCardsTool::call()` emits `configured_board_id` in its base result literal on no condition, which was a property of the code asserted nowhere. The moment anything else answers this envelope (a second tool, a channel-server relay, a responder that emits the header conditionally) a row observation silently becomes an identity claim and the probes' `IDENTITY MISMATCH` verdict is computed from the wrong quantity **with nothing red anywhere**.

**Decision — keep the fallback, and make its removal condition a state someone READS.** Three parts:

**1. The probe reports the provenance.** `BoardToolsScopeHeader` becomes a value object read ONCE per response (`read()` → `boardId`, `swimlaneId`, `boardSpelling`), and the new `ScopeHeaderSpelling` enum owns the operator sentence for each of `Configured` / `Legacy` / `Absent`. Both probes append it to their `ok` line and their `IDENTITY MISMATCH` tail. A skewed responder is now **accepted and named**: *⚠ Header spelling: LEGACY — … the legacy `board_id` spelling … an observation read under an identity's name … card#7325 (DL-304)*. **The note states the READING and offers the version cause as the likely one** — an absent `configured_board_id` is all the read establishes, and this entry names two other producers of that state (a relay, a conditionally-emitting responder) for which *"upgrade the responding install"* is the wrong instruction; a `⚠ VERSION SKEW` label asserted the likeliest cause in the loudest word on the line, which is DL-302's `ISOLATION`→`IDENTITY MISMATCH` finding one file over. **One read, not one per value:** a second entry point re-deriving the same newest-first chain to answer *"which key did that come from"* could disagree with the value it describes, and the disagreement would print as a wrong claim about install versions. **One sentence, not one per probe:** DL-302's own review caught a first pass that corrected one probe's copy of the identity-echo caveat and left the other saying the false thing, so the second copy of this text was never written. **And the CAUSE half of the mismatch tail is read off that same provenance** (`ScopeHeaderSpelling::mismatchCause()`): a responder that identified itself as ANOTHER agent is a credential fault, so the tail names the token path / the pinned key; one that echoed no identity at all shows nothing about the credential, so it names the ROUTE instead (a wrong vhost, a relay, or any JSON service answering `{ok:true,result:{}}`). ⛔ **Dropping the old *"(or … answered no header at all)"* parenthetical without that split made the `Absent` branch WORSE than the guess it replaced**: the tail asserted the other disjunct as fact and the spelling sentence denied it two sentences later in the same string, sending an operator at a healthy token. One read owns the value, the spelling, and the cause, because a cause chosen anywhere else can disagree with the spelling printed beside it — which is this entry's own defect, re-minted at the sibling site. **DL-302's Decision 5 records both fail tails naming a bearer-resolution cause; the log is append-only, and this entry NARROWS that to the branch where the responder identified itself.**

**2. The unreachability becomes a guard.** `AgentToolsCallTest` enumerates every arm of the response literal (empty window · rows on the configured board · rows on a foreign board · rows with no readable board · a configured shared lane · a configured coord block) and pins that `configured_board_id` is present and correct on each, plus that `configured_coord_board_id` appears with `coord_cards`. It asserts the CALL as well as the key — an arm that returned nothing would satisfy a bare `assertArrayHasKey` on nothing. The card's option B warned that a test asserting only the fallback's *absence of use* would certify whatever replaced it; this is the presence witness instead.

**3. The condition itself lives on the card and in `docs/board-tools.md` § Which spelling the probe read**, as two things an operator can check: *(a)* every probe target answers under `configured_board_id` — read off the probe's own last sentence, per target, because the subject is a REMOTE responder no reading of this repo can reach; *(b)* nothing but `board_my_cards` answers this envelope. Both true ⇒ the fallback and its two skew tests go.

**⚠ THE VERSION COMPARE THE CONDITION WAS PHRASED AS CANNOT BE RUN, and that is a finding, not a shortcut.** *"The oldest bridge version any probed install runs"* ≥ *"the release that first emitted `configured_board_id`"* needs a version off the wire. **MEASURED:** the board-tools envelope is `{ok, tool, result}` / `{ok, error}` — `DispatchOutcome::body()` is its ONLY serializer — and carries no version. Adding one would not answer the question either: a responder old enough to lack `configured_board_id` is old enough to lack the version field, so the field would be absent on exactly the population the compare is about. The **spelling is the predicate that compare was a proxy for**, measured directly, on the round trip the probe already makes.

**MEASURED state of the condition at this entry, so the card is not the only place it is written down.** (2) is **unreleased**: `git tag --contains 32bf970` (card#7295's merge on `dev`) is empty, and `v0.74.1` — the newest tag — is an ancestor of the branch this lands on, so **no release yet emits `configured_board_id` unconditionally** and the earliest install that can satisfy (1) is one running the release this entry ships in. (1) is **already false for a known target**: the co-resident prod install this box's rule-7 topology puts behind the same loopback gate is at `0.74.1` and its `BoardMyCardsTool` carries no `configured_board_id` at all — read out of its checkout, **not** probed, because no live call was made for this change. ⇒ The fallback stays, and this is what "stays" is grounded on.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Delete the fallback now.** Rejected, and not this card's question. It breaks a genuinely supported old responder — one is running on this very box — and DL-302 measured the case as real.
  - **`warn` instead of `ok` when the fallback fires.** Rejected on measurement, not taste: DL-302 ships in the same release as this entry, so at the moment the line first appears **every** install in the field answers under the legacy spelling. A `warn` would paint the commonest and entirely healthy state yellow on every probe, and a signal that fires on the normal case is one an operator learns to skip — which would cost the very legibility this change buys. If the population inverts (most targets upgraded, a straggler left), promoting it is a one-line change with a live reason; that is the trigger.
  - **Add a version field to the tool envelope and compare versions.** Rejected: absent on precisely the responders it would have to describe (above), and it grows the cross-seat response contract to carry a diagnostic the spelling already answers.
  - **A `bridge:check` leg that FAILS on a legacy responder.** Rejected: changes what `bridge:check` rejects, which is hard-gated, and it certifies an upgrade schedule rather than an install.
  - **Two statics (`boardId()` + a new `boardIdSpelling()`).** Rejected: a second derivation of one chain, which is canon #5's defect with a wrong-statement-about-versions failure mode.

- **Consequences:** new `ScopeHeaderSpelling`; `BoardToolsScopeHeader` (value object + `read()`, docblock's ownerless instruction replaced by a pointer to this entry); `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheck` + `SshTransportProbe` (one header read each, provenance appended to both `ok` lines and both mismatch tails; the mismatch tails drop their *"(or … answered no header at all)"* parenthetical in favour of a cause and a remediation READ off the spelling, one branch each); `AgentToolsCallTest` (the presence witness, plus two inline fakes extracted at their second caller); new `BoardToolsScopeHeaderTest`; `BoardToolsHttpProbeCheckTest` + `SshTransportProbeTest` (provenance asserted on the healthy, skewed and absent arms; the two *"delete with the fallback"* instructions replaced by a pointer here); the `board-tools-ssh-live-probe` golden regenerated for the one added sentence; `docs/board-tools.md` (new § **Which spelling the probe read**, the § 6 verify pointer, and the `configured_board_id` bullet's unconditional-presence claim); `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **Every new assertion was watched failing first**, each under the mutant of the thing it guards: the header dropped from the base literal (6 arms red), the coord echo dropped (1), `read()` reporting `Configured` for a legacy response (4 across three files), both probes' provenance suppressed (5), and the legacy note stripped of its skew wording and its owner (3). The fix round added three more: `mismatchCause()` collapsed onto the credential wording (3 red — the two probes' absent arms plus the enum's own), collapsed onto the route wording (3 red — the two probes' identified arms plus the enum's), and the legacy note's *"Likeliest cause … a relay, or a responder that emits the header conditionally"* reduced back to the bare *"Upgrade the responding install past DL-302."* (1). **The `Absent` branch's new text was watched red on BOTH legs before it existed** — the pre-fix output the run printed is the finding itself: *"…the presented bearer resolved to a DIFFERENT agent's window — look for a token collision or a mis-pinned bearer at …. Header spelling: NEITHER — … so there was no identity echo to compare."*
