## DL-305 — correlation is not completion: a merge moves a card only on an explicit CLOSING FORM, and a bare mention is a NO-OP rather than a demotion (card#7348)

- **Date:** 2026-08-23
- **Status:** implemented (card#7348, from roundtable #343 / #342). **⚠ CHANGES WHAT THE WRITEBACK ACTS ON** — the always-ask class, adopted by the operator before any code, with the DL-token scope fork closed by them on the record. No new `writeback.json` key, no migration, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change. Operator-visible: merge moves stop firing for titles that only CITE a card, `bridge:check` gains two lines per healthy run, and one PR-title convention changes.
- **The number:** the board stamps this card `DL-0305`; the log's own header regex strips leading zeros (DL-295), so `## DL-305` and `DL-0305` name one decision — the same two spellings this file already carries for `## DL-031` / `## DL-291`.

**The defect, verified at source rather than relayed.** `PrOutcome::forMergedBase()` returned `merged_to_main` for a base of `main` and `merged` otherwise — **a pure function of the base ref, with no completion signal in it at all** — and `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` handed it whichever `card#N` / `DL-NNN` token appeared in the PR title or head branch. So *"this PR mentions card N"* and *"card N's work is shipped"* were one proposition, and the `promote_on_release` sweep then faithfully propagated the result into a **terminal, irreversible** stage. A case-insensitive grep of the classifier for `closes|fixes|resolves|closing` returned **13 hits, every one the word "resolves" in the DL-token-RESOLUTION sense** inside `Log::warning` prose, against a `card` control of 308 — the grep discriminates, the count is not zero, and the conclusion holds: **no closure predicate existed anywhere.**

**The harm is measured, at peers.** 17 live wrong-retirement candidates in one pending release bundle (`sola-pm`). One card on which a PM ruled *"THIS CARD DOES NOT CLOSE ON THAT COMMIT"* and moved to Prioritized at 11:52:54, which the writeback moved back to `shipped_to_dev` at 15:06:51 the same day. A third install holds 800 cards in Shipped behind a `main` frozen pre-cutover — **a fuse, not a mitigation**: the dangerous leg activates on unfreeze and the first release evaluates all 800 at once. ⚠ **One evidence item is NARROWED and is recorded that way rather than repeated**: the reversal incident was attributed through `last_stage_move.actor_id`, and that field identifies a **kanban USER, not a writer** — when that narrowing was written, two independent writers on this very install (the board CLI and the writeback) resolved to user 3, so the identical evidence would have produced the wrong attribution here. *(This install has since cut the writeback over to its own dedicated kanban user — card#7463 — so its `actor_id` discriminates now. The narrowing is kept, not deleted: it is the reason the peer's attribution is still pending, and the repair here does not reach back into evidence gathered before it.)* The source-level defect stands on the code and needs no actor field; the incident's attribution is pending that install's own token check. **This entry's own exposure numbers are the same shape and are not immunity**: 0 multi-token hijacks across 300 merged PR titles, 0 reversals across 18 declined cards — protected by a CONVENTION (one card per PR, cited only when it closes it), which fails silently the first time a card is cited for context.

**Decision — a closure grammar over the PR TITLE, gating exactly the merge outcomes.**

**1. `ClosureGrammar` (new, `app/Bridge/Support`).** A closing VERB — GitHub's own linking-keyword set, `close[sd]?` / `fix(e[sd])?` / `resolve[sd]?`, case-insensitive — followed by a mandatory separator and then a token **flush against it**. It answers `closedCardIds()` / `closedDls()` / `closesCard()` / `closesDl()`, and renders its own operator sentence from its vector set (the DL-239 discipline, now on three grammars).
  - **It restates NEITHER token pattern.** It matches the verb bridge and hands the REMAINDER to `CardTokenGrammar::parseAnchored()` / `DlTokenGrammar::parseAnchored()` — new **position tests** on the owning grammars, expressed against each class's own `PATTERN`, which can only ever return what `parse()` would return for that text, or null. Pasting either pattern here would be the exact restatement DL-239 removed, and a grammar move would then silently stop being a closure. A test drives **both owners' full vector sets** through the closure predicate, so a second, narrower accept-set cannot form here.
  - **ADJACENCY is the ruling that makes the predicate mean anything.** `Closes the regression card#4811 documents` closes nothing. A "verb somewhere, token somewhere" co-occurrence test would read almost every real PR title as a closure and therefore close nothing at all.
  - **⛔ One verb closes one token.** `Closes card#1 and card#2` closes only card 1. This is GitHub's rule too; the strict reading costs an UNDER-promoted card, the loose one costs the terminal move this exists to stop.

**2. The gate is `PrOutcome::requiresClosure()` — the merge outcomes, and only those.** The boundary is the CLAIM each outcome makes, not its severity: `merged` / `merged_to_main` are the two that say *this card's work is shipped*. `opened` is reversible and is what STAMPS the card's PR refs so the reconciler can find the PR later; `closed_unmerged` is an abandon disposition (revivable, DL-195) whose withholding would strand a card in In-Review; a branch ref cannot carry a closing verb, so gating `started` would make every branch-create INERT — the silent-inert shape `bridge:check` exists to warn about. Dependabot cards (no card token, own handler) and the draft overlay (a marker, not a stage) are untouched.

**3. ⛔ A BARE MENTION IS A NO-OP FOR THE STAGE, NEVER A DEMOTION — the load-bearing half.** The writeback re-classifies in-window PRs on **every** pass: redeliveries, `bridge:replay`, and `bridge:reconcile` on a schedule. A rule that returned an *earlier* stage for a mention would not gently correct the mistaken cards — it would **mass-demote every already-correct card on the first run after this shipped**, because every historical PR is a bare mention under the new grammar. Withholding the move leaves every existing stage exactly where it is, which is also what makes the migration free: **nothing to backfill.** (Credit: `sola-pm` flagged this before anyone built the naive version.) It carries **its own acceptance witness** rather than being implied by the no-op one.

**4. The closing form must name the card that MOVES, through the same resolution that selected it.** A `Closes DL-NNN` authorizes every card that DL resolved to (DL-148 is one-to-many and the claim is made about the DL); a `Closes card#N` authorizes only the card it names, so the DL-selected set is **filtered** rather than accepted or rejected whole. ⛔ **The DL-218 foreign-mention guard is left intact and is not re-opened from the other side**: on the `card#` path the resolved DL is deliberately passed as `null`, because that path is reached only when the DL resolved to nothing or to a DIFFERENT card — so a `Closes DL-9` there is a claim about someone else's work and must not authorize the `card#` the guard just ruled authoritative.

**4b. A LOG LINE THE GATE MADE FALSE, corrected in the same change.** The DL-218 foreign-mention warn ended *"moving card#N, not the DL card(s)"* — true while the only thing between it and a move was the handler, and **false the moment this gate can withhold one**: on a merge with no closing form it announced a move that never happened, in the very log an operator reads to find out why nothing moved. It now states the RULING (*"the card token in force is card#N"*), which is what is unconditionally true where it is emitted — the discipline the title-vs-branch guard six lines above already followed for the DL-148 reason. ⚠ **Its push-path twin keeps the move claim on purpose:** `started` is not a gated outcome, so nothing downstream of that line can withhold its move, and rewriting it would weaken a true statement to match a sibling's constraint it does not share.

**5. The TITLE is the only closure surface.** The head branch names what the work is ON, not that it is finished — three merged PRs here track one card, and `refCorroborates()`'s own note records that real branches are overwhelmingly `<type>/<id>-slug`. Reading a slug as a completion assertion would make an accidental word (`fix/closes-card-7348`) load-bearing.

**6. `bridge:reconcile` applies the IDENTICAL gate.** It re-derives the same proposition from the same evidence, so it must read the same closing form out of the same field (`GitHubReadClient::getPull()` now projects `title`). Without it the backstop would re-plan on a schedule exactly the move the event path had just declined — **the defect arriving an hour later with a CLI's name on it**, through the leg that exists to repair drift. The gate sits AFTER the `merged_to_main` terminal return — that outcome is out of this command's scope by construction (the promote workflow owns it), so gating it would report a withheld move on every release PR and withhold nothing; the placement narrows where the answer can matter, never what the answer is. Its DL compare goes through `ExternalReferenceNormalizer::canonicalize()` — the one place in the closure path that needs it, because here a title's `DL-305` meets a STORED `dl_number` written `DL-0305`, where the classifier compares two tokens parsed out of one string by one grammar.

**7. Said at setup time, which was the third ask.** `bridge:check` gains a per-mapping `ok` line naming the gated merge outcomes **with their stage ids** and the rendered accept-set — a peer wired a brand-new board into this classifier hours before the defect surfaced and nothing in the setup path warned them. It is scoped to mappings that map a merge outcome at all, so a `started`/`opened`-only mapping stays silent (the `Severity` corollary-(B) ruling). It is the first non-warning leg on `WritebackMappingConfigCheck`, and it earns its line because what it reports — that a merge now needs a closing form — is a property of the CODE the operator is running, which `writeback.json` cannot tell them however carefully they read it.

**8. `bridge:check` also REPORTS the `identity_id` the config declares** (roundtable #343's addendum). It is named as what it primarily IS — the echo-suppression key — with the writer attribution stated as the second thing it consequently declares; describing it as merely an attribution field would teach the wrong repair to an operator whose writeback is looping on its own writes. The line reports a CONFIGURED value and says so: nothing here resolves the token against the API. `last_stage_move.actor_id` is a card's only writer attribution, so it stops discriminating the moment two writers share a user — measured in both directions: one install where a board CLI's token and the writeback token both resolved to user 3 (a move was very nearly mis-attributed to the writeback on exactly that evidence), one where they were distinct and the same question answered cleanly. ⚠ **The colliding install has since been repaired** (card#7463 cut the writeback over to its own kanban user), and that is an argument FOR the leg, not against it: the property is a function of how an install was provisioned, so the next one can be misconfigured identically and nothing else would report it. The text is past-tense throughout for the same reason a docblock asserting a repaired collision is the stale claim this leg exists to prevent. ⛔ **It REPORTS; it does not CERTIFY, and the bound is the point.** The collision that was actually measured is with a token held entirely outside this install's config, invisible from here in principle. A separation ASSERTION would therefore stay green on the very install shape that has the defect — worse than no assertion, because it manufactures the assurance the operator came for. `WritebackIdentityCheck` stops being silent-when-healthy for this, deliberately and on the record.

**9. NOT extended to the release-promote sweep (DL-207).** That leg asks whether a card **already at** `stages.merged` has its commit on `main` — a question about a transition some earlier decision already made, not a fresh completion claim. The gate belongs where the claim is first made, and gating the sweep would silently stop promoting for every install whose historical titles lack closing forms. ⚠ **Stated cost, not overlooked:** cards that reached Shipped BEFORE this ships stay eligible, so a large historical Shipped backlog wants an audit before `promote_on_release` is enabled. That is `docs/writeback.md`'s § and this entry's, not a hidden residue.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Return an earlier stage for a bare mention (the naive reading).** Rejected on the mechanism above — it mass-demotes every already-correct card on the first pass, because the writeback re-classifies in-window PRs every time. This is the one alternative that looks like a stronger fix and is strictly worse.
  - **Gate `card#N` only, leave `DL-NNN` as it was.** Rejected by the operator on the record (roundtable #343): it leaves a second door into the same terminal stage, which is the defect and not a subset of it. The constraint *failure direction must stay safe* argues for covering every path into a terminal stage, not the one that was measured.
  - **Gate every outcome, not just the merges.** Rejected: it makes the branch-create `started` trigger permanently inert (a branch ref cannot carry a closing verb) and strands abandoned-PR cards in In-Review. Neither outcome claims completion, so neither is what this is about.
  - **A per-mapping `require_closure_grammar` opt-in.** Rejected: default-off leaves the defect live everywhere, and default-on-with-an-escape-hatch makes the dangerous behaviour a permanent supported configuration. The no-op semantics are what make the unconditional change safe to ship, so the switch buys nothing and costs a config key on the fail-closed path.
  - **Read the PR BODY as a closure surface (GitHub's own convention).** Rejected as out of scope and as a widening: the classifier reads no body today, and adding one grows the correlation surface — a change to what the system accepts, which is its own gate.
  - **A `bridge:check` leg that ASSERTS writeback/agent identity separation.** Rejected on measurement, not appetite: the tokens that were measured colliding are not in this install's config, so the assertion would be silent on the defect it names. Reporting the identity answers the operator's question honestly; the enumeration is theirs to run.
  - **Gate the release-promote sweep too.** Rejected — see 9: it re-decides a completed transition and would stop promoting on every install with historical titles.

- **Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Support/ClosureGrammar.php`; `CardTokenGrammar` + `DlTokenGrammar` gain `parseAnchored()`; `PrOutcome` gains `MERGE_OUTCOMES` + `requiresClosure()`; `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier` gains `closureFilter()` + `closingCards()` + `warnMentionWithoutClosure()`, gates its two merge-move returns, and its DL-218 warn stops asserting a move (the DL-287 near-miss REFUSAL path is untouched — it emits an alert, not a move, and silencing it would lose a signal); `GitHubReadClient::getPull()` projects `title`; `ReconcileCommand` gains the same gate + `closes()`; `WritebackMappingConfigCheck` gains the mention-vs-closure `ok` leg (and its class docblock + trailing `Silence` reason are corrected — it is no longer an all-warnings check); `WritebackIdentityCheck` reports the declared `identity_id`; new `ClosureGrammarTest` + `WritebackIdentityCheckTest`; `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest`, `ReconcileCommandTest` and `WritebackMappingConfigCheckTest` extended (six existing merged-PR fixtures gained a closing form — the INPUT changed, no assertion was weakened); `docs/writeback.md` (new § **Mention vs closure**, the token step-1 identity note, the reconcile and `promote_on_release` clauses, and the *Card-token correlation* pointer), `docs/config-schema.md`, `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`, `docs/CHECK-REGISTRY-PLAN.md` (a bracketed correction: the spellings-agree case it cites no longer asserts an empty result, and the new leg is fixture-reached rather than a fifth member of its unreached set), `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

⚠ **A LATE CORRECTION, recorded rather than folded in.** While this branch was open, the install whose measured token collision motivated consequence 8 **repaired it** (card#7463: the writeback cut over to its own kanban user, a `board_custom` credential without `task.delete`). Three surfaces here had been written in the PRESENT tense about that collision and were therefore **already stale on the day they were authored** — `WritebackIdentityCheck`'s docblock, `docs/writeback.md`, and this entry. All three are now past-tense with the repair named. Two things did NOT change: the leg stays (the property is a function of how an install was provisioned, so a fresh one can be misconfigured identically and nothing else reports it), and the evidence narrowing above stays (the repair here does not reach back into evidence gathered before it, and the peer's attribution is still pending its own token check). The same pass also corrected how the line DESCRIBES `identity_id`: it is first the **echo-suppression key**, and only consequently a claim about the writing user — a line calling it an attribution field teaches the wrong repair to an operator whose writeback is looping on its own writes. The finding now also says it reports a **configured** value and resolves nothing against the API.

**Every new guard was watched failing first**, each under the mutant of the thing it guards — twelve, re-run against the final tree rather than the tree each was first written for: the classifier gate deleted (4 red, including two of the three witnesses); `PrOutcome::requiresClosure()` forced false (8 across three files); the reconcile gate deleted (3, including the third witness); adjacency dropped from `ClosureGrammar` (16); the foreign DL passed into the `card#` filter (1 — the DL-218 door, red exactly where it should be); the withheld-remainder warning re-keyed on *nothing closed* instead of the set difference (1); the reconcile DL compare reduced to an exact string match (1); the `bridge:check` closure leg removed (3); the identity report removed (1, re-witnessed after the card#7463 cutover correction rewrote that line); and each grammar's `parseAnchored()` stripped of its offset-0 requirement (1 each — the two halves of the adjacency rule, witnessed separately). **The mass-demotion assertion was isolated by a twelfth mutation that KEEPS the log line and demotes anyway** (`$expected` re-derived from `stages.opened` rather than returning), which reds witness 3 ALONE on *"Output `SKIP-DRIFT` was printed."* — so that assertion is measuring the demotion and not the message beside it. ⚠ The first version of that mutation reded nothing there: it re-assigned `$outcome` after `$expected` had already been computed, so it changed a label and no stage. A mutation that fails to mutate scores as a pass, which is how a demotion witness would have been recorded as proven while asserting nothing.


## DL-306 — the standup digest may carry ONLY what the bridge measures; a field it cannot source is ABSENT, and the two asks that need a liveness signal are not built (card#7332)

- **Date:** 2026-08-23
- **Status:** implemented (card#7332, roundtable #341 ask 3). **OFF by default. No migration, no new required `.env`, no receiver accept/reject change, no token-scope change** — an install that does not set `BRIDGE_STANDUP_ENABLED=true` registers no callback and behaves byte-identically.
- **Context:** rt#341 (aimla-pm) asked for three things: a fleet-status digest, an autonomy watchdog that nudges an idle seat, and a periodic PM standup push. Asks 1 and 2 both need to answer *"is this seat quiet / stuck?"*, and the bridge cannot. **Re-measured on this branch rather than inherited from the FR:** `command grep -rnE 'last_activity|lastActivity|last_seen|lastSeen|heartbeat' app/ config/` matches, outside the files this change adds, exactly three — `BoardDivergenceLedger`, `WritebackBoardDivergence`, `EventConsumerReconciler` — none of them a per-seat signal. ⇒ **The bridge knows DELIVERY, not ACTIVITY.** It can say *"I pushed an event at this seat at T"*; it cannot say the seat read it, acted on it, or is mid-turn on something else. Ask 3 is the one piece with no idle precondition to get wrong, so it is the only one carded and the only one built here.

**The failure this entry exists to prevent is not a missing feature, it is a plausible number.** A digest is read at a glance, by someone deciding whom to re-engage. A `last_activity` computed from a push timestamp, or a `now_depth: 0` on a board whose Now column the bridge cannot identify, is not a small inaccuracy — it is the vacuous-green failure with a nicer face, because its reader has no way to tell it from a measurement. An absent field announces itself; a defaulted one does not.

**Decision — three parts.**

**1. Absence is the contract, and it is structural rather than remembered.** `SeatSnapshot::toArray()` emits `last_delivery_at` only when the ledger holds a DELIVERED dispatch for that seat — never a null, an epoch, or `"unknown"`. `BoardSnapshot` has **no public constructor**: `depth()` and `unavailable()` are the only two ways to build a row, so a row carrying both a number and an excuse, or neither, cannot be expressed. A board whose `writeback.json` mapping declares no `coord_card_lane_stage_ids` yields **no row at all** rather than a zero — three states, never two, the discipline `bridge:stats` already applies to the divergence ledger. The `unseen_inbox_intents` **zero IS printed**, and the asymmetry is the point: that leg ran and found nothing, which is a measurement, where the absent key means nothing looked.

**⛔ `outcome = 'delivered'` is the filter, not `processed_at is not null`.** A GATE-DROP is also "processed", and until DL-036 the two were byte-identical in `agent_dispatches`. Reading a drop as a delivery would show a seat nobody routes anything to as freshly served — this card's exact defect, in the one place the schema makes it easy. The cost is that pre-DL-036 rows (NULL `outcome`) never answer; an absent key is the right answer for a row whose outcome is unknowable.

**2. Four requested fields are NOT built, each named in `StandupDigest`'s docblock rather than silently dropped.** (a) A per-seat **context-%** — no producer the bridge can read. sola-pm's rt#341 round corrects the record that the emitter exists in the coord layer; it is still not usable here, for two reasons that survive the correction: `coord-post` **omits the stamp on cross-project posts by design**, and it only refreshes **when a seat posts**, so a seat working silently for an hour reads as quiet. It is a lower bound on activity, never a heartbeat — it corroborates, it cannot exonerate. (b) **`last_activity` / idle / quiet-for-N** — the missing signal itself. (c) An **open `to:<agent>` thread count** — the bridge sees coordination events, not thread lifecycle, and keeps no thread-state store, so it cannot say which threads are still open. `unseen_inbox_intents` is the neighbouring fact it CAN state and **ships under that name**; renaming it to the field that was asked for would be this entry's own defect. (d) An **adaptive cadence** keyed on a seat looking stuck — its predicate IS the missing signal, so the cadence is a fixed per-install interval.

**3. It rides the DL-199 gate, not a cron — and the cost of that is stated, not discovered.** The card says "cron"; this design has none, because DL-012 shipped a command and scheduled it nowhere (three installs, ~45 days, zero runs) and DL-199's answer was to remove the exception rather than add a second daemon. `StandupGate` inherits all four load-bearing properties verbatim: after-response, interval-gated, non-blocking lock, never throws. **⚠ Consequence: the pass fires on the first inbound webhook AFTER the interval lapses, so an install receiving nothing pushes nothing.** That is a delivery cadence, not a wall clock; `bridge:standup` is the manual entry point for an operator who wants one, and `--dry-run` prints the digest as JSON and pushes nothing. **⚠ One cost retention does not pay:** a pass makes OUTBOUND calls (a board read per mapped board, then the push), each bounded by `KanbanHttpClient::TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, after the response and at most once per interval — an unreachable kanban holds the FPM worker for that timeout before giving up. That, not caution, is why this is **off by default** where retention is on.

**⛔ The Now-lane depth is counted from each row's own `workflow_stage_id`, over a BOARD-scoped read — deliberately not a `q=… workflow_stage_id=<s>` search**, which would be one request instead of a page walk. That q-term is a QueryParser token an un-upgraded kanban does not recognise, and an unrecognised token is routed to FREE TEXT: the answer comes back `200` and EMPTY, **indistinguishable from a Now lane that is genuinely empty** (`KanbanClient::swimlaneCards` already records the shape). `now_depth: 0` is the most consequential value in this digest to get wrong — it is the one that says *"this seat has nothing queued"* — so it is decided on a fact each row asserts about itself, over the `board_id=` term measured honoured, rather than on a filter the server may have dropped in silence. A **truncated** read yields no number at all: past the ceiling the count is a lower bound, and a lower bound printed under the key `now_depth` is a wrong number rather than a missing one, wrong in the reassuring direction.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Ship the three fields the FR named, with the thread count as asked.** Rejected: two of the three are derivable and the third is not, and shipping an inbox backlog under the label *"open threads"* is precisely the mislabelling ask 3 was separated from ask 2 to avoid.
  - **Default `last_delivery_at` to the epoch / `"never"` / `null` so the shape is uniform.** Rejected: a uniform shape is a consumer convenience bought with a false statement, and each of the three spellings flattens to `0`/`""` somewhere downstream.
  - **A real scheduler (cron / `schedule:run`) for a true wall-clock cadence.** Rejected: it reintroduces the DL-012 exception — a periodic job nobody watches, whose failure mode is silence — for a REPORT. The command exists for an operator who wants to make that trade on their own install.
  - **A `bridge:check` posture leg, like `RetentionPostureCheck`.** Rejected **for now, and on cost rather than principle**: every registered check moves `bridge:check`'s inventory line, which regenerates the whole golden corpus — a large mechanical diff riding a feature PR. `bridge:standup --dry-run` answers the same question more directly (it shows the actual digest, not a posture claim about it). Recorded here as the deliberate gap it is; the misconfigured path is not silent meanwhile — it warns once per day and pushes nothing.
  - **A second sender rather than the `channel_push` handler.** Rejected (canon #5): that handler already owns the agent-config endpoint fallback, the fail-closed bearer read, the socket validation and the DL-014 prefix gate. A second sender would be a second, quietly weaker copy of all four. The digest's payload carries no `socket`/`url`, which is exactly what selects the agent-config branch — the only branch a token may ride.
  - **Staging the digest to the inbox as well as pushing it.** Rejected as scope: the inbox is the durable backstop for signals the bridge was ASKED to relay, and a self-generated periodic report that misses a window is regenerated by the next pass rather than lost.

- **Consequences:** new `app/Bridge/Standup/` (`StandupConfig`, `StandupDigest`, `SeatSnapshot`, `BoardSnapshot`, `StandupService`, `StandupGate`) + `bridge:standup`; `WebhookController` schedules the second gate; three new `BRIDGE_STANDUP_*` env keys (`docs/config-schema.md`, `CLAUDE_DEPLOYMENT.md`). **`BridgePaths::unseenInboxLines()` is extracted from `InboxCommand` at its second real caller** — one definition of "unseen" (already-seen filtered, duplicate ids collapsed), so `bridge:inbox` and the digest cannot disagree about one inbox; `bridge:inbox`'s behaviour is unchanged — but **its pre-existing `test_inbox_collapses_duplicate_ids_on_read` was NOT the witness it is named for**, measured by mutating the collapse away while extracting it: the test stayed GREEN, because the cursor advance `array_unique()`s its ids (so it records one id whether the line was rendered once or twice) and an `expectsOutputToContain()` is satisfied by a doubled line. **A guard whose stated scope exceeds its actual predicate is the defect, and moving the code it names into a shared primitive widened it** — the rule now has two readers instead of one. Closed here: the `bridge:inbox` test asserts the occurrence COUNT (the only quantity that discriminates), and the primitive gets its own `BridgePathsUnseenInboxLinesTest`. Both, plus the digest's count, were watched red under that same mutant. **`BRIDGE_STANDUP_AGENT` is shape-validated at the config boundary** rather than concatenated into a path: the name becomes `<config_dir>/<agent>.yml`, so `../other-install/pm` would read a YAML outside the config dir and push this install's fleet snapshot at whatever channel it names.

**Every new assertion was watched failing first, under the mutant of the thing it guards** — an epoch-filled `last_delivery_at`, a gate-drop read as a delivery, a truncated read's lower bound printed as the depth, a `now_depth: 0` invented for a board with no lane model, a gate that fires while disabled, a blocking lock, a depth counting every card, the inbox dedup removed, the last-error marker never cleared, a swallowed misconfiguration, and a narrowed `catch` that lets a failing push escape the terminating callback. **⚠ The mutation harness's first run was killed mid-mutation and left one mutant on disk**, after which every later verdict measured a tree that was already red for an unrelated reason and the control was the only thing that said so — the harness now proves the filter GREEN immediately before each mutation and byte-verifies the restore, and a verdict over a non-green baseline is withheld rather than reported.

---

*[Additive annotation, 2026-09-03 (card#8432) — ADDITIVE, nothing above removed; DL-306 stays frozen as written.]* ⭐ **THE GATE SHAPE THIS ENTRY COPIED FROM DL-199 IS NOW HOISTED, AND `StandupGate` BINDS IT RATHER THAN RESTATING IT (DL-343).** This entry inherited DL-199's four properties *"verbatim"* — which is precisely how the app came to hold three hand-written copies of the interval marker, the non-blocking lock and the never-throws shell, DL-325's being the third. The digest's own decisions are untouched: what it may carry, the absent-rather-than-inferred field rule, the delivery-cadence cost, the misconfig back-off and `runPass()`'s two ingresses all stand exactly as written. What moved is the mechanism underneath, into `App\Bridge\Support\AfterResponseGate`.

## DL-307 — a `phpunit.xml` pin holds only if it is written TWICE, and the DB pins are deliberately left where an export can still reach them (card#7474)

- **Date:** 2026-08-23
- **Context:** Six other tenant seats share this deployment host, and roundtable rt#349 measured three concurrent PHP suites from different tenants colliding. This suite pinned no `REDIS_DB`/`REDIS_CACHE_DB`, so the indices resolved from whatever `.env` was present — measured at DB 4 with such a `.env`, and 0/1 (the values every other seat also gets by default) without one. A neighbouring suite writing or flushing the same keyspace is a wrong test result in either direction, **including a false green that gets merged**. The card's prescription was: pin both indices, and add `force="true"` to those pins and to the existing `DB_CONNECTION`/`DB_DATABASE` pins, because their present correctness depends on nothing happening to export those variables — a property of the environment, not of the configuration.
- **Decision:** pin `REDIS_DB=13` / `REDIS_CACHE_DB=12` (indices claimed for this suite and published to the other seats, so they are a commitment rather than a preference), and write every pin that must actually hold as a **pair** — `<env … force="true"/>` *and* `<server …/>`. Leave the `DB_*` group unforced and unpaired, against the card's own instruction. Add `Tests\Unit\PhpunitConfigPinTest` as the drift guard on the pairing.
- **Why a pair — `force="true"` alone does not do what its name implies, and this was measured before anything was built (canon #9).** With `REDIS_DB=9` exported against a pin written `<env … value="13" force="true"/>`, one probe through the real bootstrap reported: `getenv()='13'`, `$_ENV='13'`, **`$_SERVER='9'`, `env()='9'`, `config()='9'`**. PHPUnit's `PhpHandler::handleEnvVariables()` honors `force` by writing `putenv()` and `$_ENV` unconditionally and never touches `$_SERVER` — where an exported variable lands under this build's `variables_order=GPCS`. Laravel resolves `env()` through Dotenv's repository, whose `DEFAULT_ADAPTERS` are `ServerConstAdapter` **then** `EnvConstAdapter` (putenv appended last), so `$_SERVER` is read first and the forced pin loses. `handleServerVariables()` assigns `$_SERVER` unconditionally, so a `<server>` entry closes it: with the pair in place the same run reads `13` at every layer. **Had the card's instruction been followed and not checked, this change would have shipped a comment promising durability the file did not have** — the mostly-right artifact, which is worse than the unpinned state it replaced, because the next reader would trust it.
- **⛔ Why the `DB_*` group is the exception, and why leaving it is the correct call rather than the incomplete one.** `.github/workflows/laravel-tests.yml`'s `phpunit-mariadb` matrix (10.6 and 11) and the local recipe in `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` § Running MariaDB tests locally exercise the MariaDB driver by **exporting** `DB_CONNECTION`/`DB_HOST`/`DB_DATABASE` — which works *only* because an unforced pin yields to a real environment variable. Forcing them would make both matrix legs silently re-run SQLite: a green CI that has stopped testing the one thing it exists to test, and the same false-green class this card was filed to remove. The card's premise — that the pins are effective today only because nothing exports those variables — is exactly right and exactly inverted here: something *does* export them, on purpose, and that export is the coverage. Measured and preserved: with `DB_CONNECTION=mysql` exported, `config('database.default')` is `mysql`. The absence of `force` is now commented as load-bearing, so the next pass at "finish the force sweep" cannot take it for an oversight.
- **Which pins got which treatment, and why not all of them.** **Paired** (`<env force>` + `<server>`): `REDIS_DB` and `REDIS_CACHE_DB`, whose leaking reaches another tenant's data rather than only this suite's; and `BRIDGE_INSTALL_SUFFIX`, whose leaking reds every DB-touching test (G-013's symptom). **`force="true"` alone**: the values whose leaking would let the suite reach shared or outward infrastructure or change a result — `CACHE_STORE`, `QUEUE_CONNECTION`, `SESSION_DRIVER`, `BROADCAST_CONNECTION`, `MAIL_MAILER`, and the three telemetry switches. That tier buys the child-process/`getenv()` layer and *not* the in-process one, and is labelled as such rather than left to imply more. **Neither**: `APP_ENV` (Laravel's own environment selection — and every isolation-critical value is pinned individually, so a leaked `APP_ENV` cannot reach one through a `.env.<env>` file), `APP_MAINTENANCE_DRIVER` and `BCRYPT_ROUNDS` (an override changes duration or storage of nothing the suite asserts on). A blanket force over the whole block was rejected: it would have hidden the `DB_*` exception inside a uniform sweep.
- **Alternatives considered.** (a) **`force="true"` everywhere, per the card** — rejected on the measurement above: it does not deliver the property the card wants, and on `DB_*` it actively destroys CI coverage. (b) **`<server>` alone, dropping `<env>`** — rejected: `$_SERVER` is not inherited by a child process, and this suite spawns them (`Tests\Support\NestedSuite`, the `bin/` script harnesses), so the pinned value would stop at the process boundary. (c) **A runtime `config()` pin in `Tests\TestCase::setUp()`**, the fix G-017 took — not chosen *here* (a Redis index is not something a test overrides per-case, so the config file is its natural home and a `setUp()` pin would put one key's truth in two files), but it remains the right shape for a per-test-overridable value and G-017 is unchanged. (d) **A dedicated `phpunit-mariadb.xml` so `DB_*` could be forced in the main config** — rejected as out of scope and not clearly better: it adds a second config file to keep in sync and would need its own entry in the changelog gate's path scope, which is itself a change to what CI accepts and would need its own ruling.
- **Consequences:** `phpunit.xml` (two new pins, the pairing, `force` on the tier above, and three comment blocks — the mechanism, the `DB_*` exception, and the Redis claim); new `tests/Unit/PhpunitConfigPinTest.php`; `CLAUDE_TESTING.md` § Database configuration (rewritten — it claimed the block "sets the test environment unconditionally", which was never true and is now the subject of the section); `CLAUDE_GOTCHAS.md` **G-013** and **G-017**, both of which stated a mechanism this measurement falsifies; `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. **No `app/` change, no migration, no config key, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change.** The Redis pins are **latent, not live** — `CACHE_STORE=array` and `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync` mean nothing here selects Redis today — which is what makes them free to add and worth adding before something does.
- **Two doc claims corrected, because encountering a false claim makes it yours (canon #16).** **G-013** attributed the ambient `BRIDGE_INSTALL_SUFFIX` to a project-root `.env`. A `.env` cannot beat a `phpunit.xml` pin at all: phpunit writes before bootstrap and Laravel's Dotenv repository is `immutable()`, so loading `.env` is a no-op for any key already set — measured, with `BRIDGE_INSTALL_SUFFIX=-dev` in a `.env` and `config()` reading the pinned `''`. The real vector is an export, and G-013's remediation advice (add the variable to the wrapper invocation) was aimed at the wrong one. **G-017** concluded correctly that forcing did not fix its export, but explained it as `<env>` not reaching the `getenv()` layer; `force` does reach `getenv()`, measured, and the export wins from `$_SERVER` instead. Both entries are corrected in place with the measurement, per this log's convention of naming what a later finding falsified.
- **Bound, stated.** **UNMEASURED: whether Redis DB 13 or 12 is occupied by another tenant.** Their configurations are permission-denied to this seat, which is rt#349's own central point — pinning protects the neighbours from this suite, not this suite from them. The published-values table is the only substitute for a cross-seat audit no seat can perform. Also unmeasured: whether the paired pins hold under `php artisan test` as opposed to `vendor/bin/phpunit` — collision's `TestCommand::clearEnv()` clears every `.env`-named variable from the repository before spawning phpunit when `--env` is absent, which is a *different* interaction that this suite does not use (CI runs `vendor/bin/phpunit`).

## DL-308 — a merge into the integration branch from the card's OWN branch closes it: the DL-305 accept-set is widened with a structural term, because the lexical one accepted nothing this shop writes (card#7348)

- **Date:** 2026-08-23
- **Status:** implemented (card#7348, roundtable #343 — the widening is aimla-pm's ruling on the property they endorsed in DL-305, and operator-approved because it changes what the system acts on). **No migration, no new config key, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change.** DL-305 is not reverted and not weakened: this WIDENS its accept-set.
- **The number:** the board stamps this card `DL-0308`; the log's own header regex strips leading zeros (DL-295), so `## DL-308` and `DL-0308` name one decision.

- **Context — DL-305 shipped a gate nothing could satisfy, and it fails QUIET.** DL-305 is correct about its subject and its tests are good. Its accept-set is the defect, and the defect is an adoption cost nobody measured before it landed. Re-measured here against the shipped `ClosureGrammar::closesCard()` called on real merged-PR titles pulled from GitHub — not re-implemented, the actual class: **0 of 351 correlated merged PRs across all four PupFuzz repos close anything.** The house convention is `type(scope): summary (card#N[, DL-NNN])` and has never contained a closing verb; only an artificial `Closes card#7464` control passes, which is what makes the run a measurement rather than an absence. ⇒ Shipping DL-305 as-is means **no merged PR ever moves its card to Shipped**, with **no red anywhere**: CI passes, the merge succeeds, the card silently stands still. A board drifting out of sync with reality is precisely the failure this bridge exists to prevent, so the cure would have re-created the disease with the opposite sign. Prod is two versions behind (`v0.74.1`, DL-305 not an ancestor), which is the only reason this is not already an incident rather than a blocker on a card.

- **Decision — widen the accept-set with a STRUCTURAL term; keep everything else exactly as DL-305 built it.** On a gated outcome a card now moves when EITHER route is satisfied, and both are:
  1. **STRUCTURAL** (new, `PrOutcome::mergeClosesCard()`): the PR **merged into the integration branch** AND the **head branch ref itself names that card**.
  2. **LEXICAL** (DL-305, unchanged): a closing form in the PR **title** naming the card or the DL that resolved it.

  Untouched: the DL-218 foreign-mention guard, the title-vs-branch authority rule (card#5287), the DL-287 near-miss refusal, the one-grammar-over-both-stems shape, and the ungated `opened` / `closed_unmerged` / `started` / `reopened` outcomes.

- **The property this preserves, in the words it was agreed in:** *"no token that merely APPEARS may move a stage."* A foreign mention cannot satisfy (1) — **quoting someone else's card id does not rename your branch.** What the widening treats as closing is *a token corroborated by the branch's own identity, merged into the integration branch*, and merged-to-integration is exactly what the Shipped stage asserts. The head ref is not prose: it is minted by this install's own tooling (`board-card-start` → `card-<id>-slug`), which is why `cardTokenResolution()` has always treated it as AUTHORITATIVE over the title. DL-305's stated reason for excluding it — *"the branch names the work, not its completion"* — is true and is not what the structural term reads: it reads branch IDENTITY plus the fact of a merge, never the slug's words.

- **⛔ Why the STRICT card-token reading, and what it costs — disclosed here rather than discovered later.** The ref must carry a `CardTokenGrammar` token, the same authority that decides what names a card everywhere else, so **no second accept-set is minted**. It deliberately does NOT reuse `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::refCorroborates()` (the bare-id test: does any digit run in the ref equal the card id). That primitive's own docblock ACCEPTS an accidental-collision bound — `chore/bump-1-2-3` corroborating `card#2` — explicitly on the grounds that it *"only ever RELAXES a guard ... and never widens what can be selected."* **That justification does not survive being moved here, where the predicate authorizes a TERMINAL-STAGE move.** Measured price of the strict reading, on the same corpus: the legacy `<type>/<id>-slug` spelling carries the id but no token, so it misses — **55 vs 56 of 59 on the newest 25 merged PRs per repo (ceiling 56), and 271 vs 332 of 351 across all history.** The gap is entirely the older convention tailing off; the current one is `card-<id>-slug`. Every miss is LOUD (the withheld-merge warning fires, naming the ref it read) and the lexical route stays open. Under-promotion is recoverable by hand; the terminal move is not.
- **Reach, stated as the number that actually matters:** on the live convention this takes the gate from **0% to 93.2%** of correlated merged PRs (0 → 55 of 59), measured through the shipped predicate with both discriminating controls pinned (the artificial closing form still closes; a branch naming card 7464 does not close 7465).

*[Annotation, 2026-08-31 (card#8294) — ADDITIVE, nothing above removed; this entry stays frozen as written.] The reach figure above and the phrase **"on the live convention"** are a measurement of a CONVENTION, not a property of this predicate, and the convention has since moved. The house branch style flipped from `card-<id>-slug` to `<type>/<id>-slug` on 2026-08-29 — which carries the card's DIGITS but not the `card` TOKEN this decision deliberately requires — and the titles kept the bare `(card#N)` DL-305 rules a correlation. So both routes went dark at once: re-measured 2026-08-31 over this repo's newest 120 merged PRs (73 card-correlating and non-exempt), the structural route fires on **49 and misses on 24**, the lexical route fires on **0**, and the **8 most recent card-correlating PRs — #602 through #609 — take NEITHER route**. Every one merged green, logged `mention-vs-closure, DL-305/DL-308`, moved nothing, and was corrected by hand. **Nothing in this decision was wrong and nothing in it changed**; what was missing is that the dependency on the branch shape was declared in no document and asserted by no check, so a convention change could and did revoke a shipped gate silently. ⇒ card#8294 takes **this entry's own first Alternative** — *"change the convention instead: require a closing verb in every PR title, and extend `pr-title-lint` to red a non-closing one"* — as an ADDITION, not a reversal: both routes still close, the structural term is untouched, and the new `pr-title-lint` step reds only a PR that takes neither. Two of that alternative's three rejection grounds are unchanged (it retrains authors; it does nothing for historical PRs); the third, cost-vs-fit, is re-decided against the measured cost of the silence. The convention itself now lives in `CLAUDE_CONVENTIONS.md` § *PR titles*, which is the surface whose absence this annotation is really about.]*

*[Annotation, 2026-09-01 (card#8344 / DL-327) — ADDITIVE, nothing above removed; this entry stays frozen as written.] The structural route this entry created is the door the `[no-close]` marker exists to shut, and the reason is a PREMISE of this decision rather than a flaw in it. The argument above is that the head ref carries the branch's IDENTITY because this install's own tooling minted it for that card — which is true, and remains true, of a PR written FOR the card while deliberately NOT finishing it. Such a PR has exactly the ref a closing PR has, so the premise holds and the conclusion is still wrong; measured on real merges (`mezzanine#24` → card 7341, roundtable 388). **Nothing in this entry is reversed and the structural term is unchanged**: `PrOutcome::mergeClosesCard()` gains one conjunct, `! NoCloseGrammar::marks($title)`, which can only WITHHOLD. Read together with the 2026-08-31 annotation above, this entry's accept-set has now been narrowed twice for the same reason — a ref's identity is strong evidence of WHICH card a merge is about and weaker evidence that the merge FINISHES it — and DL-327 is where that is recorded, along with why no predicate over the artifact could have supplied the missing half.]*

- **⛔ Release merges are NOT widened.** Only the integration merge takes the structural route. A release PR's head is a disposable `release/vX` that names no card, so the term would rarely fire there anyway — stating it as a *condition* is what stops a future release convention that DID name a card from silently acquiring a terminal-stage move nobody approved. `merged_to_main` still needs a closing form, and DL-207's promote sweep still owns Shipped→Released and is still not gated (DL-305 §9 stands).

- **`bridge:reconcile` gets the identical term, and `GitHubReadClient::getPull()` now projects `head_ref`.** Same lockstep argument DL-305 made for `title`, now cutting both ways: a term on one path and not the other means the backstop and the event path **disagree about which merges close a card**, and `--fix` runs on a schedule, so the disagreement arrives hourly with a CLI's name on it. The term therefore lives on `PrOutcome` and **neither path spells it**. The ref is available on the whole population the backstop reads: GitHub retains `head.ref` on the PR record after the branch is deleted, which is the normal post-merge state of every PR this leg touches (`head.repo` is the field that goes null on a deleted fork, and nothing here reads it). An absent ref reads as `''`, which names no card — the same safe direction the title takes.

- **The operator-facing sentence is now composed, not restated.** DL-305 left two surfaces — the withheld-merge warning and `bridge:check`'s per-mapping line — rendering `ClosureGrammar::describe()` under a sentence asserting the TITLE is the only thing that can move a card. That sentence went FALSE the moment a second route landed, and on `bridge:check` it is the worst possible surface for it: its whole job is telling an operator what they inherited. `PrOutcome::describeClosure()` composes both halves, each rendered from its own authority (`ClosureGrammar` and `CardTokenGrammar`), so neither can be retyped or go stale — the DL-239 discipline extended across two authorities rather than abandoned at the seam. The warning additionally **names the head ref it read**: with two closure surfaces, a line quoting only the title sends an operator to rewrite prose when the answer is that their branch is called `fix/streaming-timeout`.

- **⚠ Two witnesses were RE-ANCHORED, and that is a decision, not a green-washing.** DL-305's witnesses 1 and 3a ran a merged-to-dev PR on branch `card-4811-widget` whose title merely mentioned card#4811, asserting NO move. **That fixture is now an ACCEPTED case** — it is a PR that IS card 4811's work, merged to the integration branch. No assertion was weakened; the accept-set changed by ruling, and the witnesses had to be re-pointed at the vector that is still refused: a title citing a card the BRANCH DOES NOT NAME, which is the peer incident this card was filed for. Their fixture's default head is now `fix/streaming-timeout`, which also makes witness 2 evidence about the LEXICAL route specifically (with a card-naming branch it would have passed for the other reason). The re-anchoring is recorded in the test file itself, where the next auditor reads it.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Change the convention instead — require a closing verb in every PR title, and extend `pr-title-lint` to red a non-closing one.** The honest option and the named fallback if widening had been refused. Rejected on cost and on fit: it retrains every author, every template and every release tool across four repos, and `Closes DL-218` reads oddly for a decision-log token. It also does nothing for the 351 historical PRs.
  - **Ship DL-305 as-is and accept a manual promotion pass.** Rejected: it fails quiet, which is the property that makes drift invisible, and "someone will remember to sweep the board" is not a mechanism.
  - **Reuse `refCorroborates()`'s bare-id test** (+61 historical, +1 recent). Rejected on the accepted-collision bound above: the reasoning that made that bound acceptable is scoped to a flag that cannot authorize anything.
  - **Hoist `pr-title-lint`'s branch predicate into a PHP authority and use THAT.** The canon-#5-correct answer to the divergence named below, and rejected here as scope: it changes what a CI gate accepts (a hard gate) and deserves its own ruling rather than riding this one.
  - **Let the head ref's DL token close the DL-resolved set.** Rejected as unmeasured — no branch in the corpus needs it, and it would widen the one-to-many DL path on a structural term whose whole safety argument is that a branch names ONE card.
  - **Apply the structural term to `merged_to_main` too.** Rejected — see the release-merge clause.

- **⚠ A KNOWN DIVERGENCE, filed rather than repaired.** `.github/workflows/pr-title-lint.yml` answers *"does this branch name a card id"* with its own wider predicate (`^([a-z-]+/)?(card-?)?([0-9]+)-`, card#6822) and EXTRACTS the id from it, so `fix/6100-slug` is a card-id branch to CI and is not one to this gate. Two answers to one question is the drift shape this repo keeps paying for (DL-239's whole lineage). It is recorded in `PrOutcome::mergeClosesCard()`'s docblock and is the natural home for the loose-reading question if the residual above ever costs enough to matter.

- **⚠ TWO RESIDUALS aimla-pm named, recorded and deliberately NOT built.** Neither is a condition of the agreement. (a) **A multi-PR card promotes at its FIRST merged PR** — three merged PRs here track one card, and the structural term fires on each. (b) **A human's "does not close on this commit" ruling on the card's own work PR is overridden** — the peer incident, in the one configuration the widening cannot discriminate. **Their shared root, which is the durable finding: the grammar layer can read INTENT; it cannot read AUTHORITY.** No predicate over a title and a branch ref can know that a person decided otherwise. The fix is therefore card-side — a hold/pin marker the writeback refuses to move past *whatever the grammar concludes* — which is a different layer, a different surface (kanban, not the bridge), and its own decision. Named here as the follow-up; the operator is filing it.

  *[Annotation, 2026-08-30 (card#8289) — ADDITIVE, nothing above removed.]* **That follow-up was mostly ALREADY BUILT, and the clause calling it *"a different surface (kanban, not the bridge)"* is the part that was wrong.** The marker shipped in 2026-07 as `PinGuard` (DL-178) and is read BY THE BRIDGE; what it lacked was reach — DL-178 scoped the consult to the `started` outcome on purpose, so it never fired on a merge, which is exactly the move residual (b) is about. card#8289 hoists the consult to every outcome, so **residual (b) is now closed for a human who RECORDS the ruling on the card** (a non-empty `block_reason` or a `no-automove` tag) and stands unchanged for one who does not. Residual (a) — the multi-PR card promoting at its first merged PR — is untouched. See the card#8289 annotation on DL-178 for the ruling and its two overrides.

- **Consequences:** `PrOutcome` gains `INTEGRATION_MERGE` / `RELEASE_MERGE` constants (`MERGE_OUTCOMES` is now composed from them; `forMergedBase()` stops spelling the strings), `mergeClosesCard()` and `describeClosure()`; `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifier::closureFilter()` takes the head ref and ORs the structural term in, its withheld-merge warning renders `describeClosure()` and names the ref, and its class docblock's *"the TITLE is the only closure surface"* paragraph is corrected (it was the DL-305 argument this entry overturns); `GitHubReadClient::getPull()` projects `head_ref`; `ReconcileCommand::closes()` takes the ref + outcome and asks the structural term first, and its skip line names the ref; `WritebackMappingConfigCheck` renders `describeClosure()` (its `ClosureGrammar` import is gone — it no longer speaks to one authority). Tests: `PrOutcomeTest` +4, `GitHubPrCardMoveClassifierTest` +4 (two re-anchored, fixture generalized), `ReconcileCommandTest` +3, `GitHubReadClientTest` and `WritebackMappingConfigCheckTest` extended. `ClosureGrammar` and `ClosureGrammarTest` are **untouched**, which is the cheapest available evidence that the lexical route was widened around rather than modified. Docs: `docs/writeback.md` (§ *Mention vs closure* rewritten, the step-1 bullet, the *Card-token correlation* clause, the reconcile clause), `docs/config-schema.md`, `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

- **Every new predicate was watched failing first (canon #9) — eight mutations, each proven to have LANDED before its verdict was read** (sha256 before/after, the mutated line read back off disk, and a byte-identical restore verified; a mutation that fails to mutate scores as a pass, which is the trap this harness exists to avoid): the structural term deleted from the classifier filter (3 red); the integration-branch condition dropped so a release merge closes on a branch name (2, incl. the release witness); the term re-keyed to *"the ref names ANY card"* rather than THIS card (3 — the bundled-DL filter, the backstop negative, and the predicate test); the term deleted from `bridge:reconcile` while the event path keeps it (1 — the divergence itself); `head_ref` no longer projected by `GitHubReadClient` (3); the head ref not passed into the classifier's filter (3); the ref dropped from the withheld-merge warning (1); and `bridge:check` reverted to the lexical accept-set alone (1). **A finding the mutation run produced rather than confirmed:** the end-to-end foreign-mention witness stays GREEN under the ANY-card mutation, because on that event the title-vs-branch rule refuses the foreign card at SELECTION and it never reaches the closure filter. The witness therefore does not cover the keying — three other tests do — and its comment now says so instead of claiming a discrimination it does not have.

- **Bounds, stated.** **UNMEASURED: the peer installs.** The corpus is this seat's four repos; aimla's and sola's branch conventions were not read, and an install whose branches do not name cards gets DL-305's behaviour unchanged (loud under-promotion, never a wrong move) — the safe direction, but it means the reach figure above is this shop's, not the fleet's. **UNMEASURED: `head.ref` on a PR whose head repository was deleted outright** (not merely the branch); the retention claim is for the branch-deleted case, which is the population the backstop actually reads. **NOT EXERCISED against live GitHub:** the reconcile leg is covered by faked HTTP, as the rest of that command's suite is.

## DL-309 — the vendored normalizer re-mirrors kanban's single-decorated-integer rule, and `TrackedCardRef` stops deriving a PR number OUTSIDE it (card#7536)

- **Date:** 2026-08-24
- **Status:** implemented (card#7536, operator-approved for parts 1 and 2 of that card — each changes what the bridge DERIVES from a stored value, so it was gated). **No migration, no new config key, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change, no HTTP contract change.**
- **The number:** allocated with `next-dl bridge` (DL-295), never a scan of this file. `DL-0310` was claimed by a redundant second call to the allocator in the same session and is **burned, not used** — the counter is raise-only and mints no obligation to fill a gap.

- **Context — two authorities, two answers, and the bridge's was a fabrication.** kanban-board's `ExternalReferenceNormalizer` (its **DL-251**, merged 2026-08-23) ruled that *a correlation value that is not a single decorated integer derives NO ref*. The bridge carries a deliberate 1:1 **mirror** of that class at `app/Bridge/Support/ExternalReferenceNormalizer.php`, and the mirror did not move — so on the deployed v0.75.0 prod install the same stored value answered two ways: `'1.5'` → PR `15` here, nothing there; `'2026-08-23'` → `20260823` here, nothing there; `'PR 12 of 34'` → `1234` here, nothing there. Well-formed values (`'DL-028'`, `'85'`) agreed before and after. **Each fabricated ref names a REAL, unrelated pull request or decision**, which is what makes silence the harm: nothing on either side reports a mismatch. The 2026-08-24 census over 753 cards on boards 5/8/12 found zero drifted values, so the divergence was latent — real in code, unexercised in data.

- **Decision 1 — re-mirror the authority, both halves, byte-identical.** `canonicalize()` takes `float|int|string` and renders a float faithfully **before** the system branch, and a numeric system's ref must be **one** digit run (`/^\D*(\d+)\D*$/`) rather than the concatenation of every run found. The method body is byte-identical to kanban's post-DL-251 source, so the mirror stays diffable — the docblocks differ in exactly one word, saying *kanban DL-251*, because **this repo's own DL-251 is a different decision** and an unqualified reference here would name it.
- **⛔ The float half is NOT dead code here, and it is not carried on mirror-fidelity grounds alone.** kanban's sibling audit recorded the bridge's float half as *unreachable — every caller casts to string first*, and that was TRUE and was re-verified against all four pre-change call sites (`KanbanClient::correlateDl` takes `string $dl` and casts the card side; `ReconcileCommand::closes` guards `is_string || is_int` and reads `ClosureGrammar::closedDls()`, a `list<string>`). **Decision 2 below makes it reachable**: `TrackedCardRef` reads `pr_number` straight off a decoded card payload, where a number-typed kanban field arrives as a PHP **float**. Porting only the digit-run half would have left `1.5` truncating to PR 1 through the weak-mode `int|string` coercion at the new call site — the exact defect, one layer down.

- **Decision 2 — `TrackedCardRef::fromPayload` asks the normalizer WHICH pull request a `pr_number` names, instead of casting.** It ran its own `(int) $pn`, so fixing the normalizer alone would not have closed the bridge side: **measured, not asserted** — with the normalizer fixed and this untouched, 3 of the new tests stay RED. One question, one authority (canon #5).
- **⛔ What deliberately does NOT move: the ADMISSION test.** The leg stays a *positive bare number* (`is_numeric($pn) && (float) $pn > 0`), exactly as before. Routing the raw value through the normalizer with the admission test dropped would have **widened** what the reconcile and the promote sweep act on: `-5` canonicalizes to the ref `"5"` and `'#85'` to `"85"` — both refs the kanban server really does index — so a value nobody meant as a PR number would have started driving an outward GitHub read and a card move. That widening is a separate ruling nobody has made, and it is pinned by a test rather than left to prose: two mutants (drop the sign term; drop `is_numeric`) each red it on the exact value class it guards.

- **Blast radius, enumerated by consumer** — `canonicalize()` now has five call sites across three consumers, and every one narrows in the same direction, toward the server:
  1. **`TrackedCardRef::fromPayload`** (reconcile + DL-207 promote) — a `pr_number` naming no single integer is no longer a tracked card; it reaches no GitHub read and no move.
  2. **`KanbanClient::correlateDl`** (scan mode only; `ref` is the default and the only mode the multi-repo adopters run) — a card whose stored `dl_number` carries several digit runs no longer false-matches a DL token. The `$want` side cannot move: `DlTokenGrammar` yields one run by construction.
  3. **`ReconcileCommand::closes`** — the same narrowing on the card's own `dl_number` in the DL closure compare.
  4. **`canonicalizeSource`** and everything keyed on it (dependabot repo attribution, `bridge:check` source coverage, `WritebackConfig`'s repo index) — **untouched**; the source path has its own signature and its own callers, all proven strings.

- **Seen to fail (canon #9).** Against the pre-change files with the new tests in place: **12 red** (5 provider cases + 7 tests), including the real surface — `bridge:reconcile --fix` over a card carrying `pr_number: 1.5` fetched `/pulls/1` and PATCHed the card, and now sends neither. Controls kept deliberately green on both sides so the refusal is scoped to values naming no single integer, not to floats or numeric strings generally: `85` / `85.0` / `'85'` / `'085'` all still track PR 85, and `canonicalize('github_pr', 85.0)` is still `'85'`.

- **Sibling audit — reported, NOT fixed (canon #7).** Two further sites derive a PR identity from a payload value with `is_numeric` + `(int)`, outside this change's approved scope, and each changes what the system accepts, so each needs its own ruling: **`CardTokenCorroboration::tracksPr`** (a card storing `'1.5'` corroborates an event for PR 1, which is what decides whether an uncorroborated title-only `card#` token may write) and **`KanbanClient::correlatePr` / `correlateIssue`** scan branches (a card storing `'1.5'` matches PR 1 — legacy mode only; `ref` mode asks the server and already refuses). Appended to card#7536, which is the class item. **`KanbanMoveCardHandler`'s `stamp_pr` cast is NOT in the class**: that value is the classifier's own PR number off a GitHub delivery, an integer at the source. Part 3 of the card — integrality validation in the toolkit's `kbcard --pr` / `--issue`, the operator path that MINTS such a value — is a different repo and is not this change.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Canonicalize the float to agree with the string (`1.5` → `"15"` on both paths).** Rejected upstream and rejected again here: it fixes the type-dependence and keeps the disease, because `"15"` is a real, different pull request. Refusing is the only answer that cannot correlate a card to somebody else's work.
  - **Improve the mirror locally instead of tracking the authority** (e.g. keep `int|string` and pre-cast at the new call site). Rejected: the class's whole contract is *answer exactly as the server does*, and a local variant is a second implementation that no 1:1 diff would ever flag.
  - **Leave the float half out as unreachable defensive code (canon #6).** Rejected on measurement, not on principle — Decision 2 makes a float reach it on the very next line of this change.

- **Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Support/ExternalReferenceNormalizer.php`, `app/Bridge/Writeback/TrackedCardRef.php`, three test files, `docs/writeback.md` § Reconciliation, `docs/kanban-integration-contract.md`. The delta an operator can observe is **an absent correlation where a wrong one used to be**: a card carrying a malformed `pr_number`/`dl_number` is now simply not tracked by `bridge:reconcile` or the promote sweep, with no skip line — it names no PR, so it is not a skipped card, it is not a card. **UNMEASURED, and inherited from the card:** whether any live card holds such a value; the census that found zero was read on 2026-08-24 and is not re-run here.

## DL-311 — the corroboration gate and both `scan` correlations stop deriving a PR/issue number OUTSIDE the normalizer, and the question gets ONE implementation (card#7564)

- **Date:** 2026-08-24
- **Status:** implemented (card#7564, operator-approved as ONE ruling over the whole class — each site changes what the bridge MATCHES and therefore what it accepts, so it was gated). **No migration, no new config key, no token-scope change, no receiver accept/reject change, no HTTP contract change.**
- **The number:** allocated with `next-dl bridge` (DL-295), never a scan of this file.

- **Context — DL-309 closed the sites its investigation named, not the SHAPE.** Three more sites answered *"which pull request / issue does this stored value name"* with a bare `(int)` cast, outside the normalizer that DL-309 made the authority, so a card storing `'1.5'` still read as PR **1** — a real, unrelated pull request the kanban server derives no ref from at all (its DL-251). Re-verified against merged `dev` (`6175df2`) rather than inherited.

- **Decision 1 — `CardTokenCorroboration::tracksPr` asks the normalizer, and the direction of its failure is the severity.** `refuses()` returns `! tracksPr(...)`, so this predicate is what stands between a title-only `card#` token and a card mutation: a false *"same PR"* does not refuse a write, it **ALLOWS** one. A card storing `'1.5'` corroborated an event for PR 1 and the uncorroborated title-only move (and the card#5953 `block_reason` SET) went through onto a card the pull request had nothing to do with. **Reachable on the default configuration.** The docblock claimed *"anything non-numeric on either side compares equal to nothing — fail-closed"*, which was true of NON-numeric values and silent about the numeric ones that truncate; that claim is true again. `tracksPr` stays public and keeps both consumers — the gate and the move handler's stamp (replay-vs-second-PR) — because it is one question asked for two purposes.
- **Decision 2 — `KanbanClient::correlatePr` / `correlateIssue` scan branches ask the same authority.** `correlateDl`'s scan branch already canonicalized; the PR and issue keys cast. So `scan` matched a card that `ref` mode — which asks the server — had already refused: **two modes of one correlation answering one card differently**, which is the same two-authorities defect DL-309 exists to end, one boundary over. ⚠ Ranked **present-but-not-reachable**: `BRIDGE_WRITEBACK_CORRELATION` defaults to `ref` and no install here runs `scan`; a config flip reaches it. Its test constructs the mode explicitly and is **synthetic, not a live-path witness**.
- **⛔ The `scan` branch is NOT dead and was NOT removed.** Asked and answered before the fix: it is the documented, supported fallback for a kanban predating by-ref (< v0.17.2) **or one whose `task_external_references` is not backfilled** — a DATA state, not only a version state — and `WritebackByRefCheck`'s live operator-facing warning still ends *"…or set `BRIDGE_WRITEBACK_CORRELATION=scan`"*. Retiring it is a support-drop decision nobody has made. The cast was fixed inside it; the branch and its wiring are untouched.

- **Decision 3 — ONE predicate, hoisted, not four spellings of it (canon #5).** `BareRefNumber` now owns the whole question and is shared by the three sites above **plus `TrackedCardRef`**, whose inline form it replaces byte-equivalently. Extracting at the fourth call site rather than writing a fifth is the point: DL-309's own sibling audit is what found instances 2–4, and a new local copy beside them would have re-minted the divergence the class item exists to close.
- **⛔ ADMISSION vs DERIVATION — the split DL-309 turned on, held at every site.** The **derivation** (which identifier an admitted value names) is what moved to the normalizer, everywhere. The **admission** (a POSITIVE BARE number) moved only as far as being hoisted — its predicate is unchanged from the form DL-309 pinned, and sharing it wholesale with the normalizer was again declined: `-5` canonicalizes to `"5"` and `'#85'` to `"85"`, refs the kanban server really does index, so admitting them would start correlating cards off values nobody meant as a PR number. **One qualification, and it is a preservation rather than a change:** `tracksPr`'s pre-change admission was `is_numeric` alone, with the SIGN carried by the `(int) === (int)` comparison it replaced (`-5 ≠ 5`); canonicalization discards the sign, so the shared `> 0` term is what keeps that refusal rather than widening it. Everything the change moves, moves toward refusing.

- **Blast radius, enumerated by consumer** — every one narrows, and only on values naming no single integer:
  1. **`CardTokenCorroboration::tracksPr`** → the uncorroborated title-only `card#` move (`KanbanMoveCardHandler`) and `block_reason` SET (`KanbanBlockReasonHandler`) are REFUSED — alert + card note — where they used to be written; and the stamp's replay-vs-second-PR test records a drop rather than staying silent.
  2. **`KanbanClient::correlatePr`** (scan only) → a dependabot correlation no longer false-matches.
  3. **`KanbanClient::correlateIssue`** (scan only) → the coord-card correlation no longer false-matches.
  4. **`TrackedCardRef::fromPayload`** → **unchanged**; the hoist is behavior-preserving and DL-309's admission mutants still red it.

- **Seen to fail (canon #9).** Against the pre-change call sites with the new tests in place: **5 red** — 2 on the predicate (`CardTokenCorroborationTest`), 1 at the REAL surface (the move handler sends the PATCH for a card storing `'1.5'` on an event for PR 1, and now sends none), and 2 on the scan arms, split into one test each so neither hid behind the other's failure. ⚠ The two scan reds are **synthetic** — the mode is constructed, not exercised by any configured install. The primitive's own tests are new code, so they were falsified by mutation instead: dropping the `> 0` admission term reds **4** (including DL-309's own `TrackedCardRef` pins, which is the evidence the hoist preserved that predicate), and replacing the derivation with `(string) (int)` reds **10**. Controls kept deliberately green throughout: `85` / `85.0` / `'085'` / `'148'` corroborate and correlate exactly as before.

- **Sibling sweep — the open axis card#7564 named, now closed with a null result.** Two predicates over `app/`: every `is_numeric` site (63) and every `(int)`/`(float)` cast applied directly to a payload/card read (~40), each hit read rather than counted. No further site derives an external identifier from a caller-supplied correlation value; the rest cast **kanban- or GitHub-generated** ids (task id, board id, stage id, swimlane id, a delivery's `pull_request.number`, a page `meta.total`) or operator config. `KanbanMoveCardHandler`'s `stamp_pr` stays dispositioned OUT of the class for that reason, as does `CardNote::render`, which was checked and is faithful — an operator's refusal note shows `'1.5'`, not `1`. ⚠ **UNMEASURED, inherited from the card:** whether any live card holds such a value. The 2026-08-24 census over 753 cards found zero and was not re-run.

- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Fix only `tracksPr` (the reachable one) and leave the scan branches.** Rejected — that is what DL-309 did with the sites it found, and it is why this decision exists. The class item, not the instance, is what closes the question.
  - **Delete the `scan` branch instead of fixing it.** Rejected on evidence: it is reachable by config and documented as the by-ref fallback, including in a live `bridge:check` remediation string. Not this change's ruling to make.
  - **Share the normalizer's admission too (drop the `> 0` / `is_numeric` terms).** Rejected for the second time, for DL-309's reason: it widens what the writeback acts on toward values nobody meant as a PR number.

- **Consequences:** `app/Bridge/Writeback/BareRefNumber.php` (new), `CardTokenCorroboration.php`, `KanbanClient.php`, `TrackedCardRef.php`, four test files, `docs/writeback.md` (§ Precedence — the corroboration gate; § Correlation mode `ref` vs `scan`), `docs/CHANGELOG.md`. The delta an operator can observe is **a refusal where a wrong write used to happen**: an uncorroborated title-only `card#` on a card whose `pr_number` names no single pull request now alerts (`card_token_uncorroborated`) and leaves a card note instead of moving the card.
